texts.job.34.11: Porque él pagará al hombre según su obra, Y él le hará hallar conforme á su camino.
texts.job.34.12: Sí, por cierto, Dios no hará injusticia, Y el Omnipotente no pervertirá el derecho.
texts.job.34.13: ¿Quién visitó por él la tierra? ¿Y quién puso en orden todo el mundo?
texts.job.34.14: Si él pusiese sobre el hombre su corazón, Y recogiese así su espíritu y su aliento,
texts.job.34.15: Toda carne perecería juntamente, Y el hombre se tornaría en polvo.
texts.job.34.16: Si pues hay en ti entendimiento, oye esto: Escucha la voz de mis palabras.
texts.job.34.17: ¿Enseñorearáse el que aborrece juicio? ¿Y condenarás tú al que es tan justo?
texts.job.34.18: ¿Hase de decir al rey: Perverso; Y á los príncipes: Impíos?
texts.job.34.19: ¿Cuánto menos á aquel que no hace acepción de personas de príncipes, Ni el rico es de él más respetado que el pobre? Porque todos son obras de sus manos.
texts.job.34.20: En un momento morirán, y á media noche Se alborotarán los pueblos, y pasarán, Y sin mano será quitado el poderoso.
texts.job.34.21: Porque sus ojos están sobre los caminos del hombre, Y ve todos sus pasos.
texts.job.34.22: No hay tinieblas ni sombra de muerte Donde se encubran los que obran maldad.
texts.job.34.23: No carga pues él al hombre más de lo justo, Para que vaya con Dios á juicio.
texts.job.34.24: El quebrantará á los fuertes sin pesquisa, Y hará estar otros en su lugar.
texts.job.34.25: Por tanto él hará notorias las obras de ellos, Cuando los trastornará en la noche, y serán quebrantados.
texts.job.34.26: Como á malos los herirá En lugar donde sean vistos:
texts.job.34.27: Por cuanto así se apartaron de él, Y no consideraron todos sus caminos;
texts.job.34.28: Haciendo venir delante de él el clamor del pobre, Y que oiga el clamor de los necesitados.
texts.job.34.29: Y si él diere reposo, ¿quién inquietará? Si escondiere el rostro, ¿quién lo mirará? Esto sobre una nación, y lo mismo sobre un hombre;
texts.job.34.30: Haciendo que no reine el hombre hipócrita Para vejaciones del pueblo.
texts.job.34.31: De seguro conviene se diga á Dios: Llevado he ya castigo, no más ofenderé:
texts.job.34.32: Enséñame tú lo que yo no veo: Que si hice mal, no lo haré más.
texts.job.34.33: ¿Ha de ser eso según tu mente? El te retribuirá, ora rehuses, Ora aceptes, y no yo: Di si no, lo que tú sabes.
texts.job.34.34: Los hombres de seso dirán conmigo, Y el hombre sabio me oirá:
texts.job.34.35: Que Job no habla con sabiduría, Y que sus palabras no son con entendimiento.
texts.job.34.36: Deseo yo que Job sea probado ampliamente, A causa de sus respuestas por los hombres inicuos.
texts.job.34.37: Porque á su pecado añadió impiedad: Bate las manos entre nosotros, Y contra Dios multiplica sus palabras.
texts.job.35.1: Y PROCEDIENDO Eliú en su razonamiento, dijo:
texts.job.35.2: ¿Piensas ser conforme á derecho Esto que dijiste: Más justo soy yo que Dios?
texts.job.35.3: Porque dijiste: ¿Qué ventaja sacarás tú de ello? ¿O qué provecho tendré de mi pecado?
texts.job.35.4: Yo te responderé razones, Y á tus compañeros contigo.
texts.job.35.5: Mira á los cielos, y ve, Y considera que las nubes son más altas que tú.
texts.job.35.6: Si pecares, ¿qué habrás hecho contra él? Y si tus rebeliones se multiplicaren, ¿qué le harás tú?
texts.job.35.7: Si fueres justo, ¿qué le darás á el? ¿O qué recibirá de tu mano?
texts.job.35.8: Al hombre como tú dañará tu impiedad, Y al hijo del hombre aprovechará tu justicia.
texts.job.35.9: A causa de la multitud de las violencias clamarán, Y se lamentarán por el poderío de los grandes.
texts.job.35.10: Y ninguno dice: ¿Dónde está Dios mi Hacedor, Que da canciones en la noche,
texts.job.35.11: Que nos enseña más que á las bestias de la tierra, Y nos hace sabios más que las aves del cielo?
texts.job.35.12: Allí clamarán, y él no oirá, Por la soberbia de los malos.
texts.job.35.13: Ciertamente Dios no oirá la vanidad, Ni la mirará el Omnipotente.
texts.job.35.14: Aunque más digas, No lo mirará; Haz juicio delante de él, y en él espera.
texts.job.35.15: Mas ahora, porque en su ira no visita, Ni conoce con rigor,
texts.job.35.16: Por eso Job abrió su boca vanamente, Y multiplica palabras sin sabiduría.
texts.job.36.2: Espérame un poco, y enseñarte he; Porque todavía tengo razones en orden á Dios.
texts.job.36.3: Tomaré mi noticia de lejos, Y atribuiré justicia á mi Hacedor.
texts.job.36.4: Porque de cierto no son mentira mis palabras; Contigo está el que es íntegro en sus conceptos.
texts.job.36.5: He aquí que Dios es grande, mas no desestima á nadie; Es poderoso en fuerza de sabiduría.
texts.job.36.6: No otorgará vida al impío, Y á los afligidos dará su derecho.
texts.job.36.7: No quitará sus ojos del justo; Antes bien con los reyes los pondrá en solio para siempre, Y serán ensalzados.
texts.job.36.8: Y si estuvieren prendidos en grillos, Y aprisionados en las cuerdas de aflicción,
texts.job.36.9: El les dará á conocer la obra de ellos, Y que prevalecieron sus rebeliones.
texts.job.36.10: Despierta además el oído de ellos para la corrección, Y díce les que se conviertan de la iniquidad.
texts.job.36.11: Si oyeren, y le sirvieren, Acabarán sus días en bien, y sus años en deleites.
texts.job.36.12: Mas si no oyeren, serán pasados á cuchillo, Y perecerán sin sabiduría.
texts.job.36.13: Empero los hipócritas de corazón lo irritarán más, Y no clamarán cuando él los atare.
texts.job.36.14: Fallecerá el alma de ellos en su mocedad, Y su vida entre los sodomitas.
texts.job.36.15: Al pobre librará de su pobreza, Y en la aflicción despertará su oído.
texts.job.36.16: Asimismo te apartaría de la boca de la angustia A lugar espacioso, libre de todo apuro; Y te asentará mesa llena de grosura.
texts.job.36.17: Mas tú has llenado el juicio del impío, En vez de sustentar el juicio y la justicia.
texts.job.36.18: Por lo cual teme que en su ira no te quite con golpe, El cual no puedas apartar de ti con gran rescate.
texts.job.36.19: ¿Hará él estima de tus riquezas, ni del oro, Ni de todas las fuerzas del poder?
texts.job.36.20: No anheles la noche, En que desaparecen los pueblos de su lugar.
texts.job.36.21: Guárdate, no tornes á la iniquidad; Pues ésta escogiste más bien que la aflicción.
texts.job.36.22: He aquí que Dios es excelso con su potencia; ¿Qué enseñador semejante á él?
texts.job.36.23: ¿Quién le ha prescrito su camino? ¿Y quién le dirá: Iniquidad has hecho?
texts.job.36.24: Acuérdate de engrandecer su obra, La cual contemplan los hombres.
texts.job.36.25: Los hombres todos la ven; Mírala el hombre de lejos.
texts.job.36.26: He aquí, Dios es grande, y nosotros no le conocemos; Ni se puede rastrear el número de sus años.
texts.job.36.27: El reduce las gotas de las aguas, Al derramarse la lluvia según el vapor;
texts.job.36.28: Las cuales destilan las nubes, Goteando en abundancia sobre los hombres.
texts.job.36.29: ¿Quién podrá tampoco comprender la extensión de las nubes, Y el sonido estrepitoso de su pabellón?
texts.job.36.30: He aquí que sobre él extiende su luz, Y cobija con ella las raíces de la mar.
texts.job.36.31: Bien que por esos medios castiga á los pueblos, A la multitud da comida.
texts.job.36.32: Con las nubes encubre la luz, Y mándale no brillar, interponiendo aquéllas.
texts.job.36.33: Tocante á ella anunciará el trueno, su compañero, Que hay acumulación de ira sobre el que se eleva.
texts.job.37.1: A ESTO también se espanta mi corazón, Y salta de su lugar.
texts.job.37.2: Oid atentamente su voz terrible, y el sonido que sale de su boca.
texts.job.37.3: Debajo de todos los cielos lo dirige, Y su luz hasta los fines de la tierra.
texts.job.37.4: Después de ella bramará el sonido, Tronará él con la voz de su magnificencia; Y aunque sea oída su voz, no los detiene.
texts.job.37.5: Tronará Dios maravillosamente con su voz; El hace grandes cosas, que nosotros no entendemos.
texts.job.37.6: Porque á la nieve dice: Desciende á la tierra; También á la llovizna, Y á los aguaceros de su fortaleza.
texts.job.37.7: Así hace retirarse á todo hombre, Para que los hombres todos reconozcan su obra.
texts.job.37.8: La bestia se entrará en su escondrijo, Y estaráse en sus moradas.
texts.job.37.9: Del mediodía viene el torbellino, Y el frío de los vientos del norte.
texts.job.37.10: Por el soplo de Dios se da el hielo, Y las anchas aguas son constreñidas.
texts.job.37.11: Regando también llega á disipar la densa nube, Y con su luz esparce la niebla.
texts.job.37.12: Asimismo por sus designios se revuelven las nubes en derredor, Para hacer sobre la haz del mundo, En la tierra, lo que él les mandara.
texts.job.37.13: Unas veces por azote, otras pos causa de su tierra, Otras por misericordia las hará parecer.
texts.job.37.14: Escucha esto, Job; Repósate, y considera las maravillas de Dios.
texts.job.37.15: ¿Supiste tú cuándo Dios las ponía en concierto, Y hacía levantar la luz de su nube?
texts.job.37.16: ¿Has tú conocido las diferencias de las nubes, Las maravillas del Perfecto en sabiduría?
texts.job.37.17: ¿Por qué están calientes tus vestidos Cuando se fija el viento del mediodía sobre la tierra?
texts.job.37.18: ¿Extendiste tú con él los cielos, Firmes como un espejo sólido?
texts.job.37.19: Muéstranos qué le hemos de decir; Porque nosotros no podemos componer las ideas á causa de las tinieblas.
texts.job.37.20: ¿Será preciso contarle cuando yo hablaré? Por más que el hombre razone, quedará como abismado.
texts.job.37.21: He aquí aún: no se puede mirar la luz esplendente en los cielos, Luego que pasa el viento y los limpia,
texts.job.37.22: Viniendo de la parte del norte la dorada claridad. En Dios hay una majestad terrible.
texts.job.37.23: El es Todopoderoso, al cual no alcanzamos, grande en potencia; Y en juicio y en multitud de justicia no afligirá.
texts.job.37.24: Temerlo han por tanto los hombres: El no mira á los sabios de corazón.
texts.job.38.1: Y RESPONDIO Jehová á Job desde un torbellino, y dijo:
texts.job.38.2: ¿Quién es ése que oscurece el consejo Con palabras sin sabiduría?
texts.job.38.3: Ahora ciñe como varón tus lomos; Yo te preguntaré, y hazme saber tú.
texts.job.38.4: ¿Dónde estabas cuando yo fundaba la tierra? Házme lo saber, si tienes inteligencia.
texts.job.38.5: ¿Quién ordenó sus medidas, si lo sabes? ¿O quién extendió sobre ella cordel?
texts.job.38.6: ¿Sobre qué están fundadas sus basas? ¿O quién puso su piedra angular,
texts.job.38.7: Cuando las estrellas todas del alba alababan, Y se regocijaban todos los hijos de Dios?
texts.job.38.8: ¿Quién encerró con puertas la mar, Cuando se derramaba por fuera como saliendo de madre;
texts.job.38.9: Cuando puse yo nubes por vestidura suya, Y por su faja oscuridad.
texts.job.38.10: Y establecí sobre ella mi decreto, Y le puse puertas y cerrojo,
texts.job.38.11: Y dije: Hasta aquí vendrás, y no pasarás adelante, Y ahí parará la hinchazón de tus ondas?
texts.job.38.12: ¿Has tu mandado á la mañana en tus días? ¿Has mostrado al alba su lugar,
texts.job.38.13: Para que ocupe los fines de la tierra, Y que sean sacudidos de ella los impíos?
texts.job.38.14: Trasmúdase como lodo bajo de sello, Y viene á estar como con vestidura:
texts.job.38.15: Mas la luz de los impíos es quitada de ellos, Y el brazo enaltecido es quebrantado.
texts.job.38.16: ¿Has entrado tú hasta los profundos de la mar, Y has andado escudriñando el abismo?
texts.job.38.17: ¿Hante sido descubiertas las puertas de la muerte, Y has visto las puertas de la sombra de muerte?
texts.job.38.18: ¿Has tú considerado hasta las anchuras de la tierra? Declara si sabes todo esto.
texts.job.38.19: ¿Por dónde va el camino á la habitación de la luz, Y dónde está el lugar de las tinieblas?
texts.job.38.20: ¿Si llevarás tú ambas cosas á sus términos, Y entenderás las sendas de su casa?
texts.job.38.21: ¿Sabíaslo tú porque hubieses ya nacido, O porque es grande el número de tus días?
texts.job.38.22: ¿Has tú entrado en los tesoros de la nieve, O has visto los tesoros del granizo,
texts.job.38.23: Lo cual tengo yo reservado para el tiempo de angustia, Para el día de la guerra y de la batalla?
texts.job.38.24: ¿Por qué camino se reparte la luz, Y se esparce el viento solano sobre la tierra?
texts.job.38.25: ¿Quién repartió conducto al turbión, Y camino á los relámpagos y truenos,
texts.job.38.26: Haciendo llover sobre la tierra deshabitada, Sobre el desierto, donde no hay hombre,
texts.job.38.27: Para hartar la tierra desierta é inculta, Y para hacer brotar la tierna hierba?
texts.job.38.28: ¿Tiene la lluvia padre? ¿O quién engendró las gotas del rocío?
texts.job.38.29: ¿De qué vientre salió el hielo? Y la escarcha del cielo, ¿quién la engendró?
texts.job.38.30: Las aguas se endurecen á manera de piedra, Y congélase la haz del abismo.
texts.job.38.31: ¿Podrás tú impedir las delicias de las Pléyades, O desatarás las ligaduras del Orión?
texts.job.38.32: ¿Sacarás tú á su tiempo los signos de los cielos, O guiarás el Arcturo con sus hijos?
texts.job.38.33: ¿Supiste tú las ordenanzas de los cielos? ¿Dispondrás tú de su potestad en la tierra?
texts.job.38.34: ¿Alzarás tú á las nubes tu voz, Para que te cubra muchedumbre de aguas?
texts.job.38.35: ¿Enviarás tú los relámpagos, para que ellos vayan? ¿Y diránte ellos: Henos aquí?
texts.job.38.36: ¿Quién puso la sabiduría en el interior? ¿O quién dió al entendimiento la inteligencia?
texts.job.38.37: ¿Quién puso por cuenta los cielos con sabiduría? Y los odres de los cielos, ¿quién los hace parar,
texts.job.38.38: Cuando el polvo se ha convertido en dureza, Y los terrones se han pegado unos con otros?
texts.job.38.39: ¿CAZARAS tú la presa para el león? ¿Y saciarás el hambre de los leoncillos,
texts.job.38.40: Cuando están echados en las cuevas, O se están en sus guaridas para acechar?
texts.job.38.41: ¿Quién preparó al cuervo su alimento, Cuando sus pollos claman á Dios, Bullendo de un lado á otro por carecer de comida?
texts.job.39.1: ¿Sabes tú el tiempo en que paren las cabras monteses? ¿O miraste tú las ciervas cuando están pariendo?
texts.job.39.2: ¿Contaste tú los meses de su preñez, Y sabes el tiempo cuando han de parir?
texts.job.39.3: Encórvanse, hacen salir sus hijos, Pasan sus dolores.
texts.job.39.4: Sus hijos están sanos, crecen con el pasto: Salen y no vuelven á ellas.
texts.job.39.5: ¿Quién echó libre al asno montés, y quién soltó sus ataduras?
texts.job.39.6: Al cual yo puse casa en la soledad, Y sus moradas en lugares estériles.
texts.job.39.7: Búrlase de la multitud de la ciudad: No oye las voces del arriero.
texts.job.39.8: Lo oculto de los montes es su pasto, Y anda buscando todo lo que está verde.
texts.job.39.9: ¿Querrá el unicornio servirte á ti, Ni quedar á tu pesebre?
texts.job.39.10: ¿Atarás tú al unicornio con su coyunda para el surco? ¿Labrará los valles en pos de ti?
texts.job.39.11: ¿Confiarás tú en él, por ser grande su fortaleza, Y le fiarás tu labor?
texts.job.39.12: ¿Fiarás de él que te tornará tu simiente, Y que la allegará en tu era?
texts.job.39.13: ¿Diste tú hermosas alas al pavo real, O alas y plumas al avestruz?
texts.job.39.14: El cual desampara en la tierra sus huevos, Y sobre el polvo los calienta,
texts.job.39.15: Y olvídase de que los pisará el pie, Y que los quebrará bestia del campo.
texts.job.39.16: Endurécese para con sus hijos, como si no fuesen suyos, No temiendo que su trabajo haya sido en vano:
texts.job.39.17: Porque le privó Dios de sabiduría, Y no le dió inteligencia.
texts.job.39.18: Luego que se levanta en alto, Búrlase del caballo y de su jinete.
texts.job.39.19: ¿Diste tú al caballo la fortaleza? ¿Vestiste tú su cerviz de relincho?
texts.job.39.20: ¿Le intimidarás tú como á alguna langosta? El resoplido de su nariz es formidable:
texts.job.39.21: Escarba la tierra, alégrase en su fuerza, Sale al encuentro de las armas:
texts.job.39.22: Hace burla del espanto, y no teme, Ni vuelve el rostro delante de la espada.
texts.job.39.23: Contra él suena la aljaba, El hierro de la lanza y de la pica:
texts.job.39.24: Y él con ímpetu y furor escarba la tierra, Sin importarle el sonido de la bocina;
texts.job.39.25: Antes como que dice entre los clarines: ­Ea! Y desde lejos huele la batalla, el grito de los capitanes, y la vocería.
texts.job.39.26: ¿Vuela el gavilán por tu industria, Y extiende hacia el mediodía sus alas?
texts.job.39.27: ¿Se remonta el águila por tu mandamiento, Y pone en alto su nido?
texts.job.39.28: Ella habita y está en la piedra, En la cumbre del peñasco y de la roca.
texts.job.39.29: Desde allí acecha la comida: Sus ojos observan de muy lejos.
texts.job.39.30: Sus pollos chupan la sangre: Y donde hubiere cadáveres, allí está.
texts.job.40.1: A más de eso respondió Jehová á Job y dijo:
texts.job.40.2: ¿Es sabiduría contender con el Omnipotente? El que disputa con Dios, responda á esto.
texts.job.40.3: Y respondió Job á Jehová, y dijo:
texts.job.40.4: He aquí que yo soy vil, ¿qué te responderé? Mi mano pongo sobre mi boca.
texts.job.40.5: Una vez hablé, y no responderé: Aun dos veces, mas no tornaré á hablar.
texts.job.40.6: ENTONCES respondió Jehová á Job desde la oscuridad, y dijo:
texts.job.40.7: Cíñete ahora como varón tus lomos; Yo te preguntaré, y explícame.
texts.job.40.8: ¿Invalidarás tú también mi juicio? ¿Me condenarás á mí, para justificarte á ti?
texts.job.40.9: ¿Tienes tú brazo como Dios? ¿Y tronarás tú con voz como él?
texts.job.40.10: Atavíate ahora de majestad y de alteza: Y vístete de honra y de hermosura.
texts.job.40.11: Esparce furores de tu ira: Y mira á todo soberbio, y abátelo.
texts.job.40.12: Mira á todo soberbio, y humíllalo, Y quebranta á los impíos en su asiento.
texts.job.40.13: Encúbrelos á todos en el polvo, Venda sus rostros en la oscuridad;
texts.job.40.14: Y yo también te confesaré Que podrá salvarte tu diestra.
texts.job.40.15: He aquí ahora behemoth, al cual yo hice contigo; Hierba come como buey.
texts.job.40.16: He aquí ahora que su fuerza está en sus lomos, Y su fortaleza en el ombligo de su vientre.
texts.job.40.17: Su cola mueve como un cedro, Y los nervios de sus genitales son entretejidos.
texts.job.40.18: Sus huesos son fuertes como bronce, Y sus miembros como barras de hierro.
texts.job.40.19: El es la cabeza de los caminos de Dios: El que lo hizo, puede hacer que su cuchillo á él se acerque.
texts.job.40.20: Ciertamente los montes producen hierba para él: Y toda bestia del campo retoza allá.
texts.job.40.21: Echaráse debajo de las sombras, En lo oculto de las cañas, y de los lugares húmedos.
texts.job.40.22: Los árboles sombríos lo cubren con su sombra; Los sauces del arroyo lo cercan.
texts.job.40.23: He aquí que él tomará el río sin inmutarse: Y confíase que el Jordán pasará por su boca.
texts.job.40.24: ¿Tomarálo alguno por sus ojos en armadijos, Y horadará su nariz?
texts.job.41.1: ¿SACARAS tú al leviathán con el anzuelo, O con la cuerda que le echares en su lengua?
texts.job.41.2: ¿Pondrás tú garfio en sus narices, Y horadarás con espinas su quijada?
texts.job.41.3: ¿Multiplicará él ruegos para contigo? ¿Hablaráte él lisonjas?
texts.job.41.4: ¿Hará concierto contigo Para que lo tomes por siervo perpetuo?
texts.job.41.5: ¿Jugarás tú con él como con pájaro, O lo atarás para tus niñas?
texts.job.41.6: ¿Harán de él banquete los compañeros? ¿Partiránlo entre los mercaderes?
texts.job.41.7: ¿Cortarás tú con cuchillo su cuero, O con asta de pescadores su cabeza?
texts.job.41.8: Pon tu mano sobre él; Te acordarás de la batalla, y nunca más tornarás.
texts.job.41.9: He aquí que la esperanza acerca de él será burlada; Porque aun á su sola vista se desmayarán.
texts.job.41.10: Nadie hay tan osado que lo despierte: ¿Quién pues podrá estar delante de mí?
texts.job.41.11: ¿Quién me ha anticipado, para que yo restituya? Todo lo que hay debajo del cielo es mío.
texts.job.41.12: Yo no callaré sus miembros, Ni lo de sus fuerzas y la gracia de su disposición.
texts.job.41.13: ¿Quién descubrirá la delantera de su vestidura? ¿Quién se llegará á él con freno doble?
texts.job.41.14: ¿Quién abrirá las puertas de su rostro? Los órdenes de sus dientes espantan.
texts.job.41.15: La gloria de su vestido son escudos fuertes, Cerrados entre sí estrechamente.
texts.job.41.16: El uno se junta con el otro, Que viento no entra entre ellos.
texts.job.41.17: Pegado está el uno con el otro, Están trabados entre sí, que no se pueden apartar.
texts.job.41.18: Con sus estornudos encienden lumbre, Y sus ojos son como los párpados del alba.
texts.job.41.19: De su boca salen hachas de fuego, Centellas de fuego proceden.
texts.job.41.20: De sus narices sale humo, Como de una olla ó caldero que hierve.
texts.job.41.21: Su aliento enciende los carbones, Y de su boca sale llama.
texts.job.41.22: En su cerviz mora la fortaleza, Y espárcese el desaliento delante de él.
texts.job.41.23: Las partes momias de su carne están apretadas: Están en él firmes, y no se mueven.
texts.job.41.24: Su corazón es firme como una piedra, Y fuerte como la muela de abajo.
texts.job.41.25: De su grandeza tienen temor los fuertes, Y á causa de su desfallecimiento hacen por purificarse.
texts.job.41.26: Cuando alguno lo alcanzare, ni espada, Ni lanza, ni dardo, ni coselete durará.
texts.job.41.27: El hierro estima por pajas, Y el acero por leño podrido.
texts.job.41.28: Saeta no le hace huir; Las piedras de honda se le tornan aristas.
texts.job.41.29: Tiene toda arma por hojarascas, Y del blandir de la pica se burla.
texts.job.41.30: Por debajo tiene agudas conchas; Imprime su agudez en el suelo.
texts.job.41.31: Hace hervir como una olla la profunda mar, Y tórnala como una olla de ungüento.
texts.job.41.32: En pos de sí hace resplandecer la senda, Que parece que la mar es cana.
texts.job.41.33: No hay sobre la tierra su semejante, Hecho para nada temer.
texts.job.41.34: Menosprecia toda cosa alta: Es rey sobre todos los soberbios.
texts.job.42.1: Y RESPONDIO Job á Jehová, y dijo:
texts.job.42.2: Yo conozco que todo lo puedes, Y que no hay pensamiento que se esconda de ti.
texts.job.42.3: ¿Quién es el que oscurece el consejo sin ciencia? Por tanto yo denunciaba lo que no entendía; Cosas que me eran ocultas, y que no las sabía.
texts.job.42.4: Oye te ruego, y hablaré; Te preguntaré, y tú me enseñarás.
texts.job.42.5: De oídas te había oído; Mas ahora mis ojos te ven.
texts.job.42.6: Por tanto me aborrezco, y me arrepiento En el polvo y en la ceniza.
texts.job.42.7: Y aconteció que después que habló Jehová estas palabras á Job, Jehová dijo á Eliphaz Temanita: Mi ira se encendió contra ti y tus dos compañeros: porque no habéis hablado por mí lo recto, como mi siervo Job.
texts.job.42.8: Ahora pues, tomaos siete becerros y siete carneros, y andad á mi siervo Job, y ofreced holocausto por vosotros, y mi siervo Job orará por vosotros; porque de cierto á él atenderé para no trataros afrentosamente, por cuanto no habéis hablado por mí con rec
texts.job.42.9: Fueron pues Eliphaz Temanita, y Bildad Suhita, y Sophar Naamatita, é hicieron como Jehová les dijo: y Jehová atendió á Job.
texts.job.42.10: Y mudó Jehová la aflicción de Job, orando él por sus amigos: y aumentó al doble todas las cosas que habían sido de Job.
texts.job.42.11: Y vinieron é él todos sus hermanos, y todas sus hermanas, y todos los que antes le habían conocido, y comieron con él pan en su casa, y condoliéronse de él, y consoláronle de todo aquel mal que sobre él había Jehová traído; y cada uno de ellos le dió una
texts.job.42.12: Y bendijo Jehová la postrimería de Job más que su principio; porque tuvo catorce mil ovejas, y seis mil camellos, y mil yuntas de bueyes, y mil asnas.
texts.job.42.13: Y tuvo siete hijos y tres hijas.
texts.job.42.14: Y llamó el nombre de la una, Jemimah, y el nombre de la segunda, Cesiah, y el nombre de la tercera, Keren-happuch.
texts.job.42.15: Y no se hallaron mujeres tan hermosas como las hijas de Job en toda la tierra: y dióles su padre herencia entre sus hermanos.
texts.job.42.16: Y después de esto vivió Job ciento y cuarenta años, y vió á sus hijos, y á los hijos de sus hijos, hasta la cuarta generación.
texts.job.42.17: Murió pues Job viejo, y lleno de días.

texts.job.1.1: There was a man in the land of Uz, whose name was Job; and that man was perfect and upright, and one that feared God, and turned away from evil.
texts.job.1.2: And there were born unto him seven sons and three daughters.
texts.job.1.3: His substance also was seven thousand sheep, and three thousand camels, and five hundred yoke of oxen, and five hundred she-asses, and a very great household; so that this man was the greatest of all the children of the east.
texts.job.1.4: And his sons went and held a feast in the house of each one upon his day; and they sent and called for their three sisters to eat and to drink with them.
texts.job.1.5: And it was so, when the days of their feasting were gone about, that Job sent and sanctified them, and rose up early in the morning, and offered burnt-offerings according to the number of them all: for Job said, It may be that my sons have sinned, and renounced God in their hearts. Thus did Job continually.
texts.job.1.6: Now it came to pass on the day when the sons of God came to present themselves before Jehovah, that Satan also came among them.
texts.job.1.7: And Jehovah said unto Satan, Whence comest thou? Then Satan answered Jehovah, and said, From going to and fro in the earth, and from walking up and down in it.
texts.job.1.8: And Jehovah said unto Satan, Hast thou considered my servant Job? for there is none like him in the earth, a perfect and an upright man, one that feareth God, and turneth away from evil.
texts.job.1.9: Then Satan answered Jehovah, and said, Doth Job fear God for nought?
texts.job.1.10: Hast not thou made a hedge about him, and about his house, and about all that he hath, on every side? thou hast blessed the work of his hands, and his substance is increased in the land.
texts.job.1.11: But put forth thy hand now, and touch all that he hath, and he will renounce thee to thy face.
texts.job.1.12: And Jehovah said unto Satan, Behold, all that he hath is in thy power; only upon himself put not forth thy hand. So Satan went forth from the presence of Jehovah.
texts.job.1.13: And it fell on a day when his sons and his daughters were eating and drinking wine in their eldest brother's house,
texts.job.1.14: that there came a messenger unto Job, and said, The oxen were plowing, and the asses feeding beside them;
texts.job.1.15: and the Sabeans fell [upon them], and took them away: yea, they have slain the servants with the edge of the sword; and I only am escaped alone to tell thee.
texts.job.1.16: While he was yet speaking, there came also another, and said, The fire of God is fallen from heaven, and hath burned up the sheep and the servants, and consumed them; and I only am escaped alone to tell thee.
texts.job.1.17: While he was yet speaking, there came also another, and said, The Chaldeans made three bands, and fell upon the camels, and have taken them away, yea, and slain the servants with the edge of the sword; and I only am escaped alone to tell thee.
texts.job.1.18: While he was yet speaking, there came also another, and said, Thy sons and thy daughters were eating and drinking wine in their eldest brother's house;
texts.job.1.19: and, behold, there came a great wind from the wilderness, and smote the four corners of the house, and it fell upon the young men, and they are dead; and I only am escaped alone to tell thee.
texts.job.1.20: Then Job arose, and rent his robe, and shaved his head, and fell down upon the ground, and worshipped;
texts.job.1.21: and he said, Naked came I out of my mother's womb, and naked shall I return thither: Jehovah gave, and Jehovah hath taken away; blessed be the name of Jehovah.
texts.job.1.22: In all this Job sinned not, nor charged God foolishly.
texts.job.2.1: Again it came to pass on the day when the sons of God came to present themselves before Jehovah, that Satan came also among them to present himself before Jehovah.
texts.job.2.2: And Jehovah said unto Satan, From whence comest thou? And Satan answered Jehovah, and said, From going to and fro in the earth, and from walking up and down in it.
texts.job.2.3: And Jehovah said unto Satan, Hast thou considered my servant Job? for there is none like him in the earth, a perfect and an upright man, one that feareth God, and turneth away from evil: and he still holdeth fast his integrity, although thou movedst me against him, to destroy him without cause.
texts.job.2.4: And Satan answered Jehovah, and said, Skin for skin, yea, all that a man hath will he give for his life.
texts.job.2.5: But put forth thy hand now, and touch his bone and his flesh, and he will renounce thee to thy face.
texts.job.2.6: And Jehovah said unto Satan, Behold, he is in thy hand; only spare his life.
texts.job.2.7: So Satan went forth from the presence of Jehovah, and smote Job with sore boils from the sole of his foot unto his crown.
texts.job.2.8: And he took him a potsherd to scrape himself therewith; and he sat among the ashes.
texts.job.2.9: Then said his wife unto him, Dost thou still hold fast thine integrity? renounce God, and die.
texts.job.2.10: But he said unto her, Thou speakest as one of the foolish women speaketh. What? shall we receive good at the hand of God, and shall we not receive evil? In all this did not Job sin with his lips.
texts.job.2.11: Now when Job's three friends heard of all this evil that was come upon him, they came every one from his own place: Eliphaz the Temanite, and Bildad the Shuhite, and Zophar the Naamathite, and they made an appointment together to come to bemoan him and to comfort him.
texts.job.2.12: And when they lifted up their eyes afar off, and knew him not, they lifted up their voice, and wept; and they rent every one his robe, and sprinkled dust upon their heads toward heaven.
texts.job.2.13: So they sat down with him upon the ground seven days and seven nights, and none spake a word unto him: for they saw that his grief was very great.
texts.job.3.1: After this opened Job his mouth, and cursed his day.
texts.job.3.3: Let the day perish wherein I was born, And the night which said, There is a man-child conceived.
texts.job.3.4: Let that day be darkness; Let not God from above seek for it, Neither let the light shine upon it.
texts.job.3.5: Let darkness and the shadow of death claim it for their own; Let a cloud dwell upon it; Let all that maketh black the day terrify it.
texts.job.3.6: As for that night, let thick darkness seize upon it: Let it not rejoice among the days of the year; Let it not come into the number of the months.
texts.job.3.7: Lo, let that night be barren; Let no joyful voice come therein.
texts.job.3.8: Let them curse it that curse the day, Who are ready to rouse up leviathan.
texts.job.3.9: Let the stars of the twilight thereof be dark: Let it look for light, but have none; Neither let it behold the eyelids of the morning:
texts.job.3.10: Because it shut not up the doors of my [mother's] womb, Nor hid trouble from mine eyes.
texts.job.3.11: Why died I not from the womb? Why did I not give up the ghost when my mother bare me?
texts.job.3.12: Why did the knees receive me? Or why the breast, that I should suck?
texts.job.3.13: For now should I have lain down and been quiet; I should have slept; then had I been at rest,
texts.job.3.14: With kings and counsellors of the earth, Who built up waste places for themselves;
texts.job.3.15: Or with princes that had gold, Who filled their houses with silver:
texts.job.3.16: Or as a hidden untimely birth I had not been, As infants that never saw light.
texts.job.3.17: There the wicked cease from troubling; And there the weary are at rest.
texts.job.3.18: There the prisoners are at ease together; They hear not the voice of the taskmaster.
texts.job.3.19: The small and the great are there: And the servant is free from his master.
texts.job.3.20: Wherefore is light given to him that is in misery, And life unto the bitter in soul;
texts.job.3.21: Who long for death, but it cometh not, And dig for it more than for hid treasures;
texts.job.3.22: Who rejoice exceedingly, And are glad, when they can find the grave?
texts.job.3.23: [Why is light given] to a man whose way is hid, And whom God hath hedged in?
texts.job.3.24: For my sighing cometh before I eat, And my groanings are poured out like water.
texts.job.3.25: For the thing which I fear cometh upon me, And that which I am afraid of cometh unto me.
texts.job.3.26: I am not at ease, neither am I quiet, neither have I rest; But trouble cometh.
texts.job.4.1: Then answered Eliphaz the Temanite, and said,
texts.job.4.2: If one assay to commune with thee, wilt thou be grieved? But who can withhold himself from speaking?
texts.job.4.3: Behold, thou hast instructed many, And thou hast strengthened the weak hands.
texts.job.4.4: Thy words have upholden him that was falling, And thou hast made firm the feeble knees.
texts.job.4.5: But now it is come unto thee, and thou faintest; It toucheth thee, and thou art troubled.
texts.job.4.6: Is not thy fear [of God] thy confidence, [And] the integrity of thy ways thy hope?
texts.job.4.7: Remember, I pray thee, who [ever] perished, being innocent? Or where were the upright cut off?
texts.job.4.8: According as I have seen, they that plow iniquity, And sow trouble, reap the same.
texts.job.4.9: By the breath of God they perish, And by the blast of his anger are they consumed.
texts.job.4.10: The roaring of the lion, and the voice of the fierce lion, And the teeth of the young lions, are broken.
texts.job.4.11: The old lion perisheth for lack of prey, And the whelps of the lioness are scattered abroad.
texts.job.4.12: Now a thing was secretly brought to me, And mine ear received a whisper thereof.
texts.job.4.13: In thoughts from the visions of the night, When deep sleep falleth on men,
texts.job.4.14: Fear came upon me, and trembling, Which made all my bones to shake.
texts.job.4.15: Then a spirit passed before my face; The hair of my flesh stood up.
texts.job.4.16: It stood still, but I could not discern the appearance thereof; A form was before mine eyes: [There was] silence, and I heard a voice, [saying],
texts.job.4.17: Shall mortal man be more just than God? Shall a man be more pure than his Maker?
texts.job.4.18: Behold, he putteth no trust in his servants; And his angels he chargeth with folly:
texts.job.4.19: How much more them that dwell in houses of clay, Whose foundation is in the dust, Who are crushed before the moth!
texts.job.4.20: Betwixt morning and evening they are destroyed: They perish for ever without any regarding it.
texts.job.4.21: Is not their tent-cord plucked up within them? They die, and that without wisdom.
texts.job.5.1: Call now; is there any that will answer thee? And to which of the holy ones wilt thou turn?
texts.job.5.2: For vexation killeth the foolish man, And jealousy slayeth the silly one.
texts.job.5.3: I have seen the foolish taking root: But suddenly I cursed his habitation.
texts.job.5.4: His children are far from safety, And they are crushed in the gate, Neither is there any to deliver them:
texts.job.5.5: Whose harvest the hungry eateth up, And taketh it even out of the thorns; And the snare gapeth for their substance.
texts.job.5.6: For affliction cometh not forth from the dust, Neither doth trouble spring out of the ground;
texts.job.5.7: But man is born unto trouble, As the sparks fly upward.
texts.job.5.8: But as for me, I would seek unto God, And unto God would I commit my cause;
texts.job.5.9: Who doeth great things and unsearchable, Marvellous things without number:
texts.job.5.10: Who giveth rain upon the earth, And sendeth waters upon the fields;
texts.job.5.11: So that he setteth up on high those that are low, And those that mourn are exalted to safety.
texts.job.5.12: He frustrateth the devices of the crafty, So that their hands cannot perform their enterprise.
texts.job.5.13: He taketh the wise in their own craftiness; And the counsel of the cunning is carried headlong.
texts.job.5.14: They meet with darkness in the day-time, And grope at noonday as in the night.
texts.job.5.15: But he saveth from the sword of their mouth, Even the needy from the hand of the mighty.
texts.job.5.16: So the poor hath hope, And iniquity stoppeth her mouth.
texts.job.5.17: Behold, happy is the man whom God correcteth: Therefore despise not thou the chastening of the Almighty.
texts.job.5.18: For he maketh sore, and bindeth up; He woundeth, and his hands make whole.
texts.job.5.19: He will deliver thee in six troubles; Yea, in seven there shall no evil touch thee.
texts.job.5.20: In famine he will redeem thee from death; And in war from the power of the sword.
texts.job.5.21: Thou shalt be hid from the scourge of the tongue; Neither shalt thou be afraid of destruction when it cometh.
texts.job.5.22: At destruction and dearth thou shalt laugh; Neither shalt thou be afraid of the beasts of the earth.
texts.job.5.23: For thou shalt be in league with the stones of the field; And the beasts of the field shall be at peace with thee.
texts.job.5.24: And thou shalt know that thy tent is in peace; And thou shalt visit thy fold, and shalt miss nothing.
texts.job.5.25: Thou shalt know also that thy seed shall be great, And thine offspring as the grass of the earth.
texts.job.5.26: Thou shalt come to thy grave in a full age, Like as a shock of grain cometh in in its season.
texts.job.5.27: Lo this, we have searched it, so it is; Hear it, and know thou it for thy good.
texts.job.6.2: Oh that my vexation were but weighed, And all my calamity laid in the balances!
texts.job.6.3: For now it would be heavier than the sand of the seas: Therefore have my words been rash.
texts.job.6.4: For the arrows of the Almighty are within me, The poison whereof my spirit drinketh up: The terrors of God do set themselves in array against me.
texts.job.6.5: Doth the wild ass bray when he hath grass? Or loweth the ox over his fodder?
texts.job.6.6: Can that which hath no savor be eaten without salt? Or is there any taste in the white of an egg?
texts.job.6.7: My soul refuseth to touch [them]; They are as loathsome food to me.
texts.job.6.8: Oh that I might have my request; And that God would grant [me] the thing that I long for!
texts.job.6.9: Even that it would please God to crush me; That he would let loose his hand, and cut me off!
texts.job.6.10: And be it still my consolation, Yea, let me exult in pain that spareth not, That I have not denied the words of the Holy One.
texts.job.6.11: What is my strength, that I should wait? And what is mine end, that I should be patient?
texts.job.6.12: Is my strength the strength of stones? Or is my flesh of brass?
texts.job.6.13: Is it not that I have no help in me, And that wisdom is driven quite from me?
texts.job.6.14: To him that is ready to faint kindness [should be showed] from his friend; Even to him that forsaketh the fear of the Almighty.
texts.job.6.15: My brethren have dealt deceitfully as a brook, As the channel of brooks that pass away;
texts.job.6.16: Which are black by reason of the ice, [And] wherein the snow hideth itself:
texts.job.6.17: What time they wax warm, they vanish; When it is hot, they are consumed out of their place.
texts.job.6.18: The caravans [that travel] by the way of them turn aside; They go up into the waste, and perish.
texts.job.6.19: The caravans of Tema looked, The companies of Sheba waited for them.
texts.job.6.20: They were put to shame because they had hoped; They came thither, and were confounded.
texts.job.6.21: For now ye are nothing; Ye see a terror, and are afraid.
texts.job.6.22: Did I say, Give unto me? Or, Offer a present for me of your substance?
texts.job.6.23: Or, Deliver me from the adversary's hand? Or, Redeem me from the hand of the oppressors?
texts.job.6.24: Teach me, and I will hold my peace; And cause me to understand wherein I have erred.
texts.job.6.25: How forcible are words of uprightness! But your reproof, what doth it reprove?
texts.job.6.26: Do ye think to reprove words, Seeing that the speeches of one that is desperate are as wind?
texts.job.6.27: Yea, ye would cast [lots] upon the fatherless, And make merchandise of your friend.
texts.job.6.28: Now therefore be pleased to look upon me; For surely I shall not lie to your face.
texts.job.6.29: Return, I pray you, let there be no injustice; Yea, return again, my cause is righteous.
texts.job.6.30: Is there injustice on my tongue? Cannot my taste discern mischievous things?
texts.job.7.1: Is there not a warfare to man upon earth? And are not his days like the days of a hireling?
texts.job.7.2: As a servant that earnestly desireth the shadow, And as a hireling that looketh for his wages:
texts.job.7.3: So am I made to possess months of misery, And wearisome nights are appointed to me.
texts.job.7.4: When I lie down, I say, When shall I arise, and the night be gone? And I am full of tossings to and fro unto the dawning of the day.
texts.job.7.5: My flesh is clothed with worms and clods of dust; My skin closeth up, and breaketh out afresh.
texts.job.7.6: My days are swifter than a weaver's shuttle, And are spent without hope.
texts.job.7.7: Oh remember that my life is a breath: Mine eye shall no more see good.
texts.job.7.8: The eye of him that seeth me shall behold me no more; Thine eyes shall be upon me, but I shall not be.
texts.job.7.9: As the cloud is consumed and vanisheth away, So he that goeth down to Sheol shall come up no more.
texts.job.7.10: He shall return no more to his house, Neither shall his place know him any more.
texts.job.7.11: Therefore I will not refrain my mouth; I will speak in the anguish of my spirit; I will complain in the bitterness of my soul.
texts.job.7.12: Am I a sea, or a sea-monster, That thou settest a watch over me?
texts.job.7.13: When I say, My bed shall comfort me, My couch shall ease my complaint;
texts.job.7.14: Then thou scarest me with dreams, And terrifiest me through visions:
texts.job.7.15: So that my soul chooseth strangling, And death rather than [these] my bones.
texts.job.7.16: I loathe [my life]; I would not live alway: Let me alone; for my days are vanity.
texts.job.7.17: What is man, that thou shouldest magnify him, And that thou shouldest set thy mind upon him,
texts.job.7.18: And that thou shouldest visit him every morning, And try him every moment?
texts.job.7.19: How long wilt thou not look away from me, Nor let me alone till I swallow down my spittle?
texts.job.7.20: If I have sinned, what do I unto thee, O thou watcher of men? Why hast thou set me as a mark for thee, So that I am a burden to myself?
texts.job.7.21: And why dost thou not pardon my transgression, and take away mine iniquity? For now shall I lie down in the dust; And thou wilt seek me diligently, but I shall not be.
texts.job.8.1: Then answered Bildad the Shuhite, and said,
texts.job.8.2: How long wilt thou speak these things? And [how long] shall the words of thy mouth be [like] a mighty wind?
texts.job.8.3: Doth God pervert justice? Or doth the Almighty pervert righteousness?
texts.job.8.4: If thy children have sinned against him, And he hath delivered them into the hand of their transgression;
texts.job.8.5: If thou wouldest seek diligently unto God, And make thy supplication to the Almighty;
texts.job.8.6: If thou wert pure and upright: Surely now he would awake for thee, And make the habitation of thy righteousness prosperous.
texts.job.8.7: And though thy beginning was small, Yet thy latter end would greatly increase.
texts.job.8.8: For inquire, I pray thee, of the former age, And apply thyself to that which their fathers have searched out:
texts.job.8.9: (For we are but of yesterday, and know nothing, Because our days upon earth are a shadow);
texts.job.8.10: Shall not they teach thee, and tell thee, And utter words out of their heart?
texts.job.8.11: Can the rush grow up without mire? Can the flag grow without water?
texts.job.8.12: Whilst it is yet in its greenness, [and] not cut down, It withereth before any [other] herb.
texts.job.8.13: So are the paths of all that forget God; And the hope of the godless man shall perish:
texts.job.8.14: Whose confidence shall break in sunder, And whose trust is a spider's web.
texts.job.8.15: He shall lean upon his house, but it shall not stand: He shall hold fast thereby, but it shall not endure.
texts.job.8.16: He is green before the sun, And his shoots go forth over his garden.
texts.job.8.17: His roots are wrapped about the [stone] -heap, He beholdeth the place of stones.
texts.job.8.18: If he be destroyed from his place, Then it shall deny him, [saying], I have not seen thee.
texts.job.8.19: Behold, this is the joy of his way; And out of the earth shall others spring.
texts.job.8.20: Behold, God will not cast away a perfect man, Neither will he uphold the evil-doers.
texts.job.8.21: He will yet fill thy mouth with laughter, And thy lips with shouting.
texts.job.8.22: They that hate thee shall be clothed with shame; And the tent of the wicked shall be no more.
texts.job.9.2: Of a truth I know that it is so: But how can man be just with God?
texts.job.9.3: If he be pleased to contend with him, He cannot answer him one of a thousand.
texts.job.9.4: [He is] wise in heart, and mighty in strength: Who hath hardened himself against him, and prospered?-
texts.job.9.5: [Him] that removeth the mountains, and they know it not, When he overturneth them in his anger;
texts.job.9.6: That shaketh the earth out of its place, And the pillars thereof tremble;
texts.job.9.7: That commandeth the sun, and it riseth not, And sealeth up the stars;
texts.job.9.8: That alone stretcheth out the heavens, And treadeth upon the waves of the sea;
texts.job.9.9: That maketh the Bear, Orion, and the Pleiades, And the chambers of the south;
texts.job.9.10: That doeth great things past finding out, Yea, marvellous things without number.
texts.job.9.11: Lo, he goeth by me, and I see him not: He passeth on also, but I perceive him not.
texts.job.9.12: Behold, he seizeth [the prey], who can hinder him? Who will say unto him, What doest thou?
texts.job.9.13: God will not withdraw his anger; The helpers of Rahab do stoop under him.
texts.job.9.14: How much less shall I answer him, And choose out my words [to reason] with him?
texts.job.9.15: Whom, though I were righteous, yet would I not answer; I would make supplication to my judge.
texts.job.9.16: If I had called, and he had answered me, Yet would I not believe that he hearkened unto my voice.
texts.job.9.17: For he breaketh me with a tempest, And multiplieth my wounds without cause.
texts.job.9.18: He will not suffer me to take my breath, But filleth me with bitterness.
texts.job.9.19: If [we speak] of strength, lo, [he is] mighty! And if of justice, Who, [saith he], will summon me?
texts.job.9.20: Though I be righteous, mine own mouth shall condemn me: Though I be perfect, it shall prove me perverse.
texts.job.9.21: I am perfect; I regard not myself; I despise my life.
texts.job.9.22: It is all one; therefore I say, He destroyeth the perfect and the wicked.
texts.job.9.23: If the scourge slay suddenly, He will mock at the trial of the innocent.
texts.job.9.24: The earth is given into the hand of the wicked; He covereth the faces of the judges thereof: If [it be] not [he], who then is it?
texts.job.9.25: Now my days are swifter than a post: They flee away, they see no good,
texts.job.9.26: They are passed away as the swift ships; As the eagle that swoopeth on the prey.
texts.job.9.27: If I say, I will forget my complaint, I will put off my [sad] countenance, and be of good cheer;
texts.job.9.28: I am afraid of all my sorrows, I know that thou wilt not hold me innocent.
texts.job.9.29: I shall be condemned; Why then do I labor in vain?
texts.job.9.30: If I wash myself with snow water, And make my hands never so clean;
texts.job.9.31: Yet wilt thou plunge me in the ditch, And mine own clothes shall abhor me.
texts.job.9.32: For he is not a man, as I am, that I should answer him, That we should come together in judgment.
texts.job.9.33: There is no umpire betwixt us, That might lay his hand upon us both.
texts.job.9.34: Let him take his rod away from me, And let not his terror make me afraid:
texts.job.9.35: Then would I speak, and not fear him; For I am not so in myself.
texts.job.10.1: My soul is weary of my life; I will give free course to my complaint; I will speak in the bitterness of my soul.
texts.job.10.2: I will say unto God, Do not condemn me; Show me wherefore thou contendest with me.
texts.job.10.3: Is it good unto thee that thou shouldest oppress, That thou shouldest despise the work of thy hands, And shine upon the counsel of the wicked?
texts.job.10.4: Hast thou eyes of flesh? Or seest thou as man seeth?
texts.job.10.5: Are thy days as the days of man, Or thy years as man's days,
texts.job.10.6: That thou inquirest after mine iniquity, And searchest after my sin,
texts.job.10.7: Although thou knowest that I am not wicked, And there is none that can deliver out of thy hand?
texts.job.10.8: Thy hands have framed me and fashioned me Together round about; yet thou dost destroy me.
texts.job.10.9: Remember, I beseech thee, that thou hast fashioned me as clay; And wilt thou bring me into dust again?
texts.job.10.10: Hast thou not poured me out as milk, And curdled me like cheese?
texts.job.10.11: Thou hast clothed me with skin and flesh, And knit me together with bones and sinews.
texts.job.10.12: Thou hast granted me life and lovingkindness; And thy visitation hath preserved my spirit.
texts.job.10.13: Yet these things thou didst hide in thy heart; I know that this is with thee:
texts.job.10.14: If I sin, then thou markest me, And thou wilt not acquit me from mine iniquity.
texts.job.10.15: If I be wicked, woe unto me; And if I be righteous, yet shall I not lift up my head; Being filled with ignominy, And looking upon mine affliction.
texts.job.10.16: And if [my head] exalt itself, thou huntest me as a lion; And again thou showest thyself marvellous upon me.
texts.job.10.17: Thou renewest thy witnesses against me, And increasest thine indignation upon me: Changes and warfare are with me.
texts.job.10.18: Wherefore then hast thou brought me forth out of the womb? I had given up the ghost, and no eye had seen me.
texts.job.10.19: I should have been as though I had not been; I should have been carried from the womb to the grave.
texts.job.10.20: Are not my days few? cease then, And let me alone, that I may take comfort a little,
texts.job.10.21: Before I go whence I shall not return, [Even] to the land of darkness and of the shadow of death;
texts.job.10.22: The land dark as midnight, [The land] of the shadow of death, without any order, And where the light is as midnight.
texts.job.11.1: Then answered Zophar the Naamathite, and said,
texts.job.11.2: Should not the multitude of words be answered? And should a man full of talk be justified?
texts.job.11.3: Should thy boastings make men hold their peace? And when thou mockest, shall no man make thee ashamed?
texts.job.11.4: For thou sayest, My doctrine is pure, And I am clean in thine eyes.
texts.job.11.5: But oh that God would speak, And open his lips against thee,
texts.job.11.6: And that he would show thee the secrets of wisdom! For he is manifold in understanding. Know therefore that God exacteth of thee less than thine iniquity deserveth.
texts.job.11.7: Canst thou by searching find out God? Canst thou find out the Almighty unto perfection?
texts.job.11.8: It is high as heaven; what canst thou do? Deeper than Sheol; what canst thou know?
texts.job.11.9: The measure thereof is longer than the earth, And broader than the sea.
texts.job.11.10: If he pass through, and shut up, And all unto judgment, then who can hinder him?
texts.job.11.11: For he knoweth false men: He seeth iniquity also, even though he consider it not.
texts.job.11.12: But vain man is void of understanding, Yea, man is born [as] a wild ass's colt.
texts.job.11.13: If thou set thy heart aright, And stretch out thy hands toward him;
texts.job.11.14: If iniquity be in thy hand, put it far away, And let not unrighteousness dwell in thy tents.
texts.job.11.15: Surely then shalt thou lift up thy face without spot; Yea, thou shalt be stedfast, and shalt not fear:
texts.job.11.16: For thou shalt forget thy misery; Thou shalt remember it as waters that are passed away,
texts.job.11.17: And [thy] life shall be clearer than the noonday; Though there be darkness, it shall be as the morning.
texts.job.11.18: And thou shalt be secure, because there is hope; Yea, thou shalt search [about thee], and shalt take thy rest in safety.
texts.job.11.19: Also thou shalt lie down, and none shall make thee afraid; Yea, many shall make suit unto thee.
texts.job.11.20: But the eyes of the wicked shall fail, And they shall have no way to flee; And their hope shall be the giving up of the ghost.
texts.job.12.2: No doubt but ye are the people, And wisdom shall die with you.
texts.job.12.3: But I have understanding as well as you; I am not inferior to you: Yea, who knoweth not such things as these?
texts.job.12.4: I am as one that is a laughing-stock to his neighbor, I who called upon God, and he answered: The just, the perfect man is a laughing-stock.
texts.job.12.5: In the thought of him that is at ease there is contempt for misfortune; It is ready for them whose foot slippeth.
texts.job.12.6: The tents of robbers prosper, And they that provoke God are secure; Into whose hand God bringeth [abundantly].
texts.job.12.7: But ask now the beasts, and they shall teach thee; And the birds of the heavens, and they shall tell thee:
texts.job.12.8: Or speak to the earth, and it shall teach thee; And the fishes of the sea shall declare unto thee.
texts.job.12.9: Who knoweth not in all these, That the hand of Jehovah hath wrought this,
texts.job.12.10: In whose hand is the soul of every living thing, And the breath of all mankind?
texts.job.12.11: Doth not the ear try words, Even as the palate tasteth its food?
texts.job.12.12: With aged men is wisdom, And in length of days understanding.
texts.job.12.13: With [God] is wisdom and might; He hath counsel and understanding.
texts.job.12.14: Behold, he breaketh down, and it cannot be built again; He shutteth up a man, and there can be no opening.
texts.job.12.15: Behold, he withholdeth the waters, and they dry up; Again, he sendeth them out, and they overturn the earth.
texts.job.12.16: With him is strength and wisdom; The deceived and the deceiver are his.
texts.job.12.17: He leadeth counsellors away stripped, And judges maketh he fools.
texts.job.12.18: He looseth the bond of kings, And he bindeth their loins with a girdle.
texts.job.12.19: He leadeth priests away stripped, And overthroweth the mighty.
texts.job.12.20: He removeth the speech of the trusty, And taketh away the understanding of the elders.
texts.job.12.21: He poureth contempt upon princes, And looseth the belt of the strong.
texts.job.12.22: He uncovereth deep things out of darkness, And bringeth out to light the shadow of death.
texts.job.12.23: He increaseth the nations, and he destroyeth them: He enlargeth the nations, and he leadeth them captive.
texts.job.12.24: He taketh away understanding from the chiefs of the people of the earth, And causeth them to wander in a wilderness where there is no way.
texts.job.12.25: They grope in the dark without light; And he maketh them to stagger like a drunken man.
texts.job.13.1: Lo, mine eye hath seen all [this], Mine ear hath heard and understood it.
texts.job.13.2: What ye know, [the same] do I know also: I am not inferior unto you.
texts.job.13.3: Surely I would speak to the Almighty, And I desire to reason with God.
texts.job.13.4: But ye are forgers of lies; Ye are all physicians of no value.
texts.job.13.5: Oh that ye would altogether hold your peace! And it would be your wisdom.
texts.job.13.6: Hear now my reasoning, And hearken to the pleadings of my lips.
texts.job.13.7: Will ye speak unrighteously for God, And talk deceitfully for him?
texts.job.13.8: Will ye show partiality to him? Will ye contend for God?
texts.job.13.9: Is it good that he should search you out? Or as one deceiveth a man, will ye deceive him?
texts.job.13.10: He will surely reprove you If ye do secretly show partiality.
texts.job.13.11: Shall not his majesty make you afraid, And his dread fall upon you?
texts.job.13.12: Your memorable sayings are proverbs of ashes, Your defences are defences of clay.
texts.job.13.13: Hold your peace, let me alone, that I may speak; And let come on me what will.
texts.job.13.14: Wherefore should I take my flesh in my teeth, And put my life in my hand?
texts.job.13.15: Behold, he will slay me; I have no hope: Nevertheless I will maintain my ways before him.
texts.job.13.16: This also shall be my salvation, That a godless man shall not come before him.
texts.job.13.17: Hear diligently my speech, And let my declaration be in your ears.
texts.job.13.18: Behold now, I have set my cause in order; I know that I am righteous.
texts.job.13.19: Who is he that will contend with me? For then would I hold my peace and give up the ghost.
texts.job.13.20: Only do not two things unto me; Then will I not hide myself from thy face:
texts.job.13.21: Withdraw thy hand far from me; And let not thy terror make me afraid.
texts.job.13.22: Then call thou, and I will answer; Or let me speak, and answer thou me.
texts.job.13.23: How many are mine iniquities and sins? Make me to know my transgression and my sin.
texts.job.13.24: Wherefore hidest thou thy face, And holdest me for thine enemy?
texts.job.13.25: Wilt thou harass a driven leaf? And wilt thou pursue the dry stubble?
texts.job.13.26: For thou writest bitter things against me, And makest me to inherit the iniquities of my youth:
texts.job.13.27: Thou puttest my feet also in the stocks, And markest all my paths; Thou settest a bound to the soles of my feet:
texts.job.13.28: Though I am like a rotten thing that consumeth, Like a garment that is moth-eaten.
texts.job.14.1: Man, that is born of a woman, Is of few days, and full of trouble.
texts.job.14.2: He cometh forth like a flower, and is cut down: He fleeth also as a shadow, and continueth not.
texts.job.14.3: And dost thou open thine eyes upon such a one, And bringest me into judgment with thee?
texts.job.14.4: Who can bring a clean thing out of an unclean? not one.
texts.job.14.5: Seeing his days are determined, The number of his months is with thee, And thou hast appointed his bounds that he cannot pass;
texts.job.14.6: Look away from him, that he may rest, Till he shall accomplish, as a hireling, his day.
texts.job.14.7: For there is hope of a tree, If it be cut down, that it will sprout again, And that the tender branch thereof will not cease.
texts.job.14.8: Though the root thereof wax old in the earth, And the stock thereof die in the ground;
texts.job.14.9: Yet through the scent of water it will bud, And put forth boughs like a plant.
texts.job.14.10: But man dieth, and is laid low: Yea, man giveth up the ghost, and where is he?
texts.job.14.11: [As] the waters fail from the sea, And the river wasteth and drieth up;
texts.job.14.12: So man lieth down and riseth not: Till the heavens be no more, they shall not awake, Nor be roused out of their sleep.
texts.job.14.13: Oh that thou wouldest hide me in Sheol, That thou wouldest keep me secret, until thy wrath be past, That thou wouldest appoint me a set time, and remember me!
texts.job.14.14: If a man die, shall he live [again]? All the days of my warfare would I wait, Till my release should come.
texts.job.14.15: Thou wouldest call, and I would answer thee: Thou wouldest have a desire to the work of thy hands.
texts.job.14.16: But now thou numberest my steps: Dost thou not watch over my sin?
texts.job.14.17: My transgression is sealed up in a bag, And thou fastenest up mine iniquity.
texts.job.14.18: But the mountain falling cometh to nought; And the rock is removed out of its place;
texts.job.14.19: The waters wear the stones; The overflowings thereof wash away the dust of the earth: So thou destroyest the hope of man.
texts.job.14.20: Thou prevailest for ever against him, and he passeth; Thou changest his countenance, and sendest him away.
texts.job.14.21: His sons come to honor, and he knoweth it not; And they are brought low, but he perceiveth it not of them.
texts.job.14.22: But his flesh upon him hath pain, And his soul within him mourneth.
texts.job.15.1: Then answered Eliphaz the Temanite, and said,
texts.job.15.2: Should a wise man make answer with vain knowledge, And fill himself with the east wind?
texts.job.15.3: Should he reason with unprofitable talk, Or with speeches wherewith he can do no good?
texts.job.15.4: Yea, thou doest away with fear, And hinderest devotion before God.
texts.job.15.5: For thine iniquity teacheth thy mouth, And thou choosest the tongue of the crafty.
texts.job.15.6: Thine own mouth condemneth thee, and not I; Yea, thine own lips testify against thee.
texts.job.15.7: Art thou the first man that was born? Or wast thou brought forth before the hills?
texts.job.15.8: Hast thou heard the secret counsel of God? And dost thou limit wisdom to thyself?
texts.job.15.9: What knowest thou, that we know not? What understandest thou, which is not in us?
texts.job.15.10: With us are both the gray-headed and the very aged men, Much elder than thy father.
texts.job.15.11: Are the consolations of God too small for thee, Even the word that is gentle toward thee?
texts.job.15.12: Why doth thy heart carry thee away? And why do thine eyes flash,
texts.job.15.13: That against God thou turnest thy spirit, And lettest words go out of thy mouth?
texts.job.15.14: What is man, that he should be clean? And he that is born of a woman, that he should be righteous?
texts.job.15.15: Behold, he putteth no trust in his holy ones; Yea, the heavens are not clean in his sight:
texts.job.15.16: How much less one that is abominable and corrupt, A man that drinketh iniquity like water!
texts.job.15.17: I will show thee, hear thou me; And that which I have seen I will declare:
texts.job.15.18: (Which wise men have told From their fathers, and have not hid it;
texts.job.15.19: Unto whom alone the land was given, And no stranger passed among them):
texts.job.15.20: The wicked man travaileth with pain all his days, Even the number of years that are laid up for the oppressor.
texts.job.15.21: A sound of terrors is in his ears; In prosperity the destroyer shall come upon him.
texts.job.15.22: He believeth not that he shall return out of darkness, And he is waited for of the sword.
texts.job.15.23: He wandereth abroad for bread, [saying], Where is it? He knoweth that the day of darkness is ready at his hand.
texts.job.15.24: Distress and anguish make him afraid; They prevail against him, as a king ready to the battle.
texts.job.15.25: Because he hath stretched out his hand against God, And behaveth himself proudly against the Almighty;
texts.job.15.26: He runneth upon him with a [stiff] neck, With the thick bosses of his bucklers;
texts.job.15.27: Because he hath covered his face with his fatness, And gathered fat upon his loins;
texts.job.15.28: And he hath dwelt in desolate cities, In houses which no man inhabited, Which were ready to become heaps;
texts.job.15.29: He shall not be rich, neither shall his substance continue, Neither shall their possessions be extended on the earth.
texts.job.15.30: He shall not depart out of darkness; The flame shall dry up his branches, And by the breath of [God's] mouth shall he go away.
texts.job.15.31: Let him not trust in vanity, deceiving himself; For vanity shall be his recompense.
texts.job.15.32: It shall be accomplished before his time, And his branch shall not be green.
texts.job.15.33: He shall shake off his unripe grape as the vine, And shall cast off his flower as the olive-tree.
texts.job.15.34: For the company of the godless shall be barren, And fire shall consume the tents of bribery.
texts.job.15.35: They conceive mischief, and bring forth iniquity, And their heart prepareth deceit.
texts.job.16.2: I have heard many such things: Miserable comforters are ye all.
texts.job.16.3: Shall vain words have an end? Or what provoketh thee that thou answerest?
texts.job.16.4: I also could speak as ye do; If your soul were in my soul's stead, I could join words together against you, And shake my head at you.
texts.job.16.5: [But] I would strengthen you with my mouth, And the solace of my lips would assuage [your grief].
texts.job.16.6: Though I speak, my grief is not assuaged; And though I forbear, what am I eased?
texts.job.16.7: But now he hath made me weary: Thou hast made desolate all my company.
texts.job.16.8: And thou hast laid fast hold on me, [which] is a witness [against me]: And my leanness riseth up against me, It testifieth to my face.
texts.job.16.9: He hath torn me in his wrath, and persecuted me; He hath gnashed upon me with his teeth: Mine adversary sharpeneth his eyes upon me.
texts.job.16.10: They have gaped upon me with their mouth; They have smitten me upon the cheek reproachfully: They gather themselves together against me.
texts.job.16.11: God delivereth me to the ungodly, And casteth me into the hands of the wicked.
texts.job.16.12: I was at ease, and he brake me asunder; Yea, he hath taken me by the neck, and dashed me to pieces: He hath also set me up for his mark.
texts.job.16.13: His archers compass me round about; He cleaveth my reins asunder, and doth not spare; He poureth out my gall upon the ground.
texts.job.16.14: He breaketh me with breach upon breach; He runneth upon me like a giant.
texts.job.16.15: I have sewed sackcloth upon my skin, And have laid my horn in the dust.
texts.job.16.16: My face is red with weeping, And on my eyelids is the shadow of death;
texts.job.16.17: Although there is no violence in my hands, And my prayer is pure.
texts.job.16.18: O earth, cover not thou my blood, And let my cry have no [resting] -place.
texts.job.16.19: Even now, behold, my witness is in heaven, And he that voucheth for me is on high.
texts.job.16.20: My friends scoff at me: [But] mine eye poureth out tears unto God,
texts.job.16.21: That he would maintain the right of a man with God, And of a son of man with his neighbor!
texts.job.16.22: For when a few years are come, I shall go the way whence I shall not return.
texts.job.17.1: My spirit is consumed, my days are extinct, The grave is [ready] for me.
texts.job.17.2: Surely there are mockers with me, And mine eye dwelleth upon their provocation.
texts.job.17.3: Give now a pledge, be surety for me with thyself; Who is there that will strike hands with me?
texts.job.17.4: For thou hast hid their heart from understanding: Therefore shalt thou not exalt [them].
texts.job.17.5: He that denounceth his friends for a prey, Even the eyes of his children shall fail.
texts.job.17.6: But he hath made me a byword of the people; And they spit in my face.
texts.job.17.7: Mine eye also is dim by reason of sorrow, And all my members are as a shadow.
texts.job.17.8: Upright men shall be astonished at this, And the innocent shall stir up himself against the godless.
texts.job.17.9: Yet shall the righteous hold on his way, And he that hath clean hands shall wax stronger and stronger.
texts.job.17.10: But as for you all, come on now again; And I shall not find a wise man among you.
texts.job.17.11: My days are past, my purposes are broken off, Even the thoughts of my heart.
texts.job.17.12: They change the night into day: The light, [say they], is near unto the darkness.
texts.job.17.13: If I look for Sheol as my house; If I have spread my couch in the darkness;
texts.job.17.14: If I have said to corruption, Thou art my father; To the worm, [Thou art] my mother, and my sister;
texts.job.17.15: Where then is my hope? And as for my hope, who shall see it?
texts.job.17.16: It shall go down to the bars of Sheol, When once there is rest in the dust.
texts.job.18.1: Then answered Bildad the Shuhite, and said,
texts.job.18.2: How long will ye hunt for words? Consider, and afterwards we will speak.
texts.job.18.3: Wherefore are we counted as beasts, [And] are become unclean in your sight?
texts.job.18.4: Thou that tearest thyself in thine anger, Shall the earth be forsaken for thee? Or shall the rock be removed out of its place?
texts.job.18.5: Yea, the light of the wicked shall be put out, And the spark of his fire shall not shine.
texts.job.18.6: The light shall be dark in his tent, And his lamp above him shall be put out.
texts.job.18.7: The steps of his strength shall be straitened, And his own counsel shall cast him down.
texts.job.18.8: For he is cast into a net by his own feet, And he walketh upon the toils.
texts.job.18.9: A gin shall take [him] by the heel, [And] a snare shall lay hold on him.
texts.job.18.10: A noose is hid for him in the ground, And a trap for him in the way.
texts.job.18.11: Terrors shall make him afraid on every side, And shall chase him at his heels.
texts.job.18.12: His strength shall be hunger-bitten, And calamity shall be ready at his side.
texts.job.18.13: The members of his body shall be devoured, [Yea], the first-born of death shall devour his members.
texts.job.18.14: He shall be rooted out of his tent where he trusteth; And he shall be brought to the king of terrors.
texts.job.18.15: There shall dwell in his tent that which is none of his: Brimstone shall be scattered upon his habitation.
texts.job.18.16: His roots shall be dried up beneath, And above shall his branch be cut off.
texts.job.18.17: His remembrance shall perish from the earth, And he shall have no name in the street.
texts.job.18.18: He shall be driven from light into darkness, And chased out of the world.
texts.job.18.19: He shall have neither son nor son's son among his people, Nor any remaining where he sojourned.
texts.job.18.20: They that come after shall be astonished at his day, As they that went before were affrighted.
texts.job.18.21: Surely such are the dwellings of the unrighteous, And this is the place of him that knoweth not God.
texts.job.19.2: How long will ye vex my soul, And break me in pieces with words?
texts.job.19.3: These ten times have ye reproached me: Ye are not ashamed that ye deal hardly with me.
texts.job.19.4: And be it indeed that I have erred, Mine error remaineth with myself.
texts.job.19.5: If indeed ye will magnify yourselves against me, And plead against me my reproach;
texts.job.19.6: Know now that God hath subverted me [in my cause], And hath compassed me with his net.
texts.job.19.7: Behold, I cry out of wrong, but I am not heard: I cry for help, but there is no justice.
texts.job.19.8: He hath walled up my way that I cannot pass, And hath set darkness in my paths.
texts.job.19.9: He hath stripped me of my glory, And taken the crown from my head.
texts.job.19.10: He hath broken me down on every side, and I am gone; And my hope hath he plucked up like a tree.
texts.job.19.11: He hath also kindled his wrath against me, And he counteth me unto him as [one of] his adversaries.
texts.job.19.12: His troops come on together, And cast up their way against me, And encamp round about my tent.
texts.job.19.13: He hath put my brethren far from me, And mine acquaintance are wholly estranged from me.
texts.job.19.14: My kinsfolk have failed, And my familiar friends have forgotten me.
texts.job.19.15: They that dwell in my house, and my maids, count me for a stranger; I am an alien in their sight.
texts.job.19.16: I call unto my servant, and he giveth me no answer, [Though] I entreat him with my mouth.
texts.job.19.17: My breath is strange to my wife, And my supplication to the children of mine own mother.
texts.job.19.18: Even young children despise me; If I arise, they speak against me.
texts.job.19.19: All my familiar friends abhor me, And they whom I loved are turned against me.
texts.job.19.20: My bone cleaveth to my skin and to my flesh, And I am escaped with the skin of my teeth.
texts.job.19.21: Have pity upon me, have pity upon me, O ye my friends; For the hand of God hath touched me.
texts.job.19.22: Why do ye persecute me as God, And are not satisfied with my flesh?
texts.job.19.23: Oh that my words were now written! Oh that they were inscribed in a book!
texts.job.19.24: That with an iron pen and lead They were graven in the rock for ever!
texts.job.19.25: But as for me I know that my Redeemer liveth, And at last he will stand up upon the earth:
texts.job.19.26: And after my skin, [even] this [body], is destroyed, Then without my flesh shall I see God;
texts.job.19.27: Whom I, even I, shall see, on my side, And mine eyes shall behold, and not as a stranger. My heart is consumed within me.
texts.job.19.28: If ye say, How we will persecute him! And that the root of the matter is found in me;
texts.job.19.29: Be ye afraid of the sword: For wrath [bringeth] the punishments of the sword, That ye may know there is a judgment.
texts.job.20.1: Then answered Zophar the Naamathite, and said,
texts.job.20.2: Therefore do my thoughts give answer to me, Even by reason of my haste that is in me.
texts.job.20.3: I have heard the reproof which putteth me to shame; And the spirit of my understanding answereth me.
texts.job.20.4: Knowest thou [not] this of old time, Since man was placed upon earth,
texts.job.20.5: That the triumphing of the wicked is short, And the joy of the godless but for a moment?
texts.job.20.6: Though his height mount up to the heavens, And his head reach unto the clouds;
texts.job.20.7: Yet he shall perish for ever like his own dung: They that have seen him shall say, Where is he?
texts.job.20.8: He shall fly away as a dream, and shall not be found: Yea, he shall be chased away as a vision of the night.
texts.job.20.9: The eye which saw him shall see him no more; Neither shall his place any more behold him.
texts.job.20.10: His children shall seek the favor of the poor, And his hands shall give back his wealth.
texts.job.20.11: His bones are full of his youth, But it shall lie down with him in the dust.
texts.job.20.12: Though wickedness be sweet in his mouth, Though he hide it under his tongue,
texts.job.20.13: Though he spare it, and will not let it go, But keep it still within his mouth;
texts.job.20.14: Yet his food in his bowels is turned, It is the gall of asps within him.
texts.job.20.15: He hath swallowed down riches, and he shall vomit them up again; God will cast them out of his belly.
texts.job.20.16: He shall suck the poison of asps: The viper's tongue shall slay him.
texts.job.20.17: He shall not look upon the rivers, The flowing streams of honey and butter.
texts.job.20.18: That which he labored for shall he restore, and shall not swallow it down; According to the substance that he hath gotten, he shall not rejoice.
texts.job.20.19: For he hath oppressed and forsaken the poor; He hath violently taken away a house, and he shall not build it up.
texts.job.20.20: Because he knew no quietness within him, He shall not save aught of that wherein he delighteth.
texts.job.20.21: There was nothing left that he devoured not; Therefore his prosperity shall not endure.
texts.job.20.22: In the fulness of his sufficiency he shall be in straits: The hand of every one that is in misery shall come upon him.
texts.job.20.23: When he is about to fill his belly, [God] will cast the fierceness of his wrath upon him, And will rain it upon him while he is eating.
texts.job.20.24: He shall flee from the iron weapon, And the bow of brass shall strike him through.
texts.job.20.25: He draweth it forth, and it cometh out of his body; Yea, the glittering point cometh out of his gall: Terrors are upon him.
texts.job.20.26: All darkness is laid up for his treasures: A fire not blown [by man] shall devour him; It shall consume that which is left in his tent.
texts.job.20.27: The heavens shall reveal his iniquity, And the earth shall rise up against him.
texts.job.20.28: The increase of his house shall depart; [His goods] shall flow away in the day of his wrath.
texts.job.20.29: This is the portion of a wicked man from God, And the heritage appointed unto him by God.
texts.job.21.2: Hear diligently my speech; And let this be your consolations.
texts.job.21.3: Suffer me, and I also will speak; And after that I have spoken, mock on.
texts.job.21.4: As for me, is my complaint to man? And why should I not be impatient?
texts.job.21.5: Mark me, and be astonished, And lay your hand upon your mouth.
texts.job.21.6: Even when I remember I am troubled, And horror taketh hold on my flesh.
texts.job.21.7: Wherefore do the wicked live, Become old, yea, wax mighty in power?
texts.job.21.8: Their seed is established with them in their sight, And their offspring before their eyes.
texts.job.21.9: Their houses are safe from fear, Neither is the rod of God upon them.
texts.job.21.10: Their bull gendereth, and faileth not; Their cow calveth, and casteth not her calf.
texts.job.21.11: They send forth their little ones like a flock, And their children dance.
texts.job.21.12: They sing to the timbrel and harp, And rejoice at the sound of the pipe.
texts.job.21.13: They spend their days in prosperity, And in a moment they go down to Sheol.
texts.job.21.14: And they say unto God, Depart from us; For we desire not the knowledge of thy ways.
texts.job.21.15: What is the Almighty, that we should serve him? And what profit should we have, if we pray unto him?
texts.job.21.16: Lo, their prosperity is not in their hand: The counsel of the wicked is far from me.
texts.job.21.17: How oft is it that the lamp of the wicked is put out? That their calamity cometh upon them? That [God] distributeth sorrows in his anger?
texts.job.21.18: That they are as stubble before the wind, And as chaff that the storm carrieth away?
texts.job.21.19: [Ye say], God layeth up his iniquity for his children. Let him recompense it unto himself, that he may know it:
texts.job.21.20: Let his own eyes see his destruction, And let him drink of the wrath of the Almighty.
texts.job.21.21: For what careth he for his house after him, When the number of his months is cut off?
texts.job.21.22: Shall any teach God knowledge, Seeing he judgeth those that are high?
texts.job.21.23: One dieth in his full strength, Being wholly at ease and quiet:
texts.job.21.24: His pails are full of milk, And the marrow of his bones is moistened.
texts.job.21.25: And another dieth in bitterness of soul, And never tasteth of good.
texts.job.21.26: They lie down alike in the dust, And the worm covereth them.
texts.job.21.27: Behold, I know your thoughts, And the devices wherewith ye would wrong me.
texts.job.21.28: For ye say, Where is the house of the prince? And where is the tent wherein the wicked dwelt?
texts.job.21.29: Have ye not asked wayfaring men? And do ye not know their evidences,
texts.job.21.30: That the evil man is reserved to the day of calamity? That they are led forth to the day of wrath?
texts.job.21.31: Who shall declare his way to his face? And who shall repay him what he hath done?
texts.job.21.32: Yet shall he be borne to the grave, And men shall keep watch over the tomb.
texts.job.21.33: The clods of the valley shall be sweet unto him, And all men shall draw after him, As there were innumerable before him.
texts.job.21.34: How then comfort ye me in vain, Seeing in your answers there remaineth [only] falsehood?
texts.job.22.1: Then answered Eliphaz the Temanite, and said,
texts.job.22.2: Can a man be profitable unto God? Surely he that is wise is profitable unto himself.
texts.job.22.3: Is it any pleasure to the Almighty, that thou art righteous? Or is it gain [to him], that thou makest thy ways perfect?
texts.job.22.4: Is it for thy fear [of him] that he reproveth thee, That he entereth with thee into judgment?
texts.job.22.5: Is not thy wickedness great? Neither is there any end to thine iniquities.
