texts.job.22.6: For thou hast taken pledges of thy brother for nought, And stripped the naked of their clothing.
texts.job.22.7: Thou hast not given water to the weary to drink, And thou hast withholden bread from the hungry.
texts.job.22.8: But as for the mighty man, he had the earth; And the honorable man, he dwelt in it.
texts.job.22.9: Thou hast sent widows away empty, And the arms of the fatherless have been broken.
texts.job.22.10: Therefore snares are round about thee, And sudden fear troubleth thee,
texts.job.22.11: Or darkness, so that thou canst not see, And abundance of waters cover thee.
texts.job.22.12: Is not God in the height of heaven? And behold the height of the stars, how high they are!
texts.job.22.13: And thou sayest, What doth God know? Can he judge through the thick darkness?
texts.job.22.14: Thick clouds are a covering to him, so that he seeth not; And he walketh on the vault of heaven.
texts.job.22.15: Wilt thou keep the old way Which wicked men have trodden?
texts.job.22.16: Who were snatched away before their time, Whose foundation was poured out as a stream,
texts.job.22.17: Who said unto God, Depart from us; And, What can the Almighty do for us?
texts.job.22.18: Yet he filled their houses with good things: But the counsel of the wicked is far from me.
texts.job.22.19: The righteous see it, and are glad; And the innocent laugh them to scorn,
texts.job.22.20: [Saying], Surely they that did rise up against us are cut off, And the remnant of them the fire hath consumed.
texts.job.22.21: Acquaint now thyself with him, and be at peace: Thereby good shall come unto thee.
texts.job.22.22: Receive, I pray thee, the law from his mouth, And lay up his words in thy heart.
texts.job.22.23: If thou return to the Almighty, thou shalt be built up, If thou put away unrighteousness far from thy tents.
texts.job.22.24: And lay thou [thy] treasure in the dust, And [the gold of] Ophir among the stones of the brooks;
texts.job.22.25: And the Almighty will be thy treasure, And precious silver unto thee.
texts.job.22.26: For then shalt thou delight thyself in the Almighty, And shalt lift up thy face unto God.
texts.job.22.27: Thou shalt make thy prayer unto him, and he will hear thee; And thou shalt pay thy vows.
texts.job.22.28: Thou shalt also decree a thing, and it shall be established unto thee; And light shall shine upon thy ways.
texts.job.22.29: When they cast [thee] down, thou shalt say, [There is] lifting up; And the humble person he will save.
texts.job.22.30: He will deliver [even] him that is not innocent: Yea, he shall be delivered through the cleanness of thy hands.
texts.job.23.2: Even to-day is my complaint rebellious: My stroke is heavier than my groaning.
texts.job.23.3: Oh that I knew where I might find him! That I might come even to his seat!
texts.job.23.4: I would set my cause in order before him, And fill my mouth with arguments.
texts.job.23.5: I would know the words which he would answer me, And understand what he would say unto me.
texts.job.23.6: Would he contend with me in the greatness of his power? Nay; but he would give heed unto me.
texts.job.23.7: There the upright might reason with him; So should I be delivered for ever from my judge.
texts.job.23.8: Behold, I go forward, but he is not [there]; And backward, but I cannot perceive him;
texts.job.23.9: On the left hand, when he doth work, but I cannot behold him; He hideth himself on the right hand, that I cannot see him.
texts.job.23.10: But he knoweth the way that I take; When he hath tried me, I shall come forth as gold.
texts.job.23.11: My foot hath held fast to his steps; His way have I kept, and turned not aside.
texts.job.23.12: I have not gone back from the commandment of his lips; I have treasured up the words of his mouth more than my necessary food.
texts.job.23.13: But he is in one [mind], and who can turn him? And what his soul desireth, even that he doeth.
texts.job.23.14: For he performeth that which is appointed for me: And many such things are with him.
texts.job.23.15: Therefore am I terrified at his presence; When I consider, I am afraid of him.
texts.job.23.16: For God hath made my heart faint, And the Almighty hath terrified me;
texts.job.23.17: Because I was not cut off before the darkness, Neither did he cover the thick darkness from my face.
texts.job.24.1: Why are times not laid up by the Almighty? And why do not they that know him see his days?
texts.job.24.2: There are that remove the landmarks; They violently take away flocks, and feed them.
texts.job.24.3: They drive away the ass of the fatherless; They take the widow's ox for a pledge.
texts.job.24.4: They turn the needy out of the way: The poor of the earth all hide themselves.
texts.job.24.5: Behold, as wild asses in the desert They go forth to their work, seeking diligently for food; The wilderness [yieldeth] them bread for their children.
texts.job.24.6: They cut their provender in the field; And they glean the vintage of the wicked.
texts.job.24.7: They lie all night naked without clothing, And have no covering in the cold.
texts.job.24.8: They are wet with the showers of the mountains, And embrace the rock for want of a shelter.
texts.job.24.9: There are that pluck the fatherless from the breast, And take a pledge of the poor;
texts.job.24.10: [So that] they go about naked without clothing, And being hungry they carry the sheaves.
texts.job.24.11: They make oil within the walls of these men; They tread [their] winepresses, and suffer thirst.
texts.job.24.12: From out of the populous city men groan, And the soul of the wounded crieth out: Yet God regardeth not the folly.
texts.job.24.13: These are of them that rebel against the light; They know not the ways thereof, Nor abide in the paths thereof.
texts.job.24.14: The murderer riseth with the light; He killeth the poor and needy; And in the night he is as a thief.
texts.job.24.15: The eye also of the adulterer waiteth for the twilight, Saying, No eye shall see me: And he disguiseth his face.
texts.job.24.16: In the dark they dig through houses: They shut themselves up in the day-time; They know not the light.
texts.job.24.17: For the morning is to all of them as thick darkness; For they know the terrors of the thick darkness.
texts.job.24.18: Swiftly they [pass away] upon the face of the waters; Their portion is cursed in the earth: They turn not into the way of the vineyards.
texts.job.24.19: Drought and heat consume the snow waters: [So doth] Sheol [those that] have sinned.
texts.job.24.20: The womb shall forget him; The worm shall feed sweetly on him; He shall be no more remembered; And unrighteousness shall be broken as a tree.
texts.job.24.21: He devoureth the barren that beareth not, And doeth not good to the widow.
texts.job.24.22: Yet [God] preserveth the mighty by his power: He riseth up that hath no assurance of life.
texts.job.24.23: [God] giveth them to be in security, and they rest thereon; And his eyes are upon their ways.
texts.job.24.24: They are exalted; yet a little while, and they are gone; Yea, they are brought low, they are taken out of the way as all others, And are cut off as the tops of the ears of grain.
texts.job.24.25: And if it be not so now, who will prove me a liar, And make my speech nothing worth?
texts.job.25.1: Then answered Bildad the Shuhite, and said,
texts.job.25.2: Dominion and fear are with him; He maketh peace in his high places.
texts.job.25.3: Is there any number of his armies? And upon whom doth not his light arise?
texts.job.25.4: How then can man be just with God? Or how can he be clean that is born of a woman?
texts.job.25.5: Behold, even the moon hath no brightness, And the stars are not pure in his sight:
texts.job.25.6: How much less man, that is a worm! And the son of man, that is a worm!
texts.job.26.2: How hast thou helped him that is without power! How hast thou saved the arm that hath no strength!
texts.job.26.3: How hast thou counselled him that hath no wisdom, And plentifully declared sound knowledge!
texts.job.26.4: To whom hast thou uttered words? And whose spirit came forth from thee?
texts.job.26.5: They that are deceased tremble Beneath the waters and the inhabitants thereof.
texts.job.26.6: Sheol is naked before [God], And Abaddon hath no covering.
texts.job.26.7: He stretcheth out the north over empty space, And hangeth the earth upon nothing.
texts.job.26.8: He bindeth up the waters in his thick clouds; And the cloud is not rent under them.
texts.job.26.9: He incloseth the face of his throne, And spreadeth his cloud upon it.
texts.job.26.10: He hath described a boundary upon the face of the waters, Unto the confines of light and darkness.
texts.job.26.11: The pillars of heaven tremble And are astonished at his rebuke.
texts.job.26.12: He stirreth up the sea with his power, And by his understanding he smiteth through Rahab.
texts.job.26.13: By his Spirit the heavens are garnished; His hand hath pierced the swift serpent.
texts.job.26.14: Lo, these are but the outskirts of his ways: And how small a whisper do we hear of him! But the thunder of his power who can understand?
texts.job.27.1: And Job again took up his parable, and said,
texts.job.27.2: As God liveth, who hath taken away my right, And the Almighty, who hath vexed my soul:
texts.job.27.3: (For my life is yet whole in me, And the spirit of God is in my nostrils);
texts.job.27.4: Surely my lips shall not speak unrighteousness, Neither shall my tongue utter deceit.
texts.job.27.5: Far be it from me that I should justify you: Till I die I will not put away mine integrity from me.
texts.job.27.6: My righteousness I hold fast, and will not let it go: My heart shall not reproach [me] so long as I live.
texts.job.27.7: Let mine enemy be as the wicked, And let him that riseth up against me be as the unrighteous.
texts.job.27.8: For what is the hope of the godless, though he get him gain, When God taketh away his soul?
texts.job.27.9: Will God hear his cry, When trouble cometh upon him?
texts.job.27.10: Will he delight himself in the Almighty, And call upon God at all times?
texts.job.27.11: I will teach you concerning the hand of God; That which is with the Almighty will I not conceal.
texts.job.27.12: Behold, all ye yourselves have seen it; Why then are ye become altogether vain?
texts.job.27.13: This is the portion of a wicked man with God, And the heritage of oppressors, which they receive from the Almighty:
texts.job.27.14: If his children be multiplied, it is for the sword; And his offspring shall not be satisfied with bread.
texts.job.27.15: Those that remain of him shall be buried in death, And his widows shall make no lamentation.
texts.job.27.16: Though he heap up silver as the dust, And prepare raiment as the clay;
texts.job.27.17: He may prepare it, but the just shall put it on, And the innocent shall divide the silver.
texts.job.27.18: He buildeth his house as the moth, And as a booth which the keeper maketh.
texts.job.27.19: He lieth down rich, but he shall not be gathered [to his fathers]; He openeth his eyes, and he is not.
texts.job.27.20: Terrors overtake him like waters; A tempest stealeth him away in the night.
texts.job.27.21: The east wind carrieth him away, and he departeth; And it sweepeth him out of his place.
texts.job.27.22: For [God] shall hurl at him, and not spare: He would fain flee out of his hand.
texts.job.27.23: Men shall clap their hands at him, And shall hiss him out of his place.
texts.job.28.1: Surely there is a mine for silver, And a place for gold which they refine.
texts.job.28.2: Iron is taken out of the earth, And copper is molten out of the stone.
texts.job.28.3: [Man] setteth an end to darkness, And searcheth out, to the furthest bound, The stones of obscurity and of thick darkness.
texts.job.28.4: He breaketh open a shaft away from where men sojourn; They are forgotten of the foot; They hang afar from men, they swing to and fro.
texts.job.28.5: As for the earth, out of it cometh bread; And underneath it is turned up as it were by fire.
texts.job.28.6: The stones thereof are the place of sapphires, And it hath dust of gold.
texts.job.28.7: That path no bird of prey knoweth, Neither hath the falcon's eye seen it:
texts.job.28.8: The proud beasts have not trodden it, Nor hath the fierce lion passed thereby.
texts.job.28.9: He putteth forth his hand upon the flinty rock; He overturneth the mountains by the roots.
texts.job.28.10: He cutteth out channels among the rocks; And his eye seeth every precious thing.
texts.job.28.11: He bindeth the streams that they trickle not; And the thing that is hid bringeth he forth to light.
texts.job.28.12: But where shall wisdom be found? And where is the place of understanding?
texts.job.28.13: Man knoweth not the price thereof; Neither is it found in the land of the living.
texts.job.28.14: The deep saith, It is not in me; And the sea saith, It is not with me.
texts.job.28.15: It cannot be gotten for gold, Neither shall silver be weighed for the price thereof.
texts.job.28.16: It cannot be valued with the gold of Ophir, With the precious onyx, or the sapphire.
texts.job.28.17: Gold and glass cannot equal it, Neither shall it be exchanged for jewels of fine gold.
texts.job.28.18: No mention shall be made of coral or of crystal: Yea, the price of wisdom is above rubies.
texts.job.28.19: The topaz of Ethiopia shall not equal it, Neither shall it be valued with pure gold.
texts.job.28.20: Whence then cometh wisdom? And where is the place of understanding?
texts.job.28.21: Seeing it is hid from the eyes of all living, And kept close from the birds of the heavens.
texts.job.28.22: Destruction and Death say, We have heard a rumor thereof with our ears.
texts.job.28.23: God understandeth the way thereof, And he knoweth the place thereof.
texts.job.28.24: For he looketh to the ends of the earth, And seeth under the whole heaven;
texts.job.28.25: To make a weight for the wind: Yea, he meteth out the waters by measure.
texts.job.28.26: When he made a decree for the rain, And a way for the lightning of the thunder;
texts.job.28.27: Then did he see it, and declare it; He established it, yea, and searched it out.
texts.job.28.28: And unto man he said, Behold, the fear of the Lord, that is wisdom; And to depart from evil is understanding.
texts.job.29.1: And Job again took up his parable, and said,
texts.job.29.2: Oh that I were as in the months of old, As in the days when God watched over me;
texts.job.29.3: When his lamp shined upon my head, And by his light I walked through darkness;
texts.job.29.4: As I was in the ripeness of my days, When the friendship of God was upon my tent;
texts.job.29.5: When the Almighty was yet with me, And my children were about me;
texts.job.29.6: When my steps were washed with butter, And the rock poured me out streams of oil!
texts.job.29.7: When I went forth to the gate unto the city, When I prepared my seat in the street,
texts.job.29.8: The young men saw me and hid themselves, And the aged rose up and stood;
texts.job.29.9: The princes refrained from talking, And laid their hand on their mouth;
texts.job.29.10: The voice of the nobles was hushed, And their tongue cleaved to the roof of their mouth.
texts.job.29.11: For when the ear heard [me], then it blessed me; And when the eye saw [me], it gave witness unto me:
texts.job.29.12: Because I delivered the poor that cried, The fatherless also, that had none to help him.
texts.job.29.13: The blessing of him that was ready to perish came upon me; And I caused the widow's heart to sing for joy.
texts.job.29.14: I put on righteousness, and it clothed me: My justice was as a robe and a diadem.
texts.job.29.15: I was eyes to the blind, And feet was I to the lame.
texts.job.29.16: I was a father to the needy: And the cause of him that I knew not I searched out.
texts.job.29.17: And I brake the jaws of the unrighteous, And plucked the prey out of his teeth.
texts.job.29.18: Then I said, I shall die in my nest, And I shall multiply my days as the sand:
texts.job.29.19: My root is spread out to the waters, And the dew lieth all night upon my branch;
texts.job.29.20: My glory is fresh in me, And my bow is renewed in my hand.
texts.job.29.21: Unto me men gave ear, and waited, And kept silence for my counsel.
texts.job.29.22: After my words they spake not again; And my speech distilled upon them.
texts.job.29.23: And they waited for me as for the rain; And they opened their mouth wide [as] for the latter rain.
texts.job.29.24: I smiled on them, when they had no confidence; And the light of my countenance they cast not down.
texts.job.29.25: I chose out their way, and sat [as] chief, And dwelt as a king in the army, As one that comforteth the mourners.
texts.job.30.1: But now they that are younger than I have me in derision, Whose fathers I disdained to set with the dogs of my flock.
texts.job.30.2: Yea, the strength of their hands, whereto should it profit me? Men in whom ripe age is perished.
texts.job.30.3: They are gaunt with want and famine; They gnaw the dry ground, in the gloom of wasteness and desolation.
texts.job.30.4: They pluck salt-wort by the bushes; And the roots of the broom are their food.
texts.job.30.5: They are driven forth from the midst [of men]; They cry after them as after a thief;
texts.job.30.6: So that they dwell in frightful valleys, In holes of the earth and of the rocks.
texts.job.30.7: Among the bushes they bray; Under the nettles they are gathered together.
texts.job.30.8: [They are] children of fools, yea, children of base men; They were scourged out of the land.
texts.job.30.9: And now I am become their song, Yea, I am a byword unto them.
texts.job.30.10: They abhor me, they stand aloof from me, And spare not to spit in my face.
texts.job.30.11: For he hath loosed his cord, and afflicted me; And they have cast off the bridle before me.
texts.job.30.12: Upon my right hand rise the rabble; They thrust aside my feet, And they cast up against me their ways of destruction.
texts.job.30.13: They mar my path, They set forward my calamity, [Even] men that have no helper.
texts.job.30.14: As through a wide breach they come: In the midst of the ruin they roll themselves [upon me].
texts.job.30.15: Terrors are turned upon me; They chase mine honor as the wind; And my welfare is passed away as a cloud.
texts.job.30.16: And now my soul is poured out within me; Days of affliction have taken hold upon me.
texts.job.30.17: In the night season my bones are pierced in me, And the [pains] that gnaw me take no rest.
texts.job.30.18: By [God's] great force is my garment disfigured; It bindeth me about as the collar of my coat.
texts.job.30.19: He hath cast me into the mire, And I am become like dust and ashes.
texts.job.30.20: I cry unto thee, and thou dost not answer me: I stand up, and thou gazest at me.
texts.job.30.21: Thou art turned to be cruel to me; With the might of thy hand thou persecutest me.
texts.job.30.22: Thou liftest me up to the wind, thou causest me to ride [upon it]; And thou dissolvest me in the storm.
texts.job.30.23: For I know that thou wilt bring me to death, And to the house appointed for all living.
texts.job.30.24: Howbeit doth not one stretch out the hand in his fall? Or in his calamity therefore cry for help?
texts.job.30.25: Did not I weep for him that was in trouble? Was not my soul grieved for the needy?
texts.job.30.26: When I looked for good, then evil came; And when I waited for light, there came darkness.
texts.job.30.27: My heart is troubled, and resteth not; Days of affliction are come upon me.
texts.job.30.28: I go mourning without the sun: I stand up in the assembly, and cry for help.
texts.job.30.29: I am a brother to jackals, And a companion to ostriches.
texts.job.30.30: My skin is black, [and falleth] from me, And my bones are burned with heat.
texts.job.30.31: Therefore is my harp [turned] to mourning, And my pipe into the voice of them that weep.
texts.job.31.1: I made a covenant with mine eyes; How then should I look upon a virgin?
texts.job.31.2: For what is the portion from God above, And the heritage from the Almighty on high?
texts.job.31.3: Is it not calamity to the unrighteous, And disaster to the workers of iniquity?
texts.job.31.4: Doth not he see my ways, And number all my steps?
texts.job.31.5: If I have walked with falsehood, And my foot hath hasted to deceit
texts.job.31.6: (Let me be weighed in an even balance, That God may know mine integrity);
texts.job.31.7: If my step hath turned out of the way, And my heart walked after mine eyes, And if any spot hath cleaved to my hands:
texts.job.31.8: Then let me sow, and let another eat; Yea, let the produce of my field be rooted out.
texts.job.31.9: If my heart hath been enticed unto a woman, And I have laid wait at my neighbor's door;
texts.job.31.10: Then let my wife grind unto another, And let others bow down upon her.
texts.job.31.11: For that were a heinous crime; Yea, it were an iniquity to be punished by the judges:
texts.job.31.12: For it is a fire that consumeth unto Destruction, And would root out all mine increase.
texts.job.31.13: If I have despised the cause of my man-servant or of my maid-servant, When they contended with me;
texts.job.31.14: What then shall I do when God riseth up? And when he visiteth, what shall I answer him?
texts.job.31.15: Did not he that made me in the womb make him? And did not one fashion us in the womb?
texts.job.31.16: If I have withheld the poor from [their] desire, Or have caused the eyes of the widow to fail,
texts.job.31.17: Or have eaten my morsel alone, And the fatherless hath not eaten thereof
texts.job.31.18: (Nay, from my youth he grew up with me as with a father, And her have I guided from my mother's womb);
texts.job.31.19: If I have seen any perish for want of clothing, Or that the needy had no covering;
texts.job.31.20: If his loins have not blessed me, And if he hath not been warmed with the fleece of my sheep;
texts.job.31.21: If I have lifted up my hand against the fatherless, Because I saw my help in the gate:
texts.job.31.22: Then let my shoulder fall from the shoulder-blade, And mine arm be broken from the bone.
texts.job.31.23: For calamity from God is a terror to me, And by reason of his majesty I can do nothing.
texts.job.31.24: If I have made gold my hope, And have said to the fine gold, [Thou art] my confidence;
texts.job.31.25: If I have rejoiced because my wealth was great, And because my hand had gotten much;
texts.job.31.26: If I have beheld the sun when it shined, Or the moon walking in brightness,
texts.job.31.27: And my heart hath been secretly enticed, And my mouth hath kissed my hand:
texts.job.31.28: This also were an iniquity to be punished by the judges; For I should have denied the God that is above.
texts.job.31.29: If I have rejoiced at the destruction of him that hated me, Or lifted up myself when evil found him;
texts.job.31.30: (Yea, I have not suffered by mouth to sin By asking his life with a curse);
texts.job.31.31: If the men of my tent have not said, Who can find one that hath not been filled with his meat?
texts.job.31.32: (The sojourner hath not lodged in the street; But I have opened my doors to the traveller);
texts.job.31.33: If like Adam I have covered my transgressions, By hiding mine iniquity in my bosom,
texts.job.31.34: Because I feared the great multitude, And the contempt of families terrified me, So that I kept silence, and went not out of the door-
texts.job.31.35: Oh that I had one to hear me! (Lo, here is my signature, let the Almighty answer me); And [that I had] the indictment which mine adversary hath written!
texts.job.31.36: Surely I would carry it upon my shoulder; I would bind it unto me as a crown:
texts.job.31.37: I would declare unto him the number of my steps; As a prince would I go near unto him.
texts.job.31.38: If my land crieth out against me, And the furrows thereof weep together;
texts.job.31.39: If I have eaten the fruits thereof without money, Or have caused the owners thereof to lose their life:
texts.job.31.40: Let thistles grow instead of wheat, And cockle instead of barley. The words of Job are ended.
texts.job.32.1: So these three men ceased to answer Job, because he was righteous in his own eyes.
texts.job.32.2: Then was kindled the wrath of Elihu the son of Barachel the Buzite, of the family of Ram: against Job was his wrath kindled, because he justified himself rather than God.
texts.job.32.3: Also against his three friends was his wrath kindled, because they had found no answer, and yet had condemned Job.
texts.job.32.4: Now Elihu had waited to speak unto Job, because they were elder than he.
texts.job.32.5: And when Elihu saw that there was no answer in the mouth of these three men, his wrath was kindled.
texts.job.32.6: And Elihu the son of Barachel the Buzite answered and said, I am young, and ye are very old; Wherefore I held back, and durst not show you mine opinion.
texts.job.32.7: I said, Days should speak, And multitude of years should teach wisdom.
texts.job.32.8: But there is a spirit in man, And the breath of the Almighty giveth them understanding.
texts.job.32.9: It is not the great that are wise, Nor the aged that understand justice.
texts.job.32.10: Therefore I said, Hearken to me; I also will show mine opinion.
texts.job.32.11: Behold, I waited for your words, I listened for your reasonings, Whilst ye searched out what to say.
texts.job.32.12: Yea, I attended unto you, And, behold, there was none that convinced Job, Or that answered his words, among you.
texts.job.32.13: Beware lest ye say, We have found wisdom; God may vanquish him, not man:
texts.job.32.14: For he hath not directed his words against me; Neither will I answer him with your speeches.
texts.job.32.15: They are amazed, they answer no more: They have not a word to say.
texts.job.32.16: And shall I wait, because they speak not, Because they stand still, and answer no more?
texts.job.32.17: I also will answer my part, I also will show mine opinion.
texts.job.32.18: For I am full of words; The spirit within me constraineth me.
texts.job.32.19: Behold, my breast is as wine which hath no vent; Like new wine-skins it is ready to burst.
texts.job.32.20: I will speak, that I may be refreshed; I will open my lips and answer.
texts.job.32.21: Let me not, I pray you, respect any man's person; Neither will I give flattering titles unto any man.
texts.job.32.22: For I know not to give flattering titles; [Else] would my Maker soon take me away.
texts.job.33.1: Howbeit, Job, I pray thee, hear my speech, And hearken to all my words.
texts.job.33.2: Behold now, I have opened my mouth; My tongue hath spoken in my mouth.
texts.job.33.3: My words [shall utter] the uprightness of my heart; And that which my lips know they shall speak sincerely.
texts.job.33.4: The Spirit of God hath made me, And the breath of the Almighty giveth me life.
texts.job.33.5: If thou canst, answer thou me; Set [thy words] in order before me, stand forth.
texts.job.33.6: Behold, I am toward God even as thou art: I also am formed out of the clay.
texts.job.33.7: Behold, my terror shall not make thee afraid, Neither shall my pressure be heavy upon thee.
texts.job.33.8: Surely thou hast spoken in my hearing, And I have heard the voice of [thy] words, [saying],
texts.job.33.9: I am clean, without transgression; I am innocent, neither is there iniquity in me:
texts.job.33.10: Behold, he findeth occasions against me, He counteth me for his enemy:
texts.job.33.11: He putteth my feet in the stocks, He marketh all my paths.
texts.job.33.12: Behold, I will answer thee, in this thou art not just; For God is greater than man.
texts.job.33.13: Why dost thou strive against him, For that he giveth not account of any of his matters?
texts.job.33.14: For God speaketh once, Yea twice, [though man] regardeth it not.
texts.job.33.15: In a dream, in a vision of the night, When deep sleep falleth upon men, In slumberings upon the bed;
texts.job.33.16: Then he openeth the ears of men, And sealeth their instruction,
texts.job.33.17: That he may withdraw man [from his] purpose, And hide pride from man;
texts.job.33.18: He keepeth back his soul from the pit, And his life from perishing by the sword.
texts.job.33.19: He is chastened also with pain upon his bed, And with continual strife in his bones;
texts.job.33.20: So that his life abhorreth bread, And his soul dainty food.
texts.job.33.21: His flesh is consumed away, that it cannot be seen; And his bones that were not seen stick out.
texts.job.33.22: Yea, his soul draweth near unto the pit, And his life to the destroyers.
texts.job.33.23: If there be with him an angel, An interpreter, one among a thousand, To show unto man what is right for him;
texts.job.33.24: Then [God] is gracious unto him, and saith, Deliver him from going down to the pit, I have found a ransom.
texts.job.33.25: His flesh shall be fresher than a child's; He returneth to the days of his youth.
texts.job.33.26: He prayeth unto God, and he is favorable unto him, So that he seeth his face with joy: And he restoreth unto man his righteousness.
texts.job.33.27: He singeth before men, and saith, I have sinned, and perverted that which was right, And it profited me not:
texts.job.33.28: He hath redeemed my soul from going into the pit, And my life shall behold the light.
texts.job.33.29: Lo, all these things doth God work, Twice, [yea] thrice, with a man,
texts.job.33.30: To bring back his soul from the pit, That he may be enlightened with the light of the living.
texts.job.33.31: Mark well, O Job, hearken unto me: Hold thy peace, and I will speak.
texts.job.33.32: If thou hast anything to say, answer me: Speak, for I desire to justify thee.
texts.job.33.33: If not, hearken thou unto me: Hold thy peace, and I will teach thee wisdom.
texts.job.34.2: Hear my words, ye wise men; And give ear unto me, ye that have knowledge.
texts.job.34.3: For the ear trieth words, As the palate tasteth food.
texts.job.34.4: Let us choose for us that which is right: Let us know among ourselves what is good.
texts.job.34.5: For Job hath said, I am righteous, And God hath taken away my right:
texts.job.34.6: Notwithstanding my right I am [accounted] a liar; My wound is incurable, [though I am] without transgression.
texts.job.34.7: What man is like Job, Who drinketh up scoffing like water,
texts.job.34.8: Who goeth in company with the workers of iniquity, And walketh with wicked men?
texts.job.34.9: For he hath said, It profiteth a man nothing That he should delight himself with God.
texts.job.34.10: Therefore hearken unto me, ye men of understanding: Far be it from God, that he should do wickedness, And from the Almighty, that he should commit iniquity.
texts.job.34.11: For the work of a man will he render unto him, And cause every man to find according to his ways.
texts.job.34.12: Yea, of a surety, God will not do wickedly, Neither will the Almighty pervert justice.
texts.job.34.13: Who gave him a charge over the earth? Or who hath disposed the whole world?
texts.job.34.14: If he set his heart upon himself, [If] he gather unto himself his spirit and his breath;
texts.job.34.15: All flesh shall perish together, And man shall turn again unto dust.
texts.job.34.16: If now [thou hast] understanding, hear this: Hearken to the voice of my words.
texts.job.34.17: Shall even one that hateth justice govern? And wilt thou condemn him that is righteous [and] mighty?-
texts.job.34.18: [Him] that saith to a king, [Thou art] vile, [Or] to nobles, [Ye are] wicked;
texts.job.34.19: That respecteth not the persons of princes, Nor regardeth the rich more than the poor; For they all are the work of his hands.
texts.job.34.20: In a moment they die, even at midnight; The people are shaken and pass away, And the mighty are taken away without hand.
texts.job.34.21: For his eyes are upon the ways of a man, And he seeth all his goings.
texts.job.34.22: There is no darkness, nor thick gloom, Where the workers of iniquity may hide themselves.
texts.job.34.23: For he needeth not further to consider a man, That he should go before God in judgment.
texts.job.34.24: He breaketh in pieces mighty men [in ways] past finding out, And setteth others in their stead.
texts.job.34.25: Therefore he taketh knowledge of their works; And he overturneth them in the night, so that they are destroyed.
texts.job.34.26: He striketh them as wicked men In the open sight of others;
texts.job.34.27: Because they turned aside from following him, And would not have regard in any of his ways:
texts.job.34.28: So that they caused the cry of the poor to come unto him, And he heard the cry of the afflicted.
texts.job.34.29: When he giveth quietness, who then can condemn? And when he hideth his face, who then can behold him? Alike whether [it be done] unto a nation, or unto a man:
texts.job.34.30: That the godless man reign not, That there be none to ensnare the people.
texts.job.34.31: For hath any said unto God, I have borne [chastisement], I will not offend [any more]:
texts.job.34.32: That which I see not teach thou me: If I have done iniquity, I will do it no more?
texts.job.34.33: Shall his recompense be as thou wilt, that thou refusest it? For thou must choose, and not I: Therefore speak what thou knowest.
texts.job.34.34: Men of understanding will say unto me, Yea, every wise man that heareth me:
texts.job.34.35: Job speaketh without knowledge, And his words are without wisdom.
texts.job.34.36: Would that Job were tried unto the end, Because of his answering like wicked men.
texts.job.34.37: For he addeth rebellion unto his sin; He clappeth his hands among us, And multiplieth his words against God.
texts.job.35.2: Thinkest thou this to be [thy] right, [Or] sayest thou, My righteousness is more than God's,
texts.job.35.3: That thou sayest, What advantage will it be unto thee? [And], What profit shall I have, more than if I had sinned?
texts.job.35.4: I will answer thee, And thy companions with thee.
texts.job.35.5: Look unto the heavens, and see; And behold the skies, which are higher than thou.
texts.job.35.6: If thou hast sinned, what effectest thou against him? And if thy transgressions be multiplied, what doest thou unto him?
texts.job.35.7: If thou be righteous, what givest thou him? Or what receiveth he of thy hand?
texts.job.35.8: Thy wickedness [may hurt] a man as thou art; And thy righteousness [may profit] a son of man.
texts.job.35.9: By reason of the multitude of oppressions they cry out; They cry for help by reason of the arm of the mighty.
texts.job.35.10: But none saith, Where is God my Maker, Who giveth songs in the night,
texts.job.35.11: Who teacheth us more than the beasts of the earth, And maketh us wiser than the birds of the heavens?
texts.job.35.12: There they cry, but none giveth answer, Because of the pride of evil men.
texts.job.35.13: Surely God will not hear an empty [cry], Neither will the Almighty regard it.
texts.job.35.14: How much less when thou sayest thou beholdest him not, The cause is before him, and thou waitest for him!
texts.job.35.15: But now, because he hath not visited in his anger, Neither doth he greatly regard arrogance;
texts.job.35.16: Therefore doth Job open his mouth in vanity; He multiplieth words without knowledge.
texts.job.36.2: Suffer me a little, and I will show thee; For I have yet somewhat to say on God's behalf.
texts.job.36.3: I will fetch my knowledge from afar, And will ascribe righteousness to my Maker.
texts.job.36.4: For truly my words are not false: One that is perfect in knowledge is with thee.
texts.job.36.5: Behold, God is mighty, and despiseth not any: He is mighty in strength of understanding.
texts.job.36.6: He preserveth not the life of the wicked, But giveth to the afflicted [their] right.
texts.job.36.7: He withdraweth not his eyes from the righteous: But with kings upon the throne He setteth them for ever, and they are exalted.
texts.job.36.8: And if they be bound in fetters, And be taken in the cords of afflictions;
texts.job.36.9: Then he showeth them their work, And their transgressions, that they have behaved themselves proudly.
texts.job.36.10: He openeth also their ear to instruction, And commandeth that they return from iniquity.
texts.job.36.11: If they hearken and serve [him], They shall spend their days in prosperity, And their years in pleasures.
texts.job.36.12: But if they hearken not, they shall perish by the sword, And they shall die without knowledge.
texts.job.36.13: But they that are godless in heart lay up anger: They cry not for help when he bindeth them.
texts.job.36.14: They die in youth, And their life [perisheth] among the unclean.
texts.job.36.15: He delivereth the afflicted by their affliction, And openeth their ear in oppression.
texts.job.36.16: Yea, he would have allured thee out of distress Into a broad place, where there is no straitness; And that which is set on thy table would be full of fatness.
texts.job.36.17: But thou art full of the judgment of the wicked: Judgment and justice take hold [on thee].
texts.job.36.18: For let not wrath stir thee up against chastisements; Neither let the greatness of the ransom turn thee aside.
texts.job.36.19: Will thy cry avail, [that thou be] not in distress, Or all the forces of [thy] strength?
texts.job.36.20: Desire not the night, When peoples are cut off in their place.
texts.job.36.21: Take heed, regard not iniquity: For this hast thou chosen rather than affliction.
texts.job.36.22: Behold, God doeth loftily in his power: Who is a teacher like unto him?
texts.job.36.23: Who hath enjoined him his way? Or who can say, Thou hast wrought unrighteousness?
texts.job.36.24: Remember that thou magnify his work, Whereof men have sung.
texts.job.36.25: All men have looked thereon; Man beholdeth it afar off.
texts.job.36.26: Behold, God is great, and we know him not; The number of his years is unsearchable.
texts.job.36.27: For he draweth up the drops of water, Which distil in rain from his vapor,
texts.job.36.28: Which the skies pour down And drop upon man abundantly.
texts.job.36.29: Yea, can any understand the spreadings of the clouds, The thunderings of his pavilion?
texts.job.36.30: Behold, he spreadeth his light around him; And he covereth the bottom of the sea.
texts.job.36.31: For by these he judgeth the peoples; He giveth food in abundance.
texts.job.36.32: He covereth his hands with the lightning, And giveth it a charge that it strike the mark.
texts.job.36.33: The noise thereof telleth concerning him, The cattle also concerning [the storm] that cometh up.
texts.job.37.1: Yea, at this my heart trembleth, And is moved out of its place.
texts.job.37.2: Hear, oh, hear the noise of his voice, And the sound that goeth out of his mouth.
texts.job.37.3: He sendeth it forth under the whole heaven, And his lightening unto the ends of the earth.
texts.job.37.4: After it a voice roareth; He thundereth with the voice of his majesty; And he restraineth not [the lightnings] when his voice is heard.
texts.job.37.5: God thundereth marvellously with his voice; Great things doeth he, which we cannot comprehend.
texts.job.37.6: For he saith to the snow, Fall thou on the earth; Likewise to the shower of rain, And to the showers of his mighty rain.
texts.job.37.7: He sealeth up the hand of every man, That all men whom he hath made may know [it].
texts.job.37.8: Then the beasts go into coverts, And remain in their dens.
texts.job.37.9: Out of the chamber [of the south] cometh the storm, And cold out of the north.
texts.job.37.10: By the breath of God ice is given; And the breadth of the waters is straitened.
texts.job.37.11: Yea, he ladeth the thick cloud with moisture; He spreadeth abroad the cloud of his lightning:
texts.job.37.12: And it is turned round about by his guidance, That they may do whatsoever he commandeth them Upon the face of the habitable world,
texts.job.37.13: Whether it be for correction, or for his land, Or for lovingkindness, that he cause it to come.
texts.job.37.14: Hearken unto this, O Job: Stand still, and consider the wondrous works of God.
texts.job.37.15: Dost thou know how God layeth [his charge] upon them, And causeth the lightning of his cloud to shine?
texts.job.37.16: Dost thou know the balancings of the clouds, The wondrous works of him who is perfect in knowledge?
texts.job.37.17: How thy garments are warm, When the earth is still by reason of the south [wind]?
texts.job.37.18: Canst thou with him spread out the sky, Which is strong as a molten mirror?
texts.job.37.19: Teach us what we shall say unto him; [For] we cannot set [our speech] in order by reason of darkness.
texts.job.37.20: Shall it be told him that I would speak? Or should a man wish that he were swallowed up?
texts.job.37.21: And now men see not the light which is bright in the skies; But the wind passeth, and cleareth them.
texts.job.37.22: Out of the north cometh golden splendor: God hath upon him terrible majesty.
texts.job.37.23: [Touching] the Almighty, we cannot find him out He is excellent in power; And in justice and plenteous righteousness he will not afflict.
texts.job.37.24: Men do therefore fear him: He regardeth not any that are wise of heart.
texts.job.38.1: Then Jehovah answered Job out of the whirlwind, and said,
texts.job.38.2: Who is this that darkeneth counsel By words without knowledge?
texts.job.38.3: Gird up now thy loins like a man; For I will demand of thee, and declare thou unto me.
texts.job.38.4: Where wast thou when I laid the foundations of the earth? Declare, if thou hast understanding.
texts.job.38.5: Who determined the measures thereof, if thou knowest? Or who stretched the line upon it?
texts.job.38.6: Whereupon were the foundations thereof fastened? Or who laid the corner-stone thereof,
texts.job.38.7: When the morning stars sang together, And all the sons of God shouted for joy?
texts.job.38.8: Or [who] shut up the sea with doors, When it brake forth, [as if] it had issued out of the womb;
texts.job.38.9: When I made clouds the garment thereof, And thick darkness a swaddling-band for it,
texts.job.38.10: And marked out for it my bound, And set bars and doors,
texts.job.38.11: And said, Hitherto shalt thou come, but no further; And here shall thy proud waves be stayed?
texts.job.38.12: Hast thou commanded the morning since thy days [began], [And] caused the dayspring to know its place;
texts.job.38.13: That it might take hold of the ends of the earth, And the wicked be shaken out of it?
texts.job.38.14: It is changed as clay under the seal; And [all things] stand forth as a garment:
texts.job.38.15: And from the wicked their light is withholden, And the high arm is broken.
texts.job.38.16: Hast thou entered into the springs of the sea? Or hast thou walked in the recesses of the deep?
texts.job.38.17: Have the gates of death been revealed unto thee? Or hast thou seen the gates of the shadow of death?
texts.job.38.18: Hast thou comprehended the earth in its breadth? Declare, if thou knowest it all.
texts.job.38.19: Where is the way to the dwelling of light? And as for darkness, where is the place thereof,
texts.job.38.20: That thou shouldest take it to the bound thereof, And that thou shouldest discern the paths to the house thereof?
texts.job.38.21: [Doubtless], thou knowest, for thou wast then born, And the number of thy days is great!
texts.job.38.22: Hast thou entered the treasuries of the snow, Or hast thou seen the treasures of the hail,
texts.job.38.23: Which I have reserved against the time of trouble, Against the day of battle and war?
texts.job.38.24: By what way is the light parted, Or the east wind scattered upon the earth?
texts.job.38.25: Who hath cleft a channel for the waterflood, Or the way for the lightning of the thunder;
texts.job.38.26: To cause it to rain on a land where no man is; On the wilderness, wherein there is no man;
texts.job.38.27: To satisfy the waste and desolate [ground], And to cause the tender grass to spring forth?
texts.job.38.28: Hath the rain a father? Or who hath begotten the drops of dew?
texts.job.38.29: Out of whose womb came the ice? And the hoary frost of heaven, who hath gendered it?
texts.job.38.30: The waters hide themselves [and become] like stone, And the face of the deep is frozen.
texts.job.38.31: Canst thou bind the cluster of the Pleiades, Or loose the bands of Orion?
texts.job.38.32: Canst thou lead forth the Mazzaroth in their season? Or canst thou guide the Bear with her train?
texts.job.38.33: Knowest thou the ordinances of the heavens? Canst thou establish the dominion thereof in the earth?
texts.job.38.34: Canst thou lift up thy voice to the clouds, That abundance of waters may cover thee?
texts.job.38.35: Canst thou send forth lightnings, that they may go, And say unto thee, Here we are?
texts.job.38.36: Who hath put wisdom in the inward parts? Or who hath given understanding to the mind?
texts.job.38.37: Who can number the clouds by wisdom? Or who can pour out the bottles of heaven,
texts.job.38.38: When the dust runneth into a mass, And the clods cleave fast together?
texts.job.38.39: Canst thou hunt the prey for the lioness, Or satisfy the appetite of the young lions,
texts.job.38.40: When they couch in their dens, [And] abide in the covert to lie in wait?
texts.job.38.41: Who provideth for the raven his prey, When his young ones cry unto God, [And] wander for lack of food?
texts.job.39.1: Knowest thou the time when the wild goats of the rock bring forth? [Or] canst thou mark when the hinds do calve?
texts.job.39.2: Canst thou number the months that they fulfil? Or knowest thou the time when they bring forth?
texts.job.39.3: They bow themselves, they bring forth their young, They cast out their pains.
texts.job.39.4: Their young ones become strong, they grow up in the open field; They go forth, and return not again.
texts.job.39.5: Who hath sent out the wild ass free? Or who hath loosed the bonds of the swift ass,
texts.job.39.6: Whose home I have made the wilderness, And the salt land his dwelling-place?
texts.job.39.7: He scorneth the tumult of the city, Neither heareth he the shoutings of the driver.
texts.job.39.8: The range of the mountains is his pasture, And he searcheth after every green thing.
texts.job.39.9: Will the wild-ox be content to serve thee? Or will he abide by thy crib?
texts.job.39.10: Canst thou bind the wild-ox with his band in the furrow? Or will he harrow the valleys after thee?
texts.job.39.11: Wilt thou trust him, because his strength is great? Or wilt thou leave to him thy labor?
texts.job.39.12: Wilt thou confide in him, that he will bring home thy seed, And gather [the grain] of thy threshing-floor?
texts.job.39.13: The wings of the ostrich wave proudly; [But] are they the pinions and plumage of love?
texts.job.39.14: For she leaveth her eggs on the earth, And warmeth them in the dust,
texts.job.39.15: And forgetteth that the foot may crush them, Or that the wild beast may trample them.
texts.job.39.16: She dealeth hardly with her young ones, as if they were not hers: Though her labor be in vain, [she is] without fear;
texts.job.39.17: Because God hath deprived her of wisdom, Neither hath he imparted to her understanding.
texts.job.39.18: What time she lifteth up herself on high, She scorneth the horse and his rider.
texts.job.39.19: Hast thou given the horse [his] might? Hast thou clothed his neck with the quivering mane?
texts.job.39.20: Hast thou made him to leap as a locust? The glory of his snorting is terrible.
texts.job.39.21: He paweth in the valley, and rejoiceth in his strength: He goeth out to meet the armed men.
texts.job.39.22: He mocketh at fear, and is not dismayed; Neither turneth he back from the sword.
texts.job.39.23: The quiver rattleth against him, The flashing spear and the javelin.
texts.job.39.24: He swalloweth the ground with fierceness and rage; Neither believeth he that it is the voice of the trumpet.
texts.job.39.25: As oft as the trumpet [soundeth] he saith, Aha! And he smelleth the battle afar off, The thunder of the captains, and the shouting.
texts.job.39.26: Is it by thy wisdom that the hawk soareth, (And) stretcheth her wings toward the south?
texts.job.39.27: Is it at thy command that the eagle mounteth up, And maketh her nest on high?
texts.job.39.28: On the cliff she dwelleth, and maketh her home, Upon the point of the cliff, and the stronghold.
texts.job.39.29: From thence she spieth out the prey; Her eyes behold it afar off.
texts.job.39.30: Her young ones also suck up blood: And where the slain are, there is she.
texts.job.40.1: Moreover Jehovah answered Job, and said,
texts.job.40.2: Shall he that cavilleth contend with the Almighty? He that argueth with God, let him answer it.
texts.job.40.3: Then Job answered Jehovah, and said,
texts.job.40.4: Behold, I am of small account; What shall I answer thee? I lay my hand upon my mouth.
texts.job.40.5: Once have I spoken, and I will not answer; Yea, twice, but I will proceed no further.
texts.job.40.6: Then Jehovah answered Job out of the whirlwind, and said,
texts.job.40.7: Gird up thy loins now like a man: I will demand of thee, and declare thou unto me.
texts.job.40.8: Wilt thou even annul my judgment? Wilt thou condemn me, that thou mayest be justified?
texts.job.40.9: Or hast thou an arm like God? And canst thou thunder with a voice like him?
texts.job.40.10: Deck thyself now with excellency and dignity; And array thyself with honor and majesty.
texts.job.40.11: Pour forth the overflowings of thine anger; And look upon every one that is proud, and abase him.
texts.job.40.12: Look on every one that is proud, [and] bring him low; And tread down the wicked where they stand.
texts.job.40.13: Hide them in the dust together; Bind their faces in the hidden [place].
texts.job.40.14: Then will I also confess of thee That thine own right hand can save thee.
texts.job.40.15: Behold now, behemoth, which I made as well as thee; He eateth grass as an ox.
texts.job.40.16: Lo now, his strength is in his loins, And his force is in the muscles of his belly.
texts.job.40.17: He moveth his tail like a cedar: The sinews of his thighs are knit together.
texts.job.40.18: His bones are [as] tubes of brass; His limbs are like bars of iron.
texts.job.40.19: He is the chief of the ways of God: He [only] that made him giveth him his sword.
texts.job.40.20: Surely the mountains bring him forth food, Where all the beasts of the field do play.
texts.job.40.21: He lieth under the lotus-trees, In the covert of the reed, and the fen.
texts.job.40.22: The lotus-trees cover him with their shade; The willows of the brook compass him about.
texts.job.40.23: Behold, if a river overflow, he trembleth not; He is confident, though a Jordan swell even to his mouth.
texts.job.40.24: Shall any take him when he is on the watch, Or pierce through his nose with a snare?
texts.job.41.1: Canst thou draw out leviathan with a fishhook? Or press down his tongue with a cord?
texts.job.41.2: Canst thou put a rope into his nose? Or pierce his jaw through with a hook?
texts.job.41.3: Will he make many supplications unto thee? Or will he speak soft words unto thee?
texts.job.41.4: Will he make a covenant with thee, That thou shouldest take him for a servant for ever?
texts.job.41.5: Wilt thou play with him as with a bird? Or wilt thou bind him for thy maidens?
texts.job.41.6: Will the bands [of fishermen] make traffic of him? Will they part him among the merchants?
texts.job.41.7: Canst thou fill his skin with barbed irons, Or his head with fish-spears?
texts.job.41.8: Lay thy hand upon him; Remember the battle, and do so no more.
texts.job.41.9: Behold, the hope of him is in vain: Will not one be cast down even at the sight of him?
texts.job.41.10: None is so fierce that he dare stir him up; Who then is he that can stand before me?
texts.job.41.11: Who hath first given unto me, that I should repay him? [Whatsoever is] under the whole heaven is mine.
texts.job.41.12: I will not keep silence concerning his limbs, Nor his mighty strength, nor his goodly frame.
texts.job.41.13: Who can strip off his outer garment? Who shall come within his jaws?
texts.job.41.14: Who can open the doors of his face? Round about his teeth is terror.
texts.job.41.15: [His] strong scales are [his] pride, Shut up together [as with] a close seal.
texts.job.41.16: One is so near to another, That no air can come between them.
texts.job.41.17: They are joined one to another; They stick together, so that they cannot be sundered.
texts.job.41.18: His sneezings flash forth light, And his eyes are like the eyelids of the morning.
texts.job.41.19: Out of his mouth go burning torches, And sparks of fire leap forth.
texts.job.41.20: Out of his nostrils a smoke goeth, As of a boiling pot and [burning] rushes.
texts.job.41.21: His breath kindleth coals, And a flame goeth forth from his mouth.
texts.job.41.22: In his neck abideth strength, And terror danceth before him.
texts.job.41.23: The flakes of his flesh are joined together: They are firm upon him; they cannot be moved.
texts.job.41.24: His heart is as firm as a stone; Yea, firm as the nether millstone.
texts.job.41.25: When he raiseth himself up, the mighty are afraid: By reason of consternation they are beside themselves.
texts.job.41.26: If one lay at him with the sword, it cannot avail; Nor the spear, the dart, nor the pointed shaft.
texts.job.41.27: He counteth iron as straw, [And] brass as rotten wood.
texts.job.41.28: The arrow cannot make him flee: Sling-stones are turned with him into stubble.
texts.job.41.29: Clubs are counted as stubble: He laugheth at the rushing of the javelin.
texts.job.41.30: His underparts are [like] sharp potsherds: He spreadeth [as it were] a threshing-wain upon the mire.
texts.job.41.31: He maketh the deep to boil like a pot: He maketh the sea like a pot of ointment.
texts.job.41.32: He maketh a path to shine after him; One would think the deep to be hoary.
texts.job.41.33: Upon earth there is not his like, That is made without fear.
texts.job.41.34: He beholdeth everything that is high: He is king over all the sons of pride.
texts.job.42.1: Then Job answered Jehovah, and said,
texts.job.42.2: I know that thou canst do all things, And that no purpose of thine can be restrained.
texts.job.42.3: Who is this that hideth counsel without knowledge? Therefore have I uttered that which I understood not, Things too wonderful for me, which I knew not.
texts.job.42.4: Hear, I beseech thee, and I will speak; I will demand of thee, and declare thou unto me.
texts.job.42.5: I had heard of thee by the hearing of the ear; But now mine eye seeth thee:
texts.job.42.6: Wherefore I abhor [myself], And repent in dust and ashes.
texts.job.42.7: And it was so, that, after Jehovah had spoken these words unto Job, Jehovah said to Eliphaz the Temanite, My wrath is kindled against thee, and against thy two friends; for ye have not spoken of me the thing that is right, as my servant Job hath.
texts.job.42.8: Now therefore, take unto you seven bullocks and seven rams, and go to my servant Job, and offer up for yourselves a burnt-offering; and my servant Job shall pray for you; for him will I accept, that I deal not with you after your folly; for ye have not spoken of me the thing that is right, as my servant Job hath.
texts.job.42.9: So Eliphaz the Temanite and Bildad the Shuhite and Zophar the Naamathite went, and did according as Jehovah commanded them: and Jehovah accepted Job.
texts.job.42.10: And Jehovah turned the captivity of Job, when he prayed for his friends: and Jehovah gave Job twice as much as he had before.
texts.job.42.11: Then came there unto him all his brethren, and all his sisters, and all they that had been of his acquaintance before, and did eat bread with him in his house: and they bemoaned him, and comforted him concerning all the evil that Jehovah had brought upon him: every man also gave him a piece of money, and every one a ring of gold.
texts.job.42.12: So Jehovah blessed the latter end of Job more than his beginning: And he had fourteen thousand sheep, and six thousand camels, and a thousand yoke of oxen, and a thousand she-asses.
texts.job.42.13: He had also seven sons and three daughters.
texts.job.42.14: And he called the name of the first, Jemimah: and the name of the second, Keziah; and the name of the third, Keren-happuch.
texts.job.42.15: And in all the land were no women found so fair as the daughters of Job: and their father gave them inheritance among their brethren.
texts.job.42.16: And after this Job lived a hundred and forty years, and saw his sons, and his sons' sons, [even] four generations.
texts.job.42.17: So Job died, being old and full of days.

texts.job.1.1: Il y avait dans le pays d'Uts un homme qui s'appelait Job. Et cet homme était intègre et droit; il craignait Dieu, et se détournait du mal.
texts.job.1.2: Il lui naquit sept fils et trois filles.
texts.job.1.3: Il possédait sept mille brebis, trois mille chameaux, cinq cents paires de boeufs, cinq cents ânesses, et un très grand nombre de serviteurs. Et cet homme était le plus considérable de tous les fils de l'Orient.
texts.job.1.4: Ses fils allaient les uns chez les autres et donnaient tour à tour un festin, et ils invitaient leurs trois soeurs à manger et à boire avec eux.
texts.job.1.5: Et quand les jours de festin étaient passés, Job appelait et sanctifiait ses fils, puis il se levait de bon matin et offrait pour chacun d'eux un holocauste; car Job disait: Peut-être mes fils ont-ils péché et ont-ils offensé Dieu dans leur coeur. C'est ainsi que Job avait coutume d'agir.
texts.job.1.6: Or, les fils de Dieu vinrent un jour se présenter devant l'Eternel, et Satan vint aussi au milieu d'eux.
texts.job.1.7: L'Eternel dit à Satan: D'où viens-tu? Et Satan répondit à l'Eternel: De parcourir la terre et de m'y promener.
texts.job.1.8: L'Eternel dit à Satan: As-tu remarqué mon serviteur Job? Il n'y a personne comme lui sur la terre; c'est un homme intègre et droit, craignant Dieu, et se détournant du mal.
texts.job.1.9: Et Satan répondit à l'Eternel: Est-ce d'une manière désintéressée que Job craint Dieu?
texts.job.1.10: Ne l'as-tu pas protégé, lui, sa maison, et tout ce qui est à lui? Tu as béni l'oeuvre de ses mains, et ses troupeaux couvrent le pays.
texts.job.1.11: Mais étends ta main, touche à tout ce qui lui appartient, et je suis sûr qu'il te maudit en face.
texts.job.1.12: L'Eternel dit à Satan: Voici, tout ce qui lui appartient, je te le livre; seulement, ne porte pas la main sur lui. Et Satan se retira de devant la face de l'Eternel.
texts.job.1.13: Un jour que les fils et les filles de Job mangeaient et buvaient du vin dans la maison de leur frère aîné,
texts.job.1.14: il arriva auprès de Job un messager qui dit: Les boeufs labouraient et les ânesses paissaient à côté d'eux;
texts.job.1.15: des Sabéens se sont jetés dessus, les ont enlevés, et ont passé les serviteurs au fil de l'épée. Et je me suis échappé moi seul, pour t'en apporter la nouvelle.
texts.job.1.16: Il parlait encore, lorsqu'un autre vint et dit: Le feu de Dieu est tombé du ciel, a embrasé les brebis et les serviteurs, et les a consumés. Et je me suis échappé moi seul, pour t'en apporter la nouvelle.
texts.job.1.17: Il parlait encore, lorsqu'un autre vint et dit: Des Chaldéens, formés en trois bandes, se sont jetés sur les chameaux, les ont enlevés, et ont passé les serviteurs au fil de l'épée. Et je me suis échappé moi seul, pour t'en apporter la nouvelle.
texts.job.1.18: Il parlait encore, lorsqu'un autre vint et dit: Tes fils et tes filles mangeaient et buvaient du vin dans la maison de leur frère aîné;
texts.job.1.19: et voici, un grand vent est venu de l'autre côté du désert, et a frappé contre les quatre coins de la maison; elle s'est écroulée sur les jeunes gens, et ils sont morts. Et je me suis échappé moi seul, pour t'en apporter la nouvelle.
texts.job.1.20: Alors Job se leva, déchira son manteau, et se rasa la tête; puis, se jetant par terre, il se prosterna,
texts.job.1.21: et dit: Je suis sorti nu du sein de ma mère, et nu je retournerai dans le sein de la terre. L'Eternel a donné, et l'Eternel a ôté; que le nom de l'Eternel soit béni!
texts.job.1.22: En tout cela, Job ne pécha point et n'attribua rien d'injuste à Dieu.
texts.job.2.1: Or, les fils de Dieu vinrent un jour se présenter devant l'Eternel, et Satan vint aussi au milieu d'eux se présenter devant l'Eternel.
texts.job.2.2: L'Eternel dit à Satan: D'où viens-tu? Et Satan répondit à l'Eternel: De parcourir la terre et de m'y promener.
texts.job.2.3: L'Eternel dit à Satan: As-tu remarqué mon serviteur Job? Il n'y a personne comme lui sur la terre; c'est un homme intègre et droit, craignant Dieu, et se détournant du mal. Il demeure ferme dans son intégrité, et tu m'excites à le perdre sans motif.
texts.job.2.4: Et Satan répondit à l'Eternel: Peau pour peau! tout ce que possède un homme, il le donne pour sa vie.
texts.job.2.5: Mais étends ta main, touche à ses os et à sa chair, et je suis sûr qu'il te maudit en face.
texts.job.2.6: L'Eternel dit à Satan: Voici, je te le livre: seulement, épargne sa vie.
texts.job.2.7: Et Satan se retira de devant la face de l'Eternel. Puis il frappa Job d'un ulcère malin, depuis la plante du pied jusqu'au sommet de la tête.
texts.job.2.8: Et Job prit un tesson pour se gratter et s'assit sur la cendre.
texts.job.2.9: Sa femme lui dit: Tu demeures ferme dans ton intégrité! Maudis Dieu, et meurs!
texts.job.2.10: Mais Job lui répondit: Tu parles comme une femme insensée. Quoi! nous recevons de Dieu le bien, et nous ne recevrions pas aussi le mal! En tout cela Job ne pécha point par ses lèvres.
texts.job.2.11: Trois amis de Job, Eliphaz de Théman, Bildad de Schuach, et Tsophar de Naama, apprirent tous les malheurs qui lui étaient arrivés. Ils se concertèrent et partirent de chez eux pour aller le plaindre et le consoler!
texts.job.2.12: Ayant de loin porté les regards sur lui, ils ne le reconnurent pas, et ils élevèrent la voix et pleurèrent. Ils déchirèrent leurs manteaux, et ils jetèrent de la poussière en l'air au-dessus de leur tête.
texts.job.2.13: Et ils se tinrent assis à terre auprès de lui sept jours et sept nuits, sans lui dire une parole, car ils voyaient combien sa douleur était grande.
texts.job.3.1: Après cela, Job ouvrit la bouche et maudit le jour de sa naissance.
texts.job.3.2: Il prit la parole et dit:
texts.job.3.3: Périsse le jour où je suis né, Et la nuit qui dit: Un enfant mâle est conçu!
texts.job.3.4: Ce jour! qu'il se change en ténèbres, Que Dieu n'en ait point souci dans le ciel, Et que la lumière ne rayonne plus sur lui!
texts.job.3.5: Que l'obscurité et l'ombre de la mort s'en emparent, Que des nuées établissent leur demeure au-dessus de lui, Et que de noirs phénomènes l'épouvantent!
texts.job.3.6: Cette nuit! que les ténèbres en fassent leur proie, Qu'elle disparaisse de l'année, Qu'elle ne soit plus comptée parmi les mois!
texts.job.3.7: Que cette nuit devienne stérile, Que l'allégresse en soit bannie!
texts.job.3.8: Qu'elle soit maudite par ceux qui maudissent les jours, Par ceux qui savent exciter le léviathan!
texts.job.3.9: Que les étoiles de son crépuscule s'obscurcissent, Qu'elle attende en vain la lumière, Et qu'elle ne voie point les paupières de l'aurore!
texts.job.3.10: Car elle n'a pas fermé le sein qui me conçut, Ni dérobé la souffrance à mes regards.
texts.job.3.11: Pourquoi ne suis-je pas mort dans le ventre de ma mère? Pourquoi n'ai-je pas expiré au sortir de ses entrailles?
texts.job.3.12: Pourquoi ai-je trouvé des genoux pour me recevoir, Et des mamelles pour m'allaiter?
texts.job.3.13: Je serais couché maintenant, je serais tranquille, Je dormirais, je reposerais,
texts.job.3.14: Avec les rois et les grands de la terre, Qui se bâtirent des mausolées,
texts.job.3.15: Avec les princes qui avaient de l'or, Et qui remplirent d'argent leurs demeures.
texts.job.3.16: Ou je n'existerais pas, je serais comme un avorton caché, Comme des enfants qui n'ont pas vu la lumière.
texts.job.3.17: Là ne s'agitent plus les méchants, Et là se reposent ceux qui sont fatigués et sans force;
texts.job.3.18: Les captifs sont tous en paix, Ils n'entendent pas la voix de l'oppresseur;
texts.job.3.19: Le petit et le grand sont là, Et l'esclave n'est plus soumis à son maître.
texts.job.3.20: Pourquoi donne-t-il la lumière à celui qui souffre, Et la vie à ceux qui ont l'amertume dans l'âme,
texts.job.3.21: Qui espèrent en vain la mort, Et qui la convoitent plus qu'un trésor,
texts.job.3.22: Qui seraient transportés de joie Et saisis d'allégresse, s'ils trouvaient le tombeau?
texts.job.3.23: A l'homme qui ne sait où aller, Et que Dieu cerne de toutes parts?
texts.job.3.24: Mes soupirs sont ma nourriture, Et mes cris se répandent comme l'eau.
texts.job.3.25: Ce que je crains, c'est ce qui m'arrive; Ce que je redoute, c'est ce qui m'atteint.
texts.job.3.26: Je n'ai ni tranquillité, ni paix, ni repos, Et le trouble s'est emparé de moi.
texts.job.4.1: Eliphaz de Théman prit la parole et dit:
texts.job.4.2: Si nous osons ouvrir la bouche, en seras-tu peiné? Mais qui pourrait garder le silence?
texts.job.4.3: Voici, tu as souvent enseigné les autres, Tu as fortifié les mains languissantes,
texts.job.4.4: Tes paroles ont relevé ceux qui chancelaient, Tu as affermi les genoux qui pliaient.
texts.job.4.5: Et maintenant qu'il s'agit de toi, tu faiblis! Maintenant que tu es atteint, tu te troubles!
texts.job.4.6: Ta crainte de Dieu n'est-elle pas ton soutien? Ton espérance, n'est-ce pas ton intégrité?
texts.job.4.7: Cherche dans ton souvenir: quel est l'innocent qui a péri? Quels sont les justes qui ont été exterminés?
texts.job.4.8: Pour moi, je l'ai vu, ceux qui labourent l'iniquité Et qui sèment l'injustice en moissonnent les fruits;
texts.job.4.9: Ils périssent par le souffle de Dieu, Ils sont consumés par le vent de sa colère,
texts.job.4.10: Le rugissement des lions prend fin, Les dents des lionceaux sont brisées;
texts.job.4.11: Le lion périt faute de proie, Et les petits de la lionne se dispersent.
texts.job.4.12: Une parole est arrivée furtivement jusqu'à moi, Et mon oreille en a recueilli les sons légers.
texts.job.4.13: Au moment où les visions de la nuit agitent la pensée, Quand les hommes sont livrés à un profond sommeil,
texts.job.4.14: Je fus saisi de frayeur et d'épouvante, Et tous mes os tremblèrent.
texts.job.4.15: Un esprit passa près de moi.... Tous mes cheveux se hérissèrent....
texts.job.4.16: Une figure d'un aspect inconnu était devant mes yeux, Et j'entendis une voix qui murmurait doucement:
texts.job.4.17: L'homme serait-il juste devant Dieu? Serait-il pur devant celui qui l'a fait?
texts.job.4.18: Si Dieu n'a pas confiance en ses serviteurs, S'il trouve de la folie chez ses anges,
texts.job.4.19: Combien plus chez ceux qui habitent des maisons d'argile, Qui tirent leur origine de la poussière, Et qui peuvent être écrasés comme un vermisseau!
texts.job.4.20: Du matin au soir ils sont brisés, Ils périssent pour toujours, et nul n'y prend garde;
texts.job.4.21: Le fil de leur vie est coupé, Ils meurent, et ils n'ont pas acquis la sagesse.
texts.job.5.1: Crie maintenant! Qui te répondra? Auquel des saints t'adresseras-tu?
texts.job.5.2: L'insensé périt dans sa colère, Le fou meurt dans ses emportements.
texts.job.5.3: J'ai vu l'insensé prendre racine; Puis soudain j'ai maudit sa demeure.
texts.job.5.4: Plus de prospérité pour ses fils; Ils sont foulés à la porte, et personne qui les délivre!
texts.job.5.5: Sa moisson est dévorée par des affamés, Qui viennent l'enlever jusque dans les épines, Et ses biens sont engloutis par des hommes altérés.
texts.job.5.6: Le malheur ne sort pas de la poussière, Et la souffrance ne germe pas du sol;
texts.job.5.7: L'homme naît pour souffrir, Comme l'étincelle pour voler.
texts.job.5.8: Pour moi, j'aurais recours à Dieu, Et c'est à Dieu que j'exposerais ma cause.
texts.job.5.9: Il fait des choses grandes et insondables, Des merveilles sans nombre;
texts.job.5.10: Il répand la pluie sur la terre, Et envoie l'eau sur les campagnes;
texts.job.5.11: Il relève les humbles, Et délivre les affligés;
texts.job.5.12: Il anéantit les projets des hommes rusés, Et leurs mains ne peuvent les accomplir;
texts.job.5.13: Il prend les sages dans leur propre ruse, Et les desseins des hommes artificieux sont renversés:
texts.job.5.14: Ils rencontrent les ténèbres au milieu du jour, Ils tâtonnent en plein midi comme dans la nuit.
texts.job.5.15: Ainsi Dieu protège le faible contre leurs menaces, Et le sauve de la main des puissants;
texts.job.5.16: Et l'espérance soutient le malheureux, Mais l'iniquité ferme la bouche.
texts.job.5.17: Heureux l'homme que Dieu châtie! Ne méprise pas la correction du Tout-Puissant.
texts.job.5.18: Il fait la plaie, et il la bande; Il blesse, et sa main guérit.
texts.job.5.19: Six fois il te délivrera de l'angoisse, Et sept fois le mal ne t'atteindra pas.
texts.job.5.20: Il te sauvera de la mort pendant la famine, Et des coups du glaive pendant la guerre.
texts.job.5.21: Tu seras à l'abri du fléau de la langue, Tu seras sans crainte quand viendra la dévastation.
texts.job.5.22: Tu te riras de la dévastation comme de la famine, Et tu n'auras pas à redouter les bêtes de la terre;
texts.job.5.23: Car tu feras alliance avec les pierres des champs, Et les bêtes de la terre seront en paix avec toi.
texts.job.5.24: Tu jouiras du bonheur sous ta tente, Tu retrouveras tes troupeaux au complet,
texts.job.5.25: Tu verras ta postérité s'accroître, Et tes rejetons se multiplier comme l'herbe des champs.
texts.job.5.26: Tu entreras au sépulcre dans la vieillesse, Comme on emporte une gerbe en son temps.
texts.job.5.27: Voilà ce que nous avons reconnu, voilà ce qui est; A toi d'entendre et de mettre à profit.
texts.job.6.1: Job prit la parole et dit:
texts.job.6.2: Oh! s'il était possible de peser ma douleur, Et si toutes mes calamités étaient sur la balance,
texts.job.6.3: Elles seraient plus pesantes que le sable de la mer; Voilà pourquoi mes paroles vont jusqu'à la folie!
texts.job.6.4: Car les flèches du Tout-Puissant m'ont percé, Et mon âme en suce le venin; Les terreurs de Dieu se rangent en bataille contre moi.
texts.job.6.5: L'âne sauvage crie-t-il auprès de l'herbe tendre? Le boeuf mugit-il auprès de son fourrage?
texts.job.6.6: Peut-on manger ce qui est fade et sans sel? Y a-t-il de la saveur dans le blanc d'un oeuf?
texts.job.6.7: Ce que je voudrais ne pas toucher, C'est là ma nourriture, si dégoûtante soit-elle!
texts.job.6.8: Puisse mon voeu s'accomplir, Et Dieu veuille réaliser mon espérance!
texts.job.6.9: Qu'il plaise à Dieu de m'écraser, Qu'il étende sa main et qu'il m'achève!
texts.job.6.10: Il me restera du moins une consolation, Une joie dans les maux dont il m'accable: Jamais je n'ai transgressé les ordres du Saint.
texts.job.6.11: Pourquoi espérer quand je n'ai plus de force? Pourquoi attendre quand ma fin est certaine?
texts.job.6.12: Ma force est-elle une force de pierre? Mon corps est-il d'airain?
texts.job.6.13: Ne suis-je pas sans ressource, Et le salut n'est-il pas loin de moi?
texts.job.6.14: Celui qui souffre a droit à la compassion de son ami, Même quand il abandonnerait la crainte du Tout-Puissant.
texts.job.6.15: Mes frères sont perfides comme un torrent, Comme le lit des torrents qui disparaissent.
texts.job.6.16: Les glaçons en troublent le cours, La neige s'y précipite;
texts.job.6.17: Viennent les chaleurs, et ils tarissent, Les feux du soleil, et leur lit demeure à sec.
texts.job.6.18: Les caravanes se détournent de leur chemin, S'enfoncent dans le désert, et périssent.
texts.job.6.19: Les caravanes de Théma fixent le regard, Les voyageurs de Séba sont pleins d'espoir;
texts.job.6.20: Ils sont honteux d'avoir eu confiance, Ils restent confondus quand ils arrivent.
texts.job.6.21: Ainsi, vous êtes comme si vous n'existiez pas; Vous voyez mon angoisse, et vous en avez horreur!
texts.job.6.22: Vous ai-je dit: Donnez-moi quelque chose, Faites en ma faveur des présents avec vos biens,
texts.job.6.23: Délivrez-moi de la main de l'ennemi, Rachetez-moi de la main des méchants?
texts.job.6.24: Instruisez-moi, et je me tairai; Faites-moi comprendre en quoi j'ai péché.
texts.job.6.25: Que les paroles vraies sont persuasives! Mais que prouvent vos remontrances?
texts.job.6.26: Voulez-vous donc blâmer ce que j'ai dit, Et ne voir que du vent dans les discours d'un désespéré?
texts.job.6.27: Vous accablez un orphelin, Vous persécutez votre ami.
texts.job.6.28: Regardez-moi, je vous prie! Vous mentirais-je en face?
texts.job.6.29: Revenez, ne soyez pas injustes; Revenez, et reconnaissez mon innocence.
texts.job.6.30: Y a-t-il de l'iniquité sur ma langue, Et ma bouche ne discerne-t-elle pas le mal?
texts.job.7.1: Le sort de l'homme sur la terre est celui d'un soldat, Et ses jours sont ceux d'un mercenaire.
texts.job.7.2: Comme l'esclave soupire après l'ombre, Comme l'ouvrier attend son salaire,
texts.job.7.3: Ainsi j'ai pour partage des mois de douleur, J'ai pour mon lot des nuits de souffrance.
texts.job.7.4: Je me couche, et je dis: Quand me lèverai-je? quand finira la nuit? Et je suis rassasié d'agitations jusqu'au point du jour.
texts.job.7.5: Mon corps se couvre de vers et d'une croûte terreuse, Ma peau se crevasse et se dissout.
texts.job.7.6: Mes jours sont plus rapides que la navette du tisserand, Ils s'évanouissent: plus d'espérance!
texts.job.7.7: Souviens-toi que ma vie est un souffle! Mes yeux ne reverront pas le bonheur.
texts.job.7.8: L'oeil qui me regarde ne me regardera plus; Ton oeil me cherchera, et je ne serai plus.
texts.job.7.9: Comme la nuée se dissipe et s'en va, Celui qui descend au séjour des morts ne remontera pas;
texts.job.7.10: Il ne reviendra plus dans sa maison, Et le lieu qu'il habitait ne le connaîtra plus.
texts.job.7.11: C'est pourquoi je ne retiendrai point ma bouche, Je parlerai dans l'angoisse de mon coeur, Je me plaindrai dans l'amertume de mon âme.
texts.job.7.12: Suis-je une mer, ou un monstre marin, Pour que tu établisses des gardes autour de moi?
texts.job.7.13: Quand je dis: Mon lit me soulagera, Ma couche calmera mes douleurs,
texts.job.7.14: C'est alors que tu m'effraies par des songes, Que tu m'épouvantes par des visions.
texts.job.7.15: Ah! je voudrais être étranglé! Je voudrais la mort plutôt que ces os!
texts.job.7.16: Je les méprise!... je ne vivrai pas toujours... Laisse-moi, car ma vie n'est qu'un souffle.
texts.job.7.17: Qu'est-ce que l'homme, pour que tu en fasses tant de cas, Pour que tu daignes prendre garde à lui,
texts.job.7.18: Pour que tu le visites tous les matins, Pour que tu l'éprouves à tous les instants?
texts.job.7.19: Quand cesseras-tu d'avoir le regard sur moi? Quand me laisseras-tu le temps d'avaler ma salive?
texts.job.7.20: Si j'ai péché, qu'ai-je pu te faire, gardien des hommes? Pourquoi me mettre en butte à tes traits? Pourquoi me rendre à charge à moi-même?
texts.job.7.21: Que ne pardonnes-tu mon péché, Et que n'oublies-tu mon iniquité? Car je vais me coucher dans la poussière; Tu me chercheras, et je ne serai plus.
texts.job.8.1: Bildad de Schuach prit la parole et dit:
texts.job.8.2: Jusqu'à quand veux-tu discourir de la sorte, Et les paroles de ta bouche seront-elles un vent impétueux?
texts.job.8.3: Dieu renverserait-il le droit? Le Tout-Puissant renverserait-il la justice?
texts.job.8.4: Si tes fils ont péché contre lui, Il les a livrés à leur péché.
texts.job.8.5: Mais toi, si tu as recours à Dieu, Si tu implores le Tout-Puissant;
texts.job.8.6: Si tu es juste et droit, Certainement alors il veillera sur toi, Et rendra le bonheur à ton innocente demeure;
texts.job.8.7: Ton ancienne prospérité semblera peu de chose, Celle qui t'est réservée sera bien plus grande.
texts.job.8.8: Interroge ceux des générations passées, Sois attentif à l'expérience de leurs pères.
texts.job.8.9: Car nous sommes d'hier, et nous ne savons rien, Nos jours sur la terre ne sont qu'une ombre.
texts.job.8.10: Ils t'instruiront, ils te parleront, Ils tireront de leur coeur ces sentences:
texts.job.8.11: Le jonc croît-il sans marais? Le roseau croît-il sans humidité?
texts.job.8.12: Encore vert et sans qu'on le coupe, Il sèche plus vite que toutes les herbes.
texts.job.8.13: Ainsi arrive-t-il à tous ceux qui oublient Dieu, Et l'espérance de l'impie périra.
texts.job.8.14: Son assurance est brisée, Son soutien est une toile d'araignée.
texts.job.8.15: Il s'appuie sur sa maison, et elle n'est pas ferme; Il s'y cramponne, et elle ne résiste pas.
texts.job.8.16: Dans toute sa vigueur, en plein soleil, Il étend ses rameaux sur son jardin,
texts.job.8.17: Il entrelace ses racines parmi les pierres, Il pénètre jusque dans les murailles;
texts.job.8.18: L'arrache-t-on du lieu qu'il occupe, Ce lieu le renie: Je ne t'ai point connu!
texts.job.8.19: Telles sont les délices que ses voies lui procurent. Puis sur le même sol d'autres s'élèvent après lui.
texts.job.8.20: Non, Dieu ne rejette point l'homme intègre, Et il ne protège point les méchants.
texts.job.8.21: Il remplira ta bouche de cris de joie, Et tes lèvres de chants d'allégresse.
texts.job.8.22: Tes ennemis seront couverts de honte; La tente des méchants disparaîtra.
texts.job.9.1: Job prit la parole et dit:
texts.job.9.2: Je sais bien qu'il en est ainsi; Comment l'homme serait-il juste devant Dieu?
texts.job.9.3: S'il voulait contester avec lui, Sur mille choses il ne pourrait répondre à une seule.
texts.job.9.4: A lui la sagesse et la toute-puissance: Qui lui résisterait impunément?
texts.job.9.5: Il transporte soudain les montagnes, Il les renverse dans sa colère.
texts.job.9.6: Il secoue la terre sur sa base, Et ses colonnes sont ébranlées.
texts.job.9.7: Il commande au soleil, et le soleil ne paraît pas; Il met un sceau sur les étoiles.
texts.job.9.8: Seul, il étend les cieux, Il marche sur les hauteurs de la mer.
texts.job.9.9: Il a créé la Grande Ourse, l'Orion et les Pléiades, Et les étoiles des régions australes.
texts.job.9.10: Il fait des choses grandes et insondables, Des merveilles sans nombre.
texts.job.9.11: Voici, il passe près de moi, et je ne le vois pas, Il s'en va, et je ne l'aperçois pas.
texts.job.9.12: S'il enlève, qui s'y opposera? Qui lui dira: Que fais-tu?
texts.job.9.13: Dieu ne retire point sa colère; Sous lui s'inclinent les appuis de l'orgueil.
texts.job.9.14: Et moi, comment lui répondre? Quelles paroles choisir?
texts.job.9.15: Quand je serais juste, je ne répondrais pas; Je ne puis qu'implorer mon juge.
texts.job.9.16: Et quand il m'exaucerait, si je l'invoque, Je ne croirais pas qu'il eût écouté ma voix,
texts.job.9.17: Lui qui m'assaille comme par une tempête, Qui multiplie sans raison mes blessures,
texts.job.9.18: Qui ne me laisse pas respirer, Qui me rassasie d'amertume.
texts.job.9.19: Recourir à la force? Il est tout-puissant. A la justice? Qui me fera comparaître?
texts.job.9.20: Suis-je juste, ma bouche me condamnera; Suis-je innocent, il me déclarera coupable.
texts.job.9.21: Innocent! Je le suis; mais je ne tiens pas à la vie, Je méprise mon existence.
texts.job.9.22: Qu'importe après tout? Car, j'ose le dire, Il détruit l'innocent comme le coupable.
texts.job.9.23: Si du moins le fléau donnait soudain la mort!... Mais il se rit des épreuves de l'innocent.
texts.job.9.24: La terre est livrée aux mains de l'impie; Il voile la face des juges. Si ce n'est pas lui, qui est-ce donc?
texts.job.9.25: Mes jours sont plus rapides qu'un courrier; Ils fuient sans avoir vu le bonheur;
texts.job.9.26: Ils passent comme les navires de jonc, Comme l'aigle qui fond sur sa proie.
texts.job.9.27: Si je dis: Je veux oublier mes souffrances, Laisser ma tristesse, reprendre courage,
texts.job.9.28: Je suis effrayé de toutes mes douleurs. Je sais que tu ne me tiendras pas pour innocent.
texts.job.9.29: Je serai jugé coupable; Pourquoi me fatiguer en vain?
