texts.job.31.3: Is not destruction to the wicked? and a strange punishment to the workers of iniquity?
texts.job.31.4: Doth not he see my ways, and count all my steps?
texts.job.31.5: If I have walked with vanity, or if my foot hath hasted to deceit;
texts.job.31.6: Let me be weighed in an even balance, that God may know my integrity.
texts.job.31.7: If my step hath turned out of the way, and my heart walked after my eyes, and if any blot hath cleaved to my hands;
texts.job.31.8: Then let me sow, and let another eat; yes, let my offspring be rooted out.
texts.job.31.9: If my heart hath been deceived by a woman, or if I have laid wait at my neighbor's door;
texts.job.31.10: Then let my wife grind to another, and let others bow down upon her.
texts.job.31.11: For this is a hainous crime; yea, it is an iniquity to be punished by the judges.
texts.job.31.12: For it is a fire that consumeth to destruction, and would root out all my increase.
texts.job.31.13: If I despised the cause of my man-servant or of my maid-servant, when they contended with me;
texts.job.31.14: What then shall I do when God riseth up? and when he visiteth, what shall I answer him?
texts.job.31.15: Did not he that made me in the womb make him? and did not one fashion us in the womb?
texts.job.31.16: If I have withheld the poor from their desire, or have caused the eyes of the widow to fail;
texts.job.31.17: Or have eaten my morsel myself alone, and the fatherless hath not eaten of it;
texts.job.31.18: (For from my youth he was brought up with me, as with a father, and I have guided her from my mother's womb;)
texts.job.31.19: If I have seen any perish for want of clothing, or any poor without covering;
texts.job.31.20: If his loins have not blessed me, and if he hath not been warmed with the fleece of my sheep;
texts.job.31.21: If I have lifted up my hand against the fatherless, when I saw my help in the gate:
texts.job.31.22: Then let my arm fall from my shoulder-blade, and my arm be broken from the bone.
texts.job.31.23: For destruction from God was a terror to me, and by reason of his highness I could not endure.
texts.job.31.24: If I have made gold my hope, or have said to the fine gold, Thou art my confidence;
texts.job.31.25: If I have rejoiced because my wealth was great, and because my hand had gained much;
texts.job.31.26: If I have beheld the sun when it shined, or the moon walking in brightness;
texts.job.31.27: And my heart hath been secretly enticed, or my mouth hath kissed my hand:
texts.job.31.28: This also were an iniquity to be punished by the judge: for I should have denied the God that is above.
texts.job.31.29: If I have rejoiced at the destruction of him that hated me, or have lifted up myself when evil found him:
texts.job.31.30: Neither have I suffered my mouth to sin by wishing a curse to his soul.
texts.job.31.31: If the men of my tabernacle have not said, Oh that we had of his flesh! we cannot be satisfied.
texts.job.31.32: The stranger did not lodge in the street: but I opened my doors to the traveler.
texts.job.31.33: If I have covered my transgressions as Adam, by hiding my iniquity in my bosom:
texts.job.31.34: Did I fear a great multitude, or did the contempt of families terrify me, that I kept silence, and went not out of the door?
texts.job.31.35: Oh that one would hear me! behold, my desire is, that the Almighty would answer me, and that my adversary had written a book.
texts.job.31.36: Surely I would take it upon my shoulder, and bind it as a crown to me.
texts.job.31.37: I would declare to him the number of my steps; as a prince would I go near to him.
texts.job.31.38: If my land crieth against me, or its furrows likewise complain;
texts.job.31.39: If I have eaten the fruits of it without money, or have caused its owners to lose their life:
texts.job.31.40: Let thistles grow instead of wheat, and cockle instead of barley. The words of Job are ended.
texts.job.32.1: So these three men ceased to answer Job, because he was righteous in his own eyes.
texts.job.32.2: Then was kindled the wrath of Elihu the son of Barachel the Buzite, of the kindred of Ram: against Job was his wrath kindled, because he justified himself rather than God.
texts.job.32.3: Also against his three friends was his wrath kindled, because they had found no answer, and yet had condemned Job.
texts.job.32.4: Now Elihu had waited till Job had spoken because they were older than he.
texts.job.32.5: When Elihu saw that there was no answer in the mouth of these three men, then his wrath was kindled.
texts.job.32.6: And Elihu the son of Barachel the Buzite answered and said, I am young, and ye are very old; wherefore I was afraid, and durst not show you my opinion.
texts.job.32.7: I said, Days should speak, and multitude of years should teach wisdom.
texts.job.32.8: But there is a spirit in man: and the inspiration of the Almighty giveth them understanding.
texts.job.32.9: Great men are not always wise: neither do the aged understand judgment.
texts.job.32.10: Therefore I said, Hearken to me; I also will show my opinion.
texts.job.32.11: Behold, I waited for your words; I gave ear to your reasons, whilst ye searched out what to say.
texts.job.32.12: Yes, I attended to you, and behold, there was none of you that convinced Job, or that answered his words:
texts.job.32.13: Lest ye should say, We have found out wisdom: God thrusteth him down, not man.
texts.job.32.14: Now he hath not directed his words against me: neither will I answer him with your speeches.
texts.job.32.15: They were amazed, they answered no more: they left off speaking.
texts.job.32.16: When I had waited, (for they spoke not, but stood still, and answered no more;)
texts.job.32.17: I said, I will answer also my part, I also will show my opinion.
texts.job.32.18: For I am full of matter, the spirit within me constraineth me.
texts.job.32.19: Behold, my belly is as wine which hath no vent; it is ready to burst like new bottles.
texts.job.32.20: I will speak, that I may be refreshed: I will open my lips and answer.
texts.job.32.21: Let me not, I pray you, accept any man's person, neither let me give flattering titles to man.
texts.job.32.22: For I know not to give flattering titles; in so doing, my Maker would soon take me away.
texts.job.33.1: Wherefore, Job, I pray thee, hear my speeches, and hearken to all my words.
texts.job.33.2: Behold, now I have opened my mouth, my tongue hath spoken in my mouth.
texts.job.33.3: My words shall be of the uprightness of my heart: and my lips shall utter knowledge clearly.
texts.job.33.4: The Spirit of God hath made me, and the breath of the Almighty hath given me life.
texts.job.33.5: If thou canst answer me, set thy words in order before me, stand up.
texts.job.33.6: Behold, I am according to thy wish in God's stead: I also am formed out of the clay.
texts.job.33.7: Behold, my terror shall not make thee afraid, neither shall my hand be heavy upon thee.
texts.job.33.8: Surely thou hast spoken in my hearing, and I have heard the voice of thy words, saying,
texts.job.33.9: I am clean without transgression, I am innocent; neither is there iniquity in me.
texts.job.33.10: Behold, he findeth occasions against me, he counteth me for his enemy,
texts.job.33.11: He putteth my feet in the stocks, he marketh all my paths.
texts.job.33.12: Behold, in this thou art not just: I will answer thee, that God is greater than man.
texts.job.33.13: Why dost thou strive against him? for he giveth not account of any of his matters.
texts.job.33.14: For God speaketh once, yes twice, yet man perceiveth it not.
texts.job.33.15: In a dream, in a vision of the night, when deep sleep falleth upon men, in slumberings upon the bed;
texts.job.33.16: Then he openeth the ears of men, and sealeth their instruction,
texts.job.33.17: That he may withdraw man from his purpose, and hide pride from man.
texts.job.33.18: He keepeth back his soul from the pit, and his life from perishing by the sword.
texts.job.33.19: He is chastened also with pain upon his bed, and the multitude of his bones with strong pain:
texts.job.33.20: So that his life abhorreth bread, and his soul dainty food.
texts.job.33.21: His flesh is consumed away, that it cannot be seen; and his bones that were not seen stick out.
texts.job.33.22: Yes, his soul draweth near to the grave, and his life to the destroyers.
texts.job.33.23: If there is a messenger with him, an interpreter, one among a thousand, to show to man his uprightness:
texts.job.33.24: Then he is gracious to him, and saith, Deliver him from going down to the pit: I have found a ransom.
texts.job.33.25: His flesh shall be fresher than a child's: he will return to the days of his youth:
texts.job.33.26: He shall pray to God, and he will be favorable to him: and he shall see his face with joy: for he will render to man his righteousness.
texts.job.33.27: He looketh upon men, and if any shall say, I have sinned, and perverted that which was right, and it profited me not;
texts.job.33.28: He will deliver his soul from going into the pit, and his life shall see the light.
texts.job.33.29: Lo, all these things God often worketh with man,
texts.job.33.30: To bring back his soul from the pit, to be enlightened with the light of the living.
texts.job.33.31: Mark well, O Job, hearken to me: hold thy peace, and I will speak.
texts.job.33.32: If thou hast any thing to say, answer me: speak, for I desire to justify thee.
texts.job.33.33: If not, hearken to me: hold thy peace, and I shall teach thee wisdom.
texts.job.34.2: Hear my words, O ye wise men; and give ear to me, ye that have knowledge.
texts.job.34.3: For the ear trieth words, as the mouth tasteth food.
texts.job.34.4: Let us choose to us judgment: let us know among ourselves what is good.
texts.job.34.5: For Job hath said, I am righteous: and God hath taken away my judgment.
texts.job.34.6: Should I lie against my right? my wound is incurable without transgression.
texts.job.34.7: What man is like Job, who drinketh up scorning like water?
texts.job.34.8: Who goeth in company with the workers of iniquity, and walketh with wicked men.
texts.job.34.9: For he hath said, It profiteth a man nothing that he should delight himself with God.
texts.job.34.10: Therefore hearken to me, ye men of understanding: far be it from God, that he should do wickedness; and from the Almighty, that he should commit iniquity.
texts.job.34.11: For the work of a man he shall render to him, and cause every man to find according to his ways.
texts.job.34.12: Yes, surely God will not do wickedly, neither will the Almighty pervert judgment.
texts.job.34.13: Who hath given him a charge over the earth? or who hath disposed the whole world?
texts.job.34.14: If he should set his heart upon man, if he should gather to himself his spirit and his breath;
texts.job.34.15: All flesh would perish together, and man would turn again to dust.
texts.job.34.16: If now thou hast understanding, hear this: hearken to the voice of my words.
texts.job.34.17: Shall even he that hateth right govern? and wilt thou condemn him that is most just?
texts.job.34.18: Is it fit to say to a king, Thou art wicked? and to princes, Ye are ungodly?
texts.job.34.19: How much less to him that accepteth not the persons of princes, nor regardeth the rich more than the poor? for they all are the work of his hands.
texts.job.34.20: In a moment they shall die, and the people shall be troubled at midnight, and pass away: and the mighty shall be taken away without hand.
texts.job.34.21: For his eyes are upon the ways of man, and he seeth all his goings.
texts.job.34.22: There is no darkness, nor shadow of death, where the workers of iniquity may hide themselves.
texts.job.34.23: For he will not lay upon man more than right; that he should enter into judgment with God.
texts.job.34.24: He shall break in pieces mighty men without number, and set others in their stead.
texts.job.34.25: Therefore he knoweth their works, and he overturneth them in the night, so that they are destroyed.
texts.job.34.26: He striketh them as wicked men in the open sight of others;
texts.job.34.27: Because they turned back from him, and would not consider any of his ways:
texts.job.34.28: So that they cause the cry of the poor to come to him, and he heareth the cry of the afflicted.
texts.job.34.29: When he giveth quietness, who then can make trouble? and when he hideth his face, who then can behold him? whether it be done against a nation, or against a man only:
texts.job.34.30: That the hypocrite may not reign, lest the people should be ensnared.
texts.job.34.31: Surely it is meet to be said to God, I have borne chastisement, I will not offend any more:
texts.job.34.32: That which I see not teach thou me: if I have done iniquity, I will do no more.
texts.job.34.33: Should it be according to thy mind? he will recompense it, whether thou shalt refuse, or whether thou shalt choose; and not I: therefore speak what thou knowest.
texts.job.34.34: Let men of understanding tell me, and let a wise man hearken to me.
texts.job.34.35: Job hath spoken without knowledge, and his words were without wisdom.
texts.job.34.36: My desire is that Job may be tried to the end, because of his answers for wicked men.
texts.job.34.37: For he addeth rebellion to his sin, he clappeth his hands among us, and multiplieth his words against God.
texts.job.35.2: Thinkest thou this to be right, that thou saidst, My righteousness is more than God's?
texts.job.35.3: For thou saidst, What advantage will it be to thee? and, What profit shall I have, if I be cleansed from my sin?
texts.job.35.4: I will answer thee, and thy companions with thee.
texts.job.35.5: Look to the heavens, and see; and behold the clouds which are higher than thou.
texts.job.35.6: If thou sinnest, what doest thou against him? or if thy transgressions are multiplied, what doest thou to him?
texts.job.35.7: If thou art righteous, what givest thou to him? or what receiveth he from thy hand?
texts.job.35.8: Thy wickedness may hurt a man as thou art: and thy righteousness may profit the son of man.
texts.job.35.9: By reason of the multitude of oppressions they make the oppressed to cry: they cry out by reason of the arm of the mighty.
texts.job.35.10: But none saith, Where is God my maker, who giveth songs in the night;
texts.job.35.11: Who teacheth us more than the beasts of the earth, and maketh us wiser than the fowls of heaven?
texts.job.35.12: There they cry, but none giveth answer, because of the pride of evil men.
texts.job.35.13: Surely God will not hear vanity, neither will the Almighty regard it.
texts.job.35.14: Although thou sayest thou shalt not see him, yet judgment is before him; therefore trust thou in him.
texts.job.35.15: But now, because it is not so, he hath visited in his anger; yet he knoweth it not in great extremity:
texts.job.35.16: Therefore doth Job open his mouth in vain; he multiplieth words without knowledge.
texts.job.36.2: Suffer me a little, and I will show thee that I have yet to speak on God's behalf.
texts.job.36.3: I will bring my knowledge from afar, and will ascribe righteousness to my Maker.
texts.job.36.4: For truly my words shall not be false: he that is perfect in knowledge is with thee.
texts.job.36.5: Behold, God is mighty, and despiseth not any: he is mighty in strength and wisdom.
texts.job.36.6: He preserveth not the life of the wicked: but giveth right to the poor.
texts.job.36.7: He withdraweth not his eyes from the righteous: but with kings are they on the throne; yes, he doth establish them for ever, and they are exalted.
texts.job.36.8: And if they are bound in fetters, and are held in cords of affliction;
texts.job.36.9: Then he showeth them their work, and their transgressions that they have exceeded.
texts.job.36.10: He openeth also their ear to discipline, and commandeth that they return from iniquity.
texts.job.36.11: If they obey and serve him, they shall spend their days in prosperity, and their years in pleasures.
texts.job.36.12: But if they obey not, they shall perish by the sword, and they shall die without knowledge.
texts.job.36.13: But the hypocrites in heart heap up wrath: they cry not when he bindeth them.
texts.job.36.14: They die in youth, and their life is among the unclean.
texts.job.36.15: He delivereth the poor in his affliction, and openeth their ears in oppression.
texts.job.36.16: Even so would he have removed thee out of the strait into a broad place, where there is no straitness; and that which should be set on thy table would be full of fatness.
texts.job.36.17: But thou hast fulfilled the judgment of the wicked: judgment and justice take hold on thee.
texts.job.36.18: Because there is wrath, beware lest he take thee away with his stroke: then a great ransom cannot deliver thee.
texts.job.36.19: Will he esteem thy riches? no, not gold, nor all the forces of strength.
texts.job.36.20: Desire not the night, when people are cut off in their place.
texts.job.36.21: Take heed, regard not iniquity: for this hast thou chosen rather than affliction.
texts.job.36.22: Behold, God exalteth by his power: who teacheth like him?
texts.job.36.23: Who hath enjoined him his way? or who can say, Thou hast wrought iniquity?
texts.job.36.24: Remember that thou magnify his work, which men behold.
texts.job.36.25: Every man may see it; man may behold it afar off.
texts.job.36.26: Behold, God is great, and we know him not, neither can the number of his years be searched out.
texts.job.36.27: For he maketh small the drops of water: they pour down rain according to the vapor of it.
texts.job.36.28: Which the clouds do drop and distill upon man abundantly.
texts.job.36.29: Also can any understand the spreadings of the clouds, or the noise of his tabernacle?
texts.job.36.30: Behold, he spreadeth his light upon it, and covereth the bottom of the sea.
texts.job.36.31: For by them he judgeth the people; he giveth food in abundance.
texts.job.36.32: With clouds he covereth the light; and commandeth it not to shine by the intervening cloud.
texts.job.36.33: The noise of it showeth concerning it, the cattle also concerning the vapor.
texts.job.37.1: At this also my heart trembleth, and is moved out of its place.
texts.job.37.2: Hear attentively the noise of his voice, and the sound that goeth out of his mouth.
texts.job.37.3: He directeth it under the whole heaven, and his lightning to the ends of the earth.
texts.job.37.4: After it a voice roareth: he thundereth with the voice of his excellence; and he will not stay them when his voice is heard.
texts.job.37.5: God thundereth marvelously with his voice; great things he doeth, which we cannot comprehend.
texts.job.37.6: For he saith to the snow, Be thou on the earth; likewise to the small rain, and to the great rain of his strength.
texts.job.37.7: He sealeth up the hand of every man; that all men may know his work.
texts.job.37.8: Then the beasts go into dens, and remain in their places.
texts.job.37.9: From the south cometh the whirlwind: and cold from the north.
texts.job.37.10: By the breath of God frost is given: and the breadth of the waters is straitened.
texts.job.37.11: Also by watering he wearieth the thick cloud: he scattereth his bright cloud:
texts.job.37.12: And it is turned around by his counsels: that they may do whatever he commandeth them upon the face of the world on the earth.
texts.job.37.13: He causeth it to come, whether for correction, or for his land, or for mercy.
texts.job.37.14: Hearken to this, O Job: stand still, and consider the wondrous works of God.
texts.job.37.15: Dost thou know when God disposed them, and caused the light of his cloud to shine?
texts.job.37.16: Dost thou know the balancings of the clouds, the wondrous works of him who is perfect in knowledge?
texts.job.37.17: How thy garments are warm, when he quieteth the earth by the south wind?
texts.job.37.18: Hast thou with him spread out the sky which is strong, and as a molten looking-glass?
texts.job.37.19: Teach us what we shall say to him; for we cannot order our speech by reason of darkness.
texts.job.37.20: Shall it be told him that I speak? If a man shall speak, surely he will be swallowed up.
texts.job.37.21: And now men see not the bright light which is in the clouds: but the wind passeth, and cleanseth them.
texts.job.37.22: Fair weather cometh from the north: with God is terrible majesty.
texts.job.37.23: Touching the Almighty, we cannot find him out: he is excellent in power, and in judgment, and in abundance of justice: he will not afflict.
texts.job.37.24: Men therefore fear him: he respecteth not any that are wise of heart.
texts.job.38.1: Then the LORD answered Job out of the whirlwind, and said,
texts.job.38.2: Who is this that darkeneth counsel by words without knowledge?
texts.job.38.3: Gird up now thy loins like a man; for I will demand of thee, and answer thou me.
texts.job.38.4: Where wast thou when I laid the foundations of the earth? declare, if thou hast understanding.
texts.job.38.5: Who hath laid the measures of it, if thou knowest? or who hath stretched the line upon it?
texts.job.38.6: Upon what are the foundations of it fastened? or who laid its corner stone;
texts.job.38.7: When the morning stars sang together, and all the sons of God shouted for joy?
texts.job.38.8: Or who shut up the sea with doors, when it broke forth, as if it had issued out of the womb?
texts.job.38.9: When I made a cloud its garment, and thick darkness a swaddling band for it,
texts.job.38.10: And broke up for it my decreed place, and set bars and doors,
texts.job.38.11: And said, Hitherto shalt thou come, but no further: and here shall thy proud waves be stayed.
texts.job.38.12: Hast thou commanded the morning since thy days; and caused the day-spring to know its place;
texts.job.38.13: That it might take hold of the ends of earth, that the wicked might be shaken out of it?
texts.job.38.14: It is turned as clay to the seal; and they stand as a garment.
texts.job.38.15: And from the wicked their light is withheld, and the high arm shall be broken.
texts.job.38.16: Hast thou entered into the springs of the sea? or hast thou walked in the search of the depth?
texts.job.38.17: Have the gates of death been opened to thee? or hast thou seen the doors of the shades of death?
texts.job.38.18: Hast thou perceived the breadth of the earth? declare if thou knowest it all.
texts.job.38.19: Where is the way where light dwelleth? and as for darkness, where is its place,
texts.job.38.20: That thou shouldest take it to its bound, and that thou shouldest know the paths to its house?
texts.job.38.21: Knowest thou it, because thou wast then born? or because the number of thy days is great?
texts.job.38.22: Hast thou entered into the treasures of the snow? or hast thou seen the treasures of the hail,
texts.job.38.23: Which I have reserved against the time of trouble, against the day of battle and war?
texts.job.38.24: By what way is the light parted, which scattereth the east wind upon the earth?
texts.job.38.25: Who hath divided a watercourse for the overflowing of waters, or a way for the lightning of thunder;
texts.job.38.26: To cause it to rain on the earth, where no man is; on the wilderness in which there is no man;
texts.job.38.27: To satisfy the desolate and waste ground; and to cause the bud of the tender herb to spring forth?
texts.job.38.28: Hath the rain a father? or who hath begotten the drops of the dew?
texts.job.38.29: Out of whose womb came the ice? and the hoary frost of heaven, who hath gendered it?
texts.job.38.30: The waters are hid as with a stone, and the face of the deep is frozen.
texts.job.38.31: Canst thou bind the sweet influences of Pleiades, or loose the bands of Orion?
texts.job.38.32: Canst thou bring forth Mazzaroth in its season? or canst thou guide Arcturus with its sons?
texts.job.38.33: Knowest thou the ordinances of heaven? canst thou set its dominion on the earth?
texts.job.38.34: Canst thou lift thy voice to the clouds, that abundance of waters may cover thee?
texts.job.38.35: Canst thou send lightnings, that they may go, and say to thee, Here we are?
texts.job.38.36: Who hath put wisdom in the inward parts? or who hath given understanding to the heart?
texts.job.38.37: Who can number the clouds in wisdom? or who can stay the bottles of heaven,
texts.job.38.38: When the dust groweth into hardness, and the clods cleave fast together?
texts.job.38.39: Wilt thou hunt the prey for the lion? or fill the appetite of the young lions,
texts.job.38.40: When they couch in their dens, and abide in the covert to lie in wait?
texts.job.38.41: Who provideth for the raven his food? when his young ones cry to God, they wander for want of food.
texts.job.39.1: Knowest thou the time when the wild goats of the rock bring forth? or canst thou mark when the hinds do calve?
texts.job.39.2: Canst thou number the months that they fulfill? or knowest thou the time when they bring forth?
texts.job.39.3: They bow themselves, they bring forth their young ones, they cast out their sorrows.
texts.job.39.4: Their young ones are in good liking, they grow up with corn; they go forth, and return not to them.
texts.job.39.5: Who hath sent out the wild ass free? or who hath loosed the bands of the wild ass?
texts.job.39.6: Whose house I have made the wilderness, and the barren land his dwellings.
texts.job.39.7: He scorneth the multitude of the city, neither regardeth he the crying of the driver.
texts.job.39.8: The range of the mountains is his pasture, and he searcheth after every green thing.
texts.job.39.9: Will the unicorn be willing to serve thee, or abide by thy crib?
texts.job.39.10: Canst thou bind the unicorn with his band in the furrow? or will he harrow the valleys after thee?
texts.job.39.11: Wilt thou trust him, because his strength is great? or wilt thou leave thy labor to him?
texts.job.39.12: Wilt thou believe him, that he will bring home thy seed, and gather it into thy barn?
texts.job.39.13: Gavest thou the goodly wings to the peacocks? or wings and feathers to the ostrich!
texts.job.39.14: Which leaveth her eggs in the earth, and warmeth them in the dust,
texts.job.39.15: And forgetteth that the foot may crush them, or that the wild beast may break them.
texts.job.39.16: She is hardened against her young ones, as though they were not hers: her labor is in vain without fear;
texts.job.39.17: Because God hath withheld wisdom from her, neither hath he imparted to her understanding.
texts.job.39.18: When she lifteth herself on high, she scorneth the horse and his rider.
texts.job.39.19: Hast thou given the horse strength? hast thou clothed his neck with thunder?
texts.job.39.20: Canst thou make him afraid as a grasshopper? the glory of his nostrils is terrible.
texts.job.39.21: He paweth in the valley, and rejoiceth in his strength: he goeth on to meet the armed men.
texts.job.39.22: He mocketh at fear, and is not affrighted; neither turneth he back from the sword.
texts.job.39.23: The quiver rattleth against him, the glittering spear and the shield.
texts.job.39.24: He swalloweth the ground with fierceness and rage: neither believeth he that it is the sound of the trumpet.
texts.job.39.25: He saith among the trumpets, Ha, ha; and he smelleth the battle afar off, the thunder of the captains, and the shouting.
texts.job.39.26: Doth the hawk fly by thy wisdom, and stretch her wings towards the south?
texts.job.39.27: Doth the eagle mount up at thy command, and make her nest on high?
texts.job.39.28: She dwelleth and abideth on the rock, upon the crag of the rock, and the strong place.
texts.job.39.29: From thence she seeketh the prey, and her eyes behold afar off.
texts.job.39.30: Her young ones also suck up blood: and where the slain are, there is she.
texts.job.40.1: Moreover, the LORD answered Job, and said,
texts.job.40.2: Shall he that contendeth with the Almighty instruct him? he that reproveth God, let him answer it.
texts.job.40.3: Then Job answered the LORD, and said,
texts.job.40.4: Behold, I am vile; what shall I answer thee? I will lay my hand upon my mouth.
texts.job.40.5: Once have I spoken; but I will not answer: yes, twice; but I will proceed no further.
texts.job.40.6: Then the LORD answered Job out of the whirlwind, and said,
texts.job.40.7: Gird up thy loins now like a man: I will demand of thee, and declare thou to me.
texts.job.40.8: Wilt thou also disannul my judgment? wilt thou condemn me, that thou mayest be righteous?
texts.job.40.9: Hast thou an arm like God? or canst thou thunder with a voice like his?
texts.job.40.10: Deck thyself now with majesty and excellence; and array thyself with glory and beauty.
texts.job.40.11: Cast abroad the rage of thy wrath: and behold every one that is proud, and abase him.
texts.job.40.12: Look on every one that is proud, and bring him low; and tread down the wicked in their place.
texts.job.40.13: Hide them in the dust together; bind their faces in secret.
texts.job.40.14: Then will I also confess to thee that thy own right hand can save thee.
texts.job.40.15: Behold now behemoth, which I made with thee; he eateth grass as an ox.
texts.job.40.16: Lo now, his strength is in his loins, and his force is in the navel of his belly.
texts.job.40.17: He moveth his tail like a cedar: the sinews of his male organs are wrapped together.
texts.job.40.18: His bones are as strong pieces of brass; his bones are like bars of iron.
texts.job.40.19: He is the chief of the ways of God: he that made him can make his sword to approach him.
texts.job.40.20: Surely the mountains bring him forth food, where all the beasts of the field play.
texts.job.40.21: He lieth under the shady trees, in the covert of the reed, and fens.
texts.job.40.22: The shady trees cover him with their shadow; the willows of the brook encompass him.
texts.job.40.23: Behold, he drinketh up a river, and hasteth not: he trusteth that he can draw up Jordan into his mouth.
texts.job.40.24: He taketh it with his eyes: his nose pierceth through snares.
texts.job.41.1: Canst thou draw out leviathan with a hook? or his tongue with a cord which thou lettest down?
texts.job.41.2: Canst thou put a hook into his nose? or bore his jaw through with a thorn?
texts.job.41.3: Will he make many supplications to thee? will he speak soft words to thee?
texts.job.41.4: Will he make a covenant with thee? wilt thou take him for a servant for ever?
texts.job.41.5: Wilt thou play with him as with a bird? or wilt thou bind him for thy maidens?
texts.job.41.6: Shall the companions make a banquet of him? shall they part him among the merchants.
texts.job.41.7: Canst thou fill his skin with barbed irons? or his head with fish spears?
texts.job.41.8: Lay thy hand upon him, remember the battle, do no more.
texts.job.41.9: Behold, the hope of him is in vain: shall not one be cast down even at the sight of him?
texts.job.41.10: None is so fierce that he dare rouse him: who then is able to stand before me?
texts.job.41.11: Who hath first benefited me, that I should repay him? whatever is under the whole heaven is mine.
texts.job.41.12: I will not conceal his parts, nor his power, nor his comely proportion.
texts.job.41.13: Who can discover the face of his garment? or who can come to him with his double bridle?
texts.job.41.14: Who can open the doors of his face? his teeth are terrible around.
texts.job.41.15: His scales are his pride, shut together as with a close seal.
texts.job.41.16: One is so near to another, that no air can come between them.
texts.job.41.17: They are joined one to another, they stick together, that they cannot be sundered.
texts.job.41.18: His sneezings flash light, and his eyes are like the eyelids of the morning.
texts.job.41.19: Out of his mouth go burning lamps, and sparks of fire dart forth.
texts.job.41.20: Out of his nostrils issueth smoke, as out of a seething pot or caldron.
texts.job.41.21: His breath kindleth coals, and a flame issueth from his mouth.
texts.job.41.22: In his neck remaineth strength, and sorrow is turned into joy before him.
texts.job.41.23: The flakes of his flesh are joined together: they are firm in themselves; they cannot be moved.
texts.job.41.24: His heart is as firm as a stone; yes, as hard as a piece of the nether millstone.
texts.job.41.25: When he raiseth himself, the mighty are afraid: by reason of breakings they purify themselves.
texts.job.41.26: The sword of him that attacketh him cannot hold: the spear, the dart, nor the habergeon.
texts.job.41.27: He esteemeth iron as straw, and brass as rotten wood.
texts.job.41.28: The arrow cannot make him flee: sling-stones are turned with him into stubble.
texts.job.41.29: Darts are counted as stubble: he laugheth at the shaking of a spear.
texts.job.41.30: Sharp stones are under him: he spreadeth sharp pointed things upon the mire.
texts.job.41.31: He maketh the deep to boil like a pot: he maketh the sea like a pot of ointment.
texts.job.41.32: He maketh a path to shine after him; one would think the deep to be hoary.
texts.job.41.33: Upon earth there is not his like, who is made without fear.
texts.job.41.34: He beholdeth all high things: he is a king over all the children of pride.
texts.job.42.1: Then Job answered the LORD, and said,
texts.job.42.2: I know that thou canst do every thing, and that no thought can be withheld from thee.
texts.job.42.3: Who is he that hideth counsel without knowledge? therefore have I uttered that which I understood not; things too wonderful for me, which I knew not.
texts.job.42.4: Hear, I beseech thee, and I will speak: I will ask of thee, and declare thou to me.
texts.job.42.5: I have heard of thee by the hearing of the ear: but now my eye seeth thee.
texts.job.42.6: Wherefore I abhor myself, and repent in dust and ashes.
texts.job.42.7: And it was so, that after the LORD had spoken these words to Job, the LORD said to Eliphaz the Temanite, My wrath is kindled against thee, and against thy two friends: for ye have not spoken of me the thing that is right, as my servant Job hath.
texts.job.42.8: Therefore take to you now seven bullocks and seven rams, and go to my servant Job, and offer for yourselves a burnt-offering; and my servant Job shall pray for you: for him will I accept: lest I deal with you after your folly, in that ye have not spoken of me the thing which is right, like my servant Job.
texts.job.42.9: So Eliphaz the Temanite and Bildad the Shuhite and Zophar the Naamathite went, and did according as the LORD commanded them: the LORD also accepted Job.
texts.job.42.10: And the LORD turned the captivity of Job, when he prayed for his friends: also the LORD gave Job twice as much as he had before.
texts.job.42.11: Then came there to him all his brethren, and all his sisters, and all they that had been of his acquaintance before, and ate bread with him in his house: and they condoled with him, and comforted him over all the evil that the LORD had brought upon him: every man also gave him a piece of money, and every one an ear-ring of gold.
texts.job.42.12: So the LORD blessed the latter end of Job more than his beginning: for he had fourteen thousand sheep, and six thousand camels, and a thousand yoke of oxen, and a thousand she asses.
texts.job.42.13: He had also seven sons, and three daughters.
texts.job.42.14: And he called the name of the first, Jemima; and the name of the second, Kezia; and the name of the third, Keren-happuch.
texts.job.42.15: And in all the land were no women found so fair as the daughters of Job: and their father gave them inheritance among their brethren.
texts.job.42.16: After this Job lived a hundred and forty years, and saw his sons, and his sons' sons, even four generations.
texts.job.42.17: So Job died, being old and full of days.

texts.job.1.1: There was a man in the land of Uz whose name was Job; and this man was perfect and upright, and one that feared God and abstained from evil.
texts.job.1.2: And there were born to him seven sons and three daughters.
texts.job.1.3: And his substance was seven thousand sheep, and three thousand camels, and five hundred yoke of oxen, and five hundred she-asses, and very many servants; and this man was greater than all the children of the east.
texts.job.1.4: And his sons went and made a feast in the house of each one on his day; and they sent and invited their three sisters to eat and to drink with them.
texts.job.1.5: And it was so, when the days of the feasting were gone about, that Job sent and hallowed them; and he rose up early in the morning, and offered up burnt-offerings [according to] the number of them all; for Job said, It may be that my children have sinned, and cursed God in their hearts. Thus did Job continually.
texts.job.1.6: And there was a day when the sons of God came to present themselves before Jehovah; and Satan came also among them.
texts.job.1.7: And Jehovah said to Satan, Whence comest thou? And Satan answered Jehovah and said, From going to and fro in the earth, and from walking up and down in it.
texts.job.1.8: And Jehovah said to Satan, Hast thou considered my servant Job, that there is none like him on the earth, a perfect and an upright man, one that feareth God and abstaineth from evil?
texts.job.1.9: And Satan answered Jehovah and said, Doth Job fear God for nought?
texts.job.1.10: Hast not thou made a hedge about him, and about his house, and about all that he hath on every side? Thou hast blessed the work of his hands, and his substance is spread abroad in the land.
texts.job.1.11: But put forth thy hand now and touch all that he hath, [and see] if he will not curse thee to thy face!
texts.job.1.12: And Jehovah said to Satan, Behold, all that he hath is in thy hand; only upon himself put not forth thy hand. So Satan went forth from the presence of Jehovah.
texts.job.1.13: And there was a day when his sons and his daughters were eating and drinking wine in the house of their brother, the firstborn.
texts.job.1.14: And there came a messenger to Job and said, The oxen were ploughing, and the asses feeding beside them;
texts.job.1.15: and [they of] Sheba fell [upon them] and took them, and the servants have they smitten with the edge of the sword; and I only am escaped, alone, to tell thee.
texts.job.1.16: While he was yet speaking, there came another and said, The fire of God fell from heaven and burned up the sheep and the servants, and consumed them; and I only am escaped, alone, to tell thee.
texts.job.1.17: While he was yet speaking, there came another and said, The Chaldeans made three bands, and fell upon the camels and took them, and the servants have they smitten with the edge of the sword; and I only am escaped, alone, to tell thee.
texts.job.1.18: While he was yet speaking, there came another and said, Thy sons and thy daughters were eating and drinking wine in the house of their brother, the firstborn;
texts.job.1.19: and behold, there came a great wind from over the wilderness, and smote the four corners of the house, and it fell upon the young men, and they died; and I only am escaped, alone, to tell thee.
texts.job.1.20: And Job rose up, and rent his mantle, and shaved his head, and fell down on the ground, and worshipped;
texts.job.1.21: and he said, Naked came I out of my mother's womb, and naked shall I return thither: Jehovah gave, and Jehovah hath taken away; blessed be the name of Jehovah!
texts.job.1.22: In all this Job sinned not, nor ascribed anything unseemly to God.
texts.job.2.1: And there was a day when the sons of God came to present themselves before Jehovah, and Satan also came among them to present himself before Jehovah.
texts.job.2.2: And Jehovah said to Satan, From whence comest thou? And Satan answered Jehovah and said, From going to and fro in the earth, and from walking up and down in it.
texts.job.2.3: And Jehovah said to Satan, Hast thou considered my servant Job, that there is none like him on the earth, a perfect and an upright man, one that feareth God and abstaineth from evil? and still he remaineth firm in his integrity, though thou movedst me against him, to swallow him up without cause.
texts.job.2.4: And Satan answered Jehovah and said, Skin for skin, yea, all that a man hath will he give for his life;
texts.job.2.5: but put forth thy hand now, and touch his bone and his flesh, [and see] if he will not curse thee to thy face!
texts.job.2.6: And Jehovah said to Satan, Behold, he is in thy hand; only spare his life.
texts.job.2.7: And Satan went forth from the presence of Jehovah; and he smote Job with a grievous botch from the sole of his foot unto his crown.
texts.job.2.8: And he took a potsherd to scrape himself with; and he sat among the ashes.
texts.job.2.9: And his wife said to him, Dost thou still remain firm in thine integrity? curse God and die.
texts.job.2.10: But he said to her, Thou speakest as one of the foolish women speaketh. We have also received good from God, and should we not receive evil? In all this Job did not sin with his lips.
texts.job.2.11: And three friends of Job heard of all this evil that was come upon him. And they came each one from his place: Eliphaz the Temanite, and Bildad the Shuhite, and Zophar the Naamathite; and they made an appointment together to come to condole with him and to comfort him.
texts.job.2.12: And when they lifted up their eyes afar off, and knew him not, they lifted up their voice and wept. And they rent every one his mantle, and sprinkled dust upon their heads toward the heavens.
texts.job.2.13: And they sat down with him on the ground seven days and seven nights; and none spoke a word to him; for they saw that [his] anguish was very great.
texts.job.3.1: After this, Job opened his mouth and cursed his day.
texts.job.3.3: Let the day perish in which I was born, and the night that said, There is a man child conceived.
texts.job.3.4: That day -- let it be darkness, let not +God care for it from above, neither let light shine upon it:
texts.job.3.5: Let darkness and the shadow of death claim it; let clouds dwell upon it; let darkeners of the day terrify it.
texts.job.3.6: That night -- let gloom seize upon it; let it not rejoice among the days of the year; let it not come into the number of the months.
texts.job.3.7: Behold, let that night be barren; let no joyful sound come therein;
texts.job.3.8: Let them curse it that curse the day, who are ready to rouse Leviathan;
texts.job.3.9: Let the stars of its twilight be dark; let it wait for light, and have none, neither let it see the eyelids of the dawn:
texts.job.3.10: Because it shut not up the doors of the womb that bore me, and hid not trouble from mine eyes.
texts.job.3.11: Wherefore did I not die from the womb, -- come forth from the belly and expire?
texts.job.3.12: Why did the knees meet me? and wherefore the breasts, that I should suck?
texts.job.3.13: For now should I have lain down and been quiet; I should have slept: then had I been at rest,
texts.job.3.14: With kings and counsellors of the earth, who build desolate places for themselves,
texts.job.3.15: Or with princes who had gold, who filled their houses with silver;
texts.job.3.16: Or as a hidden untimely birth I had not been; as infants that have not seen the light.
texts.job.3.17: There the wicked cease from troubling; and there the wearied are at rest.
texts.job.3.18: The prisoners together are at ease; they hear not the voice of the taskmaster.
texts.job.3.19: The small and great are there, and the bondman freed from his master.
texts.job.3.20: Wherefore is light given to him that is in trouble, and life to those bitter of soul,
texts.job.3.21: Who long for death, and it [cometh] not, and dig for it more than for hidden treasures;
texts.job.3.22: Who rejoice even exultingly and are glad when they find the grave? --
texts.job.3.23: To the man whose way is hidden, and whom +God hath hedged in?
texts.job.3.24: For my sighing cometh before my bread, and my groanings are poured out like the waters.
texts.job.3.25: For I feared a fear, and it hath come upon me, and that which I dreaded hath come to me.
texts.job.3.26: I was not in safety, neither had I quietness, neither was I at rest, and trouble came.
texts.job.4.1: And Eliphaz the Temanite answered and said,
texts.job.4.2: If a word were essayed to thee, wouldest thou be grieved? But who can refrain from speaking?
texts.job.4.3: Behold, thou hast instructed many, and thou hast strengthened the weak hands;
texts.job.4.4: Thy words have upholden him that was stumbling, and thou hast braced up the bending knees:
texts.job.4.5: But now it is come upon thee, and thou grievest; it toucheth thee, and thou art troubled.
texts.job.4.6: Hath not thy piety been thy confidence, and the perfection of thy ways thy hope?
texts.job.4.7: Remember, I pray thee, who that was innocent has perished? and where were the upright cut off?
texts.job.4.8: Even as I have seen, they that plough iniquity and sow mischief, reap the same.
texts.job.4.9: By the breath of +God they perish, and by the blast of his nostrils are they consumed.
texts.job.4.10: The roar of the lion, and the voice of the fierce lion, and the teeth of the young lions, are broken;
texts.job.4.11: The old lion perisheth for lack of prey, and the whelps of the lioness are scattered.
texts.job.4.12: Now to me a word was secretly brought, and mine ear received a whisper thereof.
texts.job.4.13: In thoughts from visions of the night, when deep sleep falleth on men: --
texts.job.4.14: Fear came on me, and trembling, and made all my bones to shake;
texts.job.4.15: And a spirit passed before my face -- the hair of my flesh stood up --
texts.job.4.16: It stood still; I could not discern the appearance thereof: a form was before mine eyes; I heard a slight murmur and a voice:
texts.job.4.17: Shall [mortal] man be more just than +God? Shall a man be purer than his Maker?
texts.job.4.18: Lo, he trusteth not his servants, and his angels he chargeth with folly:
texts.job.4.19: How much more them that dwell in houses of clay, whose foundation is in the dust, who are crushed as the moth!
texts.job.4.20: From morning to evening are they smitten: without any heeding it, they perish for ever.
texts.job.4.21: Is not their tent-cord torn away in them? they die, and without wisdom.
texts.job.5.1: Call, I pray thee! Is there any that answereth thee? and to which of the holy ones wilt thou turn?
texts.job.5.2: For vexation killeth the foolish man, and envy slayeth the simple.
texts.job.5.3: I myself saw the foolish taking root, but suddenly I cursed his habitation.
texts.job.5.4: His children are far from safety, and they are crushed in the gate, and there is no deliverer:
texts.job.5.5: Whose harvest the hungry eateth up, and taketh even out of the thorns; and the snare gapeth for his substance.
texts.job.5.6: For evil cometh not forth from the dust, neither doth trouble spring out of the ground;
texts.job.5.7: For man is born to trouble, as the sparks fly upwards.
texts.job.5.8: But as for me I will seek unto ùGod, and unto God commit my cause;
texts.job.5.9: Who doeth great things and unsearchable, marvellous things without number;
texts.job.5.10: Who giveth rain on the face of the earth, and sendeth waters on the face of the fields;
texts.job.5.11: Setting up on high those that are low; and mourners are exalted to prosperity.
texts.job.5.12: He disappointeth the devices of the crafty, and their hands carry not out the enterprise.
texts.job.5.13: He taketh the wise in their own craftiness; and the counsel of the wily is carried headlong:
texts.job.5.14: They meet with darkness in a the daytime, and grope at midday as in the night.
texts.job.5.15: And he saveth the needy from the sword, from their mouth, and from the hand of the mighty.
texts.job.5.16: So the poor hath what he hopeth for, and unrighteousness stoppeth her mouth.
texts.job.5.17: Behold, happy is the man whom +God correcteth; therefore despise not the chastening of the Almighty.
texts.job.5.18: For he maketh sore, and bindeth up; he woundeth, and his hands make whole.
texts.job.5.19: He will deliver thee in six troubles, and in seven there shall no evil touch thee.
texts.job.5.20: In famine he will redeem thee from death, and in war from the power of the sword.
texts.job.5.21: Thou shalt be hidden from the scourge of the tongue; and thou shalt not be afraid of destruction when it cometh.
texts.job.5.22: At destruction and famine thou shalt laugh, and of the beasts of the earth thou shalt not be afraid.
texts.job.5.23: For thou shalt be in league with the stones of the field, and the beasts of the field shall be at peace with thee.
texts.job.5.24: And thou shalt know that thy tent is in peace; and thou wilt survey thy fold, and miss nothing.
texts.job.5.25: And thou shalt know that thy seed is numerous, and thine offspring as the herb of the earth.
texts.job.5.26: Thou shalt come to the grave in a ripe age, as a shock of corn is brought in in its season.
texts.job.5.27: Behold this, we have searched it out, so it is; hear it, and know thou it for thyself.
texts.job.6.2: Oh that my grief were thoroughly weighed, and all my calamity laid in the balances!
texts.job.6.3: For now it would be heavier than the sand of the seas; therefore my words are vehement.
texts.job.6.4: For the arrows of the Almighty are within me, their poison drinketh up my spirit: the terrors of +God are arrayed against me.
texts.job.6.5: Doth the wild ass bray by the grass? loweth an ox over his fodder?
texts.job.6.6: Shall that which is insipid be eaten without salt? Is there any taste in the white of an egg?
texts.job.6.7: What my soul refuseth to touch, that is as my loathsome food.
texts.job.6.8: Oh that I might have my request, and that +God would grant my desire!
texts.job.6.9: And that it would please +God to crush me, that he would let loose his hand and cut me off!
texts.job.6.10: Then should I yet have comfort; and in the pain which spareth not I would rejoice that I have not denied the words of the Holy One.
texts.job.6.11: What is my strength, that I should hope? and what is mine end, that I should have patience?
texts.job.6.12: Is my strength the strength of stones? is my flesh of brass?
texts.job.6.13: Is it not that there is no help in me, and soundness is driven away from me?
texts.job.6.14: For him that is fainting kindness [is meet] from his friend; or he forsaketh the fear of the Almighty.
texts.job.6.15: My brethren have dealt deceitfully as a stream, as the channel of streams which pass away,
texts.job.6.16: Which are turbid by reason of the ice, in which the snow hideth itself:
texts.job.6.17: At the time they diminish, they are dried up; when heat affecteth them, they vanish from their place:
texts.job.6.18: They wind about in the paths of their course, they go off into the waste and perish.
texts.job.6.19: The caravans of Tema looked, the companies of Sheba counted on them:
texts.job.6.20: They are ashamed at their hope; they come thither, and are confounded.
texts.job.6.21: So now ye are nothing; ye see a terrible object and are afraid.
texts.job.6.22: Did I say, Bring unto me, and make me a present from your substance?
texts.job.6.23: Or, rescue me from the hand of the oppressor, and redeem me from the hand of the violent?
texts.job.6.24: Teach me, and I will hold my tongue; and cause me to understand wherein I have erred.
texts.job.6.25: How forcible are right words! but what doth your upbraiding reprove?
texts.job.6.26: Do ye imagine to reprove words? The speeches of one that is desperate are indeed for the wind.
texts.job.6.27: Yea, ye overwhelm the fatherless, and dig [a pit] for your friend.
texts.job.6.28: Now therefore if ye will, look upon me; and it shall be to your face if I lie.
texts.job.6.29: Return, I pray you, let there be no wrong; yea, return again, my righteousness shall be in it.
texts.job.6.30: Is there wrong in my tongue? cannot my taste discern mischievous things?
texts.job.7.1: Hath not man a life of labour upon earth? and are not his days like the days of a hireling?
texts.job.7.2: As a bondman earnestly desireth the shadow, and a hireling expecteth his wages,
texts.job.7.3: So am I made to possess months of vanity, and wearisome nights are appointed to me.
texts.job.7.4: If I lie down, I say, When shall I rise up, and the darkness be gone? and I am full of tossings until the dawn.
texts.job.7.5: My flesh is clothed with worms and clods of dust; my skin is broken, and suppurates.
texts.job.7.6: My days are swifter than a weaver's shuttle, and are spent without hope.
texts.job.7.7: Remember thou that my life is wind; mine eye shall no more see good.
texts.job.7.8: The eye of him that hath seen me shall behold me no [more]: thine eyes are upon me, and I am not.
texts.job.7.9: The cloud consumeth and vanisheth away; so he that goeth down to Sheol shall not come up.
texts.job.7.10: He shall return no more to his house, neither shall his place know him again.
texts.job.7.11: Therefore I will not restrain my mouth: I will speak in the anguish of my spirit; I will complain in the bitterness of my soul.
texts.job.7.12: Am I a sea, or a sea-monster, that thou settest a watch over me?
texts.job.7.13: When I say, My bed shall comfort me, my couch shall ease my complaint;
texts.job.7.14: Then thou scarest me with dreams, and terrifiest me through visions;
texts.job.7.15: So that my soul chooseth strangling, death, rather than my bones.
texts.job.7.16: I loathe it; I shall not live always: let me alone, for my days are a breath.
texts.job.7.17: What is man, that thou makest much of him? and that thou settest thy heart upon him?
texts.job.7.18: And that thou visitest him every morning, triest him every moment?
texts.job.7.19: How long wilt thou not look away from me, nor let me alone till I swallow down my spittle?
texts.job.7.20: Have I sinned, what do I unto thee, thou Observer of men? Why hast thou set me as an object of assault for thee, so that I am become a burden to myself?
texts.job.7.21: And why dost not thou forgive my transgression and take away mine iniquity? for now shall I lie down in the dust, and thou shalt seek me early, and I shall not be.
texts.job.8.1: And Bildad the Shuhite answered and said,
texts.job.8.2: How long wilt thou speak these things? and the words of thy mouth be a strong wind?
texts.job.8.3: Doth ùGod pervert judgment, and the Almighty pervert justice?
texts.job.8.4: If thy children have sinned against him, he hath also given them over into the hand of their transgression.
texts.job.8.5: If thou seek earnestly unto ùGod, and make thy supplication to the Almighty,
texts.job.8.6: If thou be pure and upright, surely now he will awake for thee, and make the habitation of thy righteousness prosperous;
texts.job.8.7: And though thy beginning was small, yet thine end shall be very great.
texts.job.8.8: For inquire, I pray thee, of the former generation, and attend to the researches of their fathers;
texts.job.8.9: For we are [but] of yesterday, and know nothing, for our days upon earth are a shadow.
texts.job.8.10: Shall not they teach thee, [and] tell thee, and utter words out of their heart?
texts.job.8.11: Doth the papyrus shoot up without mire? doth the reed-grass grow without water?
texts.job.8.12: Whilst it is yet in its greenness [and] not cut down, it withereth before any [other] grass.
texts.job.8.13: So are the paths of all that forget ùGod; and the profane man's hope shall perish,
texts.job.8.14: Whose confidence shall be cut off, and his reliance is a spider's web.
texts.job.8.15: He shall lean upon his house, and it shall not stand; he shall lay hold on it, but it shall not endure.
texts.job.8.16: He is full of sap before the sun, and his sprout shooteth forth over his garden;
texts.job.8.17: His roots are entwined about the stoneheap; he seeth the place of stones.
texts.job.8.18: If he destroy him from his place, then it shall deny him: I have not seen thee!
texts.job.8.19: Behold, this is the joy of his way, and out of the dust shall others grow.
texts.job.8.20: Behold, ùGod will not cast off a perfect man, neither will he take evil-doers by the hand.
texts.job.8.21: Whilst he would fill thy mouth with laughing and thy lips with shouting,
texts.job.8.22: They that hate thee shall be clothed with shame, and the tent of the wicked be no more.
texts.job.9.2: Of a truth I know it is so; but how can man be just with ùGod?
texts.job.9.3: If he shall choose to strive with him, he cannot answer him one thing of a thousand.
texts.job.9.4: He is wise in heart and mighty in strength: who hath hardened himself against him, and had peace?
texts.job.9.5: Who removeth mountains, and they know it not, when he overturneth them in his anger;
texts.job.9.6: Who shaketh the earth out of its place, and the pillars thereof tremble;
texts.job.9.7: Who commandeth the sun, and it riseth not, and he sealeth up the stars;
texts.job.9.8: Who alone spreadeth out the heavens, and treadeth upon the high waves of the sea;
texts.job.9.9: Who maketh the Bear, Orion, and the Pleiades, and the chambers of the south;
texts.job.9.10: Who doeth great things past finding out, and wonders without number.
texts.job.9.11: Lo, he goeth by me, and I see [him] not; and he passeth along, and I perceive him not.
texts.job.9.12: Behold, he taketh away: who will hinder him? Who will say unto him, What doest thou?
texts.job.9.13: +God withdraweth not his anger; the proud helpers stoop under him:
texts.job.9.14: How much less shall I answer him, choose out my words [to strive] with him?
texts.job.9.15: Whom, though I were righteous, [yet] would I not answer; I would make supplication to my judge.
texts.job.9.16: If I had called, and he had answered me, I would not believe that he hearkened to my voice, --
texts.job.9.17: He, who crusheth me with a tempest, and multiplieth my wounds without cause.
texts.job.9.18: He suffereth me not to take my breath, for he filleth me with bitternesses.
texts.job.9.19: Be it a question of strength, lo, [he is] strong; and be it of judgment, who will set me a time?
texts.job.9.20: If I justified myself, mine own mouth would condemn me; were I perfect, he would prove me perverse.
texts.job.9.21: Were I perfect, [yet] would I not know my soul: I would despise my life.
texts.job.9.22: It is all one; therefore I said, he destroyeth the perfect and the wicked.
texts.job.9.23: If the scourge kill suddenly, he mocketh at the trial of the innocent.
texts.job.9.24: The earth is given over into the hand of the wicked [man]; he covereth the faces of its judges. If not, who then is it?
texts.job.9.25: And my days are swifter than a runner: they flee away, they see no good.
texts.job.9.26: They pass by like skiffs of reed; as an eagle that swoops upon the prey.
texts.job.9.27: If I say, I will forget my complaint, I will leave off my [sad] countenance, and brighten up,
texts.job.9.28: I am afraid of all my sorrows; I know that thou wilt not hold me innocent.
texts.job.9.29: Be it that I am wicked, why then do I labour in vain?
texts.job.9.30: If I washed myself with snow-water, and cleansed my hands in purity,
texts.job.9.31: Then wouldest thou plunge me in the ditch, and mine own clothes would abhor me.
texts.job.9.32: For he is not a man, as I am, that I should answer him; that we should come together in judgment.
texts.job.9.33: There is not an umpire between us, who should lay his hand upon us both.
texts.job.9.34: Let him take his rod away from me, and let not his terror make me afraid,
texts.job.9.35: [Then] I will speak, and not fear him; but it is not so with me.
texts.job.10.1: My soul is weary of my life: I will give free course to my complaint; I will speak in the bitterness of my soul.
texts.job.10.2: I will say unto +God, Do not condemn me; shew me wherefore thou strivest with me.
texts.job.10.3: Doth it please thee to oppress, that thou shouldest despise the work of thy hands, and shine upon the counsel of the wicked?
texts.job.10.4: Hast thou eyes of flesh? or seest thou as man seeth?
texts.job.10.5: Are thy days as the days of a mortal? are thy years as a man's days,
texts.job.10.6: That thou searchest after mine iniquity, and inquirest into my sin;
texts.job.10.7: Since thou knowest that I am not wicked, and that there is none that delivereth out of thy hand?
texts.job.10.8: Thy hands have bound me together and made me as one, round about; yet dost thou swallow me up!
texts.job.10.9: Remember, I beseech thee, that thou hast made me as clay, and wilt bring me into dust again.
texts.job.10.10: Hast thou not poured me out as milk, and curdled me like cheese?
texts.job.10.11: Thou hast clothed me with skin and flesh, and knit me together with bones and sinews;
texts.job.10.12: Thou hast granted me life and favour, and thy care hath preserved my spirit;
texts.job.10.13: And these things didst thou hide in thy heart; I know that this was with thee.
texts.job.10.14: If I sinned, thou wouldest mark me, and thou wouldest not acquit me of mine iniquity.
texts.job.10.15: If I were wicked, woe unto me! and righteous, I will not lift up my head, being [so] full of shame, and beholding mine affliction; --
texts.job.10.16: And it increaseth: thou huntest me as a fierce lion; and ever again thou shewest thy marvellous power upon me.
texts.job.10.17: Thou renewest thy witnesses before me and increasest thy displeasure against me; successions [of evil] and a time of toil are with me.
texts.job.10.18: And wherefore didst thou bring me forth out of the womb? I had expired, and no eye had seen me.
texts.job.10.19: I should be as though I had not been; I should have been carried from the womb to the grave.
texts.job.10.20: Are not my days few? cease then and let me alone, that I may revive a little,
texts.job.10.21: Before I go, and never to return, -- to the land of darkness and the shadow of death;
texts.job.10.22: A land of gloom, as darkness itself; of the shadow of death, without any order, where the light is as thick darkness.
texts.job.11.1: And Zophar the Naamathite answered and said,
texts.job.11.2: Should not the multitude of words be answered? and should a man of much talk be justified?
texts.job.11.3: Should thy fictions make men hold their peace? and shouldest thou mock, and no one make [thee] ashamed?
texts.job.11.4: For thou sayest, My doctrine is pure, and I am clean in thine eyes.
texts.job.11.5: But oh that +God would speak, and open his lips against thee;
texts.job.11.6: And that he would shew thee the secrets of wisdom, how that they are the double of what is realised; and know that +God passeth by [much] of thine iniquity!
texts.job.11.7: Canst thou by searching find out +God? canst thou find out the Almighty to perfection?
texts.job.11.8: [It is as] the heights of heaven; what wilt thou do? deeper than Sheol; what canst thou know?
texts.job.11.9: The measure thereof is longer than the earth, and broader than the sea.
texts.job.11.10: If he pass by, and shut up, and call to judgment, who can hinder him?
texts.job.11.11: For he knoweth vain men, and seeth wickedness when [man] doth not consider it;
texts.job.11.12: Yet a senseless man will make bold, though man be born [like] the foal of a wild ass.
texts.job.11.13: If thou prepare thy heart and stretch out thy hands toward him,
texts.job.11.14: If thou put far away the iniquity which is in thy hand, and let not wrong dwell in thy tents;
texts.job.11.15: Surely then shalt thou lift up thy face without spot, and thou shalt be stedfast and shalt not fear:
texts.job.11.16: For thou shalt forget misery; as waters that are passed away shalt thou remember it;
texts.job.11.17: And life shall arise brighter than noonday; though thou be enshrouded in darkness, thou shalt be as the morning,
texts.job.11.18: And thou shalt have confidence, because there shall be hope; and having searched about [thee], thou shalt take rest in safety.
texts.job.11.19: Yea, thou shalt lie down, and none shall make thee afraid; and many shall seek thy favour.
texts.job.11.20: But the eyes of the wicked shall fail, and [all] refuge shall vanish from them, and their hope [shall be] the breathing out of life.
texts.job.12.2: Truly ye are the people, and wisdom shall die with you!
texts.job.12.3: I also have understanding as well as you; I am not inferior to you; and who knoweth not such things as these?
texts.job.12.4: I am to be one that is a derision to his friend, I who call upon +God, and whom he will answer: a derision is the just upright [man].
texts.job.12.5: He that is ready to stumble with the foot is a lamp despised in the thought of him that is at ease.
texts.job.12.6: The tents of desolators are in peace, and they that provoke ùGod are secure; into whose hand +God bringeth.
texts.job.12.7: But ask now the beasts, and they shall teach thee; and the fowl of the heavens, and they shall tell thee;
texts.job.12.8: Or speak to the earth, and it shall teach thee; and the fishes of the sea shall declare unto thee.
texts.job.12.9: Who knoweth not in all these, that the hand of Jehovah hath wrought this?
texts.job.12.10: In whose hand is the soul of every living thing, and the spirit of all flesh of man.
texts.job.12.11: Doth not the ear try words, as the palate tasteth food?
texts.job.12.12: With the aged is wisdom, and in length of days understanding.
texts.job.12.13: With him is wisdom and might; he hath counsel and understanding.
texts.job.12.14: Behold, he breaketh down, and it is not built again; he shutteth up a man, and there is no opening.
texts.job.12.15: Behold, he withholdeth the waters, and they dry up; and he sendeth them out, and they overturn the earth.
texts.job.12.16: With him is strength and effectual knowledge; the deceived and the deceiver are his.
texts.job.12.17: He leadeth counsellors away spoiled, and judges maketh he fools;
texts.job.12.18: He weakeneth the government of kings, and bindeth their loins with a fetter;
texts.job.12.19: He leadeth priests away spoiled, and overthroweth the mighty;
texts.job.12.20: He depriveth of speech the trusty, and taketh away the judgment of the elders;
texts.job.12.21: He poureth contempt upon nobles, and slackeneth the girdle of the mighty;
texts.job.12.22: He discovereth deep things out of darkness, and bringeth out into light the shadow of death;
texts.job.12.23: He increaseth the nations, and destroyeth them; he spreadeth out the nations, and bringeth them in;
texts.job.12.24: He taketh away the understanding of the chiefs of the people of the earth, and causeth them to wander in a pathless waste.
texts.job.12.25: They grope in the dark without light, and he maketh them to stagger like a drunkard.
texts.job.13.1: Lo, mine eye hath seen all [this], mine ear hath heard and understood it.
texts.job.13.2: What ye know, I know also: I am not inferior to you.
texts.job.13.3: But I will speak to the Almighty, and will find pleasure in reasoning with ùGod;
texts.job.13.4: For ye indeed are forgers of lies, ye are all physicians of no value.
texts.job.13.5: Oh that ye would be altogether silent! and it would be your wisdom.
texts.job.13.6: Hear now my defence, and hearken to the pleadings of my lips.
texts.job.13.7: Will ye speak unrighteously for ùGod? and for him speak deceit?
texts.job.13.8: Will ye accept his person? will ye contend for ùGod?
texts.job.13.9: Will it be well if he should search you out? or as one mocketh at a man, will ye mock at him?
texts.job.13.10: He will certainly reprove you, if ye do secretly accept persons.
texts.job.13.11: Shall not his excellency terrify you? and his dread fall upon you?
texts.job.13.12: Your memorable sayings are proverbs of ashes, your bulwarks are bulwarks of mire.
texts.job.13.13: Hold your peace from me, and I will speak, and let come on me what [will]!
texts.job.13.14: Wherefore should I take my flesh in my teeth, and put my life in my hand?
texts.job.13.15: Behold, if he slay me, yet would I trust in him; but I will defend mine own ways before him.
texts.job.13.16: This also shall be my salvation, that a profane man shall not come before his face.
texts.job.13.17: Hear attentively my speech and my declaration with your ears.
texts.job.13.18: Behold now, I have ordered the cause; I know that I shall be justified.
texts.job.13.19: Who is he that contendeth with me? For if I were silent now, I should expire.
texts.job.13.20: Only do not two things unto me; then will I not hide myself from thee.
texts.job.13.21: Withdraw thy hand far from me; and let not thy terror make me afraid:
texts.job.13.22: Then call, and I will answer; or I will speak, and answer thou me.
texts.job.13.23: How many are mine iniquities and sins? Make me to know my transgression and my sin.
texts.job.13.24: Wherefore dost thou hide thy face, and countest me for thine enemy?
texts.job.13.25: Wilt thou terrify a driven leaf? and wilt thou pursue dry stubble?
texts.job.13.26: For thou writest bitter things against me, and makest me to possess the iniquities of my youth;
texts.job.13.27: And thou puttest my feet in the stocks, and markest all my paths; thou settest a bound about the soles of my feet; --
texts.job.13.28: One who, as a rotten thing consumeth, as a garment that the moth eateth.
texts.job.14.1: Man, born of woman, is of few days, and full of trouble.
texts.job.14.2: He cometh forth like a flower, and is cut down; and he fleeth as a shadow, and continueth not.
texts.job.14.3: Yet dost thou open thine eyes upon such a one, and bringest me into judgment with thee?
texts.job.14.4: Who can bring a clean [man] out of the unclean? Not one!
texts.job.14.5: If his days are determined, if the number of his months is with thee, [and] thou hast appointed his bounds which he must not pass,
texts.job.14.6: Look away from him; and let him rest, till he accomplish, as a hireling, his day.
texts.job.14.7: For there is hope for a tree: if it be cut down, it will sprout again, and its tender branch will not cease;
texts.job.14.8: Though its root grow old in the earth, and its stock die in the ground,
texts.job.14.9: Yet through the scent of water it will bud, and put forth boughs like a young plant.
texts.job.14.10: But a man dieth, and is prostrate; yea, man expireth, and where is he?
texts.job.14.11: The waters recede from the lake, and the river wasteth and drieth up:
texts.job.14.12: So man lieth down, and riseth not again; till the heavens be no more, they do not awake, nor are raised out of their sleep.
texts.job.14.13: Oh that thou wouldest hide me in Sheol, that thou wouldest keep me secret until thine anger be past, that thou wouldest appoint me a set time, and remember me, --
texts.job.14.14: (If a man die, shall he live [again]?) all the days of my time of toil would I wait, till my change should come:
texts.job.14.15: Thou wouldest call, and I would answer thee; thou wouldest have a desire after the work of thy hands.
texts.job.14.16: For now thou numberest my steps: dost thou not watch over my sin?
texts.job.14.17: My transgression is sealed up in a bag, and thou heapest up mine iniquity.
texts.job.14.18: And indeed a mountain falling cometh to nought, and the rock is removed out of its place;
texts.job.14.19: The waters wear the stones, the floods thereof wash away the dust of the earth; and thou destroyest the hope of man.
texts.job.14.20: Thou prevailest for ever against him, and he passeth away; thou changest his countenance, and dismissest him.
texts.job.14.21: His sons come to honour, and he knoweth it not; and they are brought low, and he perceiveth it not.
texts.job.14.22: But his flesh hath pain for himself alone, and his soul mourneth for himself.
texts.job.15.1: And Eliphaz the Temanite answered and said,
texts.job.15.2: Should a wise man answer with windy knowledge, and fill his belly with the east wind,
texts.job.15.3: Reasoning with unprofitable talk, and with speeches which do no good?
texts.job.15.4: Yea, thou makest piety of none effect, and restrainest meditation before ùGod.
texts.job.15.5: For thy mouth uttereth thine iniquity, and thou hast chosen the tongue of the crafty.
texts.job.15.6: Thine own mouth condemneth thee, and not I; and thy lips testify against thee.
texts.job.15.7: Art thou the first man that was born? and wast thou brought forth before the hills?
texts.job.15.8: Hast thou listened in the secret council of +God? And hast thou absorbed wisdom for thyself?
texts.job.15.9: What knowest thou that we know not? [what] understandest thou which is not in us?
texts.job.15.10: Both the greyheaded and the aged are with us, older than thy father.
texts.job.15.11: Are the consolations of ùGod too small for thee? and the word gently spoken to thee?
texts.job.15.12: Why doth thy heart carry thee away? and why do thine eyes wink?
texts.job.15.13: That thou turnest thy spirit against ùGod, and lettest words go out of thy mouth?
texts.job.15.14: What is man, that he should be pure? and he that is born of a woman, that he should be righteous?
texts.job.15.15: Behold, he putteth no trust in his holy ones, and the heavens are not pure in his sight:
texts.job.15.16: How much less the abominable and corrupt, -- man, that drinketh unrighteousness like water!
texts.job.15.17: I will shew thee, listen to me; and what I have seen I will declare;
texts.job.15.18: Which wise men have told from their fathers, and have not hidden;
texts.job.15.19: Unto whom alone the earth was given, and no stranger passed among them.
texts.job.15.20: All his days the wicked man is tormented, and numbered years are allotted to the violent.
texts.job.15.21: The sound of terrors is in his ears: in prosperity the destroyer cometh upon him.
texts.job.15.22: He believeth not that he shall return out of darkness, and he is singled out for the sword.
texts.job.15.23: He wandereth abroad for bread, -- where may it be? He knoweth that the day of darkness is ready at his hand.
texts.job.15.24: Distress and anguish make him afraid; they prevail against him, as a king ready for the battle.
texts.job.15.25: For he hath stretched out his hand against ùGod, and strengthened himself against the Almighty:
texts.job.15.26: He runneth against him, with [outstretched] neck, with the thick bosses of his bucklers;
texts.job.15.27: For he hath covered his face with his fatness, and gathered fat upon [his] flanks.
texts.job.15.28: And he dwelleth in desolate cities, in houses that no man inhabiteth, which are destined to become heaps.
texts.job.15.29: He shall not become rich, neither shall his substance continue, and their possessions shall not extend upon the earth.
texts.job.15.30: He shall not depart out of darkness; the flame shall dry up his branches; and by the breath of his mouth shall he go away.
texts.job.15.31: Let him not trust in vanity: he is deceived, for vanity shall be his recompense;
texts.job.15.32: It shall be complete before his day, and his branch shall not be green.
texts.job.15.33: He shall shake off his unripe grapes as a vine, and shall cast his flower as an olive.
texts.job.15.34: For the family of the ungodly shall be barren, and fire shall consume the tents of bribery.
texts.job.15.35: They conceive mischief, and bring forth iniquity, and their belly prepareth deceit.
texts.job.16.2: I have heard many such things: grievous comforters are ye all.
texts.job.16.3: Shall words of wind have an end? or what provoketh thee that thou answerest?
texts.job.16.4: I also could speak as ye: if your soul were in my soul's stead, I could join together words against you, and shake my head at you;
texts.job.16.5: [But] I would encourage you with my mouth, and the solace of my lips should assuage [your pain].
texts.job.16.6: If I speak, my pain is not assuaged; and if I forbear, what am I eased?
texts.job.16.7: But now he hath made me weary; ... thou hast made desolate all my family;
texts.job.16.8: Thou hast shrivelled me up! it is become a witness; and my leanness riseth up against me, it beareth witness to my face.
texts.job.16.9: His anger teareth and pursueth me; he gnasheth with his teeth against me; [as] mine adversary he sharpeneth his eyes at me.
texts.job.16.10: They gape upon me with their mouth; they smite my cheeks reproachfully; they range themselves together against me.
texts.job.16.11: ùGod hath delivered me over to the iniquitous man, and hurled me into the hands of the wicked.
texts.job.16.12: I was at rest, but he hath shattered me; he hath taken me by the neck and shaken me to pieces, and set me up for his mark.
texts.job.16.13: His arrows encompass me round about, he cleaveth my reins asunder and doth not spare; he poureth out my gall upon the ground.
texts.job.16.14: He breaketh me with breach upon breach; he runneth upon me like a mighty man.
texts.job.16.15: I have sewed sackcloth upon my skin, and rolled my horn in the dust.
texts.job.16.16: My face is red with weeping, and on my eyelids is the shadow of death;
texts.job.16.17: Although there is no violence in my hands, and my prayer is pure.
texts.job.16.18: O earth, cover not my blood, and let there be no place for my cry!
texts.job.16.19: Even now, behold, my Witness is in the heavens, and he that voucheth for me is in the heights.
texts.job.16.20: My friends are my mockers; mine eye poureth out tears unto +God.
texts.job.16.21: Oh that there were arbitration for a man with +God, as a son of man for his friend!
texts.job.16.22: For years [few] in number shall pass, -- and I shall go the way [whence] I shall not return.
texts.job.17.1: My breath is corrupt, my days are extinct, the graves are mine.
texts.job.17.2: Are there not mockers around me? and doth [not] mine eye abide in their provocation?
texts.job.17.3: Lay down now [a pledge], be thou surety for me with thyself: who is he that striketh hands with me?
texts.job.17.4: For thou hast hidden their heart from understanding; therefore thou wilt not exalt [them].
texts.job.17.5: He that betrayeth friends for a prey -- even the eyes of his children shall fail.
texts.job.17.6: And he hath made me a proverb of the peoples; and I am become one to be spit on in the face.
texts.job.17.7: And mine eye is dim by reason of grief, and all my members are as a shadow.
texts.job.17.8: Upright men [shall be] astonished at this, and the innocent shall be stirred up against the ungodly;
texts.job.17.9: But the righteous shall hold on his way, and he that hath clean hands shall increase in strength.
texts.job.17.10: But as for you all, pray come on again; and I shall not find one wise man among you.
texts.job.17.11: My days are past, my purposes are broken off, the cherished thoughts of my heart.
texts.job.17.12: They change the night into day; the light [they imagine] near in presence of the darkness.
texts.job.17.13: If I wait, Sheol is my house; I spread my bed in the darkness:
texts.job.17.14: I cry to the grave, Thou art my father! to the worm, My mother, and my sister!
texts.job.17.15: And where is then my hope? yea, my hope, who shall see it?
texts.job.17.16: It shall go down to the bars of Sheol, when [our] rest shall be together in the dust.
texts.job.18.1: And Bildad the Shuhite answered and said,
texts.job.18.2: How long will ye hunt for words? Be intelligent, and then we will speak.
texts.job.18.3: Wherefore are we counted as beasts, and reputed stupid in your sight?
texts.job.18.4: Thou that tearest thyself in thine anger, shall the earth be forsaken for thee? and shall the rock be removed out of its place?
texts.job.18.5: Yea, the light of the wicked shall be put out, and the flame of his fire shall not shine.
texts.job.18.6: The light shall become dark in his tent, and his lamp over him shall be put out.
texts.job.18.7: The steps of his strength shall be straitened, and his own counsel shall cast him down.
texts.job.18.8: For he is sent into the net by his own feet, and he walketh on the meshes;
texts.job.18.9: The gin taketh [him] by the heel, the snare layeth hold on him;
