texts.job.18.10: A cord is hidden for him in the ground, and his trap in the way.
texts.job.18.11: Terrors make him afraid on every side, and chase him at his footsteps.
texts.job.18.12: His strength is hunger-bitten, and calamity is ready at his side.
texts.job.18.13: The firstborn of death devoureth the members of his body; it will devour his members.
texts.job.18.14: His confidence shall be rooted out of his tent, and it shall lead him away to the king of terrors:
texts.job.18.15: They who are none of his shall dwell in his tent; brimstone shall be showered upon his habitation:
texts.job.18.16: His roots shall be dried up beneath, and above shall his branch be cut off;
texts.job.18.17: His remembrance shall perish from the earth, and he shall have no name on the pasture-grounds.
texts.job.18.18: He is driven from light into darkness, and chased out of the world.
texts.job.18.19: He hath neither son nor grandson among his people, nor any remaining in the places of his sojourn.
texts.job.18.20: They that come after shall be astonished at his day, as they that went before [them] were affrighted.
texts.job.18.21: Surely, such are the dwellings of the unrighteous man, and such the place of him that knoweth not ùGod.
texts.job.19.2: How long will ye vex my soul, and crush me with words?
texts.job.19.3: These ten times have ye reproached me; ye are not ashamed to stupefy me.
texts.job.19.4: And be it [that] I have erred, mine error remaineth with myself.
texts.job.19.5: If indeed ye will magnify yourselves against me, and prove against me my reproach,
texts.job.19.6: Know now that +God hath overthrown me, and hath surrounded me with his net.
texts.job.19.7: Behold, I cry out of wrong, and I am not heard; I cry aloud, but there is no judgment.
texts.job.19.8: He hath hedged up my way that I cannot pass, and he hath set darkness in my paths.
texts.job.19.9: He hath stripped me of my glory, and taken the crown from my head.
texts.job.19.10: He breaketh me down on every side, and I am gone; and my hope hath he torn up as a tree.
texts.job.19.11: And he hath kindled his anger against me, and hath counted me unto him as one of his enemies.
texts.job.19.12: His troops have come together and cast up their way against me, and have encamped round about my tent.
texts.job.19.13: He hath put my brethren far from me, and mine acquaintance are quite estranged from me.
texts.job.19.14: My kinsfolk have failed, and my known friends have forgotten me.
texts.job.19.15: The sojourners in my house and my maids count me as a stranger; I am an alien in their sight.
texts.job.19.16: I called my servant, and he answered not; I entreated him with my mouth.
texts.job.19.17: My breath is strange to my wife, and my entreaties to the children of my [mother's] womb.
texts.job.19.18: Even young children despise me; I rise up, and they speak against me.
texts.job.19.19: All my intimate friends abhor me, and they whom I loved are turned against me.
texts.job.19.20: My bones cleave to my skin and to my flesh, and I am escaped with the skin of my teeth.
texts.job.19.21: Have pity upon me, have pity upon me, ye my friends; for the hand of +God hath touched me.
texts.job.19.22: Why do ye persecute me as ùGod, and are not satisfied with my flesh?
texts.job.19.23: Oh would that my words were written! oh that they were inscribed in a book!
texts.job.19.24: That with an iron style and lead they were graven in the rock for ever!
texts.job.19.25: And [as for] me, I know that my Redeemer liveth, and the Last, he shall stand upon the earth;
texts.job.19.26: And [if] after my skin this shall be destroyed, yet from out of my flesh shall I see +God;
texts.job.19.27: Whom I shall see for myself, and mine eyes shall behold, and not another: -- my reins are consumed within me.
texts.job.19.28: If ye say, How shall we persecute him? when the root of the matter is found in me,
texts.job.19.29: Be ye yourselves afraid of the sword! for the sword is fury against misdeeds, that ye may know there is a judgment.
texts.job.20.1: And Zophar the Naamathite answered and said,
texts.job.20.2: Therefore do my thoughts give me an answer, and for this is my haste within me.
texts.job.20.3: I hear a reproof putting me to shame; and [my] spirit answereth me by mine understanding.
texts.job.20.4: Knowest thou [not] this, that of old, since man was placed upon earth,
texts.job.20.5: The exultation of the wicked is short, and the joy of the ungodly man but for a moment?
texts.job.20.6: Though his height mount up to the heavens, and his head reach unto the clouds,
texts.job.20.7: Like his own dung doth he perish for ever; they which have seen him shall say, Where is he?
texts.job.20.8: He flieth away as a dream, and is not found; and is chased away as a vision of the night.
texts.job.20.9: The eye which saw him shall [see him] not again; and his place beholdeth him no more.
texts.job.20.10: His children shall seek the favour of the poor, and his hands restore his wealth.
texts.job.20.11: His bones were full of his youthful strength; but it shall lie down with him in the dust.
texts.job.20.12: Though wickedness be sweet in his mouth [and] he hide it under his tongue,
texts.job.20.13: [Though] he spare it, and forsake it not, but keep it within his mouth,
texts.job.20.14: His food is turned in his bowels; it is the gall of asps within him.
texts.job.20.15: He hath swallowed down riches, but he shall vomit them up again: ùGod shall cast them out of his belly.
texts.job.20.16: He shall suck the poison of asps; the viper's tongue shall kill him.
texts.job.20.17: He shall not see streams, rivers, brooks of honey and butter.
texts.job.20.18: That which he laboured for shall he restore, and not swallow down; its restitution shall be according to the value, and he shall not rejoice [therein].
texts.job.20.19: For he hath oppressed, hath forsaken the poor; he hath violently taken away a house that he did not build.
texts.job.20.20: Because he knew no rest in his craving, he shall save nought of what he most desired.
texts.job.20.21: Nothing escaped his greediness; therefore his prosperity shall not endure.
texts.job.20.22: In the fulness of his sufficiency he shall be in straits; every hand of the wretched shall come upon him.
texts.job.20.23: It shall be that, to fill his belly, he will cast his fierce anger upon him, and will rain it upon him into his flesh.
texts.job.20.24: If he have fled from the iron weapon, the bow of brass shall strike him through.
texts.job.20.25: He draweth it forth; it cometh out of his body, and the glittering point out of his gall: terrors are upon him.
texts.job.20.26: All darkness is laid up for his treasures: a fire not blown shall devour him; it shall feed upon what is left in his tent.
texts.job.20.27: The heavens shall reveal his iniquity, and the earth shall rise up against him.
texts.job.20.28: The increase of his house shall depart, flowing away in the day of his anger.
texts.job.20.29: This is the portion of the wicked man from God, and the heritage appointed to him by ùGod.
texts.job.21.2: Hear attentively my speech, and let this replace your consolations.
texts.job.21.3: Suffer me and I will speak; and after I have spoken, mock on!
texts.job.21.4: As for me, is my complaint to a man? or wherefore should not my spirit be impatient?
texts.job.21.5: Mark me, and be astonished, and lay the hand upon the mouth.
texts.job.21.6: Even when I think [thereon], I am affrighted, and trembling taketh hold of my flesh.
texts.job.21.7: Wherefore do the wicked live, grow old, yea, become mighty in power?
texts.job.21.8: Their seed is established with them in their sight, and their offspring before their eyes.
texts.job.21.9: Their houses are safe from fear, neither is the rod of +God upon them.
texts.job.21.10: Their bull gendereth, and faileth not; their cow calveth, and casteth not her calf.
texts.job.21.11: They send forth their little ones like a flock, and their children dance.
texts.job.21.12: They shout to the tambour and harp, and rejoice at the sound of the pipe.
texts.job.21.13: They spend their days in prosperity, and in a moment go down to Sheol.
texts.job.21.14: And they say unto ùGod, Depart from us, for we desire not the knowledge of thy ways!
texts.job.21.15: What is the Almighty that we should serve him? and what are we profited if we pray unto him?
texts.job.21.16: Behold, their prosperity is not in their hand. The counsel of the wicked be far from me!
texts.job.21.17: How often is the lamp of the wicked put out, and cometh their calamity upon them? Doth he distribute sorrows [to them] in his anger?
texts.job.21.18: Do they become as stubble before the wind, and as chaff that the storm carrieth away?
texts.job.21.19: +God layeth up [the punishment of] his iniquity for his children; he rewardeth him, and he shall know [it]:
texts.job.21.20: His eyes shall see his destruction, and he shall drink of the fury of the Almighty.
texts.job.21.21: For what pleasure should he have in his house after him, when the number of his months is cut off?
texts.job.21.22: Can any teach ùGod knowledge? And he it is that judgeth those that are high.
texts.job.21.23: One dieth in his full strength, being wholly at ease and quiet;
texts.job.21.24: His sides are full of fat, and the marrow of his bones is moistened;
texts.job.21.25: And another dieth in bitterness of soul, and hath not tasted good:
texts.job.21.26: Together they lie down in the dust, and the worms cover them.
texts.job.21.27: Lo, I know your thoughts, and the devices ye wrongfully imagine against me.
texts.job.21.28: For ye say, Where is the house of the noble? and where the tent of the dwellings of the wicked?
texts.job.21.29: Have ye not asked the wayfarers? and do ye not regard their tokens:
texts.job.21.30: That the wicked is reserved for the day of calamity? They are led forth to the day of wrath.
texts.job.21.31: Who shall declare his way to his face? and who shall repay him what he hath done?
texts.job.21.32: Yet is he carried to the graves, and watch is kept over the tomb.
texts.job.21.33: The clods of the valley are sweet unto him; and every man followeth suit after him, as there were innumerable before him.
texts.job.21.34: How then comfort ye me in vain? Your answers remain perfidious.
texts.job.22.1: And Eliphaz the Temanite answered and said,
texts.job.22.2: Can a man be profitable to ùGod? surely it is unto himself that the wise man is profitable.
texts.job.22.3: Is it any pleasure to the Almighty if thou art righteous? And is it gain [to him] that thou makest thy ways perfect?
texts.job.22.4: Will he reason with thee for fear of thee? Will he enter with thee into judgment?
texts.job.22.5: Is not thy wickedness great? and thine iniquities without end?
texts.job.22.6: For thou hast taken a pledge of thy brother for nought, and stripped off the clothing of the naked.
texts.job.22.7: Thou hast not given water to the fainting to drink, and thou hast withholden bread from the hungry.
texts.job.22.8: But the powerful man, he had the land; and the man of high rank dwelt in it.
texts.job.22.9: Widows hast thou sent empty away, and the arms of the fatherless have been broken.
texts.job.22.10: Therefore snares are round about thee, and sudden fear troubleth thee;
texts.job.22.11: Or darkness, that thou canst not see, and floods of waters cover thee.
texts.job.22.12: Is not +God in the height of the heavens? And behold the summit of the stars: how exalted are they!
texts.job.22.13: And thou sayest, What doth ùGod know? will he judge through the dark cloud?
texts.job.22.14: Thick clouds are a covering to him, that he seeth not; and he walketh on the vault of the heavens.
texts.job.22.15: Dost thou mark the ancient path which wicked men have trodden?
texts.job.22.16: Who were carried off before the time, whose foundation was overflowed with a flood;
texts.job.22.17: Who said unto ùGod, Depart from us! and what could the Almighty do to them?
texts.job.22.18: Yet he filled their houses with good. But the counsel of the wicked is far from me.
texts.job.22.19: The righteous see it, and are glad; and the innocent laugh them to scorn:
texts.job.22.20: Is not he who rose against us destroyed, and doth not the fire consume his residue?
texts.job.22.21: Reconcile thyself now with him, and be at peace: thereby good shall come unto thee.
texts.job.22.22: Receive, I pray thee, instruction from his mouth, and lay up his words in thy heart.
texts.job.22.23: If thou return to the Almighty, thou shalt be built up. If thou remove unrighteousness far from thy tents,
texts.job.22.24: And put the precious ore with the dust, and [the gold of] Ophir among the stones of the torrents,
texts.job.22.25: Then the Almighty will be thy precious ore, and silver heaped up unto thee;
texts.job.22.26: Yea, then shalt thou delight thyself in the Almighty, and shalt lift up thy face unto +God:
texts.job.22.27: Thou shalt make thy prayer unto him, and he will hear thee, and thou shalt pay thy vows;
texts.job.22.28: And thou shalt decree a thing, and it shall be established unto thee; and light shall shine upon thy ways.
texts.job.22.29: When they are made low, then thou shalt say, Rise up! and he shall save him that is of downcast eyes.
texts.job.22.30: [Even] him that is not innocent shall he deliver; yea, he shall be delivered by the pureness of thy hands.
texts.job.23.2: Even to-day is my complaint bitter: my stroke is heavier than my groaning.
texts.job.23.3: Oh that I knew where I might find him, that I might come to his seat!
texts.job.23.4: I would order the cause before him, and fill my mouth with arguments;
texts.job.23.5: I would know the words he would answer me, and understand what he would say unto me.
texts.job.23.6: Would he plead against me with [his] great power? Nay; but he would give heed unto me.
texts.job.23.7: There would an upright man reason with him; and I should be delivered for ever from my judge.
texts.job.23.8: Lo, I go forward, but he is not there; and backward, but I do not perceive him;
texts.job.23.9: On the left hand, where he doth work, but I behold [him] not; he hideth himself on the right hand, and I see [him] not.
texts.job.23.10: But he knoweth the way that I take; he trieth me, I shall come forth as gold.
texts.job.23.11: My foot hath held to his steps; his way have I kept, and not turned aside.
texts.job.23.12: Neither have I gone back from the commandment of his lips; I have laid up the words of his mouth more than the purpose of my own heart.
texts.job.23.13: But he is in one [mind], and who can turn him? And what his soul desireth, that will he do.
texts.job.23.14: For he will perform [what] is appointed for me; and many such things are with him.
texts.job.23.15: Therefore am I troubled at his presence; I consider, and I am afraid of him.
texts.job.23.16: For ùGod hath made my heart soft, and the Almighty troubleth me;
texts.job.23.17: Because I was not cut off before the darkness, neither hath he hidden the gloom from me.
texts.job.24.1: Why are not times treasured up with the Almighty? why do not they that know him see his days?
texts.job.24.2: They remove the landmarks; they violently take away the flocks and pasture them;
texts.job.24.3: They drive away the ass of the fatherless, they take the widow's ox for a pledge;
texts.job.24.4: They turn the needy out of the way: the afflicted of the land all hide themselves.
texts.job.24.5: Lo, [as] wild asses in the desert, they go forth to their work, seeking early for the prey: the wilderness [yieldeth] them food for [their] children.
texts.job.24.6: They reap in the field the fodder thereof, and they gather the vintage of the wicked;
texts.job.24.7: They pass the night naked without clothing, and have no covering in the cold;
texts.job.24.8: They are wet with the showers of the mountains, and for want of a shelter embrace the rock ...
texts.job.24.9: They pluck the fatherless from the breast, and take a pledge of the poor:
texts.job.24.10: These go naked without clothing, and, hungry, they bear the sheaf;
texts.job.24.11: They press out oil within their walls, they tread their winepresses, and suffer thirst.
texts.job.24.12: Men groan from out of the city, and the soul of the wounded crieth out; and +God imputeth not the impiety.
texts.job.24.13: There are those that rebel against the light; they know not the ways thereof, nor abide in the paths thereof.
texts.job.24.14: The murderer riseth with the light, killeth the afflicted and needy, and in the night is as a thief.
texts.job.24.15: And the eye of the adulterer waiteth for the twilight, saying, No eye shall see me; and he putteth a covering on [his] face.
texts.job.24.16: In the dark they dig through houses; by day they shut themselves in; they know not the light:
texts.job.24.17: For the morning is to them all [as] the shadow of death; for they are familiar with the terrors of the shadow of death.
texts.job.24.18: He is swift on the face of the waters; their portion is cursed on the earth: he turneth not unto the way of the vineyards.
texts.job.24.19: Drought and heat consume snow waters; so doth Sheol those that have sinned.
texts.job.24.20: The womb forgetteth him; the worm feedeth sweetly on him: he shall be no more remembered; and unrighteousness is broken as a tree, --
texts.job.24.21: He that despoileth the barren that beareth not, and doeth not good to the widow:
texts.job.24.22: He draweth also the mighty with his power; he riseth up, and no [man] is sure of life.
texts.job.24.23: [God] setteth him in safety, and he resteth thereon; but his eyes are upon their ways.
texts.job.24.24: They are exalted for a little, and are no more; they are laid low; like all [other] are they gathered, and are cut off as the tops of the ears of corn.
texts.job.24.25: If it be not so now, who will make me a liar, and make my speech nothing worth?
texts.job.25.1: And Bildad the Shuhite answered and said,
texts.job.25.2: Dominion and fear are with him; he maketh peace in his high places.
texts.job.25.3: Is there any number of his troops? and upon whom doth not his light arise?
texts.job.25.4: And how should man be just with ùGod? Or how should he be clean that is born of a woman?
texts.job.25.5: Lo, even the moon is not bright; and the stars are not pure in his sight:
texts.job.25.6: How much less man, a worm, and the son of man, a worm!
texts.job.26.2: How hast thou helped the powerless; how saved the arm that is without strength!
texts.job.26.3: How hast thou counselled him that hath no wisdom, and abundantly declared the thing as it is!
texts.job.26.4: For whom hast thou uttered words? and whose spirit came from thee?
texts.job.26.5: The shades tremble beneath the waters and the inhabitants thereof;
texts.job.26.6: Sheol is naked before him, and destruction hath no covering.
texts.job.26.7: He stretcheth out the north over empty space, he hangeth the earth upon nothing;
texts.job.26.8: He bindeth up the waters in his thick clouds, and the cloud is not rent under them.
texts.job.26.9: He covereth the face of his throne, he spreadeth his cloud upon it.
texts.job.26.10: He hath traced a fixed circle over the waters, unto the confines of light and darkness.
texts.job.26.11: The pillars of the heavens tremble and are astonished at his rebuke.
texts.job.26.12: He stirreth up the sea by his power, and by his understanding he smiteth through Rahab.
texts.job.26.13: By his Spirit the heavens are adorned; his hand hath formed the fleeing serpent.
texts.job.26.14: Lo, these are the borders of his ways; but what a whisper of a word do we hear of him! And the thunder of his power, who can understand?
texts.job.27.1: And Job continued his parable and said,
texts.job.27.2: [As] ùGod liveth, who hath taken away my right, and the Almighty, who hath embittered my soul,
texts.job.27.3: All the while my breath is in me, and the spirit of +God is in my nostrils,
texts.job.27.4: My lips shall not speak unrighteousness, nor my tongue utter deceit!
texts.job.27.5: Be it far from me that I should justify you; till I die I will not remove my blamelessness from me.
texts.job.27.6: My righteousness I hold fast, and will not let it go: my heart reproacheth [me] not one of my days.
texts.job.27.7: Let mine enemy be as the wicked, and he that riseth up against me as the unrighteous.
texts.job.27.8: For what is the hope of the ungodly, when [God] cutteth him off, when +God taketh away his soul?
texts.job.27.9: Will ùGod hear his cry when distress cometh upon him?
texts.job.27.10: Doth he delight himself in the Almighty? will he at all times call upon +God?
texts.job.27.11: I will teach you concerning the hand of ùGod; what is with the Almighty will I not conceal.
texts.job.27.12: Behold, ye yourselves have all seen [it]; and why are ye thus altogether vain?
texts.job.27.13: This is the portion of the wicked man with ùGod, and the heritage of the violent, which they receive from the Almighty: --
texts.job.27.14: If his children be multiplied, it is for the sword, and his offspring shall not be satisfied with bread;
texts.job.27.15: Those that remain of him shall be buried by death, and his widows shall not weep.
texts.job.27.16: Though he heap up silver as the dust, and prepare clothing as the clay;
texts.job.27.17: He may prepare it, but the just shall put it on; and the innocent shall divide the silver.
texts.job.27.18: He buildeth his house as the moth, and as a booth that a keeper maketh.
texts.job.27.19: He lieth down rich, but will do so no more; he openeth his eyes, and he is not.
texts.job.27.20: Terrors overtake him like waters; a whirlwind stealeth him away in the night.
texts.job.27.21: The east wind carrieth him away and he is gone; and as a storm it hurleth him out of his place.
texts.job.27.22: And [God] shall cast upon him and not spare: he would fain flee out of his hand.
texts.job.27.23: [Men] shall clap their hands at him, and shall hiss him out of his place.
texts.job.28.1: Surely there is a vein for the silver, and a place for gold which they refine;
texts.job.28.2: Iron is taken out of the dust, and copper is molten out of the stone.
texts.job.28.3: [Man] putteth an end to the darkness, and exploreth to the utmost limit, the stones of darkness and of the shadow of death.
texts.job.28.4: He openeth a shaft far from the inhabitants [of the earth]: forgotten of the foot, they hang suspended; away below men they hover.
texts.job.28.5: As for the earth, out of it cometh bread, and underneath it is turned up as by fire;
texts.job.28.6: The stones of it are the place of sapphires, and it hath dust of gold.
texts.job.28.7: It is a path no bird of prey knoweth, and the vulture's eye hath not seen it;
texts.job.28.8: The proud beasts have not trodden it, nor the fierce lion passed over it.
texts.job.28.9: [Man] putteth forth his hand upon the flinty rock, he overturneth the mountains by the root.
texts.job.28.10: He cutteth out channels in the rocks, and his eye seeth every precious thing.
texts.job.28.11: He bindeth the streams that they drip not, and what is hidden he bringeth forth to light.
texts.job.28.12: But wisdom, where shall it be found? and where is the place of understanding?
texts.job.28.13: Man knoweth not the value thereof; and it is not found in the land of the living.
texts.job.28.14: The deep saith, It is not in me; and the sea saith, It is not with me.
texts.job.28.15: Choice gold cannot be given for it, nor silver be weighed for its price.
texts.job.28.16: It is not set in the balance with gold of Ophir, with the precious onyx, and the sapphire.
texts.job.28.17: Gold and glass cannot be compared to it, nor vessels of fine gold be its exchange.
texts.job.28.18: Corals and crystal are no more remembered; yea, the acquisition of wisdom is above rubies.
texts.job.28.19: The topaz of Ethiopia shall not be compared to it, neither shall it be set in the balance with pure gold.
texts.job.28.20: Whence then cometh wisdom? and where is the place of understanding?
texts.job.28.21: For it is hidden from the eyes of all living, and concealed from the fowl of the heavens.
texts.job.28.22: Destruction and death say, We have heard its report with our ears.
texts.job.28.23: God understandeth the way thereof, and he knoweth its place:
texts.job.28.24: For he looketh to the ends of the earth, he seeth under the whole heaven.
texts.job.28.25: In making a weight for the wind, and meting out the waters by measure,
texts.job.28.26: In appointing a statute for the rain, and a way for the thunder's flash:
texts.job.28.27: Then did he see it, and declare it; he established it, yea, and searched it out;
texts.job.28.28: And unto man he said, Lo, the fear of the Lord, that is wisdom; and to depart from evil is understanding.
texts.job.29.1: And Job continued his parable and said,
texts.job.29.2: Oh that I were as in months past, as in the days when +God preserved me;
texts.job.29.3: When his lamp shone over my head, [and] by his light I walked through darkness;
texts.job.29.4: As I was in the days of my youth, when the secret counsel of +God was over my tent,
texts.job.29.5: When the Almighty was yet with me, my young men round about me;
texts.job.29.6: When my steps were bathed in milk, and the rock poured out beside me rivers of oil! ...
texts.job.29.7: When I went out to the gate by the city, when I prepared my seat on the broadway,
texts.job.29.8: The young men saw me, and hid themselves; and the aged arose [and] stood up;
texts.job.29.9: Princes refrained from talking, and laid the hand on their mouth;
texts.job.29.10: The voice of the nobles was hushed, and their tongue cleaved to their palate.
texts.job.29.11: When the ear heard [me], then it blessed me, and when the eye saw [me], it gave witness to me;
texts.job.29.12: For I delivered the afflicted that cried, and the fatherless who had no helper.
texts.job.29.13: The blessing of him that was perishing came upon me, and I caused the widow's heart to sing for joy.
texts.job.29.14: I put on righteousness, and it clothed me; my justice was as a mantle and a turban.
texts.job.29.15: I was eyes to the blind, and feet was I to the lame;
texts.job.29.16: I was a father to the needy, and the cause which I knew not I searched out;
texts.job.29.17: And I broke the jaws of the unrighteous, and plucked the spoil out of his teeth.
texts.job.29.18: And I said, I shall die in my nest, and multiply my days as the sand;
texts.job.29.19: My root shall be spread out to the waters, and the dew will lie all night on my branch;
texts.job.29.20: My glory shall be fresh in me, and my bow be renewed in my hand.
texts.job.29.21: Unto me they listened, and waited, and kept silence for my counsel:
texts.job.29.22: After my words they spoke not again, and my speech dropped upon them;
texts.job.29.23: And they waited for me as for the rain, and they opened their mouth wide as for the latter rain.
texts.job.29.24: [If] I laughed on them, they believed [it] not; and they troubled not the serenity of my countenance.
texts.job.29.25: I chose their way, and sat as chief, and dwelt as a king in the army, as one that comforteth mourners.
texts.job.30.1: But now they that are younger than I have me in derision, whose fathers I would have disdained to set with the dogs of my flock.
texts.job.30.2: Yea, whereto [should] the strength of their hands [profit] me, [men] in whom vigour hath perished?
texts.job.30.3: Withered up through want and hunger, they flee into waste places long since desolate and desert:
texts.job.30.4: They gather the salt-wort among the bushes, and the roots of the broom for their food.
texts.job.30.5: They are driven forth from among [men] -- they cry after them as after a thief --
texts.job.30.6: To dwell in gloomy gorges, in caves of the earth and the rocks:
texts.job.30.7: They bray among the bushes; under the brambles they are gathered together:
texts.job.30.8: Sons of fools, and sons of nameless sires, they are driven out of the land.
texts.job.30.9: And now I am their song, yea, I am their byword.
texts.job.30.10: They abhor me, they stand aloof from me, yea, they spare not to spit in my face.
texts.job.30.11: For he hath loosed my cord and afflicted me; so they cast off the bridle before me.
texts.job.30.12: At [my] right hand rise the young brood; they push away my feet, and raise up against me their pernicious ways;
texts.job.30.13: They mar my path, they set forward my calamity, without any to help them;
texts.job.30.14: They come in as through a wide breach: amid the confusion they roll themselves onward.
texts.job.30.15: Terrors are turned against me; they pursue mine honour as the wind; and my welfare is passed away like a cloud.
texts.job.30.16: And now my soul is poured out in me; days of affliction have taken hold upon me.
texts.job.30.17: The night pierceth through my bones [and detacheth them] from me, and my gnawing pains take no rest:
texts.job.30.18: By their great force they have become my raiment; they bind me about as the collar of my coat.
texts.job.30.19: He hath cast me into the mire, and I have become like dust and ashes.
texts.job.30.20: I cry unto thee, and thou answerest me not; I stand up, and thou lookest at me.
texts.job.30.21: Thou art changed to a cruel one to me; with the strength of thy hand thou pursuest me.
texts.job.30.22: Thou liftest me up to the wind; thou causest me to be borne away, and dissolvest my substance.
texts.job.30.23: For I know that thou wilt bring me to death, and into the house of assemblage for all living.
texts.job.30.24: Indeed, no prayer [availeth] when he stretcheth out [his] hand: though they cry when he destroyeth.
texts.job.30.25: Did not I weep for him whose days were hard? was not my soul grieved for the needy?
texts.job.30.26: For I expected good, and there came evil; and I waited for light, but there came darkness.
texts.job.30.27: My bowels well up, and rest not; days of affliction have confronted me.
texts.job.30.28: I go about blackened, but not by the sun; I stand up, I cry in the congregation.
texts.job.30.29: I am become a brother to jackals, and a companion of ostriches.
texts.job.30.30: My skin is become black [and falleth] off me, and my bones are parched with heat.
texts.job.30.31: My harp also is [turned] to mourning, and my pipe into the voice of weepers.
texts.job.31.1: I made a covenant with mine eyes; and how should I fix my regard upon a maid?
texts.job.31.2: For what would have been [my] portion of +God from above, and what the heritage of the Almighty from on high?
texts.job.31.3: Is not calamity for the unrighteous? and misfortune for the workers of iniquity?
texts.job.31.4: Doth not he see my ways, and number all my steps?
texts.job.31.5: If I have walked with falsehood, and my foot hath hasted to deceit,
texts.job.31.6: (Let me be weighed in an even balance, and +God will take knowledge of my blamelessness;)
texts.job.31.7: If my step have turned out of the way, and my heart followed mine eyes, and if any blot cleaveth to my hands;
texts.job.31.8: Let me sow, and another eat; and let mine offspring be rooted out.
texts.job.31.9: If my heart have been enticed unto a woman, so that I laid wait at my neighbour's door,
texts.job.31.10: Let my wife grind for another, and let others bow down upon her.
texts.job.31.11: For this is an infamy; yea, it is an iniquity [to be judged by] the judges:
texts.job.31.12: For it is a fire that consumeth to destruction, and would root out all mine increase.
texts.job.31.13: If I have despised the cause of my bondman or of my bondmaid, when they contended with me,
texts.job.31.14: What then should I do when ùGod riseth up? and if he visited, what should I answer him?
texts.job.31.15: Did not he that made me in the womb make him? and did not One fashion us in the womb?
texts.job.31.16: If I have withheld the poor from [their] desire, or caused the eyes of the widow to fail;
texts.job.31.17: Or have eaten my morsel alone, so that the fatherless ate not thereof,
texts.job.31.18: (For from my youth he grew up with me as with a father, and I have guided the [widow] from my mother's womb;)
texts.job.31.19: If I have seen any perishing for want of clothing, or any needy without covering;
texts.job.31.20: If his loins have not blessed me, and if he were not warmed with the fleece of my lambs;
texts.job.31.21: If I have lifted up my hand against an orphan, because I saw my help in the gate:
texts.job.31.22: [Then] let my shoulder fall from the shoulder-blade, and mine arm be broken from the bone!
texts.job.31.23: For calamity from ùGod was a terror to me, and by reason of his excellency I was powerless.
texts.job.31.24: If I have made gold my hope, or said to the fine gold, My confidence!
texts.job.31.25: If I rejoiced because my wealth was great, and because my hand had gotten much;
texts.job.31.26: If I beheld the sun when it shone, or the moon walking in brightness,
texts.job.31.27: And my heart have been secretly enticed, so that my mouth kissed my hand:
texts.job.31.28: This also would be an iniquity for the judge, for I should have denied the ùGod who is above.
texts.job.31.29: If I rejoiced at the destruction of him that hated me, and exulted when evil befell him;
texts.job.31.30: (Neither have I suffered my mouth to sin by asking his life with a curse;)
texts.job.31.31: If the men of my tent said not, Who shall find one that hath not been satisfied with his meat? --
texts.job.31.32: The stranger did not lodge without; I opened my doors to the pathway.
texts.job.31.33: If I covered my transgressions as Adam, by hiding mine iniquity in my bosom,
texts.job.31.34: Because I feared the great multitude, and the contempt of families terrified me, so that I kept silence, and went not out of the door, ...
texts.job.31.35: Oh that I had one to hear me! Behold my signature: let the Almighty answer me! And let mine opponent write an accusation!
texts.job.31.36: Would I not take it upon my shoulder? I would bind it on to me [as] a crown;
texts.job.31.37: I would declare unto him the number of my steps; as a prince would I come near to him.
texts.job.31.38: If my land cry out against me, and its furrows weep together;
texts.job.31.39: If I have eaten the fruits thereof without money, and have tormented to death the souls of its owners:
texts.job.31.40: Let thistles grow instead of wheat, and tares instead of barley. The words of Job are ended.
texts.job.32.1: And these three men ceased to answer Job, because he was righteous in his own eyes.
texts.job.32.2: Then was kindled the anger of Elihu the son of Barachel, the Buzite, of the family of Ram: against Job was his anger kindled, because he justified himself rather than God;
texts.job.32.3: and against his three friends was his anger kindled, because they found no answer, and [yet] condemned Job.
texts.job.32.4: But Elihu had waited till Job had finished speaking, because they were older than he.
texts.job.32.5: And Elihu saw that there was no answer in the mouth of the three men, and his anger was kindled.
texts.job.32.6: And Elihu the son of Barachel the Buzite answered and said, I am young, and ye are aged; wherefore I was timid, and feared to shew you what I know.
texts.job.32.7: I said, Let days speak, and multitude of years teach wisdom.
texts.job.32.8: But there is a spirit which is in man; and the breath of the Almighty giveth them understanding.
texts.job.32.9: It is not the great that are wise; neither do the aged understand judgment.
texts.job.32.10: Therefore I say, Hearken to me; I also will shew what I know.
texts.job.32.11: Lo, I waited for your words; I gave ear to your reasonings, until ye searched out what to say.
texts.job.32.12: Yea, I gave you mine attention, and behold, there was none of you that confuted Job, that answered his words;
texts.job.32.13: That ye may not say, We have found out wisdom; ùGod will make him yield, not man.
texts.job.32.14: Now he hath not directed [his] words against me; and I will not answer him with your speeches. ...
texts.job.32.15: They were amazed, they answered no more; words failed them.
texts.job.32.16: And I waited, for they spoke not, but stood still, and answered no more; --
texts.job.32.17: I will answer, I also in my turn, I also will shew what I know:
texts.job.32.18: For I am full of matter, the spirit within me constraineth me.
texts.job.32.19: Behold, my belly is as wine which hath no vent; like new flasks, it is ready to burst.
texts.job.32.20: I will speak, that I may find relief; I will open my lips and answer.
texts.job.32.21: Let me not, I pray you, accept any man's person; neither will I give flattery to man.
texts.job.32.22: For I know not how to flatter; my Maker would soon take me away.
texts.job.33.1: Howbeit, Job, I pray thee, hear mine utterances, and hearken to all my words.
texts.job.33.2: Behold now, I have opened my mouth, my tongue speaketh in my palate,
texts.job.33.3: My words shall be of the uprightness of my heart, and my lips shall utter knowledge purely.
texts.job.33.4: The Spirit of ùGod hath made me, and the breath of the Almighty hath given me life.
texts.job.33.5: If thou canst, answer me; array [thy words] before me: take thy stand.
texts.job.33.6: Behold, before ùGod I am as thou; I also am formed out of the clay.
texts.job.33.7: Behold, my terror shall not make thee afraid, nor my burden be heavy upon thee.
texts.job.33.8: Surely thou hast spoken in my hearing, and I have heard the voice of [thy] words: --
texts.job.33.9: I am clean without transgression; I am pure, and there is no iniquity in me;
texts.job.33.10: Lo, he findeth occasions of hostility against me, he counteth me for his enemy;
texts.job.33.11: He putteth my feet in the stocks, he marketh all my paths.
texts.job.33.12: Behold, I will answer thee in this, thou art not right; for +God is greater than man.
texts.job.33.13: Why dost thou strive against him? for he giveth not account of any of his matters.
texts.job.33.14: For ùGod speaketh once, and twice, -- [and man] perceiveth it not --
texts.job.33.15: In a dream, in a vision of the night, when deep sleep falleth upon men, in slumberings upon the bed;
texts.job.33.16: Then he openeth men's ears, and sealeth their instruction,
texts.job.33.17: That he may withdraw man [from his] work, and hide pride from man.
texts.job.33.18: He keepeth back his soul from the pit, and his life from passing away by the sword.
texts.job.33.19: He is chastened also with pain upon his bed, and with constant strife in his bones;
texts.job.33.20: And his life abhorreth bread, and his soul dainty food;
texts.job.33.21: His flesh is consumed away from view, and his bones that were not seen stick out;
texts.job.33.22: And his soul draweth near to the pit, and his life to the destroyers.
texts.job.33.23: If there be a messenger with him, an interpreter, one among a thousand, to shew unto man his duty;
texts.job.33.24: Then he will be gracious unto him, and say, Deliver him from going down to the pit: I have found a ransom.
texts.job.33.25: His flesh shall be fresher than in childhood; he shall return to the days of his youth.
texts.job.33.26: He shall pray unto +God, and he will receive him with favour; and he shall see his face with shoutings, and he will render unto man his righteousness.
texts.job.33.27: He will sing before men, and say, I have sinned, and perverted what was right, and it hath not been requited to me;
texts.job.33.28: He hath delivered my soul from going into the pit, and my life shall see the light.
texts.job.33.29: Lo, all these [things] worketh ùGod twice, thrice, with man,
texts.job.33.30: To bring back his soul from the pit, that he may be enlightened with the light of the living.
texts.job.33.31: Mark well, Job, hearken unto me; be silent, and I will speak.
texts.job.33.32: If thou hast anything to say, answer me; speak, for I desire to justify thee.
texts.job.33.33: If not, hearken thou unto me; be silent, and I will teach thee wisdom.
texts.job.34.2: Hear my words, ye wise [men]; and give ear unto me, ye that have knowledge.
texts.job.34.3: For the ear trieth words, as the palate tasteth food.
texts.job.34.4: Let us choose for ourselves what is right; let us know among ourselves what is good!
texts.job.34.5: For Job hath said, I am righteous, and ùGod hath taken away my judgment:
texts.job.34.6: Should I lie against my right? My wound is incurable without transgression.
texts.job.34.7: What man is like Job? he drinketh up scorning like water,
texts.job.34.8: And goeth in company with workers of iniquity, and walketh with wicked men.
texts.job.34.9: For he hath said, It profiteth not a man if he delight himself in God.
texts.job.34.10: Therefore hearken unto me, ye men of understanding: Far be wickedness from ùGod, and wrong from the Almighty!
texts.job.34.11: For a man's work will he render to him, and cause every one to find according to [his] way.
texts.job.34.12: Yea, surely, ùGod acteth not wickedly, and the Almighty perverteth not judgment.
texts.job.34.13: Who hath entrusted to him the earth? and who hath disposed the whole world?
texts.job.34.14: If he only thought of himself, [and] gathered unto him his spirit and his breath,
texts.job.34.15: All flesh would expire together, and man would return to the dust.
texts.job.34.16: If now [thou hast] understanding, hear this: give ear to the voice of my words!
texts.job.34.17: Should he that hateth right indeed govern? and wilt thou condemn the All-just?
texts.job.34.18: Shall one say to a king, Belial? to nobles, Wicked?
texts.job.34.19: [How then to him] that accepteth not the persons of princes, nor regardeth the rich man more than the poor? for they are all the work of his hands.
texts.job.34.20: In a moment they die, even at midnight the people are convulsed and pass away; and the strong are taken away without hand.
texts.job.34.21: For his eyes are upon the ways of man, and he seeth all his steps.
texts.job.34.22: There is no darkness, nor shadow of death, where the workers of iniquity may hide themselves.
texts.job.34.23: For he doth not long consider a man, to bring him before ùGod in judgment.
texts.job.34.24: He breaketh in pieces mighty men without inquiry, and setteth others in their stead;
texts.job.34.25: Since he knoweth their actions; and he overthroweth [them] in the night, and they are crushed.
texts.job.34.26: He striketh them as wicked men in the open sight of others,
texts.job.34.27: Because they have turned back from him, and would consider none of his ways;
texts.job.34.28: So that they cause the cry of the poor to come unto him, and he heareth the cry of the afflicted.
texts.job.34.29: When he giveth quietness, who then will disturb? and when he hideth [his] face, who shall behold him? and this towards a nation, or towards a man alike;
texts.job.34.30: That the ungodly man reign not, that the people be not ensnared.
texts.job.34.31: For hath he said unto ùGod, I bear [chastisement], I will not offend;
texts.job.34.32: What I see not, teach thou me; if I have done wrong, I will do so no more?
texts.job.34.33: Shall he recompense according to thy mind? for thou hast refused [his judgment]; for thou so choosest, and not I; speak then what thou knowest.
texts.job.34.34: Men of understanding will say to me, and a wise man who heareth me:
texts.job.34.35: Job hath spoken without knowledge, and his words were not with intelligence.
texts.job.34.36: Would that Job may be tried unto the end, because of [his] answers after the manner of evil men!
texts.job.34.37: For he addeth rebellion unto his sin, he clappeth [his hands] among us, and multiplieth his words against ùGod.
texts.job.35.2: Thinkest thou this to be right, that thou saidst, My righteousness is more than ùGod's?
texts.job.35.3: For thou hast asked of what profit it is unto thee: what do I gain more than if I had sinned?
texts.job.35.4: I will reply to thee in words, and to thy companions with thee.
texts.job.35.5: Look unto the heavens and see; and survey the skies: they are higher than thou.
texts.job.35.6: If thou sinnest, what doest thou against him? If thy transgressions be multiplied, what doest thou unto him?
texts.job.35.7: If thou be righteous, what givest thou to him? or what doth he receive of thy hand?
texts.job.35.8: Thy wickedness [may affect] a man as thou [art], and thy righteousness a son of man.
texts.job.35.9: By reason of the multitude of oppressions they cry; they cry out by reason of the arm of the mighty:
texts.job.35.10: But none saith, Where is +God my Maker, who giveth songs in the night,
texts.job.35.11: Who teacheth us more than the beasts of the earth, and maketh us wiser than the fowl of the heavens?
texts.job.35.12: There they cry, and he answereth not, because of the pride of evil men.
texts.job.35.13: Surely ùGod will not hear vanity, neither will the Almighty regard it.
texts.job.35.14: Although thou sayest thou dost not see him, judgment is before him, therefore wait for him.
texts.job.35.15: But now, because he hath not visited in his anger, doth not [Job] know [his] great arrogancy?
texts.job.35.16: For Job hath opened his mouth in vanity, and made words abundant without knowledge.
texts.job.36.2: Suffer me a little, and I will shew thee that I have yet words for +God.
texts.job.36.3: I will fetch my knowledge from afar, and will ascribe righteousness to my Creator.
texts.job.36.4: For truly my words shall be no falsehood: one perfect in knowledge is with thee.
texts.job.36.5: Lo, ùGod is mighty, but despiseth not [any]; mighty in strength of understanding:
texts.job.36.6: He saveth not the wicked alive; but he doeth justice to the afflicted.
texts.job.36.7: He withdraweth not his eyes from the righteous, but with kings on the throne doth he even set them for ever; and they are exalted.
texts.job.36.8: And if, bound in fetters, they be held in cords of affliction,
texts.job.36.9: Then he sheweth them their work, and their transgressions, because they have increased.
texts.job.36.10: And he openeth their ear to discipline, and commandeth that they return from iniquity.
texts.job.36.11: If they hearken and serve [him], they shall accomplish their days in prosperity, and their years in pleasures.
texts.job.36.12: But if they hearken not, they shall pass away by the sword, and expire without knowledge.
texts.job.36.13: But the godless in heart heap up anger; they cry not when he bindeth them:
texts.job.36.14: Their soul dieth in youth, and their life is among the unclean.
texts.job.36.15: But he delivereth the afflicted in his affliction, and openeth their ear in [their] oppression.
texts.job.36.16: Even so would he have allured thee out of the jaws of distress into a broad place, where there is no straitness; and the supply of thy table [would be] full of fatness.
texts.job.36.17: But thou art full of the judgments of the wicked: judgment and justice take hold [on thee].
texts.job.36.18: Because there is wrath, [beware] lest it take thee away through chastisement: then a great ransom could not avail thee.
texts.job.36.19: Will he esteem thy riches? Not gold, nor all the resources of strength!
texts.job.36.20: Desire not the night, when peoples are cut off from their place.
texts.job.36.21: Take heed, turn not to iniquity; for this hast thou chosen rather than affliction.
texts.job.36.22: Lo, ùGod is exalted in his power: who teacheth as he?
texts.job.36.23: Who hath appointed him his way? or who hath said, Thou hast wrought unrighteousness?
texts.job.36.24: Remember that thou magnify his work, which men celebrate.
texts.job.36.25: All men look at it; man beholdeth [it] afar off.
texts.job.36.26: Lo, ùGod is great, and we comprehend [him] not, neither can the number of his years be searched out.
texts.job.36.27: For he draweth up the drops of water: they distil in rain from the vapour which he formeth,
texts.job.36.28: Which the skies pour down [and] drop upon man abundantly.
texts.job.36.29: But can any understand the spreadings of the clouds, [or] the crashing of his pavilion?
texts.job.36.30: Lo, he spreadeth his light around him, and covereth the bottom of the sea.
texts.job.36.31: For with them he judgeth the peoples; he giveth food in abundance.
texts.job.36.32: [His] hands he covereth with lightning, and commandeth it where it is to strike.
texts.job.36.33: His thundering declareth concerning him; the cattle even, concerning its coming.
texts.job.37.1: Aye, my heart trembleth at this also, and leapeth up out of its place:
texts.job.37.2: Hear attentively the roar of his voice, and the murmur going forth from his mouth.
texts.job.37.3: He sendeth it forth under the whole heaven, and his lightning unto the ends of the earth.
texts.job.37.4: After it a voice roareth: he thundereth with the voice of his excellency, and holdeth not back the flashes when his voice is heard.
texts.job.37.5: ùGod thundereth marvellously with his voice, doing great things which we do not comprehend.
texts.job.37.6: For he saith to the snow, Fall on the earth! and to the pouring rain, even the pouring rains of his might.
texts.job.37.7: He sealeth up the hand of every man; that all men may know his work.
texts.job.37.8: And the wild beast goeth into its lair, and they remain in their dens.
texts.job.37.9: From the chamber [of the south] cometh the whirlwind; and cold from the winds of the north.
texts.job.37.10: By the breath of ùGod ice is given; and the breadth of the waters is straitened.
texts.job.37.11: Also with plentiful moisture he loadeth the thick clouds, his light dispels the cloud;
texts.job.37.12: And they are turned every way by his guidance, that they may do whatsoever he commandeth them upon the face of the circuit of the earth,
texts.job.37.13: Whether he cause it to come as a rod, or for his land, or in mercy.
texts.job.37.14: Hearken unto this, Job; stand still and discern the wondrous works of ùGod.
texts.job.37.15: Dost thou know how +God hath disposed them, and how he causeth the lightning of his cloud to flash?
texts.job.37.16: Dost thou know about the balancings of the clouds, the wondrous works of him that is perfect in knowledge?
texts.job.37.17: How thy garments become warm when he quieteth the earth by the south wind?
texts.job.37.18: Hast thou with him spread out the sky, firm, like a molten mirror?
texts.job.37.19: Teach us what we shall say unto him! We cannot order [our words] by reason of darkness.
texts.job.37.20: Shall it be told him if I would speak? if a man [so] say, surely he shall be swallowed up.
texts.job.37.21: And now [men] see not the light as it gleameth, it is [hidden] in the skies. But the wind passeth by and cleareth them.
texts.job.37.22: From the north cometh gold; with +God is terrible majesty.
texts.job.37.23: The Almighty, we cannot find him out: excellent in power, and in judgment, and in abundance of justice, he doth not afflict.
texts.job.37.24: Men do therefore fear him: he respecteth not any that are wise of heart.
texts.job.38.1: And Jehovah answered Job out of the whirlwind and said,
texts.job.38.2: Who is this that darkeneth counsel by words without knowledge?
texts.job.38.3: Gird up now thy loins like a man; and I will demand of thee, and inform thou me.
texts.job.38.4: Where wast thou when I founded the earth? Declare, if thou hast understanding.
texts.job.38.5: Who set the measures thereof -- if thou knowest? or who stretched a line upon it?
texts.job.38.6: Whereupon were the foundations thereof sunken? or who laid its corner-stone,
texts.job.38.7: When the morning stars sang together, and all the sons of God shouted for joy?
texts.job.38.8: And who shut up the sea with doors, when it burst forth, issuing out of the womb?
texts.job.38.9: When I made the cloud its garment, and thick darkness a swaddling band for it;
texts.job.38.10: When I cut out for it my boundary, and set bars and doors,
texts.job.38.11: And said, Hitherto shalt thou come and no further, and here shall thy proud waves be stayed?
texts.job.38.12: Hast thou since thy days commanded the morning? hast thou caused the dawn to know its place,
texts.job.38.13: That it might take hold of the ends of the earth, and the wicked might be shaken out of it?
texts.job.38.14: It is changed like the signet-clay; and [all things] stand forth as in a garment:
texts.job.38.15: And from the wicked their light is withholden, and the uplifted arm is broken.
texts.job.38.16: Hast thou entered as far as the springs of the sea? and hast thou walked in the recesses of the deep?
texts.job.38.17: Have the gates of death been revealed unto thee? and hast thou seen the gates of the shadow of death?
texts.job.38.18: Hath thine understanding compassed the breadths of the earth? Declare if thou knowest it all.
texts.job.38.19: Where is the way to where light dwelleth? and the darkness, where is its place,
texts.job.38.20: That thou shouldest take it to its bound, and that thou shouldest know the paths to its house?
texts.job.38.21: Thou knowest, for thou wast then born, and the number of thy days is great!
texts.job.38.22: Hast thou entered into the storehouses of the snow, and hast thou seen the treasuries of the hail,
texts.job.38.23: Which I have reserved for the time of distress, for the day of battle and war?
texts.job.38.24: By what way is the light parted, [and] the east wind scattered upon the earth?
texts.job.38.25: Who hath divided a channel for the rain-flood, and a way for the thunder's flash;
texts.job.38.26: To cause it to rain on the earth, where no one is; on the wilderness wherein there is not a man;
texts.job.38.27: To satisfy the desolate and waste [ground], and to cause the sprout of the grass to spring forth?
texts.job.38.28: Hath the rain a father? or who begetteth the drops of dew?
texts.job.38.29: Out of whose womb cometh the ice? and the hoary frost of heaven, who bringeth it forth?
texts.job.38.30: When the waters lie hidden as in stone, and the face of the deep holdeth fast together.
texts.job.38.31: Canst thou fasten the bands of the Pleiades, or loosen the cords of Orion?
texts.job.38.32: Dost thou bring forth the constellations each in its season? or dost thou guide the Bear with her sons?
texts.job.38.33: Knowest thou the ordinances of the heavens? dost thou determine their rule over the earth?
texts.job.38.34: Dost thou lift up thy voice to the clouds, that floods of waters may cover thee?
texts.job.38.35: Dost thou send forth lightnings that they may go, and say unto thee, Here we are?
texts.job.38.36: Who hath put wisdom in the inward parts? or who hath given understanding to the mind?
texts.job.38.37: Who numbereth the clouds with wisdom? or who poureth out the bottles of the heavens,
texts.job.38.38: When the dust runneth as into a molten mass, and the clods cleave fast together?
texts.job.38.39: Dost thou hunt the prey for the lioness, and dost thou satisfy the appetite of the young lions,
texts.job.38.40: When they crouch in [their] dens, [and] abide in the thicket to lie in wait?
texts.job.38.41: Who provideth for the raven his food, when his young ones cry unto ùGod, [and] they wander for lack of meat?
texts.job.39.1: Knowest thou the time when the wild goats of the rock bring forth? dost thou mark the calving of the hinds?
texts.job.39.2: Dost thou number the months that they fulfil? and knowest thou the time when they bring forth?
texts.job.39.3: They bow themselves, they give birth to their young ones, they cast out their pains;
texts.job.39.4: Their young ones become strong, they grow up in the open field, they go forth, and return not unto them.
texts.job.39.5: Who hath sent out the wild ass free? and who hath loosed the bands of the onager,
texts.job.39.6: Whose house I made the wilderness, and the salt plain his dwellings?
texts.job.39.7: He laugheth at the tumult of the city, and heareth not the shouts of the driver;
texts.job.39.8: The range of the mountains is his pasture, and he searcheth after every green thing.
texts.job.39.9: Will the buffalo be willing to serve thee, or will he lodge by thy crib?
texts.job.39.10: Canst thou bind the buffalo with his cord in the furrow? or will he harrow the valleys after thee?
texts.job.39.11: Wilt thou put confidence in him, because his strength is great? and wilt thou leave thy labour to him?
texts.job.39.12: Wilt thou trust him to bring home thy seed, and gather it into thy threshing-floor?
texts.job.39.13: The wing of the ostrich beats joyously -- But is it the stork's pinion and plumage?
texts.job.39.14: For she leaveth her eggs to the earth, and warmeth them in the dust,
texts.job.39.15: And forgetteth that the foot may crush them, or that the beast of the field may trample them.
texts.job.39.16: She is hardened against her young ones, as though they were not hers; her labour is in vain, without her concern.
texts.job.39.17: For +God hath deprived her of wisdom, and hath not furnished her with understanding.
texts.job.39.18: What time she lasheth herself on high, she scorneth the horse and his rider.
texts.job.39.19: Hast thou given strength to the horse? hast thou clothed his neck with the quivering mane?
texts.job.39.20: Dost thou make him to leap as a locust? His majestic snorting is terrible.
texts.job.39.21: He paweth in the valley, and rejoiceth in [his] strength; he goeth forth to meet the armed host.
texts.job.39.22: He laugheth at fear, and is not affrighted; neither turneth he back from before the sword.
texts.job.39.23: The quiver rattleth upon him, the glittering spear and the javelin.
texts.job.39.24: He swalloweth the ground with fierceness and rage, and cannot contain himself at the sound of the trumpet:
texts.job.39.25: At the noise of the trumpets he saith, Aha! and he smelleth the battle afar off, the thunder of the captains, and the shouting.
texts.job.39.26: Doth the hawk fly by thine intelligence, [and] stretch his wings toward the south?
texts.job.39.27: Doth the eagle mount up at thy command, and make his nest on high?
texts.job.39.28: He inhabiteth the rock and maketh his dwelling on the point of the cliff, and the fastness:
texts.job.39.29: From thence he spieth out the prey, his eyes look into the distance;
texts.job.39.30: And his young ones suck up blood; and where the slain are, there is he.
texts.job.40.1: And Jehovah answered Job and said,
texts.job.40.2: Shall he that will contend with the Almighty instruct [him]? he that reproveth +God, let him answer it.
texts.job.40.3: And Job answered Jehovah and said,
texts.job.40.4: Behold, I am nought: what shall I answer thee? I will lay my hand upon my mouth.
texts.job.40.5: Once have I spoken, and I will not answer; yea twice, but I will proceed no further.
texts.job.40.6: And Jehovah answered Job out of the whirlwind and said,
texts.job.40.7: Gird up now thy loins like a man: I will demand of thee, and inform thou me.
texts.job.40.8: Wilt thou also annul my judgment? wilt thou condemn me that thou mayest be righteous?
texts.job.40.9: Hast thou an arm like ùGod? or canst thou thunder with a voice like him?
texts.job.40.10: Deck thyself now with glory and excellency, and clothe thyself with majesty and splendour.
texts.job.40.11: Cast abroad the ragings of thine anger, and look on every one that is proud, and abase him:
texts.job.40.12: Look on every one that is proud, bring him low, and tread down the wicked in their place:
texts.job.40.13: Hide them in the dust together; bind their faces in secret.
texts.job.40.14: Then will I also praise thee, because thy right hand saveth thee.
texts.job.40.15: See now the behemoth, which I made with thee: he eateth grass as an ox.
texts.job.40.16: Behold now, his strength is in his loins, and his force is in the muscles of his belly.
texts.job.40.17: He bendeth his tail like a cedar; the sinews of his thighs are woven together.
texts.job.40.18: His bones are tubes of bronze, his members are like bars of iron.
texts.job.40.19: He is the chief of ùGod's ways: he that made him gave him his sword.
texts.job.40.20: For the mountains bring him forth food, where all the beasts of the field play.
texts.job.40.21: He lieth under lotus-bushes, in the covert of the reed and fen:
texts.job.40.22: Lotus-bushes cover him with their shade; the willows of the brook surround him.
texts.job.40.23: Lo, the river overfloweth -- he startleth not: he is confident though a Jordan break forth against his mouth.
texts.job.40.24: Shall he be taken in front? will they pierce through [his] nose in the trap?
texts.job.41.1: Wilt thou draw out the leviathan with the hook, and press down his tongue with a cord?
texts.job.41.2: Wilt thou put a rush-rope into his nose, and pierce his jaw with a spike?
texts.job.41.3: Will he make many supplications unto thee? or will he speak softly unto thee?
texts.job.41.4: Will he make a covenant with thee? wilt thou take him as a bondman for ever?
texts.job.41.5: Wilt thou play with him as with a bird, and wilt thou bind him for thy maidens?
texts.job.41.6: Shall partners make traffic of him, will they divide him among merchants?
texts.job.41.7: Wilt thou fill his skin with darts, and his head with fish-spears?
texts.job.41.8: Lay thy hand upon him; remember the battle, -- do no more!
texts.job.41.9: Lo, hope as to him is belied: is not one cast down even at the sight of him?
texts.job.41.10: None is so bold as to stir him up; and who is he that will stand before me?
texts.job.41.11: Who hath first given to me, that I should repay [him]? [Whatsoever is] under the whole heaven is mine.
texts.job.41.12: I will not be silent as to his parts, the story of his power, and the beauty of his structure.
texts.job.41.13: Who can uncover the surface of his garment? who can come within his double jaws?
texts.job.41.14: Who can open the doors of his face? Round about his teeth is terror.
texts.job.41.15: The rows of his shields are a pride, shut up together [as with] a close seal.
texts.job.41.16: One is so near to another that no air can come between them;
texts.job.41.17: They are joined each to its fellow; they stick together, and cannot be sundered.
texts.job.41.18: His sneezings flash light, and his eyes are like the eyelids of the morning.
texts.job.41.19: Out of his mouth go forth flames; sparks of fire leap out:
texts.job.41.20: Out of his nostrils goeth smoke, as out of a boiling pot and cauldron.
texts.job.41.21: His breath kindleth coals, and a flame goeth out of his mouth.
texts.job.41.22: In his neck lodgeth strength, and terror danceth before him.
texts.job.41.23: The flakes of his flesh are joined together: they are fused upon him, they cannot be moved.
texts.job.41.24: His heart is firm as a stone, yea, firm as the nether [millstone].
texts.job.41.25: When he raiseth himself up, the mighty are afraid: they are beside themselves with consternation.
texts.job.41.26: If any reach him with a sword, it cannot hold; neither spear, nor dart, nor harpoon.
texts.job.41.27: He esteemeth iron as straw, bronze as rotten wood.
texts.job.41.28: The arrow will not make him flee; slingstones are turned with him into stubble.
texts.job.41.29: Clubs are counted as stubble; he laugheth at the shaking of a javelin.
texts.job.41.30: His under parts are sharp potsherds: he spreadeth a threshing-sledge upon the mire.
texts.job.41.31: He maketh the deep to boil like a pot; he maketh the sea like a pot of ointment;
texts.job.41.32: He maketh the path to shine after him: one would think the deep to be hoary.
texts.job.41.33: Upon earth there is not his like, who is made without fear.
texts.job.41.34: He beholdeth all high things; he is king over all the proud beasts.
texts.job.42.1: And Job answered Jehovah and said,
texts.job.42.2: I know that thou canst do everything, and that thou canst be hindered in no thought of thine.
texts.job.42.3: Who is he that obscureth counsel without knowledge? therefore have I uttered what I did not understand; things too wonderful for me, which I knew not.
texts.job.42.4: Hear, I beseech thee, and I will speak: I will demand of thee, and inform me.
texts.job.42.5: I had heard of thee by the hearing of the ear, but now mine eye seeth thee:
texts.job.42.6: Wherefore I abhor [myself], and repent in dust and ashes.
texts.job.42.7: And it came to pass after Jehovah had spoken these words to Job, that Jehovah said to Eliphaz the Temanite, Mine anger is kindled against thee, and against thy two friends; for ye have not spoken rightly of me, like my servant Job.
texts.job.42.8: And now, take for yourselves seven bullocks and seven rams, and go to my servant Job, and offer up for yourselves a burnt-offering; and my servant Job shall pray for you, for him will I accept: lest I deal with you [after your] folly, for ye have not spoken of me rightly, like my servant Job.
texts.job.42.9: Then Eliphaz the Temanite, and Bildad the Shuhite, and Zophar the Naamathite, went and did according as Jehovah had said unto them; and Jehovah accepted Job.
texts.job.42.10: And Jehovah turned the captivity of Job, when he had prayed for his friends; and Jehovah gave Job twice as much as he had before.
texts.job.42.11: And all his brethren, and all his sisters, and all they that had been of his acquaintance before, came to him, and they ate bread with him in his house, and they condoled with him, and comforted him concerning all the evil that Jehovah had brought upon him; and every one gave him a piece of money, and every one a golden ring.
texts.job.42.12: And Jehovah blessed the latter end of Job more than his beginning; and he had fourteen thousand sheep, and six thousand camels, and a thousand yoke of oxen, and a thousand she-asses.
texts.job.42.13: And he had seven sons and three daughters.
texts.job.42.14: And he called the name of the first, Jemimah; and the name of the second, Keziah; and the name of the third, Keren-happuch.
texts.job.42.15: And in all the land were no women found [so] fair as the daughters of Job; and their father gave them inheritance among their brethren.
texts.job.42.16: And Job lived after this a hundred and forty years, and saw his sons, and his sons' sons, four generations.
texts.job.42.17: And Job died, old and full of days.

texts.job.1.1: A man there hath been in the land of Uz -- Job his name -- and that man hath been perfect and upright -- both fearing God, and turning aside from evil.
texts.job.1.2: And there are borne to him seven sons and three daughters,
texts.job.1.3: and his substance is seven thousand sheep, and three thousand camels, and five hundred pairs of oxen, and five hundred she-asses, and a service very abundant; and that man is greater than any of the sons of the east.
texts.job.1.4: And his sons have gone and made a banquet -- the house of each [in] his day -- and have sent and called to their three sisters to eat and to drink with them;
texts.job.1.5: and it cometh to pass, when they have gone round the days of the banquet, that Job doth send and sanctify them, and hath risen early in the morning, and caused to ascend burnt-offerings -- the number of them all -- for Job said, `Perhaps my sons have sinned, yet blessed God in their heart.' Thus doth Job all the days.
texts.job.1.6: And the day is, that sons of God come in to station themselves by Jehovah, and there doth come also the Adversary in their midst.
texts.job.1.7: And Jehovah saith unto the Adversary, `Whence comest thou?' And the Adversary answereth Jehovah and saith, `From going to and fro in the land, and from walking up and down on it.'
texts.job.1.8: And Jehovah saith unto the Adversary, `Hast thou set thy heart against My servant Job because there is none like him in the land, a man perfect and upright, fearing God, and turning aside from evil?'
texts.job.1.9: And the Adversary answereth Jehovah and saith, `For nought is Job fearing God?
texts.job.1.10: Hast not Thou made a hedge for him, and for his house, and for all that he hath -- round about?
texts.job.1.11: The work of his hands Thou hast blessed, and his substance hath spread in the land, and yet, put forth, I pray Thee, Thy hand, and strike against anything that he hath -- if not: to Thy face he doth bless Thee!'
texts.job.1.12: And Jehovah saith unto the Adversary, `Lo, all that he hath [is] in thy hand, only unto him put not forth thy hand.' And the Adversary goeth out from the presence of Jehovah.
texts.job.1.13: And the day is, that his sons and his daughters are eating, and drinking wine, in the house of their brother, the first-born.
texts.job.1.14: And a messenger hath come in unto Job and saith, `The oxen have been plowing, and the she-asses feeding by their sides,
texts.job.1.15: and Sheba doth fall, and take them, and the young men they have smitten by the mouth of the sword, and I am escaped -- only I alone -- to declare [it] to thee.'
texts.job.1.16: While this [one] is speaking another also hath come and saith, `Fire of God hath fallen from the heavens, and burneth among the flock, and among the young men, and consumeth them, and I am escaped -- only I alone -- to declare [it] to thee.'
texts.job.1.17: While this [one] is speaking another also hath come and saith, `Chaldeans made three heads, and rush on the camels, and take them, and the young men they have smitten by the mouth of the sword, and I am escaped -- only I alone -- to declare [it] to thee.'
texts.job.1.18: While this [one] is speaking another also hath come and saith, `Thy sons and thy daughters are eating, and drinking wine, in the house of their brother, the first-born.
texts.job.1.19: And lo, a great wind hath come from over the wilderness, and striketh against the four corners of the house, and it falleth on the young men, and they are dead, and I am escaped -- only I alone -- to declare [it] to thee.'
texts.job.1.20: And Job riseth, and rendeth his robe, and shaveth his head, and falleth to the earth, and doth obeisance,
texts.job.1.21: and he saith, `Naked came I forth from the womb of my mother, and naked I turn back thither: Jehovah hath given and Jehovah hath taken: let the name of Jehovah be blessed.'
texts.job.1.22: In all this Job hath not sinned, nor given folly to God.
texts.job.2.1: And the day is, that sons of God come in to station themselves by Jehovah, and there doth come also the Adversary in their midst to station himself by Jehovah.
texts.job.2.2: And Jehovah saith unto the Adversary, `Whence camest thou?' And the Adversary answereth Jehovah and saith, `From going to and fro in the land, and from walking up and down in it.'
texts.job.2.3: And Jehovah saith unto the Adversary, `Hast thou set thy heart unto My servant Job because there is none like him in the land, a man perfect and upright, fearing God and turning aside from evil? and still he is keeping hold on his integrity, and thou dost move Me against him to swallow him up for nought!'
texts.job.2.4: And the Adversary answereth Jehovah and saith, `A skin for a skin, and all that a man hath he doth give for his life.
texts.job.2.5: Yet, put forth, I pray Thee, Thy hand, and strike unto his bone and unto his flesh -- if not: unto Thy face he doth bless Thee!'
texts.job.2.6: And Jehovah saith unto the Adversary, `Lo, he [is] in thy hand; only his life take care of.'
texts.job.2.7: And the Adversary goeth forth from the presence of Jehovah, and smiteth Job with a sore ulcer from the sole of his foot unto his crown.
texts.job.2.8: And he taketh to him a potsherd to scrape himself with it, and he is sitting in the midst of the ashes.
texts.job.2.9: And his wife saith to him, `Still thou art keeping hold on thine integrity: bless God and die.'
texts.job.2.10: And he saith unto her, `As one of the foolish women speaketh, thou speakest; yea, the good we receive from God, and the evil we do not receive.' In all this Job hath not sinned with his lips.
texts.job.2.11: And three of the friends of Job hear of all this evil that hath come upon him, and they come in each from his place -- Eliphaz the Temanite, and Bildad the Shuhite, and Zophar the Naamathite -- and they are met together to come in to bemoan him, and to comfort him;
texts.job.2.12: and they lift up their eyes from afar and have not discerned him, and they lift up their voice and weep, and rend each his robe, and sprinkle dust on their heads -- heavenward.
texts.job.2.13: And they sit with him on the earth seven days and seven nights, and there is none speaking unto him a word when they have seen that the pain hath been very great.
texts.job.3.1: After this hath Job opened his mouth, and revileth his day.
texts.job.3.3: Let the day perish in which I am born, And the night that hath said: `A man-child hath been conceived.'
texts.job.3.4: That day -- let it be darkness, Let not God require it from above, Nor let light shine upon it.
texts.job.3.5: Let darkness and death-shade redeem it, Let a cloud tabernacle upon it, Let them terrify it as the most bitter of days.
texts.job.3.6: That night -- let thick darkness take it, Let it not be united to days of the year, Into the number of months let it not come.
texts.job.3.7: Lo! that night -- let it be gloomy, Let no singing come into it.
texts.job.3.8: Let the cursers of day mark it, Who are ready to wake up Leviathan.
texts.job.3.9: Let the stars of its twilight be dark, Let it wait for light, and there is none, And let it not look on the eyelids of the dawn.
texts.job.3.10: Because it hath not shut the doors Of the womb that was mine! And hide misery from mine eyes.
texts.job.3.11: Why from the womb do I not die? From the belly I have come forth and gasp!
texts.job.3.12: Wherefore have knees been before me? And what [are] breasts, that I suck?
texts.job.3.13: For now, I have lain down, and am quiet, I have slept -- then there is rest to me,
texts.job.3.14: With kings and counsellors of earth, These building wastes for themselves.
texts.job.3.15: Or with princes -- they have gold, They are filling their houses [with] silver.
texts.job.3.16: (Or as a hidden abortion I am not, As infants -- they have not seen light.)
texts.job.3.17: There the wicked have ceased troubling, And there rest do the wearied in power.
texts.job.3.18: Together prisoners have been at ease, They have not heard the voice of an exactor,
texts.job.3.19: Small and great [are] there the same. And a servant [is] free from his lord.
texts.job.3.20: Why giveth He to the miserable light, and life to the bitter soul?
texts.job.3.21: Who are waiting for death, and it is not, And they seek it above hid treasures.
texts.job.3.22: Who are glad -- unto joy, They rejoice when they find a grave.
texts.job.3.23: To a man whose way hath been hidden, And whom God doth shut up?
texts.job.3.24: For before my food, my sighing cometh, And poured out as waters [are] my roarings.
texts.job.3.25: For a fear I feared and it meeteth me, And what I was afraid of doth come to me.
texts.job.3.26: I was not safe -- nor was I quiet -- Nor was I at rest -- and trouble cometh!
texts.job.4.1: And Eliphaz the Temanite answereth and saith: --
texts.job.4.2: Hath one tried a word with thee? -- Thou art weary! And to keep in words who is able?
texts.job.4.3: Lo, thou hast instructed many, And feeble hands thou makest strong.
texts.job.4.4: The stumbling one do thy words raise up, And bowing knees thou dost strengthen.
texts.job.4.5: But now, it cometh in unto thee, And thou art weary; It striketh unto thee, and thou art troubled.
texts.job.4.6: Is not thy reverence thy confidence? Thy hope -- the perfection of thy ways?
texts.job.4.7: Remember, I pray thee, Who, being innocent, hath perished? And where have the upright been cut off?
texts.job.4.8: As I have seen -- ploughers of iniquity, And sowers of misery, reap it!
texts.job.4.9: From the breath of God they perish, And from the spirit of His anger consumed.
texts.job.4.10: The roaring of a lion, And the voice of a fierce lion, And teeth of young lions have been broken.
texts.job.4.11: An old lion is perishing without prey, And the whelps of the lioness do separate.
texts.job.4.12: And unto me a thing is secretly brought, And receive doth mine ear a little of it.
texts.job.4.13: In thoughts from visions of the night, In the falling of deep sleep on men,
texts.job.4.14: Fear hath met me, and trembling, And the multitude of my bones caused to fear.
texts.job.4.15: And a spirit before my face doth pass, Stand up doth the hair of my flesh;
texts.job.4.16: It standeth, and I discern not its aspect, A similitude [is] over-against mine eyes, Silence! and a voice I hear:
texts.job.4.17: `Is mortal man than God more righteous? Than his Maker is a man cleaner?
texts.job.4.18: Lo, in His servants He putteth no credence, Nor in His messengers setteth praise.'
texts.job.4.19: Also -- the inhabitants of houses of clay, (Whose foundation [is] in the dust, They bruise them before a moth.)
texts.job.4.20: From morning to evening are beaten down, Without any regarding, for ever they perish.
texts.job.4.21: Hath not their excellency been removed with them? They die, and not in wisdom!
texts.job.5.1: Pray, call, is there any to answer thee? And unto which of the holy ones dost thou turn?
texts.job.5.2: For provocation slayeth the perverse, And envy putteth to death the simple,
texts.job.5.3: I -- I have seen the perverse taking root, And I mark his habitation straightway,
texts.job.5.4: Far are his sons from safety, And they are bruised in the gate, And there is no deliverer.
texts.job.5.5: Whose harvest the hungry doth eat, And even from the thorns taketh it, And the designing swallowed their wealth.
texts.job.5.6: For sorrow cometh not forth from the dust, Nor from the ground springeth up misery.
texts.job.5.7: For man to misery is born, And the sparks go high to fly.
texts.job.5.8: Yet I -- I inquire for God, And for God I give my word,
texts.job.5.9: Doing great things, and there is no searching. Wonderful, till there is no numbering.
texts.job.5.10: Who is giving rain on the face of the land, And is sending waters on the out-places.
texts.job.5.11: To set the low on a high place, And the mourners have been high [in] safety.
texts.job.5.12: Making void thoughts of the subtile, And their hands do not execute wisdom.
texts.job.5.13: Capturing the wise in their subtilty, And the counsel of wrestling ones was hastened,
texts.job.5.14: By day they meet darkness, And as night -- they grope at noon.
texts.job.5.15: And He saveth the wasted from their mouth, And from a strong hand the needy,
texts.job.5.16: And there is hope to the poor, And perverseness hath shut her mouth.
texts.job.5.17: Lo, the happiness of mortal man, God doth reprove him: And the chastisement of the Mighty despise not,
texts.job.5.18: For He doth pain, and He bindeth up, He smiteth, and His hands heal.
texts.job.5.19: In six distresses He delivereth thee, And in seven evil striketh not on thee.
texts.job.5.20: In famine He hath redeemed thee from death, And in battle from the hands of the sword.
texts.job.5.21: When the tongue scourgeth thou art hid, And thou art not afraid of destruction, When it cometh.
texts.job.5.22: At destruction and at hunger thou mockest, And of the beast of the earth, Thou art not afraid.
texts.job.5.23: (For with sons of the field [is] thy covenant, And the beast of the field Hath been at peace with thee.)
texts.job.5.24: And thou hast known that thy tent [is] peace, And inspected thy habitation, and errest not,
texts.job.5.25: And hast known that numerous [is] Thy seed, And thine offspring as the herb of the earth;
texts.job.5.26: Thou comest in full age unto the grave, As the going up of a stalk in its season.
texts.job.5.27: Lo, this -- we searched it out -- it [is] right, hearken; And thou, know for thyself!
texts.job.6.2: O that my provocation were thoroughly weighed, And my calamity in balances They would lift up together!
texts.job.6.3: For now, than the sands of the sea it is heavier, Therefore my words have been rash.
