texts.job.6.4: For arrows of the Mighty [are] with me, Whose poison is drinking up my spirit. Terrors of God array themselves [for] me!
texts.job.6.5: Brayeth a wild ass over tender grass? Loweth an ox over his provender?
texts.job.6.6: Eaten is an insipid thing without salt? Is there sense in the drivel of dreams?
texts.job.6.7: My soul is refusing to touch! They [are] as my sickening food.
texts.job.6.8: O that my request may come, That God may grant my hope!
texts.job.6.9: That God would please -- and bruise me, Loose His hand and cut me off!
texts.job.6.10: And yet it is my comfort, (And I exult in pain -- He doth not spare,) That I have not hidden The sayings of the Holy One.
texts.job.6.11: What [is] my power that I should hope? And what mine end That I should prolong my life?
texts.job.6.12: Is my strength the strength of stones? Is my flesh brazen?
texts.job.6.13: Is not my help with me, And substance driven from me?
texts.job.6.14: To a despiser of his friends [is] shame, And the fear of the Mighty he forsaketh.
texts.job.6.15: My brethren have deceived as a brook, As a stream of brooks they pass away.
texts.job.6.16: That are black because of ice, By them doth snow hide itself.
texts.job.6.17: By the time they are warm they have been cut off, By its being hot they have been Extinguished from their place.
texts.job.6.18: Turn aside do the paths of their way, They ascend into emptiness, and are lost.
texts.job.6.19: Passengers of Tema looked expectingly, Travellers of Sheba hoped for them.
texts.job.6.20: They were ashamed that one hath trusted, They have come unto it and are confounded.
texts.job.6.21: Surely now ye have become the same! Ye see a downfall, and are afraid.
texts.job.6.22: Is it because I said, Give to me? And, By your power bribe for me?
texts.job.6.23: And, Deliver me from the hand of an adversary? And, From the hand of terrible ones ransom me?
texts.job.6.24: Shew me, and I -- I keep silent, And what I have erred, let me understand.
texts.job.6.25: How powerful have been upright sayings, And what doth reproof from you reprove?
texts.job.6.26: For reproof -- do you reckon words? And for wind -- sayings of the desperate.
texts.job.6.27: Anger on the fatherless ye cause to fall, And are strange to your friend.
texts.job.6.28: And, now, please, look upon me, Even to your face do I lie?
texts.job.6.29: Turn back, I pray you, let it not be perverseness, Yea, turn back again -- my righteousness [is] in it.
texts.job.6.30: Is there in my tongue perverseness? Discerneth not my palate desirable things?
texts.job.7.1: Is there not a warfare to man on earth? And as the days of an hireling his days?
texts.job.7.2: As a servant desireth the shadow, And as a hireling expecteth his wage,
texts.job.7.3: So I have been caused to inherit months of vanity, And nights of misery they numbered to me.
texts.job.7.4: If I lay down then I said, `When do I rise!' And evening hath been measured, And I have been full of tossings till dawn.
texts.job.7.5: Clothed hath been my flesh [with] worms, And a clod of dust, My skin hath been shrivelled and is loathsome,
texts.job.7.6: My days swifter than a weaving machine, And they are consumed without hope.
texts.job.7.7: Remember Thou that my life [is] a breath, Mine eye turneth not back to see good.
texts.job.7.8: The eye of my beholder beholdeth me not. Thine eyes [are] upon me -- and I am not.
texts.job.7.9: Consumed hath been a cloud, and it goeth, So he who is going down to Sheol cometh not up.
texts.job.7.10: He turneth not again to his house, Nor doth his place discern him again.
texts.job.7.11: Also I -- I withhold not my mouth -- I speak in the distress of my spirit, I talk in the bitterness of my soul.
texts.job.7.12: A sea-[monster] am I, or a dragon, That thou settest over me a guard?
texts.job.7.13: When I said, `My bed doth comfort me,' He taketh away in my talking my couch.
texts.job.7.14: And thou hast affrighted me with dreams, And from visions thou terrifiest me,
texts.job.7.15: And my soul chooseth strangling, Death rather than my bones.
texts.job.7.16: I have wasted away -- not to the age do I live. Cease from me, for my days [are] vanity.
texts.job.7.17: What [is] man that Thou dost magnify him? And that Thou settest unto him Thy heart?
texts.job.7.18: And inspectest him in the mornings, In the evenings dost try him?
texts.job.7.19: How long dost Thou not look from me? Thou dost not desist till I swallow my spittle.
texts.job.7.20: I have sinned, what do I to Thee, O watcher of man? Why hast Thou set me for a mark to Thee, And I am for a burden to myself -- and what?
texts.job.7.21: Thou dost not take away my transgression, And cause to pass away mine iniquity, Because now, for dust I lie down: And Thou hast sought me -- and I am not!
texts.job.8.1: And Bildad the Shuhite answereth and saith: --
texts.job.8.2: Till when dost thou speak these things? And a strong wind -- sayings of thy mouth?
texts.job.8.3: Doth God pervert judgment? And doth the Mighty One pervert justice?
texts.job.8.4: If thy sons have sinned before Him, And He doth send them away, By the hand of their transgression,
texts.job.8.5: If thou dost seek early unto God, And unto the Mighty makest supplication,
texts.job.8.6: If pure and upright thou [art], Surely now He waketh for thee, And hath completed The habitation of thy righteousness.
texts.job.8.7: And thy beginning hath been small, And thy latter end is very great.
texts.job.8.8: For, ask I pray thee of a former generation, And prepare to a search of their fathers,
texts.job.8.9: (For of yesterday we [are], and we know not, For a shadow [are] our days on earth.)
texts.job.8.10: Do they not shew thee -- speak to thee, And from their heart bring forth words?
texts.job.8.11: `Doth a rush wise without mire? A reed increase without water?
texts.job.8.12: While it [is] in its budding -- uncropt, Even before any herb it withereth.
texts.job.8.13: So [are] the paths of all forgetting God, And the hope of the profane doth perish,
texts.job.8.14: Whose confidence is loathsome, And the house of a spider his trust.
texts.job.8.15: He leaneth on his house -- and it standeth not: He taketh hold on it -- and it abideth not.
texts.job.8.16: Green he [is] before the sun, And over his garden his branch goeth out.
texts.job.8.17: By a heap his roots are wrapped, A house of stones he looketh for.
texts.job.8.18: If [one] doth destroy him from his place, Then it hath feigned concerning him, I have not seen thee!
texts.job.8.19: Lo, this [is] the joy of his way, And from the dust others spring up.'
texts.job.8.20: Lo, God doth not reject the perfect, Nor taketh hold on the hand of evil doers.
texts.job.8.21: While he filleth with laughter thy mouth, And thy lips with shouting,
texts.job.8.22: Those hating thee do put on shame, And the tent of the wicked is not!
texts.job.9.2: Truly I have known that [it is] so, And what -- is man righteous with God?
texts.job.9.3: If he delight to strive with Him -- He doth not answer him one of a thousand.
texts.job.9.4: Wise in heart and strong in power -- Who hath hardened toward Him and is at peace?
texts.job.9.5: Who is removing mountains, And they have not known, Who hath overturned them in His anger.
texts.job.9.6: Who is shaking earth from its place, And its pillars move themselves.
texts.job.9.7: Who is speaking to the sun, and it riseth not, And the stars He sealeth up.
texts.job.9.8: Stretching out the heavens by Himself, And treading on the heights of the sea,
texts.job.9.9: Making Osh, Kesil, and Kimah, And the inner chambers of the south.
texts.job.9.10: Doing great things till there is no searching, And wonderful, till there is no numbering.
texts.job.9.11: Lo, He goeth over by me, and I see not, And He passeth on, and I attend not to it.
texts.job.9.12: Lo, He snatches away, who bringeth it back? Who saith unto Him, `What dost Thou?'
texts.job.9.13: God doth not turn back His anger, Under Him bowed have proud helpers.
texts.job.9.14: How much less do I -- I answer Him? Choose out my words with Him?
texts.job.9.15: Whom, though I were righteous, I answer not, For my judgment I make supplication.
texts.job.9.16: Though I had called and He answereth me, I do not believe that He giveth ear [to] my voice.
texts.job.9.17: Because with a tempest He bruiseth me, And hath multiplied my wounds for nought.
texts.job.9.18: He permitteth me not to refresh my spirit, But filleth me with bitter things.
texts.job.9.19: If of power, lo, the Strong One; And if of judgment -- who doth convene me?
texts.job.9.20: If I be righteous, Mine mouth doth declare me wicked, Perfect I am! -- it declareth me perverse.
texts.job.9.21: Perfect I am! -- I know not my soul, I despise my life.
texts.job.9.22: It is the same thing, therefore I said, `The perfect and the wicked He is consuming.'
texts.job.9.23: If a scourge doth put to death suddenly, At the trial of the innocent He laugheth.
texts.job.9.24: Earth hath been given Into the hand of the wicked one. The face of its judges he covereth, If not -- where, who [is] he?
texts.job.9.25: My days have been swifter than a runner, They have fled, they have not seen good,
texts.job.9.26: They have passed on with ships of reed, As an eagle darteth on food.
texts.job.9.27: Though I say, `I forget my talking, I forsake my corner, and I brighten up!'
texts.job.9.28: I have been afraid of all my griefs, I have known that Thou dost not acquit me.
texts.job.9.29: I -- I am become wicked; why [is] this? [In] vain I labour.
texts.job.9.30: If I have washed myself with snow-water, And purified with soap my hands,
texts.job.9.31: Then in corruption Thou dost dip me, And my garments have abominated me.
texts.job.9.32: But if a man like myself -- I answer him, We come together into judgment.
texts.job.9.33: If there were between us an umpire, He doth place his hand on us both.
texts.job.9.34: He doth turn aside from off me his rod, And His terror doth not make me afraid,
texts.job.9.35: I speak, and do not fear Him, But I am not right with myself.
texts.job.10.1: My soul hath been weary of my life, I leave off my talking to myself, I speak in the bitterness of my soul.
texts.job.10.2: I say unto God, `Do not condemn me, Let me know why Thou dost strive [with] me.
texts.job.10.3: Is it good for Thee that Thou dost oppress? That Thou despisest the labour of Thy hands, And on the counsel of the wicked hast shone?
texts.job.10.4: Eyes of flesh hast Thou? As man seeth -- seest Thou?
texts.job.10.5: As the days of man [are] Thy days? Thy years as the days of a man?
texts.job.10.6: That Thou inquirest for mine iniquity, And for my sin seekest?
texts.job.10.7: For Thou knowest that I am not wicked, And there is no deliverer from Thy hand.
texts.job.10.8: Thy hands have taken pains about me, And they make me together round about, And Thou swallowest me up!
texts.job.10.9: Remember, I pray Thee, That as clay Thou hast made me, And unto dust Thou dost bring me back.
texts.job.10.10: Dost Thou not as milk pour me out? And as cheese curdle me?
texts.job.10.11: Skin and flesh Thou dost put on me, And with bones and sinews dost fence me.
texts.job.10.12: Life and kindness Thou hast done with me. And Thy inspection hath preserved my spirit.
texts.job.10.13: And these Thou hast laid up in Thy heart, I have known that this [is] with Thee.
texts.job.10.14: If I sinned, then Thou hast observed me, And from mine iniquity dost not acquit me,
texts.job.10.15: If I have done wickedly -- wo to me, And righteously -- I lift not up my head, Full of shame -- then see my affliction,
texts.job.10.16: And it riseth -- as a lion Thou huntest me. And Thou turnest back -- Thou shewest Thyself wonderful in me.
texts.job.10.17: Thou renewest Thy witnesses against me, And dost multiply Thine anger with me, Changes and warfare [are] with me.
texts.job.10.18: And why from the womb Hast Thou brought me forth? I expire, and the eye doth not see me.
texts.job.10.19: As I had not been, I am, From the belly to the grave I am brought,
texts.job.10.20: Are not my days few? Cease then, and put from me, And I brighten up a little,
texts.job.10.21: Before I go, and return not, Unto a land of darkness and death-shade,
texts.job.10.22: A land of obscurity as thick darkness, Death-shade -- and no order, And the shining [is] as thick darkness.'
texts.job.11.1: And Zophar the Naamathite answereth and saith: --
texts.job.11.2: Is a multitude of words not answered? And is a man of lips justified?
texts.job.11.3: Thy devices make men keep silent, Thou scornest, and none is causing blushing!
texts.job.11.4: And thou sayest, `Pure [is] my discourse, And clean I have been in Thine eyes.'
texts.job.11.5: And yet, O that God had spoken! And doth open His lips with thee.
texts.job.11.6: And declare to thee secrets of wisdom, For counsel hath foldings. And know thou that God forgetteth for thee, [Some] of thine iniquity.
texts.job.11.7: By searching dost thou find out God? Unto perfection find out the Mighty One?
texts.job.11.8: Heights of the heavens! -- what dost thou? Deeper than Sheol! -- what knowest thou?
texts.job.11.9: Longer than earth [is] its measure, And broader than the sea.
texts.job.11.10: If He pass on, and shut up, and assemble, Who then dost reverse it?
texts.job.11.11: For he hath known men of vanity, And He seeth iniquity, And one doth not consider [it]!
texts.job.11.12: And empty man is bold, And the colt of a wild ass man is born.
texts.job.11.13: If thou -- thou hast prepared thy heart, And hast spread out unto Him thy hands,
texts.job.11.14: If iniquity [is] in thy hand, put it far off, And let not perverseness dwell in thy tents.
texts.job.11.15: For then thou liftest up thy face from blemish, And thou hast been firm, and fearest not.
texts.job.11.16: For thou dost forget misery, As waters passed away thou rememberest.
texts.job.11.17: And above the noon doth age rise, Thou fliest -- as the morning thou art.
texts.job.11.18: And thou hast trusted because their is hope, And searched -- in confidence thou liest down,
texts.job.11.19: And thou hast rested, And none is causing trembling, And many have entreated thy face;
texts.job.11.20: And the eyes of the wicked are consumed, And refuge hath perished from them, And their hope [is] a breathing out of soul!
texts.job.12.2: Truly -- ye [are] the people, And with you doth wisdom die.
texts.job.12.3: I also have a heart like you, I am not fallen more than you, And with whom is there not like these?
texts.job.12.4: A laughter to his friend I am: `He calleth to God, and He answereth him,' A laughter [is] the perfect righteous one.
texts.job.12.5: A torch -- despised in the thoughts of the secure Is prepared for those sliding with the feet.
texts.job.12.6: At peace are the tents of spoilers, And those provoking God have confidence, He into whose hand God hath brought.
texts.job.12.7: And yet, ask, I pray thee, [One of] the beasts, and it doth shew thee, And a fowl of the heavens, And it doth declare to thee.
texts.job.12.8: Or talk to the earth, and it sheweth thee, And fishes of the sea recount to thee:
texts.job.12.9: `Who hath not known in all these, That the hand of Jehovah hath done this?
texts.job.12.10: In whose hand [is] the breath of every living thing, And the spirit of all flesh of man.'
texts.job.12.11: Doth not the ear try words? And the palate taste food for itself?
texts.job.12.12: With the very aged [is] wisdom, And [with] length of days understanding.
texts.job.12.13: With Him [are] wisdom and might, To him [are] counsel and understanding.
texts.job.12.14: Lo, He breaketh down, and it is not built up, He shutteth against a man, And it is not opened.
texts.job.12.15: Lo, He keepeth in the waters, and they are dried up, And he sendeth them forth, And they overturn the land.
texts.job.12.16: With Him [are] strength and wisdom, His the deceived and deceiver.
texts.job.12.17: Causing counsellors to go away a spoil, And judges He maketh foolish.
texts.job.12.18: The bands of kings He hath opened, And He bindeth a girdle on their loins.
texts.job.12.19: Causing ministers to go away a spoil And strong ones He overthroweth.
texts.job.12.20: Turning aside the lip of the stedfast, And the reason of the aged He taketh away.
texts.job.12.21: Pouring contempt upon princes, And the girdle of the mighty He made feeble.
texts.job.12.22: Removing deep things out of darkness, And He bringeth out to light death-shade.
texts.job.12.23: Magnifying the nations, and He destroyeth them, Spreading out the nations, and He quieteth them.
texts.job.12.24: Turning aside the heart Of the heads of the people of the land, And he causeth them to wander In vacancy -- no way!
texts.job.12.25: They feel darkness, and not light, He causeth them to wander as a drunkard.
texts.job.13.1: Lo, all -- hath mine eye seen, Heard hath mine ear, and it attendeth to it.
texts.job.13.2: According to your knowledge I have known -- also I. I am not fallen more than you.
texts.job.13.3: Yet I for the Mighty One do speak, And to argue for God I delight.
texts.job.13.4: And yet, ye [are] forgers of falsehood, Physicians of nought -- all of you,
texts.job.13.5: O that ye would keep perfectly silent, And it would be to you for wisdom.
texts.job.13.6: Hear, I pray you, my argument, And to the pleadings of my lips attend,
texts.job.13.7: For God do ye speak perverseness? And for Him do ye speak deceit?
texts.job.13.8: His face do ye accept, if for God ye strive?
texts.job.13.9: Is [it] good that He doth search you, If, as one mocketh at a man, ye mock at Him?
texts.job.13.10: He doth surely reprove you, if in secret ye accept faces.
texts.job.13.11: Doth not His excellency terrify you? And His dread fall upon you?
texts.job.13.12: Your remembrances [are] similes of ashes, For high places of clay your heights.
texts.job.13.13: Keep silent from me, and I speak, And pass over me doth what?
texts.job.13.14: Wherefore do I take my flesh in my teeth? And my soul put in my hand?
texts.job.13.15: Lo, He doth slay me -- I wait not! Only, my ways unto His face I argue.
texts.job.13.16: Also -- He [is] to me for salvation, For the profane cometh not before Him.
texts.job.13.17: Hear ye diligently my word, And my declaration with your ears.
texts.job.13.18: Lo, I pray you, I have set in order the cause, I have known that I am righteous.
texts.job.13.19: Who [is] he that doth strive with me? For now I keep silent and gasp.
texts.job.13.20: Only two things, O God, do with me: Then from Thy face I am not hidden.
texts.job.13.21: Thy hand put far off from me, And Thy terror let not terrify me.
texts.job.13.22: And call Thou, and I -- I answer, Or -- I speak, and answer Thou me.
texts.job.13.23: How many iniquities and sins have I? My transgression and my sin let me know.
texts.job.13.24: Why dost Thou hide Thy face? And reckonest me for an enemy to Thee?
texts.job.13.25: A leaf driven away dost Thou terrify? And the dry stubble dost Thou pursue?
texts.job.13.26: For Thou writest against me bitter things, And causest me to possess iniquities of my youth:
texts.job.13.27: And puttest in the stocks my feet, And observest all my paths, On the roots of my feet Thou settest a print,
texts.job.13.28: And he, as a rotten thing, weareth away, As a garment hath a moth consumed him.
texts.job.14.1: Man, born of woman! Of few days, and full of trouble!
texts.job.14.2: As a flower he hath gone forth, and is cut off, And he fleeth as a shadow and standeth not.
texts.job.14.3: Also -- on this Thou hast opened Thine eyes, And dost bring me into judgment with Thee.
texts.job.14.4: Who giveth a clean thing out of an unclean? not one.
texts.job.14.5: If determined are his days, The number of his months [are] with Thee, His limit Thou hast made, And he passeth not over;
texts.job.14.6: Look away from off him that he may cease, Till he enjoy as an hireling his day.
texts.job.14.7: For there is of a tree hope, if it be cut down, That again it doth change, That its tender branch doth not cease.
texts.job.14.8: If its root becometh old in the earth, And its stem doth die in the dust,
texts.job.14.9: From the fragrance of water it doth flourish, And hath made a crop as a plant.
texts.job.14.10: And a man dieth, and becometh weak, And man expireth, and where [is] he?
texts.job.14.11: Waters have gone away from a sea, And a river becometh waste and dry.
texts.job.14.12: And man hath lain down, and riseth not, Till the wearing out of the heavens they awake not, Nor are roused from their sleep.
texts.job.14.13: O that in Sheol Thou wouldst conceal me, Hide me till the turning of Thine anger, Set for me a limit, and remember me.
texts.job.14.14: If a man dieth -- doth he revive? All days of my warfare I wait, till my change come.
texts.job.14.15: Thou dost call, and I -- I answer Thee; To the work of Thy hands Thou hast desire.
texts.job.14.16: But now, my steps Thou numberest, Thou dost not watch over my sin.
texts.job.14.17: Sealed up in a bag [is] my transgression, And Thou sewest up mine iniquity.
texts.job.14.18: And yet, a falling mountain wasteth away, And a rock is removed from its place.
texts.job.14.19: Stones have waters worn away, Their outpourings wash away the dust of earth, And the hope of man Thou hast destroyed.
texts.job.14.20: Thou prevailest [over] him for ever, and he goeth, He is changing his countenance, And Thou sendest him away.
texts.job.14.21: Honoured are his sons, and he knoweth not; And they are little, and he attendeth not to them.
texts.job.14.22: Only -- his flesh for him is pained, And his soul for him doth mourn.'
texts.job.15.1: And Eliphaz the Temanite answereth and saith: --
texts.job.15.2: Doth a wise man answer [with] vain knowledge? And fill [with] an east wind his belly?
texts.job.15.3: To reason with a word not useful? And speeches -- no profit in them?
texts.job.15.4: Yea, thou dost make reverence void, And dost diminish meditation before God.
texts.job.15.5: For thy mouth teacheth thine iniquity, And thou chooseth the tongue of the subtile.
texts.job.15.6: Thy mouth declareth thee wicked, and not I, And thy lips testify against thee.
texts.job.15.7: The first man art thou born? And before the heights wast thou formed?
texts.job.15.8: Of the secret counsel of God dost thou hear? And withdrawest thou unto thee wisdom?
texts.job.15.9: What hast thou known, and we know not? Understandest thou -- and it is not with us?
texts.job.15.10: Both the gray-headed And the very aged [are] among us -- Greater than thy father [in] days.
texts.job.15.11: Too few for thee are the comforts of God? And a gentle word [is] with thee,
texts.job.15.12: What -- doth thine heart take thee away? And what -- are thine eyes high?
texts.job.15.13: For thou turnest against God thy spirit? And hast brought out words from thy mouth:
texts.job.15.14: What [is] man that he is pure, And that he is righteous, one born of woman?
texts.job.15.15: Lo, in His holy ones He putteth no credence, And the heavens have not been pure in His eyes.
texts.job.15.16: Also -- surely abominable and filthy Is man drinking as water perverseness.
texts.job.15.17: I shew thee -- hearken to me -- And this I have seen and declare:
texts.job.15.18: Which the wise declare -- And have not hid -- from their fathers.
texts.job.15.19: To them alone was the land given, And a stranger passed not over into their midst:
texts.job.15.20: `All days of the wicked he is paining himself, And few years have been laid up for the terrible one.
texts.job.15.21: A fearful voice [is] in his ears, In peace doth a destroyer come to him.
texts.job.15.22: He believeth not to return from darkness, And watched [is] he for the sword.
texts.job.15.23: He is wandering for bread -- `Where [is] it?' He hath known that ready at his hand Is a day of darkness.
texts.job.15.24: Terrify him do adversity and distress, They prevail over him As a king ready for a boaster.
texts.job.15.25: For he stretched out against God his hand, And against the Mighty he maketh himself mighty.
texts.job.15.26: He runneth unto Him with a neck, With thick bosses of his shields.
texts.job.15.27: For he hath covered his face with his fat, And maketh vigour over [his] confidence.
texts.job.15.28: And he inhabiteth cities cut off, houses not dwelt in, That have been ready to become heaps.
texts.job.15.29: He is not rich, nor doth his wealth rise, Nor doth he stretch out on earth their continuance.
texts.job.15.30: He turneth not aside from darkness, His tender branch doth a flame dry up, And he turneth aside at the breath of His mouth!
texts.job.15.31: Let him not put credence in vanity, He hath been deceived, For vanity is his recompence.
texts.job.15.32: Not in his day is it completed, And his bending branch is not green.
texts.job.15.33: He shaketh off as a vine his unripe fruit, And casteth off as an olive his blossom.
texts.job.15.34: For the company of the profane [is] gloomy, And fire hath consumed tents of bribery.
texts.job.15.35: To conceive misery, and to bear iniquity, Even their heart doth prepare deceit.
texts.job.16.2: I have heard many such things, Miserable comforters [are] ye all.
texts.job.16.3: Is there an end to words of wind? Or what doth embolden thee that thou answerest?
texts.job.16.4: I also, like you, might speak, If your soul were in my soul's stead. I might join against you with words, And nod at you with my head.
texts.job.16.5: I might harden you with my mouth, And the moving of my lips might be sparing.
texts.job.16.6: If I speak, my pain is not restrained, And I cease -- what goeth from me?
texts.job.16.7: Only, now, it hath wearied me; Thou hast desolated all my company,
texts.job.16.8: And Thou dost loathe me, For a witness it hath been, And rise up against me doth my failure, In my face it testifieth.
texts.job.16.9: His anger hath torn, and he hateth me, He hath gnashed at me with his teeth, My adversary sharpeneth his eyes for me.
texts.job.16.10: They have gaped on me with their mouth, In reproach they have smitten my cheeks, Together against me they set themselves.
texts.job.16.11: God shutteth me up unto the perverse, And to the hands of the wicked turneth me over.
texts.job.16.12: At ease I have been, and he breaketh me, And he hath laid hold on my neck, And he breaketh me in pieces, And he raiseth me to him for a mark.
texts.job.16.13: Go round against me do his archers. He splitteth my reins, and spareth not, He poureth out to the earth my gall.
texts.job.16.14: He breaketh me -- breach upon breach, He runneth upon me as a mighty one.
texts.job.16.15: Sackcloth I have sewed on my skin, And have rolled in the dust my horn.
texts.job.16.16: My face is foul with weeping, And on mine eyelids [is] death-shade.
texts.job.16.17: Not for violence in my hands, And my prayer [is] pure.
texts.job.16.18: O earth, do not thou cover my blood! And let there not be a place for my cry.
texts.job.16.19: Also, now, lo, in the heavens [is] my witness, And my testifier in the high places.
texts.job.16.20: My interpreter [is] my friend, Unto God hath mine eye dropped:
texts.job.16.21: And he reasoneth for a man with God, And a son of man for his friend.
texts.job.16.22: When a few years do come, Then a path I return not do I go.
texts.job.17.1: My spirit hath been destroyed, My days extinguished -- graves [are] for me.
texts.job.17.2: If not -- mockeries [are] with me. And in their provocations mine eye lodgeth.
texts.job.17.3: Place, I pray Thee, my pledge with Thee; Who is he that striketh hand with me?
texts.job.17.4: For their heart Thou hast hidden From understanding, Therefore Thou dost not exalt them.
texts.job.17.5: For a portion he sheweth friendship, And the eyes of his sons are consumed.
texts.job.17.6: And he set me up for a proverb of the peoples, And a wonder before them I am.
texts.job.17.7: And dim from sorrow is mine eye, And my members as a shadow all of them.
texts.job.17.8: Astonished are the upright at this, And the innocent against the profane Stirreth himself up.
texts.job.17.9: And the righteous layeth hold [on] his way, And the clean of hands addeth strength, And -- dumb are they all.
texts.job.17.10: Return, and come in, I pray you, And I find not among you a wise man.
texts.job.17.11: My days have passed by, My devices have been broken off, The possessions of my heart!
texts.job.17.12: Night for day they appoint, Light [is] near because of darkness.
texts.job.17.13: If I wait -- Sheol [is] my house, In darkness I have spread out my couch.
texts.job.17.14: To corruption I have called: -- `Thou [art] my father.' `My mother' and `my sister' -- to the worm.
texts.job.17.15: And where [is] now my hope? Yea, my hope, who doth behold it?
texts.job.17.16: [To] the parts of Sheol ye go down, If together on the dust we may rest.
texts.job.18.1: And Bildad the Shuhite answereth and saith: --
texts.job.18.2: When do ye set an end to words? Consider ye, and afterwards do we speak.
texts.job.18.3: Wherefore have we been reckoned as cattle? We have been defiled in your eyes!
texts.job.18.4: (He is tearing himself in his anger.) For thy sake is earth forsaken? And removed is a rock from its place?
texts.job.18.5: Also, the light of the wicked is extinguished. And there doth not shine a spark of his fire.
texts.job.18.6: The light hath been dark in his tent, And his lamp over him is extinguished.
texts.job.18.7: Straitened are the steps of his strength, And cast him down doth his own counsel.
texts.job.18.8: For he is sent into a net by his own feet, And on a snare he doth walk habitually.
texts.job.18.9: Seize on the heel doth a gin, Prevail over him do the designing.
texts.job.18.10: Hidden in the earth is his cord, And his trap on the path.
texts.job.18.11: Round about terrified him have terrors, And they have scattered him -- at his feet.
texts.job.18.12: Hungry is his sorrow, And calamity is ready at his side.
texts.job.18.13: It consumeth the parts of his skin, Consume his parts doth death's first-born.
texts.job.18.14: Drawn from his tent is his confidence, And it causeth him to step to the king of terrors.
texts.job.18.15: It dwelleth in his tent -- out of his provender, Scattered over his habitation is sulphur.
texts.job.18.16: From beneath his roots are dried up, And from above cut off is his crop.
texts.job.18.17: His memorial hath perished from the land, And he hath no name on the street.
texts.job.18.18: They thrust him from light unto darkness, And from the habitable earth cast him out.
texts.job.18.19: He hath no continuator, Nor successor among his people, And none is remaining in his dwellings.
texts.job.18.20: At this day westerns have been astonished And easterns have taken fright.
texts.job.18.21: Only these [are] tabernacles of the perverse, And this the place God hath not known.
texts.job.19.2: Till when do ye afflict my soul, And bruise me with words?
texts.job.19.3: These ten times ye put me to shame, ye blush not. Ye make yourselves strange to me --
texts.job.19.4: And also -- truly, I have erred, With me doth my error remain.
texts.job.19.5: If, truly, over me ye magnify yourselves, And decide against me my reproach;
texts.job.19.6: Know now, that God turned me upside down, And His net against me hath set round,
texts.job.19.7: Lo, I cry out -- violence, and am not answered, I cry aloud, and there is no judgment.
texts.job.19.8: My way He hedged up, and I pass not over, And on my paths darkness He placeth.
texts.job.19.9: Mine honour from off me He hath stripped, And He turneth the crown from my head.
texts.job.19.10: He breaketh me down round about, and I go, And removeth like a tree my hope.
texts.job.19.11: And He kindleth against me His anger, And reckoneth me to Him as His adversaries.
texts.job.19.12: Come in do His troops together, And they raise up against me their way, And encamp round about my tent.
texts.job.19.13: My brethren from me He hath put far off, And mine acquaintances surely Have been estranged from me.
texts.job.19.14: Ceased have my neighbours And my familiar friends have forgotten me,
texts.job.19.15: Sojourners of my house and my maids, For a stranger reckon me: An alien I have been in their eyes.
texts.job.19.16: To my servant I have called, And he doth not answer, With my mouth I make supplication to him.
texts.job.19.17: My spirit is strange to my wife, And my favours to the sons of my [mother's] womb.
texts.job.19.18: Also sucklings have despised me, I rise, and they speak against me.
texts.job.19.19: Abominate me do all the men of my counsel, And those I have loved, Have been turned against me.
texts.job.19.20: To my skin and to my flesh Cleaved hath my bone, And I deliver myself with the skin of my teeth.
texts.job.19.21: Pity me, pity me, ye my friends, For the hand of God hath stricken against me.
texts.job.19.22: Why do you pursue me as God? And with my flesh are not satisfied?
texts.job.19.23: Who doth grant now, That my words may be written? Who doth grant that in a book they may be graven?
texts.job.19.24: With a pen of iron and lead -- For ever in a rock they may be hewn.
texts.job.19.25: That -- I have known my Redeemer, The Living and the Last, For the dust he doth rise.
texts.job.19.26: And after my skin hath compassed this [body], Then from my flesh I see God:
texts.job.19.27: Whom I -- I see on my side, And mine eyes have beheld, and not a stranger, Consumed have been my reins in my bosom.
texts.job.19.28: But ye say, `Why do we pursue after him?' And the root of the matter hath been found in me.
texts.job.19.29: Be ye afraid because of the sword, For furious [are] the punishments of the sword, That ye may know that [there is] a judgment.
texts.job.20.1: And Zophar the Naamathite answereth and saith: --
texts.job.20.2: Therefore my thoughts cause me to answer, And because of my sensations in me.
texts.job.20.3: The chastisement of my shame I hear, And the spirit of mine understanding Doth cause me to answer:
texts.job.20.4: This hast thou known from antiquity? Since the placing of man on earth?
texts.job.20.5: That the singing of the wicked [is] short, And the joy of the profane for a moment,
texts.job.20.6: Though his excellency go up to the heavens, And his head against a cloud he strike --
texts.job.20.7: As his own dung for ever he doth perish, His beholders say: `Where [is] he?'
texts.job.20.8: As a dream he fleeth, and they find him not, And he is driven away as a vision of the night,
texts.job.20.9: The eye hath not seen him, and addeth not. And not again doth his place behold him.
texts.job.20.10: His sons do the poor oppress, And his hands give back his wealth.
texts.job.20.11: His bones have been full of his youth, And with him on the dust it lieth down.
texts.job.20.12: Though he doth sweeten evil in his mouth, Doth hide it under his tongue,
texts.job.20.13: Hath pity on it, and doth not forsake it, And keep it back in the midst of his palate,
texts.job.20.14: His food in his bowels is turned, The bitterness of asps [is] in his heart.
texts.job.20.15: Wealth he hath swallowed, and doth vomit it. From his belly God driveth it out.
texts.job.20.16: Gall of asps he sucketh, Slay him doth the tongue of a viper.
texts.job.20.17: He looketh not on rivulets, Flowing of brooks of honey and butter.
texts.job.20.18: He is giving back [what] he laboured for, And doth not consume [it]; As a bulwark [is] his exchange, and he exults not.
texts.job.20.19: For he oppressed -- he forsook the poor, A house he hath taken violently away, And he doth not build it.
texts.job.20.20: For he hath not known ease in his belly. With his desirable thing he delivereth not himself.
texts.job.20.21: There is not a remnant to his food, Therefore his good doth not stay.
texts.job.20.22: In the fulness of his sufficiency he is straitened. Every perverse hand doth meet him.
texts.job.20.23: It cometh to pass, at the filling of his belly, He sendeth forth against him The fierceness of His anger, Yea, He raineth on him in his eating.
texts.job.20.24: He fleeth from an iron weapon, Pass through him doth a bow of brass.
texts.job.20.25: One hath drawn, And it cometh out from the body, And a glittering weapon from his gall proceedeth. On him [are] terrors.
texts.job.20.26: All darkness is hid for his treasures, Consume him doth a fire not blown, Broken is the remnant in his tent.
texts.job.20.27: Reveal do the heavens his iniquity, And earth is raising itself against him.
texts.job.20.28: Remove doth the increase of his house, Poured forth in a day of His anger.
texts.job.20.29: This [is] the portion of a wicked man from God. And an inheritance appointed him by God.
texts.job.21.2: Hear ye diligently my word, And this is your consolation.
texts.job.21.3: Bear with me, and I speak, And after my speaking -- ye may deride.
texts.job.21.4: I -- to man [is] my complaint? and if [so], wherefore May not my temper become short?
texts.job.21.5: Turn unto me, and be astonished, And put hand to mouth.
texts.job.21.6: Yea, if I have remembered, then I have been troubled. And my flesh hath taken fright.
texts.job.21.7: Wherefore do the wicked live? They have become old, Yea, they have been mighty in wealth.
texts.job.21.8: Their seed is established, Before their face with them, And their offspring before their eyes.
texts.job.21.9: Their houses [are] peace without fear, Nor [is] a rod of God upon them.
texts.job.21.10: His bullock hath eaten corn, and doth not loath. His cow bringeth forth safely, And doth not miscarry.
texts.job.21.11: They send forth as a flock their sucklings, And their children skip,
texts.job.21.12: They lift [themselves] up at timbrel and harp, And rejoice at the sound of an organ.
texts.job.21.13: They wear out in good their days, And in a moment [to] Sheol go down.
texts.job.21.14: And they say to God, `Turn aside from us, And the knowledge of Thy ways We have not desired.
texts.job.21.15: What [is] the Mighty One that we serve Him? And what do we profit when we meet with Him?'
texts.job.21.16: Lo, not in their hand [is] their good, (The counsel of the wicked Hath been far from me.)
texts.job.21.17: How oft is the lamp of the wicked extinguished, And come on them doth their calamity? Pangs He apportioneth in His anger.
texts.job.21.18: They are as straw before wind, And as chaff a hurricane hath stolen away,
texts.job.21.19: God layeth up for his sons his sorrow, He giveth recompense unto him -- and he knoweth.
texts.job.21.20: His own eyes see his destruction, And of the wrath of the Mighty he drinketh.
texts.job.21.21: For what [is] his delight in his house after him, And the number of his months cut off?
texts.job.21.22: To God doth [one] teach knowledge, And He the high doth judge?
texts.job.21.23: This [one] dieth in his perfect strength, Wholly at ease and quiet.
texts.job.21.24: His breasts have been full of milk, And marrow his bones doth moisten.
texts.job.21.25: And this [one] dieth with a bitter soul, And have not eaten with gladness.
texts.job.21.26: Together -- on the dust they lie down, And the worm doth cover them over.
texts.job.21.27: Lo, I have known your thoughts, And the devices against me ye do wrongfully.
texts.job.21.28: For ye say, `Where [is] the house of the noble? And where the tent -- The tabernacles of the wicked?'
texts.job.21.29: Have ye not asked those passing by the way? And their signs do ye not know?
texts.job.21.30: That to a day of calamity is the wicked spared. To a day of wrath they are brought.
texts.job.21.31: Who doth declare to his face his way? And [for] that which he hath done, Who doth give recompence to him?
texts.job.21.32: And he -- to the graves he is brought. And over the heap a watch is kept.
texts.job.21.33: Sweet to him have been the clods of the valley, And after him every man he draweth, And before him there is no numbering.
texts.job.21.34: And how do ye comfort me [with] vanity, And in your answers hath been left trespass?
texts.job.22.1: And Eliphaz the Temanite answereth and saith: --
texts.job.22.2: To God is a man profitable, Because a wise man to himself is profitable?
texts.job.22.3: Is it a delight to the Mighty One That thou art righteous? is it gain, That thou makest perfect thy ways?
texts.job.22.4: Because of thy reverence Doth He reason [with] thee? He entereth with thee into judgment:
texts.job.22.5: Is not thy wickedness abundant? And there is no end to thine iniquities.
texts.job.22.6: For thou takest a pledge of thy brother for nought, And the garments of the naked Thou dost strip off.
texts.job.22.7: Thou causest not the weary to drink water, And from the hungry thou withholdest bread.
texts.job.22.8: As to the man of arm -- he hath the earth, And the accepted of face -- he dwelleth in it.
texts.job.22.9: Widows thou hast sent away empty, And the arms of the fatherless are bruised.
texts.job.22.10: Therefore round about thee [are] snares, And trouble thee doth fear suddenly.
texts.job.22.11: Or darkness -- thou dost not see, And abundance of waters doth cover thee.
texts.job.22.12: Is not God high [in] heaven? And see the summit of the stars, That they are high.
texts.job.22.13: And thou hast said, `What -- hath God known? Through thickness doth He judge?
texts.job.22.14: Thick clouds [are] a secret place to Him, And He doth not see;' And the circle of the heavens He walketh habitually,
texts.job.22.15: The path of the age dost thou observe, That men of iniquity have trodden?
texts.job.22.16: Who have been cut down unexpectedly, A flood is poured out on their foundation.
texts.job.22.17: Those saying to God, `Turn aside from us,' And what doth the Mighty One to them?
texts.job.22.18: And he hath filled their houses [with] good: (And the counsel of the wicked Hath been far from me.)
texts.job.22.19: See do the righteous and they rejoice, And the innocent mocketh at them,
texts.job.22.20: `Surely our substance hath not been cut off, And their excellency hath fire consumed.'
texts.job.22.21: Acquaint thyself, I pray thee, with Him, And be at peace, Thereby thine increase [is] good.
texts.job.22.22: Receive, I pray thee, from His mouth a law, And set His sayings in thy heart.
texts.job.22.23: If thou dost return unto the Mighty Thou art built up, Thou puttest iniquity far from thy tents.
texts.job.22.24: So as to set on the dust a defence, And on a rock of the valleys a covering.
texts.job.22.25: And the Mighty hath been thy defence, And silver [is] strength to thee.
texts.job.22.26: For then on the Mighty thou delightest thyself, And dost lift up unto God thy face,
texts.job.22.27: Thou dost make supplication unto Him, And He doth hear thee, And thy vows thou completest.
texts.job.22.28: And thou decreest a saying, And it is established to thee, And on thy ways hath light shone.
texts.job.22.29: For they have made low, And thou sayest, `Lift up.' And the bowed down of eyes he saveth.
texts.job.22.30: He delivereth the not innocent, Yea, he hath been delivered By the cleanness of thy hands.
texts.job.23.2: Also -- to-day [is] my complaint bitter, My hand hath been heavy because of my sighing.
texts.job.23.3: O that I had known -- and I find Him, I come in unto His seat,
texts.job.23.4: I arrange before Him the cause, And my mouth fill [with] arguments.
texts.job.23.5: I know the words He doth answer me, And understand what He saith to me.
texts.job.23.6: In the abundance of power doth He strive with me? No! surely He putteth [it] in me.
texts.job.23.7: There the upright doth reason with Him, And I escape for ever from my judge.
texts.job.23.8: Lo, forward I go -- and He is not, And backward -- and I perceive him not.
texts.job.23.9: [To] the left in His working -- and I see not, He is covered [on] the right, and I behold not.
texts.job.23.10: For He hath known the way with me, He hath tried me -- as gold I go forth.
texts.job.23.11: On His step hath my foot laid hold, His way I have kept, and turn not aside,
texts.job.23.12: The command of His lips, and I depart not. Above my allotted portion I have laid up The sayings of His mouth.
texts.job.23.13: And He [is] in one [mind], And who doth turn Him back? And His soul hath desired -- and He doth [it].
texts.job.23.14: For He doth complete my portion, And many such things [are] with Him.
texts.job.23.15: Therefore, from His presence I am troubled, I consider, and am afraid of Him.
texts.job.23.16: And God hath made my heart soft, And the Mighty hath troubled me.
texts.job.23.17: For I have not been cut off before darkness, And before me He covered thick darkness.
texts.job.24.1: Wherefore from the Mighty One Times have not been hidden, And those knowing Him have not seen His days.
texts.job.24.2: The borders they reach, A drove they have taken violently away, Yea, they do evil.
texts.job.24.3: The ass of the fatherless they lead away, They take in pledge the ox of the widow,
texts.job.24.4: They turn aside the needy from the way, Together have hid the poor of the earth.
texts.job.24.5: Lo, wild asses in a wilderness, They have gone out about their work, Seeking early for prey, A mixture for himself -- food for young ones.
texts.job.24.6: In a field his provender they reap, And the vineyard of the wicked they glean.
texts.job.24.7: The naked they cause to lodge Without clothing. And there is no covering in the cold.
texts.job.24.8: From the inundation of hills they are wet, And without a refuge -- have embraced a rock.
texts.job.24.9: They take violently away From the breast the orphan, And on the poor they lay a pledge.
texts.job.24.10: Naked, they have gone without clothing, And hungry -- have taken away a sheaf.
texts.job.24.11: Between their walls they make oil, Wine-presses they have trodden, and thirst.
texts.job.24.12: Because of enmity men do groan, And the soul of pierced ones doth cry, And God doth not give praise.
texts.job.24.13: They have been among rebellious ones of light, They have not discerned His ways, Nor abode in His paths.
texts.job.24.14: At the light doth the murderer rise, He doth slay the poor and needy, And in the night he is as a thief.
texts.job.24.15: And the eye of an adulterer Hath observed the twilight, Saying, `No eye doth behold me.' And he putteth the face in secret.
texts.job.24.16: He hath dug in the darkness -- houses; By day they shut themselves up, They have not known light.
texts.job.24.17: When together, morning [is] to them death shade, When he discerneth the terrors of death shade.
texts.job.24.18: Light he [is] on the face of the waters, Vilified is their portion in the earth, He turneth not the way of vineyards.
texts.job.24.19: Drought -- also heat -- consume snow-waters, Sheol [those who] have sinned.
texts.job.24.20: Forget him doth the womb, Sweeten [on] him doth the worm, No more is he remembered, And broken as a tree is wickedness.
texts.job.24.21: Treating evil the barren [who] beareth not, And [to] the widow he doth no good,
texts.job.24.22: And hath drawn the mighty by his power, He riseth, and none believeth in life.
texts.job.24.23: He giveth to him confidence, and he is supported, And his eyes [are] on their ways.
texts.job.24.24: High they were [for] a little, and they are not, And they have been brought low. As all [others] they are shut up, And as the head of an ear of corn cut off.
texts.job.24.25: And if not now, who doth prove me a liar, And doth make of nothing my word?
texts.job.25.1: And Bildad the Shuhite answereth and saith: --
texts.job.25.2: The rule and fear [are] with Him, Making peace in His high places.
texts.job.25.3: Is their [any] number to His troops? And on whom ariseth not His light?
texts.job.25.4: And what? is man righteous with God? And what? is he pure -- born of a woman?
texts.job.25.5: Lo -- unto the moon, and it shineth not, And stars have not been pure in His eyes.
texts.job.25.6: How much less man -- a grub, And the son of man -- a worm!
texts.job.26.2: What -- thou hast helped the powerless, Saved an arm not strong!
texts.job.26.3: What -- thou hast given counsel to the unwise, And wise plans in abundance made known.
texts.job.26.4: With whom hast thou declared words? And whose breath came forth from thee?
texts.job.26.5: The Rephaim are formed, Beneath the waters, also their inhabitants.
texts.job.26.6: Naked [is] Sheol over-against Him, And there is no covering to destruction.
texts.job.26.7: Stretching out the north over desolation, Hanging the earth upon nothing,
texts.job.26.8: Binding up the waters in His thick clouds, And the cloud is not rent under them.
texts.job.26.9: Taking hold of the face of the throne, Spreading over it His cloud.
texts.job.26.10: A limit He hath placed on the waters, Unto the boundary of light with darkness.
texts.job.26.11: Pillars of the heavens do tremble, And they wonder because of His rebuke.
texts.job.26.12: By His power He hath quieted the sea, And by His understanding smitten the proud.
texts.job.26.13: By His Spirit the heavens He beautified, Formed hath His hand the fleeing serpent.
texts.job.26.14: Lo, these [are] the borders of His way, And how little a matter is heard of Him, And the thunder of His might Who doth understand?
texts.job.27.1: And Job addeth to lift up his simile, and saith: --
texts.job.27.2: God liveth! He turned aside my judgment, And the Mighty -- He made my soul bitter.
texts.job.27.3: For all the while my breath [is] in me, And the spirit of God in my nostrils.
texts.job.27.4: My lips do not speak perverseness, And my tongue doth not utter deceit.
texts.job.27.5: Pollution to me -- if I justify you, Till I expire I turn not aside mine integrity from me.
texts.job.27.6: On my righteousness I have laid hold, And I do not let it go, My heart doth not reproach me while I live.
texts.job.27.7: As the wicked is my enemy, And my withstander as the perverse.
texts.job.27.8: For what [is] the hope of the profane, When He doth cut off? When God doth cast off his soul?
texts.job.27.9: His cry doth God hear, When distress cometh on him?
texts.job.27.10: On the Mighty doth he delight himself? Call God at all times?
texts.job.27.11: I shew you by the hand of God, That which [is] with the Mighty I hide not.
texts.job.27.12: Lo, ye -- all of you -- have seen, And why [is] this -- ye are altogether vain?
texts.job.27.13: This [is] the portion of wicked man with God, And the inheritance of terrible ones From the Mighty they receive.
texts.job.27.14: If his sons multiply -- for them [is] a sword. And his offspring [are] not satisfied [with] bread.
texts.job.27.15: His remnant in death are buried, And his widows do not weep.
texts.job.27.16: If he heap up as dust silver, And as clay prepare clothing,
texts.job.27.17: He prepareth -- and the righteous putteth [it] on, And the silver the innocent doth apportion.
texts.job.27.18: He hath built as a moth his house, And as a booth a watchman hath made.
texts.job.27.19: Rich he lieth down, and he is not gathered, His eyes he hath opened, and he is not.
texts.job.27.20: Overtake him as waters do terrors, By night stolen him away hath a whirlwind.
texts.job.27.21: Take him up doth an east wind, and he goeth, And it frighteneth him from his place,
texts.job.27.22: And it casteth at him, and doth not spare, From its hand he diligently fleeth.
texts.job.27.23: It clappeth at him its hands, And it hisseth at him from his place.
texts.job.28.1: Surely there is for silver a source, And a place for the gold they refine;
texts.job.28.2: Iron from the dust is taken, And [from] the firm stone brass.
texts.job.28.3: An end hath he set to darkness, And to all perfection he is searching, A stone of darkness and death-shade.
texts.job.28.4: A stream hath broken out from a sojourner, Those forgotten of the foot, They were low, from man they wandered.
texts.job.28.5: The earth! from it cometh forth bread, And its under-part is turned like fire.
texts.job.28.6: A place of the sapphire [are] its stones, And it hath dust of gold.
texts.job.28.7: A path -- not known it hath a ravenous fowl, Nor scorched it hath an eye of the kite,
texts.job.28.8: Nor trodden it have the sons of pride, Not passed over it hath the fierce lion.
texts.job.28.9: Against the flint he sent forth his hand, He overturned from the root mountains.
texts.job.28.10: Among rocks, brooks he hath cleaved, And every precious thing hath his eye seen.
texts.job.28.11: From overflowing floods he hath bound, And the hidden thing bringeth out [to] light.
texts.job.28.12: And the wisdom -- whence is it found? And where [is] this, the place of understanding?
texts.job.28.13: Man hath not known its arrangement, Nor is it found in the land of the living.
texts.job.28.14: The deep hath said, `It [is] not in me,' And the sea hath said, `It is not with me.'
texts.job.28.15: Gold is not given for it, Nor is silver weighed -- its price.
texts.job.28.16: It is not valued with pure gold of Ophir, With precious onyx and sapphire,
texts.job.28.17: Not equal it do gold and crystal, Nor [is] its exchange a vessel of fine gold.
texts.job.28.18: Corals and pearl are not remembered, The acquisition of wisdom [is] above rubies.
texts.job.28.19: Not equal it doth the topaz of Cush, With pure gold it is not valued.
texts.job.28.20: And the wisdom -- whence doth it come? And where [is] this, the place of understanding?
texts.job.28.21: It hath been hid from the eyes of all living. And from the fowl of the heavens It hath been hidden.
texts.job.28.22: Destruction and death have said: `With our ears we have heard its fame.'
texts.job.28.23: God hath understood its way, And He hath known its place.
texts.job.28.24: For He to the ends of the earth doth look, Under the whole heavens He doth see,
texts.job.28.25: To make for the wind a weight, And the waters He meted out in measure.
texts.job.28.26: In His making for the rain a limit, And a way for the brightness of the voices,
texts.job.28.27: Then He hath seen and declareth it, He hath prepared it, and also searched it out,
texts.job.28.28: And He saith to man: -- `Lo, fear of the Lord, that [is] wisdom, And to turn from evil [is] understanding.'
texts.job.29.1: And Job addeth to lift up his simile, and saith: --
texts.job.29.2: Who doth make me as [in] months past, As [in] the days of God's preserving me?
texts.job.29.3: In His causing His lamp to shine on my head, By His light I walk [through] darkness.
texts.job.29.4: As I have been in days of my maturity, And the counsel of God upon my tent.
texts.job.29.5: When yet the Mighty One [is] with me. Round about me -- my young ones,
texts.job.29.6: When washing my goings with butter, And the firm rock [is] with me rivulets of oil.
texts.job.29.7: When I go out to the gate by the city, In a broad place I prepare my seat.
texts.job.29.8: Seen me have youths, and they, been hidden, And the aged have risen -- they stood up.
texts.job.29.9: Princes have kept in words, And a hand they place on their mouth.
texts.job.29.10: The voice of leaders hath been hidden, And their tongue to the palate hath cleaved.
texts.job.29.11: For the ear heard, and declareth me happy, And the eye hath seen, and testifieth [to] me.
texts.job.29.12: For I deliver the afflicted who is crying, And the fatherless who hath no helper.
texts.job.29.13: The blessing of the perishing cometh on me, And the heart of the widow I cause to sing.
texts.job.29.14: Righteousness I have put on, and it clotheth me, As a robe and a diadem my justice.
texts.job.29.15: Eyes I have been to the blind, And feet to the lame [am] I.
texts.job.29.16: A father I [am] to the needy, And the cause I have not known I search out.
texts.job.29.17: And I break the jaw-teeth of the perverse, And from his teeth I cast away prey.
texts.job.29.18: And I say, `With my nest I expire, And as the sand I multiply days.'
texts.job.29.19: My root is open unto the waters, And dew doth lodge on my branch.
texts.job.29.20: My honour [is] fresh with me, And my bow in my hand is renewed.
texts.job.29.21: To me they have hearkened, Yea, they wait, and are silent for my counsel.
texts.job.29.22: After my word they change not, And on them doth my speech drop,
texts.job.29.23: And they wait as [for] rain for me, And their mouth they have opened wide [As] for the latter rain.
texts.job.29.24: I laugh unto them -- they give no credence, And the light of my face cause not to fall.
texts.job.29.25: I choose their way, and sit head, And I dwell as a king in a troop, When mourners he doth comfort.
texts.job.30.1: And now, laughed at me, Have the younger in days than I, Whose fathers I have loathed to set With the dogs of my flock.
texts.job.30.2: Also -- the power of their hands, why [is it] to me? On them hath old age perished.
texts.job.30.3: With want and with famine gloomy, Those fleeing to a dry place, Formerly a desolation and waste,
texts.job.30.4: Those cropping mallows near a shrub, And broom-roots [is] their food.
texts.job.30.5: From the midst they are cast out, (They shout against them as a thief),
texts.job.30.6: In a frightful place of valleys to dwell, Holes of earth and clefts.
texts.job.30.7: Among shrubs they do groan, Under nettles they are gathered together.
texts.job.30.8: Sons of folly -- even sons without name, They have been smitten from the land.
texts.job.30.9: And now, their song I have been, And I am to them for a byword.
texts.job.30.10: They have abominated me, They have kept far from me, And from before me have not spared to spit.
texts.job.30.11: Because His cord He loosed and afflicteth me, And the bridle from before me, They have cast away.
texts.job.30.12: On the right hand doth a brood arise, My feet they have cast away, And they raise up against me, Their paths of calamity.
texts.job.30.13: They have broken down my path, By my calamity they profit, `He hath no helper.'
texts.job.30.14: As a wide breach they come, Under the desolation have rolled themselves.
texts.job.30.15: He hath turned against me terrors, It pursueth as the wind mine abundance, And as a thick cloud, Hath my safety passed away.
texts.job.30.16: And now, in me my soul poureth itself out, Seize me do days of affliction.
texts.job.30.17: At night my bone hath been pierced in me, And mine eyelids do not lie down.
texts.job.30.18: By the abundance of power, Is my clothing changed, As the mouth of my coat it doth gird me.
texts.job.30.19: Casting me into mire, And I am become like dust and ashes.
texts.job.30.20: I cry unto Thee, And Thou dost not answer me, I have stood, and Thou dost consider me.
texts.job.30.21: Thou art turned to be fierce to me, With the strength of Thy hand, Thou oppresest me.
texts.job.30.22: Thou dost lift me up, On the wind Thou dost cause me to ride, And Thou meltest -- Thou levellest me.
texts.job.30.23: For I have known To death Thou dost bring me back, And [to] the house appointed for all living.
texts.job.30.24: Surely not against the heap Doth He send forth the hand, Though in its ruin they have safety.
texts.job.30.25: Did not I weep for him whose day is hard? Grieved hath my soul for the needy.
texts.job.30.26: When good I expected, then cometh evil, And I wait for light, and darkness cometh.
texts.job.30.27: My bowels have boiled, and have not ceased, Gone before me have days of affliction.
texts.job.30.28: Mourning I have gone without the sun, I have risen, in an assembly I cry.
texts.job.30.29: A brother I have been to dragons, And a companion to daughters of the ostrich.
texts.job.30.30: My skin hath been black upon me, And my bone hath burned from heat,
texts.job.30.31: And my harp doth become mourning, And my organ the sound of weeping.
texts.job.31.1: A covenant I made for mine eyes, And what -- do I attend to a virgin?
texts.job.31.2: And what [is] the portion of God from above? And the inheritance of the Mighty from the heights?
texts.job.31.3: Is not calamity to the perverse? And strangeness to workers of iniquity?
texts.job.31.4: Doth not He see my ways, And all my steps number?
texts.job.31.5: If I have walked with vanity, And my foot doth hasten to deceit,
texts.job.31.6: He doth weigh me in righteous balances, And God doth know my integrity.
texts.job.31.7: If my step doth turn aside from the way, And after mine eyes hath my heart gone, And to my hands cleaved hath blemish,
texts.job.31.8: Let me sow -- and another eat, And my products let be rooted out.
texts.job.31.9: If my heart hath been enticed by woman, And by the opening of my neighbour I laid wait,
texts.job.31.10: Grind to another let my wife, And over her let others bend.
texts.job.31.11: For it [is] a wicked thing, and a judicial iniquity;
texts.job.31.12: For a fire it [is], to destruction it consumeth, And among all mine increase doth take root,
texts.job.31.13: If I despise the cause of my man-servant, And of my handmaid, In their contending with me,
texts.job.31.14: Then what do I do when God ariseth? And when He doth inspect, What do I answer Him?
texts.job.31.15: Did not He that made me in the womb make him? Yea, prepare us in the womb doth One.
texts.job.31.16: If I withhold from pleasure the poor, And the eyes of the widow do consume,
texts.job.31.17: And I do eat my morsel by myself, And the orphan hath not eat of it,
texts.job.31.18: (But from my youth He grew up with me as [with] a father, And from the belly of my mother I am led.)
texts.job.31.19: If I see [any] perishing without clothing, And there is no covering to the needy,
texts.job.31.20: If his loins have not blessed me, And from the fleece of my sheep He doth not warm himself,
texts.job.31.21: If I have waved at the fatherless my hand, When I see in [him] the gate of my court,
texts.job.31.22: My shoulder from its blade let fall, And mine arm from the bone be broken.
texts.job.31.23: For a dread unto me [is] calamity [from] God, And because of His excellency I am not able.
texts.job.31.24: If I have made gold my confidence, And to the pure gold have said, `My trust,'
texts.job.31.25: If I rejoice because great [is] my wealth, And because abundance hath my hand found,
texts.job.31.26: If I see the light when it shineth, And the precious moon walking,
texts.job.31.27: And my heart is enticed in secret, And my hand doth kiss my mouth,
texts.job.31.28: It also [is] a judicial iniquity, For I had lied to God above.
texts.job.31.29: If I rejoice at the ruin of my hater, And stirred up myself when evil found him,
texts.job.31.30: Yea, I have not suffered my mouth to sin, To ask with an oath his life.
texts.job.31.31: If not -- say ye, O men of my tent, `O that we had of his flesh, we are not satisfied.'
texts.job.31.32: In the street doth not lodge a stranger, My doors to the traveller I open.
texts.job.31.33: If I have covered as Adam my transgressions, To hide in my bosom mine iniquity,
texts.job.31.34: Because I fear a great multitude, And the contempt of families doth affright me, Then I am silent, I go not out of the opening.
texts.job.31.35: Who giveth to me a hearing? lo, my mark. The Mighty One doth answer me, And a bill hath mine adversary written.
texts.job.31.36: If not -- on my shoulder I take it up, I bind it a crown on myself.
texts.job.31.37: The number of my steps I tell Him, As a leader I approach Him.
texts.job.31.38: If against me my land doth cry out, And together its furrows weep,
texts.job.31.39: If its strength I consumed without money, And the life of its possessors, I have caused to breathe out,
texts.job.31.40: Instead of wheat let a thorn go forth, And instead of barley a useless weed! The words of Job are finished.
texts.job.32.1: And these three men cease from answering Job, for he [is] righteous in his own eyes,
texts.job.32.2: and burn doth the anger of Elihu son of Barachel the Buzite, of the family of Ram; against Job hath his anger burned, because of his justifying himself more than God;
texts.job.32.3: and against his three friends hath his anger burned, because that they have not found an answer, and condemn Job.
texts.job.32.4: And Elihu hath waited earnestly beside Job with words, for they are older than he in days.
texts.job.32.5: And Elihu seeth that there is no answer in the mouth of the three men, and his anger burneth.
texts.job.32.6: And Elihu son of Barachel the Buzite answereth and saith: -- Young I [am] in days, and ye [are] age Therefore I have feared, And am afraid of shewing you my opinion.
texts.job.32.7: I said: Days do speak, And multitude of years teach wisdom.
texts.job.32.8: Surely a spirit is in man, And the breath of the Mighty One Doth cause them to understand.
texts.job.32.9: The multitude are not wise, Nor do the aged understand judgment.
texts.job.32.10: Therefore I have said: Hearken to me, I do shew my opinion -- even I.
texts.job.32.11: Lo, I have waited for your words, I give ear unto your reasons, Till ye search out sayings.
texts.job.32.12: And unto you I attend, And lo, there is no reasoner for Job, [Or] answerer of his sayings among you.
texts.job.32.13: Lest ye say, We have found wisdom, God doth thrust him away, not man.
texts.job.32.14: And he hath not set in array words for me, And with your sayings I do not answer him.
texts.job.32.15: (They have broken down, They have not answered again, They removed from themselves words.
texts.job.32.16: And I have waited, but they do not speak, For they have stood still, They have not answered any more.)
texts.job.32.17: I answer, even I -- my share, I shew my opinion -- even I.
texts.job.32.18: For I have been full of words, Distressed me hath the spirit of my breast,
texts.job.32.19: Lo, my breast [is] as wine not opened, Like new bottles it is broken up.
texts.job.32.20: I speak, and there is refreshment to me, I open my lips and answer.
texts.job.32.21: Let me not, I pray you, accept the face of any, Nor unto man give flattering titles,
texts.job.32.22: For I have not known to give flattering titles, In a little doth my Maker take me away.
texts.job.33.1: And yet, I pray thee, O Job, Hear my speech and [to] all my words give ear.
texts.job.33.2: Lo, I pray thee, I have opened my mouth, My tongue hath spoken in the palate.
texts.job.33.3: Of the uprightness of my heart [are] my sayings, And knowledge have my lips clearly spoken.
texts.job.33.4: The Spirit of God hath made me, And the breath of the Mighty doth quicken me.
texts.job.33.5: If thou art able -- answer me, Set in array before me -- station thyself.
texts.job.33.6: Lo, I [am], according to thy word, for God, From the clay I -- I also, have been formed.
texts.job.33.7: Lo, my terror doth not frighten thee, And my burden on thee is not heavy.
texts.job.33.8: Surely -- thou hast said in mine ears, And the sounds of words I hear:
texts.job.33.9: `Pure [am] I, without transgression, Innocent [am] I, and I have no iniquity.
texts.job.33.10: Lo, occasions against me He doth find, He doth reckon me for an enemy to Him,
texts.job.33.11: He doth put in the stocks my feet, He doth watch all my paths.'
texts.job.33.12: Lo, [in] this thou hast not been righteous, I answer thee, that greater is God than man.
texts.job.33.13: Wherefore against Him hast thou striven, When [for] all His matters He answereth not?
texts.job.33.14: For once doth God speak, and twice, (He doth not behold it.)
texts.job.33.15: In a dream -- a vision of night, In the falling of deep sleep on men, In slumberings on a bed.
texts.job.33.16: Then He uncovereth the ear of men, And for their instruction sealeth:
texts.job.33.17: To turn aside man [from] doing, And pride from man He concealeth.
texts.job.33.18: He keepeth back his soul from corruption, And his life from passing away by a dart.
texts.job.33.19: And he hath been reproved With pain on his bed, And the strife of his bones [is] enduring.
texts.job.33.20: And his life hath nauseated bread, And his soul desirable food.
texts.job.33.21: His flesh is consumed from being seen, And high are his bones, they were not seen!
texts.job.33.22: And draw near to the pit doth his soul, And his life to those causing death.
texts.job.33.23: If there is by him a messenger, An interpreter -- one of a thousand, To declare for man his uprightness:
texts.job.33.24: Then He doth favour him and saith, `Ransom him from going down to the pit, I have found an atonement.'
texts.job.33.25: Fresher [is] his flesh than a child's, He returneth to the days of his youth.
texts.job.33.26: He maketh supplication unto God, And He accepteth him. And he seeth His face with shouting, And He returneth to man His righteousness.
texts.job.33.27: He looketh on men, and saith, `I sinned, And uprightness I have perverted, And it hath not been profitable to me.
texts.job.33.28: He hath ransomed my soul From going over into the pit, And my life on the light looketh.'
texts.job.33.29: Lo, all these doth God work, Twice -- thrice with man,
texts.job.33.30: To bring back his soul from the pit, To be enlightened with the light of the living.
texts.job.33.31: Attend, O Job, hearken to me, Keep silent, and I -- I do speak.
texts.job.33.32: If there are words -- answer me, Speak, for I have a desire to justify thee.
texts.job.33.33: If there are not -- hearken thou to me, Keep silent, and I teach thee wisdom.
texts.job.34.2: Hear, O wise men, my words, And, O knowing ones, give ear to me.
texts.job.34.3: For the ear doth try words, And the palate tasteth to eat.
texts.job.34.4: Judgment let us choose for ourselves, Let us know among ourselves what [is] good.
texts.job.34.5: For Job hath said, `I have been righteous, And God hath turned aside my right,
texts.job.34.6: Against my right do I lie? Mortal [is] mine arrow -- without transgression.'
texts.job.34.7: Who [is] a man like Job? He drinketh scoffing like water,
texts.job.34.8: And he hath travelled for company With workers of iniquity, So as to go with men of wickedness.
texts.job.34.9: For he hath said, `It doth not profit a man, When he delighteth himself with God.'
texts.job.34.10: Therefore, O men of heart, hearken to me; Far be it from God to do wickedness, And [from] the Mighty to do perverseness:
texts.job.34.11: For the work of man he repayeth to him, And according to the path of each He doth cause him to find.
texts.job.34.12: Yea, truly, God doth not do wickedly, And the Mighty doth not pervert judgment.
texts.job.34.13: Who hath inspected for Himself the earth? And who hath placed all the habitable world?
texts.job.34.14: If He doth set on him His heart, His spirit and his breath unto Him He gathereth.
texts.job.34.15: Expire doth all flesh together, And man to dust returneth.
texts.job.34.16: And if [there is] understanding, hear this, Give ear to the voice of my words.
texts.job.34.17: Yea, doth one hating justice govern? Or the Most Just dost thou condemn?
texts.job.34.18: Who hath said to a king -- `Worthless,' Unto princes -- `Wicked?'
texts.job.34.19: That hath not accepted the person of princes, Nor hath known the rich before the poor, For a work of His hands [are] all of them.
texts.job.34.20: [In] a moment they die, and at midnight Shake do people, and they pass away, And they remove the mighty without hand.
texts.job.34.21: For His eyes [are] on the ways of each, And all his steps He doth see.
texts.job.34.22: There is no darkness nor death-shade, For workers of iniquity to be hidden there;
texts.job.34.23: For He doth not suffer man any more, To go unto God in judgment,
texts.job.34.24: He breaketh the mighty -- no searching! And He appointeth others in their stead.
texts.job.34.25: Therefore He knoweth their works, And He hath overturned by night, And they are bruised.
texts.job.34.26: As wicked He hath stricken them, In the place of beholders.
texts.job.34.27: Because that against right They have turned aside from after Him, And none of His ways have considered wisely,
texts.job.34.28: To cause to come in unto Him The cry of the poor, And the cry of the afflicted He heareth.
texts.job.34.29: And He giveth rest, and who maketh wrong? And hideth the face, and who beholdeth it? And in reference to a nation and to a man, [It is] the same.
texts.job.34.30: From the reigning of a profane man, From the snares of a people;
texts.job.34.31: For unto God hath any said: `I have taken away, I do not corruptly,
texts.job.34.32: Besides [that which] I see, shew Thou me, If iniquity I have done -- I do not add?'
texts.job.34.33: By thee doth He recompense, That thou hast refused -- That thou dost choose, and not I? And what thou hast known, speak.
texts.job.34.34: Let men of heart say to me, And a wise man is hearkening to me.
texts.job.34.35: Job -- not with knowledge doth he speak, And his words [are] not with wisdom.
texts.job.34.36: My Father! let Job be tried -- unto victory, Because of answers for men of iniquity,
texts.job.34.37: For he doth add to his sin, Transgression among us he vomiteth, And multiplieth his sayings to God.
texts.job.35.2: This hast thou reckoned for judgment: Thou hast said -- `My righteousness [is] more than God's?'
texts.job.35.3: For thou sayest, `What doth it profit Thee! What do I profit from my sin?'
texts.job.35.4: I return thee words, and thy friends with thee,
texts.job.35.5: Behold attentively the heavens -- and see, And behold the clouds, They have been higher than thou.
texts.job.35.6: If thou hast sinned, what dost thou against Him? And thy transgressions have been multiplied, What dost thou to Him?
texts.job.35.7: If thou hast been righteous, What dost thou give to Him? Or what from thy hand doth He receive?
texts.job.35.8: For a man like thyself [is] thy wickedness, And for a son of man thy righteousness.
texts.job.35.9: Because of the multitude of oppressions They cause to cry out, They cry because of the arm of the mighty.
texts.job.35.10: And none said, `Where [is] God my maker? Giving songs in the night,
texts.job.35.11: Teaching us more than the beasts of the earth, Yea, than the fowl of the heavens He maketh us wiser.'
texts.job.35.12: There they cry, and He doth not answer, Because of the pride of evil doers.
texts.job.35.13: Surely vanity God doth not hear, And the Mighty doth not behold it.
texts.job.35.14: Yea, though thou sayest thou dost not behold Him, Judgment [is] before Him, and stay for Him.
texts.job.35.15: And, now, because there is not, He hath appointed His anger, And He hath not known in great extremity.
texts.job.35.16: And Job [with] vanity doth open his mouth, Without knowledge words he multiplieth.
texts.job.36.2: Honour me a little, and I shew thee, That yet for God [are] words.
texts.job.36.3: I lift up my knowledge from afar, And to my Maker I ascribe righteousness.
texts.job.36.4: For, truly, my words [are] not false, The perfect in knowledge [is] with thee.
texts.job.36.5: Lo, God [is] mighty, and despiseth not, Mighty [in] power [and] heart.
texts.job.36.6: He reviveth not the wicked, And the judgment of the poor appointeth;
texts.job.36.7: He withdraweth not from the righteous His eyes, And [from] kings on the throne, And causeth them to sit for ever, and they are high,
texts.job.36.8: And if prisoners in fetters They are captured with cords of affliction,
texts.job.36.9: Then He declareth to them their work, And their transgressions, Because they have become mighty,
texts.job.36.10: And He uncovereth their ear for instruction, And saith that they turn back from iniquity.
texts.job.36.11: If they do hear and serve, They complete their days in good, And their years in pleasantness.
texts.job.36.12: And if they do not hearken, By the dart they pass away, And expire without knowledge.
texts.job.36.13: And the profane in heart set the face, They cry not when He hath bound them.
texts.job.36.14: Their soul dieth in youth, And their life among the defiled.
texts.job.36.15: He draweth out the afflicted in his affliction, And uncovereth in oppression their ear.
texts.job.36.16: And also He moved thee from a strait place, [To] a broad place -- no straitness under it, And the sitting beyond of thy table Hath been full of fatness.
texts.job.36.17: And the judgment of the wicked thou hast fulfilled, Judgment and justice are upheld -- because of fury,
texts.job.36.18: Lest He move thee with a stroke, And the abundance of an atonement turn thee not aside.
texts.job.36.19: Doth He value thy riches? He hath gold, and all the forces of power.
texts.job.36.20: Desire not the night, For the going up of peoples in their stead.
texts.job.36.21: Take heed -- do not turn unto iniquity, For on this thou hast fixed Rather than [on] affliction.
texts.job.36.22: Lo, God doth sit on high by His power, Who [is] like Him -- a teacher?
texts.job.36.23: Who hath appointed unto Him his way? And who said, `Thou hast done iniquity?'
texts.job.36.24: Remember that thou magnify His work That men have beheld.
texts.job.36.25: All men have looked on it, Man looketh attentively from afar.
texts.job.36.26: Lo, God [is] high, And we know not the number of His years, Yea, there [is] no searching.
texts.job.36.27: When He doth diminish droppings of the waters, They refine rain according to its vapour,
texts.job.36.28: Which clouds do drop, They distil on man abundantly.
texts.job.36.29: Yea, doth [any] understand The spreadings out of a cloud? The noises of His tabernacle?
texts.job.36.30: Lo, He hath spread over it His light, And the roots of the sea He hath covered,
texts.job.36.31: For by them He doth judge peoples, He giveth food in abundance.
texts.job.36.32: By two palms He hath covered the light, And layeth a charge over it in meeting,
texts.job.36.33: He sheweth by it [to] his friend substance, Anger against perversity.
texts.job.37.1: Also, at this my heart trembleth, And it moveth from its place.
texts.job.37.2: Hearken diligently to the trembling of His voice, Yea, the sound from His mouth goeth forth.
texts.job.37.3: Under the whole heavens He directeth it, And its light [is] over the skirts of the earth.
texts.job.37.4: After it roar doth a voice -- He thundereth with the voice of His excellency, And He doth not hold them back, When His voice is heard.
texts.job.37.5: God thundereth with His voice wonderfully, Doing great things and we know not.
texts.job.37.6: For to snow He saith, `Be [on] the earth.' And the small rain and great rain of His power.
texts.job.37.7: Into the hand of every man he sealeth, For the knowledge by all men of His work.
texts.job.37.8: And enter doth the beast into covert, And in its habitations it doth continue.
texts.job.37.9: From the inner chamber cometh a hurricane, And from scatterings winds -- cold,
texts.job.37.10: From the breath of God is frost given, And the breadth of waters is straitened,
texts.job.37.11: Yea, by filling He doth press out a cloud, Scatter a cloud doth His light.
texts.job.37.12: And it is turning itself round by His counsels, For their doing all He commandeth them, On the face of the habitable earth.
texts.job.37.13: Whether for a rod, or for His land, Or for kindness -- He doth cause it to come.
texts.job.37.14: Hear this, O Job, Stand and consider the wonders of God.
texts.job.37.15: Dost thou know when God doth place them, And caused to shine the light of His cloud?
texts.job.37.16: Dost thou know the balancings of a cloud? The wonders of the Perfect in knowledge?
texts.job.37.17: How thy garments [are] warm, In the quieting of the earth from the south?
texts.job.37.18: Thou hast made an expanse with Him For the clouds -- strong as a hard mirror!
texts.job.37.19: Let us know what we say to Him, We set not in array because of darkness.
texts.job.37.20: Is it declared to Him that I speak? If a man hath spoken, surely he is swallowed up.
texts.job.37.21: And now, they have not seen the light, Bright it [is] in the clouds, And the wind hath passed by and cleanseth them.
texts.job.37.22: From the golden north it cometh, Beside God [is] fearful honour.
texts.job.37.23: The Mighty! we have not found Him out, High in power and judgment, He doth not answer! And abundant in righteousness,
texts.job.37.24: Therefore do men fear Him, He seeth not any of the wise of heart.
texts.job.38.1: And Jehovah answereth Job out of the whirlwind, and saith: --
