texts.job.15.28: And had inhabited demolished cities, houses, wherein men would not dwell, that were destined to become heaps.
texts.job.15.29: He shall not be rich, nor shall his substance continue, neither shall their shadow stretch along on the earth;
texts.job.15.30: He shall not depart out of darkness, his young branch, shall the flame dry up, and he shall depart, by the breath of his own mouth!
texts.job.15.31: Let no one trust in him that—by vanity—is deceived, for, vanity, shall be his recompense;
texts.job.15.32: Before his day, shall it be accomplished, with, his palm-top, not covered with leaves;
texts.job.15.33: He shall wrong—like a vine—his sour grapes, and shall cast off—as an olive-tree—his blossom.
texts.job.15.34: For, the family of the impious, is unfruitful, and, a fire, hath devoured the tents of bribery;
texts.job.15.35: Conceiving mischief, and bringing forth iniquity, yea, their inmost soul, prepareth deceit.
texts.job.16.2: I have heard many such things, Wearisome comforters, are ye all!
texts.job.16.3: Is there to be an end to windy words? Or what so strongly exciteth thee, that thou must respond?
texts.job.16.4: I also, like you, could speak,—If your soul were in the place of my soul, I could string together words against you, and could therewith shake over you my head.
texts.job.16.5: I could make you determined, by my mouth, and then my lip-solace should restrain you.
texts.job.16.6: Though I do speak, unassuaged is my stinging pain,—And, if I forbear, of what am I relieved?
texts.job.16.7: But, now, hath he wearied me, thou hast destroyed all my family;
texts.job.16.8: And, having captured me, it hath served, as a witness; and so my wasting away hath risen up against me, in my face, it answereth.
texts.job.16.9: His anger, hath torn and persecuted me, He hath gnashed upon me with his teeth, Mine adversary, hath sharpened his eyes for me.
texts.job.16.10: They have gaped upon me with their mouth, With reproach, have they smitten my cheek, Together, against me, have they closed their ranks.
texts.job.16.11: GOD doth abandon me to him that is perverse, and, into the hands of the lawless, he throweth me headlong.
texts.job.16.12: At ease, was I when he shattered me, Yea he seized me by my neck, and dashed me in pieces, then set me up for himself as a mark:
texts.job.16.13: His archers came round against me, He clave asunder my reins, and spared not, He poured out, on the earth, my gall:
texts.job.16.14: He made a breach in me, breach upon breach, He ran upon me, like a mighty man.
texts.job.16.15: Sackcloth, sewed I on my skin, and rolled—in the dust—my horn:
texts.job.16.16: My face, is reddened from weeping, and, upon mine eyelashes, is the death-shade:—
texts.job.16.17: Though no violence was in my hands, and, my prayer, was pure.
texts.job.16.18: O earth! do not cover my blood, and let there be no place for mine outcry.
texts.job.16.19: Even now, lo! in the heavens, is my witness,
texts.job.16.20: And, he that voucheth for me is on high. My friends are, they who scorn me, Unto GOD, hath mine eye shed tears:—
texts.job.16.21: That one might plead, for a man, with GOD,—Even a son of man, for his friend!
texts.job.16.22: When, a few years, come, then, by a path by which I shall not return, shall I depart.
texts.job.17.1: My spirit, is broken, My days, are extinguished, Graves, are left me.
texts.job.17.2: Verily there are mockers, with me! And, on their insults, mine eye doth rest.
texts.job.17.3: Appoint it, I pray thee—be thou surety for me with thyself, Who is there that, on my side, can pledge himself?
texts.job.17.4: For, their heart, hast thou kept back from understanding, On this account, thou wilt not exalt them.
texts.job.17.5: He that, for a share, denounceth friends, even, the eyes of his children, shall be dim.
texts.job.17.6: But he hath set me, as the byword of peoples, And, one to be spit on in the face, do I become.
texts.job.17.7: Therefore hath mine eye become dim from vexation, and, my members, are like a shadow, all of them.
texts.job.17.8: Upright men shall be astounded over this, and, the innocent, against the impious, shall rouse themselves.
texts.job.17.9: That the righteous may hold on his way, and, the clean of hands, increase in strength.
texts.job.17.10: But indeed, as for them all, will ye bethink yourselves and enter into it, I pray you? Or shall I not find, among you, one who is wise?
texts.job.17.11: My days, are past, my purposes, are broken off, the possessions of my heart!
texts.job.17.12: Night for day, they appoint, Light, is near, by reason of darkness!
texts.job.17.13: If I wait for hades as my house, in darkness, have spread out my couch;
texts.job.17.14: To corruption, have exclaimed, My father, thou! My mother! and My sister! to the worm.
texts.job.17.15: Where then would be my hope? And, as for my blessedness, who should see it!
texts.job.17.16: With me to hades, would they go down, If, wholly—into the dust, is the descent!
texts.job.18.1: Then responded Bildad the Shuhite, and said:—
texts.job.18.2: How long will ye make a perversion of words? Ye should understand, and, afterwards, we could speak.
texts.job.18.3: Wherefore are we accounted like beasts? or appear stupid, in thine eyes?
texts.job.18.4: One tearing in pieces his own soul in his anger,—For thy sake, shall the earth be forsaken? or the rock be moved out of its place?
texts.job.18.5: Even the light of the lawless, shall go out,—Neither shall shine the flame of his fire;
texts.job.18.6: The light, hath darkened in his tent, Yea, his lamp above him, goeth out;
texts.job.18.7: The steppings of his strength are hemmed in, and his own counsel casteth him down;
texts.job.18.8: For he is thrust into a net by his own feet, and, upon a trap, he marcheth;
texts.job.18.9: There catcheth him—by the heel—a gin, there holdeth him fast—a noose:
texts.job.18.10: Concealed in the ground is a cord for him,—and a snare for him, on the path.
texts.job.18.11: Round about, terrors have startled him, and have driven him to his feet.
texts.job.18.12: Let his strength be famished, and, calamity, be ready at his side;
texts.job.18.13: Let it devour the members of his body, Let the firstborn of death devour his members;
texts.job.18.14: Uprooted, out of his tent, be his confidence, and let it drive him down to the king of terrors;
texts.job.18.15: There shall dwell in his tent, what is naught-of-his, Let brimstone be strewed over his dwelling;
texts.job.18.16: Beneath, let his roots be dried up, and, above, be cut off his branch;
texts.job.18.17: His memorial, have perished out of the land, and let him have no name over the face of the open field;
texts.job.18.18: Let them thrust him out of light into darkness, Yea, out of the world, let them chase him;
texts.job.18.19: Let him have neither scion nor seed among his people, neither any survivor in his place of sojourn:
texts.job.18.20: Over his day, have they been astounded who come behind, and, them who are in advance, a shudder hath seized.
texts.job.18.21: Surely, these, are the dwellings of him that is perverse, and, this, is the place of him that knoweth not GOD.
texts.job.19.2: How long will ye grieve my soul? or crush me with words?
texts.job.19.3: These ten times, have ye reviled me, Shameless ye wrong me.
texts.job.19.4: And even if indeed I have erred, with myself lodgeth mine error.
texts.job.19.5: If indeed, against me, ye must needs magnify yourselves, and plead, against me, my reproach.
texts.job.19.6: Know, then, that, God, hath overthrown me, and, within his net, enclosed me.
texts.job.19.7: Lo! I cry—out: Violence! but receive no answer, I cry aloud, but there is no vindication;
texts.job.19.8: My way, hath he walled up, that I cannot pass, and, upon my paths, hath he made darkness rest;
texts.job.19.9: My glory—from off me, hath he stripped, and hath removed the crown of my head;
texts.job.19.10: He hath ruined me on every side, and I am gone, and he hath taken away—like a tree—my hope;
texts.job.19.11: Yea he hath kindled against me his anger, and accounted me towards him like unto his adversaries;
texts.job.19.12: Together, enter his troops and have cast up, against me, their mound, and have encamped all around my tent;
texts.job.19.13: My Brethren—from beside me, hath he moved far away, and, mine acquaintance, are wholly estranged from me;
texts.job.19.14: Failed me, have my near of kin, and, mine intimate acquaintances, have forgotten me;
texts.job.19.15: Ye guests of my house and my maidens, A stranger, have ye accounted me, An alien, have I become in their eyes;
texts.job.19.16: To mine own servant, I called, and he would not answer, With mine own mouth, I kept entreating him;
texts.job.19.17: My breath, is strange to my wife, and I am loathsome to the sons of my own mother;
texts.job.19.18: Even young children, despise me, I rise up, and they speak against me;
texts.job.19.19: All the men of mine intimate circle abhor me, and, these whom I loved, have turned against me;
texts.job.19.20: Unto my skin and unto my flesh, have my bones cleaved, and I have escaped with the akin of my teeth.
texts.job.19.21: Pity me! pity me! ye, my friends, for, the hand of GOD, hath stricken me!
texts.job.19.22: Wherefore should ye persecute me as GOD? and, with my flesh, should not he satisfied?
texts.job.19.23: Oh, then, that my words, could be written, Oh that, in a record, they could be inscribed:
texts.job.19.24: That, with a stylus of iron and [with] lead, for all time—in the rock, they could be graven!
texts.job.19.25: But, I, know that, my redeemer, liveth, and, as the Last over [my] dust, will he arise;
texts.job.19.26: And, though, after my skin is struck off, this [followeth], yet, apart from my flesh, shall I see GOD:
texts.job.19.27: Whom, I myself, shall see, on my side, and, mine own eyes, [shall] have looked upon, and not those of a stranger. Exhausted are my deepest desires in my bosom!
texts.job.19.28: Surely ye should say—Why should we persecute him? seeing, the root of the matter, is found in me.
texts.job.19.29: Be ye afraid—on your part—of the face of the sword, because, wrath, [bringeth] the punishments of the sword, to the end ye may know the Almighty.
texts.job.20.1: Then responded Zophar the Naamathite, and said:—
texts.job.20.2: Not so, do my thoughts answer me, and to this end, is my haste within me:
texts.job.20.3: The correction meant to confound me, I must hear, but, the spirit—out of my understanding, will give me a reply.
texts.job.20.4: Knowest thou, this—from antiquity, from the placing of man upon earth:—
texts.job.20.5: That, the joy-shout of the lawless, is short, and, the rejoicing of the impious, for a moment?
texts.job.20.6: Though his elevation mount up to the heavens, and, his head, to the clouds, doth reach,
texts.job.20.7: Like his own stubble, shall he utterly perish, They who had seen him, shall say, Where is he?
texts.job.20.8: Like a dream, shall he fly away, and they shall not find him, yea he shall be chased away, as a vision of the night.
texts.job.20.9: The eye that hath scanned him, shall not do it again, neither, any more, shall his place behold him:
texts.job.20.10: His children, shall seek the favour of the poor, and, his own hand, shall give back his wealth.
texts.job.20.11: His bones, are full of youthful vigour, yet, with him—in the dust, shall it lie down.
texts.job.20.12: Though, a sweet taste in his mouth, be given by vice, though he hide it under his tongue;
texts.job.20.13: Though he spare it, and will not let it go, but retain it in the midst of his mouth,
texts.job.20.14: His food, in his stomach, is changed, the gall of adders, within him!
texts.job.20.15: Wealth, hath he swallowed, and hath vomited the same, Out of his belly, shall, GOD, drive it forth:
texts.job.20.16: The poison of adders, shall he suck, The tongue of the viper shall slay him;
texts.job.20.17: Let him not see in the channels the flowings of torrents of honey and milk.
texts.job.20.18: In vain, he toiled, he shall not swallow, like wealth to be restored, in which he cannot exult!
texts.job.20.19: For he hath oppressed—hath forsaken the poor, A house, hath he seized, which he cannot rebuild.
texts.job.20.20: Surely he hath known no peace in his inmost mind,—With his dearest thing, shall he not get away:
texts.job.20.21: Nothing escaped his devouring greed,—For this cause, shall his prosperity not continue:
texts.job.20.22: When his abundance is gone, he shall be in straits, All the power of distress, shall come upon him.
texts.job.20.23: It shall be that, to fill his belly, he will thrust at him the glow of his anger, and rain [it] upon him for his punishment.
texts.job.20.24: He shall flee from the armour of iron,—There shall pierce him, a bow of bronze!
texts.job.20.25: He hath drawn it out, and it hath come forth out of his back,—yea the flashing arrow-head, out of his gall, There shall march on him—terrors:
texts.job.20.26: Every misfortune, is laid up for his treasures,—There shall consume, a fire, not blown up,—it shall destroy what remaineth in his tent:
texts.job.20.27: The heavens shall reveal his iniquity, and, the earth, be rising up against him:
texts.job.20.28: The increase of his house shall vanish, melting away in the day of his anger.
texts.job.20.29: This, is the portion of the lawless man, from God, and the inheritance decreed him from the Mighty One.
texts.job.21.2: Hear ye patiently my words, and let this be your consolation:
texts.job.21.3: Suffer me, that, I, may speak, and, after I have spoken, thou canst mock!
texts.job.21.4: Did, I, unto man, make my complaint? Wherefore, then, should my spirit not be impatient?
texts.job.21.5: Turn round to me, and be astonished, and lay hand on mouth!
texts.job.21.6: When I call to mind, then am I dismayed, and there seizeth my flesh a shuddering:—
texts.job.21.7: Wherefore do, lawless men, live, advance in years, even wax mighty in power?
texts.job.21.8: Their seed, is established in their sight, along with them, yea their offspring, before their eyes;
texts.job.21.9: Their houses, are at peace, without dread, neither is, the rod of GOD, upon them;
texts.job.21.10: His bull, covereth, and causeth not aversion, His cow safely calveth, and casteth not her young;
texts.job.21.11: They send forth—like a flock—their young ones, and, their children, skip about for joy;
texts.job.21.12: They rejoice aloud as [with] timbrel and lyre, and make merry to the sound of the pipe;
texts.job.21.13: They complete, in prosperity, their days, and, in a moment to hades, they sink down.
texts.job.21.14: Yet they said unto GOD, Depart from us, and, In the knowledge of thy ways, find we no pleasure.
texts.job.21.15: What is the Almighty, that we should serve him? Or what shall we profit, that we should urge him?
texts.job.21.16: Lo! not in their own hand, is their welfare, The counsel of lawless men, is far from me!
texts.job.21.17: How oft, the lamp of the lawless, goeth out, and their calamity, cometh upon them, Sorrows, apportioneth he in his anger;
texts.job.21.18: They become as straw before the wind, and as chaff, which the storm stealeth away.
texts.job.21.19: Shall, GOD, reserve, for his children, his sorrow? Let him recompense him so that he may know it;
texts.job.21.20: His own eyes, shall see his misfortune, and, the wrath of the Almighty, shall he drink.
texts.job.21.21: For what shall be his pleasure in his house after him, when, the number of his months, is cut in twain?
texts.job.21.22: Is it, to GOD, one can teach knowledge, seeing that, he, shall judge, them who are on high?
texts.job.21.23: This, man dieth, in the very perfection of his prosperity, wholly tranquil and secure;
texts.job.21.24: His veins, are filled with nourishment, and, the marrow of his bones, is fresh;
texts.job.21.25: Whereas, this other man, dieth, in bitterness of soul, and hath never tasted good fortune:
texts.job.21.26: Together, in the dust, they lie down, and, the worm, spreadeth a covering over them.
texts.job.21.27: Lo! I know your plans, and the devices, wherewith ye would do me violence!
texts.job.21.28: For ye say, Where is the house of the noble-minded? And where the dwelling-tent of the lawless?
texts.job.21.29: Have ye not asked the passers-by in the way? And, their signs, can ye not recognise?
texts.job.21.30: That, to the day of calamity, is the wicked reserved, to the day of indignant visitation, are they led.
texts.job.21.31: Who can declare—to his face—his way? And, what, he, hath done, who shall recompense to him?
texts.job.21.32: Yet, he, to the graves, is borne, and, over the tomb, one keepeth watch;
texts.job.21.33: Pleasant to him are the mounds of the torrent-bed,—and, after him, doth every man march, as, before him, there were without number.
texts.job.21.34: How then should ye comfort me with vanity, since, as for your replies, there lurketh, [in them] treachery?
texts.job.22.1: Then responded Eliphaz the Temanite, and said:—
texts.job.22.2: Unto GOD, can a man act as friend? Surely a discreet man befriendeth himself!
texts.job.22.3: Is it a pleasure to the Almighty, that thou shouldst be righteous? or any profit, that thou shouldst be blameless in thy ways?
texts.job.22.4: Is it, for thy reverence, that he will accuse thee? will enter with thee into judgment?
texts.job.22.5: Is not, thy wickedness, great? and, without end, [are not] thine iniquities?
texts.job.22.6: Surely then hast been wont to put thy brother in pledge, for nothing, and, the garments of the ill-clad, hast thou stripped off:
texts.job.22.7: No water—to the weary, hast thou given to drink, and, from the hungry, thou hast withheld bread:
texts.job.22.8: A man of might, to him, pertaineth the land, and, the favorite, dwelleth therein:
texts.job.22.9: Widows, thou hast sent away empty, and, the arms of the fatherless, thou dost crush.
texts.job.22.10: For this cause, round about thee, are snares, and a dread startleth thee suddenly;
texts.job.22.11: Or darkness—thou canst not see, and, a flood of waters, covereth thee.
texts.job.22.12: Is not, GOD, [in] the height of the heavens? Behold, then, the head of the stars, that they are high.
texts.job.22.13: Wilt thou say then, What doth GOD know? Out through a thick cloud, can he judge?
texts.job.22.14: Dark clouds, are a veil to him, and he cannot see, or, the vault of the heavens, doth he walk?
texts.job.22.15: The path of the ancient time, wilt thou mark, which the men of iniquity trod?
texts.job.22.16: Who were snatched away before the time, and, a stream, washed away their foundation?
texts.job.22.17: Who had been saying unto GOD, Depart from us! and—What can the Almighty do for himself?
texts.job.22.18: Yet, he, had filled their houses with good! The counsel of the lawless, then, is far from me:
texts.job.22.19: The righteous shall see and rejoice, and, the innocent, shall laugh them to scorn:
texts.job.22.20: If our assailants do not vanish, then, their abundance, a fire consumeth!
texts.job.22.21: Shew thyself to be one with him—I pray thee—and prosper, thereby, shall there come on thee blessing.
texts.job.22.22: Accept, I beseech thee, from his mouth—instruction,—and lay up his sayings in thy heart.
texts.job.22.23: If thou return unto the Almighty and submit thyself, if thou far remove perversity from thy tent,
texts.job.22.24: Then lay up, in the dust, precious ore, and, among the stones of the torrent-beds, fine gold:
texts.job.22.25: So shall, the Almighty, become, thy precious ores, yea glittering silver unto thee!
texts.job.22.26: For, then, in the Almighty, shalt thou take exquisite delight, and shalt lift up—unto GOD—thy face;
texts.job.22.27: Thou shalt make entreaty unto him, and he will hear thee, and, thy vows, shalt thou pay;
texts.job.22.28: And thou shalt decree a purpose, and it shall be fulfilled unto thee, and, upon thy ways, shall have shone a light;
texts.job.22.29: When men cast themselves down, then thou shalt say: Up! And, him that is of downcast eyes, shall he save;
texts.job.22.30: He shall deliver the innocent, and thou shalt escape by the pureness of thy hands.
texts.job.23.2: Even to-day, is my complaint rebellion? His hand, is heavier than my groaning.
texts.job.23.3: Oh that I knew where I might find him! I would come even unto his dwelling-place;
texts.job.23.4: I would set out, before him, a plea, and, my mouth, would I fill with arguments;
texts.job.23.5: I would note the words wherewith he would respond to me, and would mark what he would say to me.
texts.job.23.6: Would he, with fulness of might, contend with me? Nay, surely, he, would give heed to me!
texts.job.23.7: There an upright man, might reason with him, so should I deliver myself completely from my judge.
texts.job.23.8: Behold! eastward, I go, but he is not there, and, westward, but I perceive him not;
texts.job.23.9: On the north, where he worketh, but I get no vision, He hideth himself on the south that I cannot see him.
texts.job.23.10: But, he, knoweth the way that I choose, Having tried me, as gold, I shall come forth.
texts.job.23.11: Of his steps, my foot taketh hold, His way, have I kept, and not swerved;
texts.job.23.12: The command of his lips, and would not go back, and, in my bosom, have I treasured the words of his lips.
texts.job.23.13: But, he, is one, and who can turn him? What his soul desired, he hath done.
texts.job.23.14: Surely he will accomplish what is decreed for me, and, many such things, hath he in store.
texts.job.23.15: For this cause, from his presence, am I driven in fear, I diligently consider and am kept back from him in dread:
texts.job.23.16: Yea, GOD, hath made timid my heart, and, the Almighty, hath put me in terror.
texts.job.23.17: Because I was not cut off before the darkness, nor, before my face, did the gloom form a shroud.
texts.job.24.1: Wherefore, since from the Almighty times are not hid, have, his knowing ones, no vision of his days?
texts.job.24.2: Boundaries, men move back, flocks, they seize and consume;
texts.job.24.3: The ass of the fatherless, they drive off, they take in pledge the ox of the widow;
texts.job.24.4: They turn aside the needy out of the way, at once, are the humbled of the land made to hide themselves.
texts.job.24.5: Lo! [as] wild asses in the wilderness, they go forth with their work, eager seekers for prey, the waste plain, yieldeth them food for their young;
texts.job.24.6: In the field—a man’s fodder, they cut down, and, the vineyard of the lawless, they strip of its late berries;
texts.job.24.7: Ill-clad, they are left to lodge without clothing, and have no covering in the cold;
texts.job.24.8: With the sweeping rain of the mountains, are they wet, and, through having no shelter, they embrace a rock.
texts.job.24.9: Men tear, from the breast, the fatherless, and, over the poor, they take a pledge;
texts.job.24.10: Naked, they go about without clothing, and, famished, they carry the sheaves;
texts.job.24.11: Between their walls, are they exposed to the sun, Wine-presses, they tread, and yet are thirsty;
texts.job.24.12: Out of the city—out of the houses, they make outcry. and, the soul of the wounded, calleth for help, and, GOD, doth not regard it as foolish.
texts.job.24.13: They, have become rebels against the light,—they are not acquainted with the ways thereof, neither abide they in the paths thereof.
texts.job.24.14: With the light, riseth the murderer, He slayeth the poor and needy, And, in the night, he becometh like a thief.
texts.job.24.15: And, the eye of the adulterer, watcheth for the evening twilight, saying, Not an eye will see me! A covering for the face, he putteth on;
texts.job.24.16: He breaketh, in the dark, into houses,—By day, they lock themselves in, They know not the light;
texts.job.24.17: For, in the case of all such, morning to them is the death-shade, For, to be recognised, is a death-shade terror.
texts.job.24.18: Swift is he on the face of the waters, Speedily vanished their share in the land, He turneth not to the way of the vineyards.
texts.job.24.19: Drought and heat, steal away snow water, Hades, them who have sinned.
texts.job.24.20: Maternal love shall forget him, the worm shall find him sweet, No more shall he be remembered, but perversity shall be shivered like a tree.
texts.job.24.21: He oppresseth the barren who beareth not, and, to the widow, he doeth not good;
texts.job.24.22: Yea he draggeth along the mighty by his strength, He riseth up, and none hath assurance of life;
texts.job.24.23: It is given him to be secure, and confident, yet, his eyes, are upon their ways.
texts.job.24.24: They are exalted a little, and are not, Yea having been laid low, like all men, are they gathered, Even as the top of an ear of corn, do they hang down.
texts.job.24.25: But, if not, who then can convict me of falsehood? or make of no account my words?
texts.job.25.1: Then responded Bildad the Shuhite, and said:—
texts.job.25.2: Dominion and dread, are with him, who causeth prosperity among his lofty ones;
texts.job.25.3: Is there any number to his troops? And upon whom ariseth not his light?
texts.job.25.4: How then shall, a mortal, be just with GOD? Or how shall he be pure who is born of a woman?
texts.job.25.5: Look as far as the moon, and it is not clear, and, the stars, are not bright in his eyes!
texts.job.25.6: How much less a mortal who is a creeping thing? Or a son of the earth-born who is a worm?
texts.job.26.2: How hast thou given help to one of no-strength? given victory to an arm of no-power?
texts.job.26.3: How hast thou given counsel to one of no-wisdom? or, effective wisdom, abundantly made known?
texts.job.26.4: Whom hast thou taught speech? Whose inspiration hath come from thee?
texts.job.26.5: The shades, tremble, beneath the waters and their inhabitants;
texts.job.26.6: Naked is hades before him, and there is no covering to destruction;
texts.job.26.7: Who stretcheth out the north over emptiness, hangeth the earth upon nothingness;
texts.job.26.8: Who bindeth up the waters in his thick clouds, and the cloud is not rent beneath them;
texts.job.26.9: Who shutteth-in the face of the throne, he spreadeth over it his cloud;
texts.job.26.10: A, boundary, hath he encircled on the face of the waters, as far as where light ends in darkness;
texts.job.26.11: The pillars of the heavens, are shaken, and are terrified at his rebuke:
texts.job.26.12: By his strength, hath he excited the sea, and, by his skill, hath he shattered the Crocodile:
texts.job.26.13: By his spirit, hath he arched the heavens, His hand hath pierced the fleeing serpent.
texts.job.26.14: Lo! these, are the fringes of his way, and what a whisper of a word hath been heard of him! But, the thunder of his might, who could understand?
texts.job.27.1: And Job again took up his measure, and said:—
texts.job.27.2: As GOD liveth who hath taken away my right, even the Almighty, who hath embittered my soul;
texts.job.27.3: All the while my inspiration is in me, and the spirit of GOD is in my nostrils,
texts.job.27.4: Verily my lips shall not speak perversity, nor shall, my tongue, utter deceit.
texts.job.27.5: Far be it from me! that I should justify, you,—Even until I breathe my last, will I not let go mine integrity from me:
texts.job.27.6: On my righteousness, have I taken fast hold, and will not give it up, My heart shall not reproach any of my days.
texts.job.27.7: Let mine enemy be a veritably lawless one! And, he that lifteth himself up against me, one veritably perverse!
texts.job.27.8: For what shall be the hope of the impious, though he graspeth with greed, when GOD shall draw forth his soul?
texts.job.27.9: His outcry, will GOD hear, when there cometh upon him distress?
texts.job.27.10: Verily, in the Almighty, he will not find delight, nor call on GOD continually!
texts.job.27.11: I would teach you, by the hand of GOD, That which is with the Almighty, will I not conceal.
texts.job.27.12: Lo! ye, have, all of you, seen, Wherefore, then, is it, that ye are utterly without purpose?
texts.job.27.13: This, is the portion of a lawless man with GOD, That, the heritage of tyrants—from the Almighty, he shall receive.
texts.job.27.14: If his children be multiplied, for them, [there is] the sword, and, his offspring, shall not be filled with bread;
texts.job.27.15: His survivors, by pestilence, shall come to the grave, and, his widows, shall not weep;
texts.job.27.16: Though he heap up silver like, dust, and, like a pile, he prepare clothing,
texts.job.27.17: He may prepare, but, the righteous, shall put on, and, the silver, shall the innocent apportion.
texts.job.27.18: He hath built, like a moth, his house,—like a hut, which a watcher hath made.
texts.job.27.19: The rich man, shall lie down, and not do it again, his eyes, hath he opened, and then is not.
texts.job.27.20: There shall reach him—like waters—terrors, By night, a storm-wind hath stolen him away;
texts.job.27.21: An east wind shall lift him up, and he shall depart, and it shall sweep him away out of his place;
texts.job.27.22: And He will cast upon him and not spare, Out of his hand, shall he, swiftly flee;
texts.job.27.23: He shall clap over him his hands, and shall hiss him forth out of his place.
texts.job.28.1: Though there is, for silver, a vein, and a place for the gold they refine;
texts.job.28.2: Iron, out of the ore, is taken, and, stone, poureth out copper;
texts.job.28.3: An end, hath one set to the darkness, and, into every extremity, is, he, making search, for the stone of darkness and death-shade;
texts.job.28.4: He hath sunken a shaft, away from the inhabitants; Places forsaken by the foot, they hang down, away from men, sway to and fro;
texts.job.28.5: As for the earth, out of it, cometh forth bread, and, under it, is upturned, as it were fire;
texts.job.28.6: The place of sapphires, are the stones thereof, and it hath, nuggets of gold:—
texts.job.28.7: A path, the vulture hath not discerned, nor hath the eye of the hawk scanned it;
texts.job.28.8: Ravenous beasts have not made a track thereof, neither hath the lion marched thereon:
texts.job.28.9: Upon the flint, hath he thrust forth his hand, He hath turned up mountains by the roots;
texts.job.28.10: Among the rocks, hath he cut open streams, and, every precious thing, hath his eye seen:
texts.job.28.11: From trickling, he restraineth, rivers, and, some hidden thing, is he bringing out to light.
texts.job.28.12: Yet where can, Wisdom, be found? And where is the place of understanding?
texts.job.28.13: Mortal knoweth not the way thereof, neither can it be found in the land of the living;
texts.job.28.14: The resounding deep, hath said, It is not in me! And, the sea, hath said, It is not with me!
texts.job.28.15: Pure gold cannot be given in its stead, neither can silver he weighed as the value thereof;
texts.job.28.16: It cannot be put into the scales against the gold of Ophir, with costly onyx, or sapphire;
texts.job.28.17: Neither gold nor crystal can compare with it, nor can, the exchange thereof, be a vessel of pure gold,
texts.job.28.18: Coral or crystal, cannot be mentioned, Yea, a possession, is wisdom, above red coral;
texts.job.28.19: The topaz of Ethiopia cannot compare with it, Against purest gold, can it not be weighed.
texts.job.28.20: Whence then cometh, wisdom? And where is the place of understanding?
texts.job.28.21: Seeing it hath been hid from the eyes of every living thing, and, from the bird of the heavens, hath it been concealed?
texts.job.28.22: Destruction and death, have said, With our ears, have we heard the report thereof!
texts.job.28.23: GOD, understandeth the way thereof, and, he, discerneth the place thereof;
texts.job.28.24: For, he, unto the ends of the earth, directeth his look, under all the heavens, he seeth;
texts.job.28.25: Making, for the wind, a weight, and, the waters, he proved by measure,
texts.job.28.26: When he made, for the rain, a decree, and a way for the lightning of thunders,
texts.job.28.27: Then, saw he it, and declared it, He settled it, yea also he searched it out;
texts.job.28.28: And said to the son of earth, Lo! the reverence of the Lord, that, is wisdom, and, to avoid evil, is understanding.
texts.job.29.1: And Job again took up his measure, and said,
texts.job.29.2: Oh that it were with me as in the months of old, as in the days, when, GOD, used to watch over me;
texts.job.29.3: When his lamp shone over my head, by whose light, I could go through darkness;
texts.job.29.4: As I was, in the days of my prime, when, the intimacy of GOD, was over my tent;
texts.job.29.5: While yet the Almighty was with me, round about me, were my young men;
texts.job.29.6: When my steps were bathed in milk, and, the rock, poured out beside me, rivulets of oil:
texts.job.29.7: When I went out to the gate unto the city, in the open place, made ready my seat,
texts.job.29.8: Young men saw me, and hid themselves, and, the aged, arose—they stood;
texts.job.29.9: Rulers, restrained speech, and, a hand, laid they on their mouth;
texts.job.29.10: The voice of nobles, was hushed, and their tongue to their palate, did cleave;
texts.job.29.11: When, the ear, heard, then it pronounced me happy, When, the eye, saw, then it bare me witness;
texts.job.29.12: Because I used to deliver the oppressed who was crying out for aid, the fatherless also, and him that had no helper;
texts.job.29.13: The blessing of him that was ready to perish, upon me was wont to descend, and, the heart of the widow, caused I to sing for joy;
texts.job.29.14: Righteousness, I put on, and it clothed me, Like a robe and turban, was my, justice;
texts.job.29.15: Eyes, became I to the, blind, and, feet to the lame, was, I!
texts.job.29.16: A father, was, I, to the needy, and, as for the cause which I knew not, I used to search it out;
texts.job.29.17: And I shivered the fangs of the perverse,—and, out of his teeth, I tare the prey.
texts.job.29.18: Then said I, Like a stem, shall I grow old, yea, as the sand, shall I multiply days:
texts.job.29.19: My root, is laid open to the waters, and, the dew, shall lodge for the night in my boughs;
texts.job.29.20: Mine honour, shall be young again with me, and, my bow, in my hand, be renewed.
texts.job.29.21: To me, men hearkened, and waited, and kept silence for my counsel;
texts.job.29.22: After I had spoken, they spake not again, and, upon them, used my speech to drop;
texts.job.29.23: And they waited, as for rain, for me, and, their mouths, they opened wide for the spring-rain;
texts.job.29.24: I laughed at them—they lost confidence, and, the light of my countenance, they suffered not to fail;
texts.job.29.25: I chose out their way, and sat chief,—and abode, as king, in an army, as one who, to mourners, giveth comfort.
texts.job.30.1: But, now, they who are of fewer days than I, have poured derision upon me; whose fathers I refused—to set with the dogs of my flock.
texts.job.30.2: Even the strength of their hands, wherefore was it mine? Upon them, vigour was lost;
texts.job.30.3: In want and hunger, they were lean,—who used to gnaw the dry ground, a dark night of desolation!
texts.job.30.4: Who used to pluck off the mallow by the bushes, with the root of the broom for their food;
texts.job.30.5: Out of the midst, were they driven, men shouted after them, as after a thief;
texts.job.30.6: In the fissures, of the ravines had they to dwell, in holes of dust and crags;
texts.job.30.7: Among the bushes, used they to shriek, Under the bramble, were they huddled together:
texts.job.30.8: Sons of the base, yea sons of the nameless, they were scourged out of the land.
texts.job.30.9: But, now, their song, have I become, Yea I serve them for a byword;
texts.job.30.10: They abhor me—have put themselves far from me, and, from my face, have not withheld—spittle!
texts.job.30.11: Because, my girdle, he had loosened and had humbled me, therefore, the bridle—in my presence, cast they off;
texts.job.30.12: On my right hand, the young brood rose up,—My feet, they thrust aside, and cast up against me their earthworks of destruction;
texts.job.30.13: They brake up my path,—My engulfing ruin, they helped forward, unaided;
texts.job.30.14: As through a wide breach, came they on, with a crashing noise, they rolled themselves along.
texts.job.30.15: There are turned upon me terrors,—Chased away as with a wind, is mine abundance, and, as a cloud, hath passed away my prosperity.
texts.job.30.16: Now, therefore, over myself, my soul poureth itself out, There seize me days of affliction:
texts.job.30.17: Night, boreth, my bones, all over me,—and, my sinews, find no rest;
texts.job.30.18: Most effectually, is my skin disfigured,—Like the collar of my tunic, it girdeth me about:
texts.job.30.19: He hath cast me into the mire, and I have become like dust and ashes.
texts.job.30.20: I cry out for help unto thee, and thou dost not answer, I stand still, and thou dost gaze at me;
texts.job.30.21: Thou art turned to become a cruel one unto me, With the might of thy hand, thou assailest me;
texts.job.30.22: Thou liftest up me to the wind, thou carriest me away, and the storm maketh me faint;
texts.job.30.23: For I know that, unto death, thou wilt bring me back, even unto the house of meeting for every one living.
texts.job.30.24: Only, against a heap of ruins, will one not thrust a hand! Surely, when one is in calamity—for that very reason, is there an outcry for help.
texts.job.30.25: Verily I wept, for him whose lot was hard, Grieved was my soul, for the needy.
texts.job.30.26: Surely, for good, I looked, but there came in evil, And I waited for light, but there came in darkness;
texts.job.30.27: I boiled within me, and rested not, There confronted me—days of affliction;
texts.job.30.28: In gloom, I walked along, without sun, I arose—in the convocation, I cried out for help;
texts.job.30.29: A brother, became I to the brutes that howl, and a companion to the birds that screech:
texts.job.30.30: My skin, turned black, and peeled off me, and, my bones, burned with heat:
texts.job.30.31: Thus is attuned to mourning—my lyre, and my flute, to the noise of them who weep.
texts.job.31.1: A covenant, I solemnised for mine eyes,—How then could I gaze upon a virgin?
texts.job.31.2: Or what would have been my portion of GOD from above? Or what inheritance of the Almighty from on high?
texts.job.31.3: Is there not calamity, for the perverse? and misfortune, for the workers of iniquity?
texts.job.31.4: Would, he, not see my ways? and of all my steps, take account?
texts.job.31.5: Verily I walked not in falsity, nor did my foot haste unto deceit:—
texts.job.31.6: Let him weigh me in balances of righteousness,—and let GOD take note of mine integrity!
texts.job.31.7: If my goings have swerved from the way,—and, after mine eyes, hath gone my heart, and, to my hands, hath adhered any stain,
texts.job.31.8: Let me sow but, another, eat. And let, what I have springing up, be uprooted!
texts.job.31.9: If my heart hath been enticed unto a woman, or, by the door of my neighbour, I have lien in wait,
texts.job.31.10: Let my wife, grind to another, and, over her, let others bend!
texts.job.31.11: Surely that had been a shameful thing! and that an iniquity for the judges!
texts.job.31.12: Surely, a fire, had that been, which, unto destruction, would have consumed, and, of all mine increase, had it torn up the root.
texts.job.31.13: If I refused the right of my servant, or my handmaid, when they contended with me,
texts.job.31.14: What then could I have done when GOD rose up? And, when he visited, what could I have answered him?
texts.job.31.15: Did not he who, in the womb, made me, make him? And is not he who formed us in the body one?
texts.job.31.16: If I withheld—from pleasure—the poor, or, the eyes of the widow, I dimmed;
texts.job.31.17: Or, used to eat my morsel alone, so that the fatherless did not eat thereof;
texts.job.31.18: Surely, from my youth, he grew up to me, as to a father, and, from my birth, I acted as guide to her:
texts.job.31.19: If I saw one perishing for lack of clothing, or that the needy had no covering;
texts.job.31.20: If his loins did not bless me, or if, with the fleece of my lambs, he did not warm himself;
texts.job.31.21: If I shook—against the fatherless—my hand, when I saw, in the gate, his need of my help,
texts.job.31.22: Let, my shoulder, from the shoulder-blade, fall, and, my arm, from the upper bone, be broken;
texts.job.31.23: For, a dread unto me, was calamity from GOD, and, from his majesty, I could not escape.
texts.job.31.24: If I made gold my stay, and, to precious metal, said, My confidence!
texts.job.31.25: If I rejoiced because great was my substance, and, an abundance, my hand had discovered;
texts.job.31.26: If I looked at the sun, when it flashed forth light, or at the moon, majestically marching along;
texts.job.31.27: And befooled secretly was my heart, so that my hand kissed my mouth,
texts.job.31.28: That too, had been a judicial iniquity, For I should have been false to GOD, above.
texts.job.31.29: If rejoiced in the misfortune of him that hated me, or exulted when calamity found him;—
texts.job.31.30: Neither did I suffer my palate to sin, by asking, with a curse, for his life:
texts.job.31.31: If the men of my household have not said, Oh for some of his flesh—we cannot get filled,
texts.job.31.32: Outside, the sojourner lodged not for the night, My doors—to the wayfarer, I threw open.
texts.job.31.33: If I covered, like Adam, my transgressions, by hiding in my bosom mine iniquity,
texts.job.31.34: Then let me be made to tremble at a great throng, yea let, the contempt of families, terrify me, so that, keeping silence, I shall not go out of the door!
texts.job.31.35: Oh that I had one to hear me, Lo! my crossmark, May, the Almighty, answer me! And would that, a book, mine opponent had written!
texts.job.31.36: Oh! would I not, upon my shoulder, lift it, or bind it as a crown upon me;
texts.job.31.37: The number of my footsteps, I would declare to him, Like a noble, would I draw near to him.
texts.job.31.38: If, against me, my ground used to cry out, and, together, my ridges did weep;
texts.job.31.39: If, the strength thereof, I used to eat, without payment, and, the soul of the holders thereof, I made groan;
texts.job.31.40: Instead of wheat, let there come forth bramble, and, instead of barley, a bad-smelling weed! Ended are the words of Job.
texts.job.32.1: So these three men ceased to respond to Job, because, he, was righteous in their eyes.
texts.job.32.2: Then was kindled the anger of Elihu, son of Barachel the Buzite of the family of Ram,—against Job, was kindled his anger, because he justified his own soul rather than God;
texts.job.32.3: and, against his three friends, was kindled his anger,—because that they found not a response, and condemned God.
texts.job.32.4: But, Elihu, had waited for Job with words, because the others were older than he.
texts.job.32.5: Howbeit, when Elihu saw that there was no response in the mouth of the three men, then was kindled his anger.
texts.job.32.6: So then Elihu, son of Barachel, the Buzite, responded and said:—Young, am I, whereas, ye, are aged, For this cause, I faltered, and feared—to shew my knowledge unto you:
texts.job.32.7: I said, Days, should speak,—and, the multitude of years, should make known wisdom.
texts.job.32.8: Yet surely, there is a spirit in men, and, the inspiration of the Almighty, giveth them understanding;
texts.job.32.9: Great men, may not be wise, nor, elders, understand justice.
texts.job.32.10: Therefore, I said, Hearken unto me, I will show my knowledge—even I.
texts.job.32.11: Lo! I waited for your words, I kept giving ear for your reasons, until ye should search out what to say;
texts.job.32.12: Yea, unto you, gave I diligent heed,—But lo! there was, for Job, nothing to convince, nor could you of you answer his speeches.
texts.job.32.13: Lest ye should say, We have found out wisdom. GOD, must put him to flight, not man.
texts.job.32.14: Since he directed not to me discourse, therefore, with your speeches, will I not reply to him.
texts.job.32.15: They were dismayed, they responded no more, they suffered speech to forsake them;
texts.job.32.16: Though I waited, yet could they not speak, Surely they came to a stand, they responded no more.
texts.job.32.17: I will respond, even I—on my part, I will shew my knowledge, even I!
texts.job.32.18: For I am full of discourse, The spirit in my bosom, presseth me on.
texts.job.32.19: Lo! my bosom, is like wine not opened, Like new wine-skins, it will burst.
texts.job.32.20: I will speak, that I may freely breathe, I will open my lips and respond.
texts.job.32.21: Let me be partial to no man, and, unto no son of earth, give flattering titles,
texts.job.32.22: Surely I know not how to give flattering titles, How soon might my Maker take me away!
texts.job.33.1: But, in very deed, hear, I pray thee, Job, my discourse, and, to all my words, give thou ear.
texts.job.33.2: Lo! I pray thee, I have opened my mouth, My tongue, with my palate, hath spoken,
texts.job.33.3: Mine utterances come straight from mine own heart, and, what I know, my lips have truly spoken;
texts.job.33.4: The spirit of GOD, hath made me, and, the inspiration of the Almighty, giveth me life.
texts.job.33.5: If thou art able to answer me, Set in order before me—take thy stand!
texts.job.33.6: Lo! I am like thyself toward GOD, From clay, have I been nipped off, even I!
texts.job.33.7: Lo! my terror, will not startle thee, nor, my hand, upon thee, be heavy.
texts.job.33.8: But thou hast spoken in mine ears, and, the sound of words, I heard:—
texts.job.33.9: Pure am, I, without transgression,—Clean am, I, and have no iniquity;
texts.job.33.10: Lo! occasions of hostility, would he find against me, He counteth me an enemy to him;
texts.job.33.11: He putteth—in the stocks—my feet, He watcheth all my paths.
texts.job.33.12: Lo! in this, thou hast not been right—let me answer thee, For, GOD, is greater than, man.
texts.job.33.13: Wherefore, against him, hast thou contended? For, with none of his reasons, will he respond.
texts.job.33.14: For, in one way, GOD may speak,—and, in a second way, one may not heed it:—
texts.job.33.15: In a dream, a vision of the night, when a deep sleep falleth upon men, in slumberings upon the bed,
texts.job.33.16: Then, uncovereth he the ear of men, and, on their correction, affixeth a seal;
texts.job.33.17: To turn a son of earth from his deed, while yet, pride, from man he concealeth:
texts.job.33.18: He keepeth back his said from the pit, and his life from passing away by a weapon.
texts.job.33.19: Or he is chastised with pain, upon his bed, and, the strife of his bones, is unceasing!
texts.job.33.20: So that his life maketh loathsome [his] food, and his soul, dainty meat;
texts.job.33.21: His flesh wasteth away out of sight, and bared are the bones once unseen;
texts.job.33.22: So doth his soul draw near to the pit, and his life to the inflicters of death:
texts.job.33.23: If there hath been near him a messenger who could interpret—one of a thousand, to declare to the son of earth His uprightness,
texts.job.33.24: Then hath he shewed him favour, and said, Set him free from going down to the pit, I have found a price of redemption!
texts.job.33.25: His flesh hath been made fresher than a child’s, he hath returned to the days of his youth;
texts.job.33.26: He made supplication unto GOD, who hath accepted him, and he hath beheld his face with a shout of triumph, Thus hath he given back to man his righteousness.
texts.job.33.27: He sang before men, and said, I sinned, and, uprightness, I perverted, yet he requited me not;
texts.job.33.28: He hath ransomed my soul from passing away into the pit,—and, my life, in the light, shall have vision.
texts.job.33.29: Lo! a these things, doth GOD work, two ways, three, with a man;
texts.job.33.30: To bring back his soul from the pit, to enlighten with the light of the living.
texts.job.33.31: Mark well, O Job, and hearken to me, Be silent, and, I, will speak:
texts.job.33.32: If there is anything to say, reply to me, Speak, for I desire to justify thee;
texts.job.33.33: If not, do, thou, hearken unto me, Be silent, that I may teach thee wisdom.
texts.job.34.2: Hear, ye wise men, my words, and, ye who know, give ear unto me;
texts.job.34.3: For, the ear, trieth words, as, the palate, tasteth in eating.
texts.job.34.4: What is right, let us choose for ourselves, Let us know, among ourselves, what is good;
texts.job.34.5: For Job hath said—I am righteous, But, GOD, hath turned away my right;
texts.job.34.6: Concerning mine own right, shall I tell a falsehood? Incurable is my disease—not for any transgression.
texts.job.34.7: What man is like Job? He drinketh in scoffing like water;
texts.job.34.8: And is on the way to keep company, with the workers of iniquity, and to walk with lawless men.
texts.job.34.9: For he hath said, It profiteth not a man, when, his good pleasure, is with God.
texts.job.34.10: Wherefore, ye men of mind, hearken unto me,—Far be it, that, GOD, should be lawless, or, the Almighty, be perverse!
texts.job.34.11: For, what any son of earth doeth, he repayeth him, and, according to every man’s course, he causeth him to find.
texts.job.34.12: Nay, verily, GOD, will not condemn unjustly,—nor, the Almighty, pervert justice.
texts.job.34.13: Who set him in charge of the earth? Or who appointed [him] the whole world?
texts.job.34.14: If he should set against him his heart, His spirit and his inspiration, unto himself he should withdraw.
texts.job.34.15: All flesh together, would cease to breathe, and, the earth-born, unto dust, would return.
texts.job.34.16: If then [thou hast] understanding, hear this, Give thou ear to the teaching of my words:—
texts.job.34.17: Shall, the very hater of right, control? Or, the just—the mighty one, wilt thou condemn?
texts.job.34.18: Doth one say to a king, Abandoned one! Or, Lawless one! unto nobles?
texts.job.34.19: For he hath shewn no respect of persons unto princes, neither hath he recognised the rich rather than the poor? For, the work of his hands, are they all.
texts.job.34.20: In a moment, they die, even in the middle of the night,—A people are convulsed when they pass away, A mighty one is removed, without hand;
texts.job.34.21: For, his eyes, are on the ways of a man, and, all his footsteps, he beholdeth,—
texts.job.34.22: No darkness, and no death-shade, where the workers of iniquity may hide.
texts.job.34.23: For, unto no man, doth he appoint a repetition,—in going unto GOD in judgment;
texts.job.34.24: He shattereth mighty ones unsearchably, and setteth up others in their stead:
texts.job.34.25: Therefore, he observeth their works,—and overturneth [them] in a night, and they are crushed;
texts.job.34.26: In the place of lawless men, hath he chastised them, in presence of beholders.
texts.job.34.27: Forasmuch, as they turned from following him, and, none of his ways, did they teach;
texts.job.34.28: Causing to reach him the outcry of the poor, Yea, the outcry of the oppressed, he heareth.
texts.job.34.29: When, he, giveth quiet, who then shall condemn? And, when he hideth [his] face, who then shall sing of him? whether unto a nation or unto mankind altogether,
texts.job.34.30: That impious men may not reign, nor be ensnarers of the people.
texts.job.34.31: For, unto GOD, hath one [ever] said—I have borne punishment, I will not be perverse;
texts.job.34.32: What I see not, do, thou, shew me, If, perverseness, I have wrought, I will do it no more?
texts.job.34.33: According to thy mind, must he requite it, that thou hast refused? For, thou, must choose, and not, I, What then thou knowest, speak!
texts.job.34.34: The men of mind, will say to me, yea any wise man hearkening unto me:—
texts.job.34.35: Job, without knowledge, doth speak, and, his words, are not with discretion.
texts.job.34.36: Would that Job might be tested to the uttermost, for replying with the men of iniquity:
texts.job.34.37: For he addeth—unto his sin—rebellion, In our midst, he clappeth his hands, and multiplieth his sayings against GOD.
texts.job.35.2: This, dost thou think to be right? Thou hast said—My righteousness is more than GOD’S.
texts.job.35.3: For thou dost say, How can one profit by thee? How can I benefit, more than by my sin?
texts.job.35.4: I, will answer thee plainly, and thy friends with thee.
texts.job.35.5: Look at the heavens and see,—and survey the skies—they are higher than thou.
texts.job.35.6: If thou sinnest, what canst thou work against him? Or, if thy transgressions be multiplied, what canst thou do unto him?
texts.job.35.7: If thou art righteous, what canst thou give unto him? Or what, at thy hand, can he accept?
texts.job.35.8: Unto a man like thyself, might thy lawlessness [reach], and, unto a son of the earth-born, thy righteousness.
texts.job.35.9: By reason of the multitude of oppressions, [men] make outcry, They cry for help, by reason of the arm of the mighty;
texts.job.35.10: But none saith—Where is GOD my maker, Who giveth songs in the night;
texts.job.35.11: Who teacheth us more than the beasts of the earth, and, beyond the bird of the heavens, giveth us wisdom?
texts.job.35.12: There, [men] make outcry, and he answereth not, because of the arrogance of evil-doers.
texts.job.35.13: Howbeit, vanity, will GOD not hear, Yea, the Almighty, will not regard it.
texts.job.35.14: How much less when thou sayest thou wilt not regard him! The cause, is before him, and thou must wait for him.
texts.job.35.15: But, now, because it is not so, [thou sayest] —His anger hath punished, and yet hath he not at all known of transgression;
texts.job.35.16: Thus, Job, vainly openeth his mouth, Without knowledge, he multiplieth words.
texts.job.36.2: Restrain thyself for me a little, and I will shew thee, that, yet—for GOD, there is justification,
texts.job.36.3: I will bring my knowledge from afar, and, to my Maker, will I attribute righteousness.
texts.job.36.4: For, of a truth—not false, are my words, One of competent knowledge, is with thee.
texts.job.36.5: Lo! GOD, is mighty, yet will he not despise, Mighty in vigour of mind;
texts.job.36.6: He will not keep alive one who is lawless, but, the right of oppressed ones, will he grant;
texts.job.36.7: He will not withdraw—from a righteous one—his eyes,—but, with kings on the throne, He hath seated men triumphantly, and they have been exalted.
texts.job.36.8: But, if, bound in fetters, they have been captured with cords of affliction,
texts.job.36.9: Then hath he declared to them their deed, and their transgressions—that they were wont to behave themselves proudly;
texts.job.36.10: Thus hath he uncovered their ear to a warning, and said—that they should turn from iniquity.
texts.job.36.11: If they would hearken, and serve, they should complete their days, in prosperity, and their years, in pleasantness;
texts.job.36.12: But, if they would not hearken, by a weapon, should they pass away, and breathe their last, no one knowing.
texts.job.36.13: Yea, the impious in heart, should store up anger, They should not cry for help, when he bound them.
texts.job.36.14: Their soul should die in youth, and their life, among the unclean.
texts.job.36.15: He would deliver the humbled in his humiliation, and would uncover—in oppression—their ear.
texts.job.36.16: Yea he might even have allured thee—out of the mouth of straitness, [into] a wide space—no narrowness there,—and, the food set down on thy table, should have been full of fatness.
texts.job.36.17: But, with the plea of a lawless one, thou art full, Plea and sentence, will take fast hold.
texts.job.36.18: Because there is wrath, [beware] lest he take thee away with a stroke, Then let not, a great ransom, mislead thee.
texts.job.36.19: Will he value thy riches? Nay not precious ore, nor all the forces of strength.
texts.job.36.20: Do not pant for the night, when peoples disappear from their place.
texts.job.36.21: Beware, do not turn unto iniquity, For, this, thou hast chosen rather than affliction.
texts.job.36.22: Lo, GOD, exalteth himself by his strength, Who like him doth teach?
texts.job.36.23: Who enjoined on him his way? and who ever said, Thou hast wrought perversity?
texts.job.36.24: Remember, that thou extol his work, of which men have sung;
texts.job.36.25: Every son of earth, hath viewed it, Mortal man, looketh at it from afar.
texts.job.36.26: Lo, GOD, is greater than we can know, The number of his years, even past finding out!
texts.job.36.27: For he draweth up drops of water, They trickle as rain through his mist;
texts.job.36.28: With which the clouds flow down, They drop on man in abundance.
texts.job.36.29: But surely none can understand the burstings of the cloud, the crashing of his pavilion!
texts.job.36.30: Lo! he hath spread out over it, his lightning, The bed of the sea, hath he covered.
texts.job.36.31: For, by those things, he executeth judgment on peoples, He giveth food in abundance:
texts.job.36.32: Upon both hands, he putteth a covering of lightning, and layeth command upon it against an assailant:
texts.job.36.33: His rolling thunder telleth concerning him,—The cattle, even, concerning him that is coming up.
texts.job.37.1: Yea, at this, my heart quaketh, and starteth up out of its place.
texts.job.37.2: Hear! oh hear! the raging of his voice, A growling sound also, out of his mouth, goeth forth;
texts.job.37.3: Under the whole heavens, he letteth it loose, His lightning also, unto the wings of the earth;
texts.job.37.4: After it, roareth a voice, He thundereth with his voice of majesty, Nor will he hold them back, when his voice is heard.
texts.job.37.5: GOD thundereth with his voice, wonderfully, Doing great things, which we cannot know;
texts.job.37.6: For, to the snow, he saith, Fall earthwards,—Also to the downpour of rain, yea the downpour of his mighty rains.
texts.job.37.7: On the hand of every man, he setteth a seal, that all men may take note of his doing.
texts.job.37.8: So then the wild-beast hath gone into covert, and, in its lairs, doth it remain.
texts.job.37.9: Out of a chamber cometh a storm-wind, and, out of the north, cold.
texts.job.37.10: By the breath of GOD, is given—frost, and, the breadth of waters, is congealed;
texts.job.37.11: Also, with moisture, burdeneth he the thick cloud, He disperseth his lightning-cloud;
texts.job.37.12: Yea, the same, in circles, turneth itself to and fro, by his steering them to their work, whithersoever he commandeth them, over the face of the world, towards the earth.
texts.job.37.13: Whether, as a rod, or for his earth, or in lovingkindness, he causeth it to come.
texts.job.37.14: Give thou ear unto this, O Job, Stay, and consider well the wonders of GOD:—
texts.job.37.15: Canst thou got to know of GOD’S giving charge over them, or of the causing of the lightning of his cloud to shine forth?
texts.job.37.16: Canst thou get to know concerning the poisings of the thick cloud, the wonders of one who is perfect in knowledge?
texts.job.37.17: That thy garments should be hot when he quieteth the earth from the south?
texts.job.37.18: Didst thou spread out, with him, the skies, strong as a molten mirror?
texts.job.37.19: Let us know what we shall say to him, We cannot set in order, by reason of darkness.
texts.job.37.20: Shall it be declared to him—that I would speak? Were any man to say aught, he might he destroyed?
texts.job.37.21: Yet, now, men see not the light, bright though it is in the skies, when, a wind, hath passed over, and cleansed them.
texts.job.37.22: Out of the north, a golden light cometh, Upon GOD, is fearful splendour:
texts.job.37.23: The Almighty, whom we have not fully found out, is great in vigour,—Neither, justice nor abounding righteousness, will he weaken.
texts.job.37.24: Therefore, do men revere him, He will not regard any who are wise in heart.
texts.job.38.1: Then Yahweh responded to Job, out of a storm, and said:—
texts.job.38.2: Who is it that darkeneth counsel, by words, without knowledge?
texts.job.38.3: Gird, I pray thee—like a strong man—thy loins, that I may ask thee, and inform thou me:
texts.job.38.4: Where wast thou, when I founded the earth? Tell, if thou knowest understanding!
texts.job.38.5: Who set the measurements thereof, if thou knowest? Or who stretched out over it a line?
texts.job.38.6: Whereon were the pedestals thereof sunk? Or who laid the corner stone thereof;—
texts.job.38.7: When the morning stars sang together, and all the sons of God shouted for joy?
texts.job.38.8: Or [who] shut in, with double doors, the sea, when, bursting out of the womb, it came forth;
texts.job.38.9: When I put a cloud as the garment thereof, and a thick cloud as the swaddling-band thereof;
texts.job.38.10: And brake off for it my boundary, and fixed a bar and double doors;
texts.job.38.11: And said—Hitherto, shalt thou come, and no further,—and, here, shalt thou set a limit to the majesty of thy waves?
texts.job.38.12: Since thy days [began] hast thou commanded the morning? or caused the dawn to know its place;
texts.job.38.13: That it might lay hold of the wings of the earth, and the lawless be shaken out of it?
texts.job.38.14: It transformeth itself like the clay of a seal, so that things stand forth like one arrayed;
texts.job.38.15: That their light may be withdrawn from the lawless, and, the lofty arm, be shivered.
texts.job.38.16: Hast thou entered as far as the springs of the sea? Or, through the secret recesses of the resounding deep, hast thou wandered?
texts.job.38.17: Have the gates of death been disclosed to thee? And, the gates of the death-shade, couldst thou descry?
texts.job.38.18: Hast thou well considered, even the breadths of the earth? Tell—if thou knowest it all!
texts.job.38.19: Where then is the way, the light shall abide? And, the darkness, where then is its place?
texts.job.38.20: That thou mayest conduct it unto the bound thereof, and that thou mayest perceive the paths to its house.
texts.job.38.21: Thou knowest, for, then, hadst thou been born! And, in number, thy days are many!
texts.job.38.22: Hast thou entered into the treasuries of the snow? And, the treasuries of the hail, couldst thou see?
texts.job.38.23: Which I have reserved for a time of distress, for the day of conflict and of war?
texts.job.38.24: Where then is the way the lightning is parted? The east wind spreadeth itself abroad over the earth.
texts.job.38.25: Who hath cloven—for the torrent—a channel? Or a way for the lightning of thunders;
texts.job.38.26: To give rain over the no-man’s land, the desert, where no son of earth is;
texts.job.38.27: To satisfy the wild and the wilderness, to cause to spring forth the meadow of young grass?
texts.job.38.28: Hath the rain a father? Or who hath begotten the drops of dew?
texts.job.38.29: Out of whose womb, came forth the ice? And, the hoar-frost of the heavens, who hath given it birth?
texts.job.38.30: Like a stone, are the waters congealed, and, the face of the roaring deep, becometh firm!
texts.job.38.31: Canst thou bind the fetters of the Pleiades? Or, the bands of Orion, canst thou unloose?
texts.job.38.32: Canst thou bring forth the signs of the Zodiac each in its season? Or, the Bear and her Young, canst thou lead?
texts.job.38.33: Knowest thou, the statutes of the heavens? Or didst thou appoint his dominion over the earth?
texts.job.38.34: Canst thou lift up, to the thick cloud, thy voice, and the overflow of waters cover thee?
texts.job.38.35: Canst thou send forth the lightnings, so that they go, and say to thee, Behold us?
texts.job.38.36: Who hath put—into cloud-forms—wisdom? Or who hath given—to the meteor—understanding?
texts.job.38.37: Who can count the thin clouds, in wisdom? And, the bottles of the heavens, who can empty out;
texts.job.38.38: When the dust is cast into a clod, and the lumps are bound together?
texts.job.38.39: Wilt thou hunt—for the Lioness—prey? Or, the craving of the Strong Lion, wilt thou satisfy;
texts.job.38.40: When they settle down in dens, abide in covert, for lying in wait?
texts.job.38.41: Who prepareth for the Raven his nourishment,—when his young ones—unto GOD—cry out, [when] they wander for lack of food?
texts.job.39.1: Knowest thou the season when the Wild Goats of the crags beget? The bringing forth of the hinds, canst thou observe?
texts.job.39.2: Canst thou count the months they fulfil? Or knowest thou the time when they give birth?
texts.job.39.3: They kneel down, their young, they bring forth; their pains, they throw off;
texts.job.39.4: Their young become strong, they grow up in the open field, they go out, and return not unto them.
texts.job.39.5: Who hath sent forth the Wild Ass free? And, the bands of the swift-runner, who hath loosed?
texts.job.39.6: Whose house I have made the waste plain, and his dwellings, the land of salt:
texts.job.39.7: He laugheth at the throng of the city, The shoutings of the driver, he heareth not;
texts.job.39.8: He espieth the mountains, his pasture-ground, and, after every green thing, maketh search.
texts.job.39.9: Will the Wild-Ox be pleased to be thy servant? or lodge for the night by thy crib?
texts.job.39.10: Canst thou bind the wild-ox, so that—with the ridge—shall run his cord? Or will he harrow the furrows after thee?
texts.job.39.11: Wilt thou trust in him, because of the greatness of his strength? Wilt thou leave unto him thy toil?
texts.job.39.12: Wilt thou put faith in him, that he will bring back thy seed? and that, corn for thy threshing-floor, he will gather?
texts.job.39.13: The wing of the Ostrich that waveth itself joyfully, Is it the pinion of lovingkindness or the plumage?
texts.job.39.14: For she leaveth—to the earth—her eggs, and, on the dust, she letteth them be warmed;
texts.job.39.15: And hath forgotten, that, a foot, may crush them,—or, the wild beast, tread on them!
texts.job.39.16: Dealing hardly with her young, as none-of-hers, In vain, her labour, without dread.
texts.job.39.17: For GOD hath suffered her to forget wisdom, and given her no share in understanding.
texts.job.39.18: What time, on high, she vibrateth her wings, she laugheth at the horse and his rider.
texts.job.39.19: Couldst thou give—to the Horse—strength? Couldst thou clothe his neck with the quivering mane?
texts.job.39.20: Couldst thou cause him to leap like a locust? The majesty of his snort, is a terror!
texts.job.39.21: He diggeth into the plain, and rejoiceth in vigour, he goeth forth to meet armour;
texts.job.39.22: He laugheth at dread, and is not dismayed, neither turneth he back, from the face of the sword;
texts.job.39.23: Against him, whiz [the arrows of] the quiver, the flashing head of spear and javelin;
texts.job.39.24: With stamping and rage, he drinketh up the ground,—he will not stand still when the horn soundeth;
texts.job.39.25: As oft as the horn soundeth, he saith, Aha! And, from afar, he scenteth the battle,—the thunder of commanders and the war-cry.
texts.job.39.26: Is it, by thine understanding, that the Bird of Passage betaketh him to his pinions? spreadeth out his wings to the south?
texts.job.39.27: Or, at thy bidding, that the Eagle mounteth, and that he setteth on high his nest?
texts.job.39.28: The crag, he inhabiteth, and so lodgeth himself, on the tooth of the crag, and high fort;
texts.job.39.29: From thence, he searcheth out food, far away, his eyes do pierce;
texts.job.39.30: And, his young brood, suck up blood, and, where the slain are, there, is he.
texts.job.40.1: And Yahweh responded to Job, and said:—
texts.job.40.2: Shall a reprover contend, with the Almighty? He that disputeth with GOD, let him answer it!
texts.job.40.3: Then Job responded to Yahweh, and said:—
texts.job.40.4: Lo! I am of no account, what shall I reply to thee? My hand, have I laid on my mouth:
texts.job.40.5: Once, have I spoken, but I will not proceed, yea twice, but I will not add.
texts.job.40.6: So then Yahweh responded to Job, out of a storm, and said:—
texts.job.40.7: Gird, I pray thee—as a strong man—thy loins, I will ask thee, and inform thou me.
texts.job.40.8: Wilt thou even frustrate my justice? Wilt thou condemn me, that thou mayest appear right?
texts.job.40.9: But if, an arm like GOD, thou hast, and, with a voice like his, thou canst thunder,
texts.job.40.10: Deck thyself, I pray thee, with majesty and grandeur, Yea, with dignity and splendour, thou shalt clothe thyself;
texts.job.40.11: Pour out thy transports of anger, and look on every one who is high, and lay him low;
texts.job.40.12: Look on every one who is high, and humble him, yea tread down the lawless, on the spot:
texts.job.40.13: Hide them in the dust all together, Their faces, bind thou in darkness;
texts.job.40.14: And, even I myself, will praise thee, in that thine own right hand can bring thee salvation.
texts.job.40.15: Behold, I pray thee, the Hippopotamus, which I made with thee, Grass—like the ox, he eateth;
texts.job.40.16: Behold, I pray thee, his strength in his loins, and his force, in the muscles of his belly;
texts.job.40.17: He bendeth down his tail like a cedar, the sinews of his thighs, are twisted together;
texts.job.40.18: His bones, are barrels of bronze, his frame, is like hammered bars of iron:
texts.job.40.19: He, is the beginning of the ways of GOD, Let his maker, present him his sword:
texts.job.40.20: Surely the mountains bring, produce, to him, where, all the wild beasts of the field, do play;
texts.job.40.21: Under the lotus-trees, he lieth down, in a covert of reed and swamp;
texts.job.40.22: The lotus-trees cover him with their shade, the willows of the torrent-bed compass him about;
texts.job.40.23: Lo! the river becometh insolent—he is not alarmed! He is confident, though a Jordan burst forth to his mouth:
texts.job.40.24: Before his eyes, shall he be caught? With a hook, can one pierce his nose?
texts.job.41.1: Canst thou draw out the Crocodile with a fish-hook? Or, with a cord, canst thou fasten down his tongue?
texts.job.41.2: Wilt thou put a rush-cord on his nose? or, with a thorn, wilt thou pierce his jaw?
texts.job.41.3: Will he multiply unto thee supplications, or will he speak unto thee softly?
texts.job.41.4: Will he solemnise a covenant with thee? Wilt thou take him for a life-long servant?
texts.job.41.5: Wilt thou sport with him, as with a little bird? Or wilt thou bind him, for thy maidens?
texts.job.41.6: Shall the companions bargain over him? or will they part him among the traders?
texts.job.41.7: Wilt thou fill, with darts, his skin? or, with fish-spears, his head?
texts.job.41.8: Lay thou upon him thy hand, remember the battle—no more!
texts.job.41.9: Lo! any hope of him, hath been found deceptive, Even at the sight of him, shall not one be overwhelmed?
texts.job.41.10: None so bold, that he will rouse him! Who then is he that, before me, can stand?
texts.job.41.11: Who hath forestalled me, that I may repay him? Under all the heavens, mine it is!
texts.job.41.12: I will not pass by in silence his parts, or the matter of strength, or the grace of his armour.
texts.job.41.13: Who hath removed his outer garment, through his double row of teeth, who would enter?
texts.job.41.14: The doors of his face, who hath opened? The circles of his teeth, are a terror!
texts.job.41.15: A pride, are his arched sides, closed up, with a firm seal;
texts.job.41.16: One to another, they join, and, air, cannot enter between them;
texts.job.41.17: Each to its fellow, they cleave, they grasp each other, and cannot be parted;
texts.job.41.18: His sneezings, flash forth light, and, his eyes, are like the eyelashes of the dawn;
texts.job.41.19: Out of his mouth, torches dart forth, sparks of fire, escape;
texts.job.41.20: Out of his nostrils, proceedeth smoke, like a blown pot and rushes;
texts.job.41.21: His breath, setteth coals ablaze, and, a flame, out of his mouth, proceedeth;
texts.job.41.22: In his neck, lodgeth strength, and, before him, danceth dismay;
texts.job.41.23: The dewlaps of his flesh, cleave together, hardened upon him, they cannot be moved;
texts.job.41.24: His heart, is hardened like a stone, yea hardened, like the nether millstone;
texts.job.41.25: At his rising up, mighty men are afraid, by reason of terror, they are beside themselves:
texts.job.41.26: As for him that assaileth him, the sword availeth not, spear, dart, or coat of mail:
texts.job.41.27: He counteth iron as broken straw, and bronze as rotten wood:
texts.job.41.28: The arrow, will not make him flee, Into chaff, are sling-stones changed by him:
texts.job.41.29: As a straw, is a club accounted, and he laugheth at the whir of the javelin;
texts.job.41.30: His underparts, are points of potsherd, a pointed threshing roller spreadeth out upon the slime:
texts.job.41.31: He causeth to boil, as a cauldron, the raging deep, the sea, he maketh like a brewing vessel:
texts.job.41.32: After him, he lighteth up a path, one might think the resounding deep to be hoary!
texts.job.41.33: There is not—upon the dust—his like, that hath been made to be without fear;
texts.job.41.34: Every thing lofty, he beholdeth, he, is king over all ravenous beasts.
texts.job.42.1: Then Job responded to Yahweh, and said:—
texts.job.42.2: I know that, all things, thou canst do, and that no purpose can be withholden from thee.
texts.job.42.3: Who is it that hideth counsel without knowledge? Therefore, have I declared, but not understood, things too wonderful for me, which I could not know.
texts.job.42.4: Hear thou, I pray thee, and, I, will speak, I will ask thee, and inform thou me.
texts.job.42.5: By the hearing of the ear, had I heard thee, but, now, mine own eye, hath seen thee.
texts.job.42.6: For this cause, I tremble and repent, on dust and ashes.
texts.job.42.7: And it came to pass, after Yahweh had spoken these words unto Job, that Yahweh, said unto Eliphaz the Temanite, Kindled is mine anger against thee and against thy two friends, for ye have not spoken concerning me the thing that is right, like my servant Job.
texts.job.42.8: Now, therefore, take unto you seven bullocks and seven rams, and go unto my servant Job, and ye shall offer up an ascending-sacrifice in your own behalf, and, Job my servant, shall pray over you,—for, him, will I accept, that I may not deal out to you disgrace, because ye have not spoken concerning me the thing that is right, like my servant Job.
texts.job.42.9: So Eliphaz the Temanite and Bildad the Shuhite [and] Zophar the Naamathite went, and did according to that which Yahweh had spoken unto them,—and Yahweh accepted Job.
texts.job.42.10: And, Yahweh himself, turned the captivity of Job, when he prayed in behalf of his friends,—and Yahweh increased all that Job had possessed, unto twice as much.
texts.job.42.11: Then came unto him all his brethren and all his sisters, and all his former acquaintances, and they did eat bread with him in his house,—and shewed sympathy with him and comforted him, over all the calamity which Yahweh had brought upon him,—and they gave him, every one a weight of money, and every one, a ring of gold.
texts.job.42.12: And, Yahweh, blessed the latter end of Job, more than his beginning,—and so he came to have fourteen thousand sheep, and six thousand camels, and a thousand yoke of oxen, and a thousand she-asses.
texts.job.42.13: And he came to have seven sons, and three daughters;
texts.job.42.14: and he called the name of the first Jemima, and the name of the second Kezia,—and the name of the third, Keren-happuch.
texts.job.42.15: And there were found no women so fair as the daughters of Job, in all the land,—and their father gave them an inheritance, in the midst of their brethren.
texts.job.42.16: And Job lived, after this, a hundred and forty years,—and saw his sons and his sons’ sons, four generations.
texts.job.42.17: So Job died, old and satisfied with days.

texts.job.1.1: Hubo un varón en tierra de Uz, llamado Job; y era este hombre perfecto y recto, temeroso de Dios y apartado del mal.
texts.job.1.2: Y le nacieron siete hijos y tres hijas.
texts.job.1.3: Su hacienda era de siete mil ovejas, tres mil camellos, quinientas yuntas de bueyes, quinientas asnas y muchísimos criados; de modo que aquel varón era el más grande de todos los orientales.
texts.job.1.4: E iban sus hijos y hacían banquetes en sus casas, cada uno en su día; y enviaban a llamar a sus tres hermanas para que comiesen y bebiesen con ellos.
texts.job.1.5: Y acontecía que, habiendo pasado turno los días del convite, Job enviaba y los santificaba, y se levantaba de mañana y ofrecía holocaustos conforme al número de todos ellos. Porque decía Job: «Quizá habrán pecado mis hijos, y habrán renunciado a Dios en sus corazones». De esta manera hacía Job todos los días.
texts.job.1.6: Un día vinieron los hijos de Dios a presentarse delante de Yahvé, entre los cuales vino también Satanás.
texts.job.1.7: Yahvé dijo a Satanás: «¿De dónde vienes?» Entonces Satanás respondió a Yahvé, y dijo: «De rodear la tierra y de andar por ella».
texts.job.1.8: Yahvé dijo a Satanás: «¿Has considerado a mi siervo Job? Porque no hay nadie como él en la tierra, un hombre perfecto y recto, que teme a Dios y se aparta del mal».
texts.job.1.9: Entonces Satanás respondió a Yahvé y dijo: «¿Acaso Job teme a Dios de balde?
texts.job.1.10: ¿No le has cercado alrededor a él, a su casa y a todo lo que tiene, por todos lados? Has bendecido la obra de sus manos, y su hacienda ha aumentado en la tierra.
texts.job.1.11: Pero extiende ahora tu mano y toca todo lo que tiene, y verás si no blasfema contra ti en tu misma cara».
texts.job.1.12: Yahvé dijo a Satanás: «He aquí, todo lo que tiene está en tu mano. Solamente no extiendas tu mano sobre él». Entonces Satanás salió de la presencia de Yahvé.
texts.job.1.13: Y aconteció un día que sus hijos y sus hijas estaban comiendo y bebiendo vino en casa de su hermano el primogénito,
texts.job.1.14: que un mensajero vino a Job y le dijo: «Estando arando los bueyes y las asnas paciendo cerca de ellos,
texts.job.1.15: los sabeos acometieron y se los llevaron. Sí, han matado a los criados a filo de espada, y solamente yo he escapado para contártelo».
texts.job.1.16: Mientras él seguía hablando, vino también otro y dijo: «Fuego de Dios ha caído del cielo y ha quemado a las ovejas y a los criados y los ha consumido, y solamente yo he escapado para contarlo».
texts.job.1.17: Mientras él seguía hablando, llegó otro y dijo: «Los caldeos han formado tres escuadrones y han arremetido contra los camellos, y se los han llevado; sí, y han matado a los criados a filo de espada; y solamente yo he escapado para contártelo».
texts.job.1.18: Mientras él seguía hablando, vino también otro y dijo: «Tus hijos y tus hijas estaban comiendo y bebiendo vino en casa de su hermano el primogénito,
texts.job.1.19: y he aquí que vino un gran viento del desierto y golpeó las cuatro esquinas de la casa, y cayó sobre los jóvenes, y están muertos. Sólo yo he escapado para contarlo».
texts.job.1.20: Entonces Job se levantó, rasgó su manto, se rasuró la cabeza, se postró en tierra y adoró.
texts.job.1.21: Y dijo: «Desnudo salí del vientre de mi madre, y desnudo volveré allá. Yahvé dio, y Yahvé ha quitado. Bendito sea el nombre de Yahvé».
texts.job.1.22: En todo esto, Job no pecó ni acusó a Dios de haber obrado mal.
texts.job.2.1: Aconteció que otro día vinieron los hijos de Dios para presentarse delante de Yahvé, y Satanás vino también entre ellos para presentarse delante de Yahvé.
texts.job.2.2: Y dijo Yahvé a Satanás: «¿De dónde vienes?» Respondió Satanás a Yahvé, y dijo: «De rodear la tierra, y de andar por ella».
texts.job.2.3: Y Yahvé dijo a Satanás: «¿No has considerado a mi siervo Job, que no hay otro como él en la tierra, varón perfecto y recto, temeroso de Dios y apartado del mal, y que todavía retiene su integridad, a pesar de que tú me incitaste contra él para que lo arruinase sin causa?»
